title: Cockpit QUIC connect aborts in ring P-256
description: Connecting Cockpit to an enrolled QUIC host crashes the phux-remote-tunnel thread (EXC_BAD_INSTRUCTION / abort). Crash dump: /tmp/cockpit-dump. Fault is ring 0.17 p256_mul_mont whose PC-relative bl targets padding because Apple subsections_via_symbols + dead_strip dropped the file-local __ecp_nistz256_mul_mont helper. Reproduced on the 0.23.3 local install and confirmed in the shipping 0.23.2 phux-cockpit binary (same bl to ecp_nistz256_neg+0x40 / zeros). CLI remote works because rustc does not dead-strip that object. Fix: disable GC/dead_strip on the Cockpit executable that links libphux_client_ffi.a, and gate the shipping binary so p256_mul_mont's bl lands on real mul code.
close_reason: Disabled Mach-O dead_strip on Cockpit artifacts that link libphux_client_ffi.a (4ca38acf). RED: check-ring-p256-helpers.py failed on the crashing 0.23.3 install (bl to 0x0). GREEN: same check passed on the rebuilt binary (bl to mul); installed app relaunched and phux ls --remote phalls-mac-mini showed 1 client attached.

title: wss/QUIC accept loops are serialized and un-timed: one stalled peer wedges the whole remote surface
description:
A peer that completes the TCP/UDP handshake and then never speaks parks the sequential accept loop forever.

WsListener::accept (crates/phux-server/src/transport.rs) ran the TLS handshake and WebSocket upgrade inline with no deadline, and the loop in runtime/client.rs awaits accept() to completion before it can accept anyone else. The kernel keeps completing TCP handshakes, so later clients connect successfully and then wait for bytes userspace never sends -- 'SSL handshake has read 0 bytes'. QUIC (transport/quic.rs) had the identical defect on incoming.await, accept_bi() and authorize_preamble(), and because the whole remote surface shares one accept path, a single unanswered UDP datagram to the QUIC port took wss down with it.

Found in production: phux --remote to a Tailscale host failed with 'QUIC handshake timed out' while TCP still connected. Reproduced deterministically: one silent TCP peer wedges the listener; it recovers the instant that peer releases.

phux-relay already had this hardening (PREAMBLE_DEADLINE / CONSUMER_STREAM_DEADLINE, tokio::spawn per connection); phux-server never received it.

Fix: bound each admission step with a deadline in both transports. Follow-up worth considering: make the handshakes concurrent (JoinSet/FuturesUnordered) so the listener is not capped at one connection per deadline under abuse.
close_reason: Fixed on main by de18f3a0 (bounded WSS/QUIC admission) and e8228458 (all peer-driven accept paths), with paused-clock regression coverage

description: Remove the authoritative work identity/store/blob implementation and Cockpit-local runner plan introduced by #49. Replace it with a client architecture that keeps windows/tabs/focus/projections in Cockpit and assigns durable work identity, evidence, artifacts, signals, policy, and execution authority to Phux. Preserve the current ephemeral in-process terminal as an explicitly non-durable local path.
notes: PR opened: phall1/phux-cockpit#51. Merge after phall1/phux#487 so the governing ADR link is live. Both local and Phux-enabled gates passed.
close_reason: Merged as phall1/phux-cockpit#51 after Phux ADR-0092; Cockpit authoritative work storage was removed and the client boundary is on main.

title: Expose and switch real server-owned Phux sessions
description: Extend phux-client-ffi to retain and expose session summaries already carried by ATTACHED, then let Cockpit copy the catalog and switch attachment to a selected server-owned session without persisting invented remote topology. Keep Phux windows/layout as follow-up until the server publishes authoritative layout.
acceptance_criteria: FFI exposes tested session id/name/window/client/focused metadata with documented lifetime; Cockpit can display and select a real session, reconnect by server identity, and reconcile its terminals; remote state remains server-owned and is not written into local topology; complete Rust and Phux-inclusive Zig gates pass.
notes: Phux FFI commit 2e99c7de exposes the owned ATTACHED session catalog. Cockpit copies names/metadata, includes server sessions in the Go to palette, selects by stable session ID, reconnects through a new client generation, freezes old canvases until READY, and reconciles terminals without persisting remote topology. Rust tests/clippy/ffi-release and Phux-inclusive Zig gates pass. Exact remote window layout remains phux-cockpit-sfe because the server publishes no authoritative layout.
close_reason: Acceptance criteria completed; remaining authoritative server window-layout seam tracked separately as phux-cockpit-sfe.

title: Raise the real Native SDK PTY capacity to Cockpit's 32-terminal bound
description: The SDK commit pinned by main still exports max_effect_ptys=4, so Cockpit truthfully refuses the fifth shell while comments/docs/tests incorrectly assume 32. Land the measured 32-slot table bound in phall1/native, pin Cockpit to it, make the cross-repo capacity invariant non-skippable, and verify live shell reachability without removing Cockpit's bounded 32-terminal registry.
acceptance_criteria: Pinned SDK exports at least 32 PTY slots with a compile-time table-size budget; Cockpit hard-fails if SDK capacity is below max_terminals; topology tests no longer skip due to four slots; gate and drive-shell-ceiling evidence pass.
notes: Completed in Native SDK commit 87917c454432de5dd1eceb52d8a55575d5581289 and Cockpit pin/guard sdk-pty-capacity; SDK and Cockpit gates pass.
close_reason: Acceptance criteria completed; remaining authoritative server window-layout seam tracked separately as phux-cockpit-sfe.

title: Goal: terminal parity with shared Phux workspaces
description: Make Phux Cockpit a first-class macOS terminal whose limits, settings, tab interactions, lifecycle, accessibility, and failure recovery are at least as clear and reliable as mainstream native terminals, while making Cockpit and Phux attach to the same server-owned session/workspace identities rather than maintaining divergent local illusions. Deliver incrementally: remove artificial terminal ceilings or expose real resource limits honestly; turn Settings into an actionable configuration surface with an obvious config-file path/edit affordance; finish tab overflow, selection, close, reorder, keyboard, pointer, and accessibility behavior; establish and test the server seam for shared Phux sessions/spaces/tabs without pretending unsupported durability.
design: Preserve libghostty-vt as terminal engine, stable provider identity independent of tab/window placement, local-first behavior, and the Cockpit/coordinator/provider/event boundaries in docs/PRODUCT_DIRECTION.md. Prefer smallest real runtime seam over compatibility shims or fake restoration.
acceptance_criteria: The app has no unexplained low shell ceiling; Settings identifies and can open/edit the active config and covers core terminal preferences; tab behavior remains usable and discoverable under overflow and multiple windows; Cockpit can discover/attach server-owned Phux session/workspace identity shared with normal Phux; tests and live-app evidence cover changed behavior; zig build test exits 0 with a PASS verdict and Phux changes receive a complete provider verdict.
close_reason: Terminal capacity, actionable settings, tab correctness, and stable server-owned Phux session discovery/selection are complete and gated. Unsupported remote window topology remains explicitly tracked as phux-cockpit-sfe.

title: Bind SQLite WAL IO to trusted directory descriptors

The current same-inode main-file proof does not bind later sidecar resolution.
acceptance_criteria: Adversarial ancestor replacement before and after sqlite open/configure cannot redirect main/WAL/SHM side effects; main and sidecars remain in one trusted inode namespace; crash recovery and full gate pass.

title: Phux: generate nonces and verify authority in every client
description: Update all production Phux HELLO call sites to generate a fresh CSPRNG nonce, retain the exact encoded HELLO transcript, verify HELLO_OK authority fingerprint/signature/incarnation/grants, expose typed verification failure, and reject zero/replayed/mismatched proofs. No client may rely on AuthorityRequest::new zero sentinel.

title: Prove evidence-store crash boundaries in subprocesses

acceptance_criteria: Every barrier has a distinguishing red proof and recovery assertion for store sequence, stream heads, blobs, and integrity; no mock-only durability claim remains.

close_reason: Superseded by Phux ADR-0092 and Cockpit #51; authoritative projections and retention belong to the Phux coordinator.

title: Implement crash-safe evidence blob commits
description: Write output/snapshot/artifact blobs to same-filesystem temp files, sync, atomically rename, then reference in a committed event-store transaction. Recover orphan temps and report missing referenced blobs as explicit evidence gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Crash at each write/sync/rename/reference boundary yields old-or-new complete state; digest/length mismatch, missing blob, symlink swap, cleanup grace, and refcount tests pass.
notes:
Independent review blocked acceptance. Replace hard-link publication with renameatx_np RENAME_EXCL; define canonical artifact revision blob payload; append event + physical blob inventory + immutable relationship in one SQLite transaction; contextual media/trust/redaction belongs on reference and trust derives from persisted event; remove mutable reference deletion; serialize purge/reference and add recoverable physical state; use streaming BLAKE3 and policy-size u64; remove unshipped v1->v2 trust-laundering migration; add orphan reconciliation and race tests. Durable gap projection may use p1q.10.3 but the seam must be explicit.
Second review remaining fixes: fsync blob root after cross-dir rename/unlink; private unlinked verified spool before sink delivery; persist within-shard directory continuation; reject verified_provider until authenticated admission exists; bounded deleting/projection recovery APIs; idempotent purge that removes tombstone and supports retry/ambiguity; strengthen v3 types and artifact projection verification; rename unit failpoint claims. title: [epic] Break up the oversized client files, starting with driver.rs at ~6k lines
description:
Filed 2026-08-15 at the maintainer's request, to be worked AFTER the phux-k0cw fleet-inbox chain lands.

THE PROBLEM. crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs is ~6000 lines and growing; it is not the only one (input_dispatch.rs and server_frame.rs are in the same class). Symptoms observed while implementing phux-k0cw:

- handle_server_frame takes 22 positional parameters. Adding ONE (the client's own session id, for the foreign-layout guard) meant touching a dozen call sites across three files, several of them test harnesses that pass a column of bare 'None's whose meaning is positional only. That is a change-amplifier: the cost of a one-field addition is proportional to the file's size, not to the change.
- DispatchCtx has grown a field per composed feature, so every unrelated test fixture must be edited when one feature adds state.
- The main loop's per-frame block mixes protocol handling, cache folding, repaint policy, and subscription bookkeeping at one indentation level, which is why a foreign-metadata push could raise the fleet repaint but not the chrome repaint and nobody noticed.
- There is already a P3 bead for part of this (phux-jr84, 'Decompose the attach god-functions; retire run_action string-switch in favor of action_registry'). This epic supersedes/absorbs its intent at a higher priority and a wider scope.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. Not a rewrite, and not a cosmetic file split that leaves the same 22-argument call threaded through three modules. A split that only moves lines makes the map worse.

THE SESSION THIS WANTS. A deliberate sit-down that first DECOMPOSES the problem before touching code:
1. Measure: line counts, function lengths, parameter counts, fan-in/fan-out per module across phux-client (and flag any other crate in the same state).
2. Identify the real seams. Candidates visible today: the frame dispatcher vs. the driver loop; the driver's cache/bookkeeping state (panes, agent_meta, foreign_* caches, subscription sets) as an owned struct with methods rather than a dozen parallel locals; repaint policy as its own type; the subscription sweeps as one 'what should this connection be watching' component.
3. Decide the parameter problem explicitly: a context struct, a builder, or fewer functions. The 22-argument signature is the single loudest symptom and should be named as a target with a chosen answer.
4. Sequence it so each step is independently landable and green, the way phux-k0cw.1-9 was sequenced. A big-bang refactor of a 6k-line file in one commit is unreviewable.
5. Only then execute.

CONSTRAINT. The test suite is the safety net and must stay green at every step; no behaviour change is in scope. Where a refactor reveals a behaviour bug, file it separately rather than fixing it silently inside the move.
design:
MEASURED DECOMPOSITION 2026-08-17 (autonomous run). THE BEAD'S ANCHORS WERE STALE AND HOW THEY WENT STALE IS THE LESSON. Three commits (024bde0f, 6d291b46, 8504f778) already split driver.rs/input_dispatch.rs/server_frame.rs into directories. Every one was a PURE FILE MOVE (+8479/-8196, +7838/-7618, +5588/-5527): no signature changed, no state reorganized. It did not merely fail to help — it made the parameter problem WORSE. The two worst signatures in the workspace today were CREATED by the driver.rs split: handle_config_reload (24 params) and refresh_fleet_if_open (19 params), helpers threading the same driver locals across a module boundary.

CURRENT MEASUREMENTS (verified): main_loop 2474 lines / 76 top-level locals (bead said 1993/62 — it GREW); its tokio::select! is 1635 lines over 11 arms, of which the conn.recv() arm is 824 and the frame-outcome fold inside it is 795. handle_server_frame 1122 lines / 22 params (confirmed). run_action 796 lines / 34 arms / 4 params. dispatch_input_events 779 lines / 9 params. DispatchCtx 37 borrow fields with 18 literal constructions at 37 lines each (~590 lines of fixture). server_frame/tests.rs has a 20-PARAMETER LOCAL SHIM at :765, 19 call sites, and 84 bare 'None,' lines with NO comments — meaning is positional only. phux-client carries 14 too_many_arguments allows, 14 too_many_lines, 5 cognitive_complexity.

THE CHOSEN ANSWER TO THE PARAMETER PROBLEM: an OWNING context struct, not a borrowing one. Rejected builder (the 22 args are &mut borrows into main_loop's stack frame; a builder relocates borrow-checking and adds construction cost on a per-frame path, and .focused_session(None).status_bar(None) is the same None column with more typing). Rejected 'fewer functions' alone (that is exactly what the previous split did, and it produced the 24-param function). WHY DispatchCtx ALREADY FAILED AT THIS: it is a bag of borrows into a flat stack frame — because main_loop owns state as 76 loose locals, every field must be &'a mut T, so the struct has no Default, cannot be constructed without naming every field, and cannot grow a field without editing every construction site. It is a 37-field positional argument list wearing a struct's clothes. THE FIX IS TO MOVE OWNERSHIP ONE LEVEL DOWN: main_loop's 76 locals become ~6 owned structs (SessionMirror, PeerWatch, ChromeCtx, ConfigState, InputState, LoopTimers) which CAN derive Default, so the ctx types become 3-5 borrow params. Precedent already in-tree: PeerInputs<'a> (attach/sidebar_zones.rs:35) is this pattern at one-tenth scale; FrameOutcome is it on the return side.

SEAM CORRECTIONS: (1) repaint POLICY is already solved — attach/repaint.rs RepaintAccumulator/Repaint/RepaintLevel, monotone drain-once, 6 tests. Do not rebuild it. The missing type is the repaint EXECUTOR (21 paint call sites at 9-19 args). (2) subscriptions.rs already extracted the sweep FUNCTIONS; what remains is making PeerWatch own their STATE (8 parallel locals, peer_inputs() rebuilt 10x). (3) The real seam in main_loop is the FRAME-OUTCOME FOLD (24 FrameOutcome fields folded into ~30 driver locals over 795 lines at one indentation level, with ZERO direct unit coverage) — that is where the bead's 'foreign-metadata push raises fleet repaint but not chrome repaint' defect lives.

THE ANTI-TRAP GUARD, a review criterion on EVERY child bead: no child may land a new or modified function with >=10 parameters, and none may add a too_many_arguments allow. The count in phux-client must be MONOTONICALLY NON-INCREASING: 14 today -> <=2 at jx39.7, enforced by a size-budget gate in jx39.7.

SCORECARD (today -> after .7): main_loop 2474->1150; locals 76->30; handle_server_frame params 22->5; worst signature 24->6; DispatchCtx fields 37->8; DispatchCtx test literals 18->0; bare None in server_frame/tests.rs 84->15; too_many_arguments allows 14->2; unit tests over the frame fold 0->6; attach/ production lines ~24900 -> ROUGHLY FLAT. That last row is the honest one and the whole point: the target is a smaller CHANGE-COST, not a smaller line count. The previous three splits moved 21000 lines and moved no number in this table.

EXPLICIT NON-TARGETS so the epic does not sprawl: attach/input.rs (VT parser, flat tables, 0 allows), render/chrome/sidebar.rs, render/chrome/status_bar.rs, attach/render.rs, attach/connection.rs, render/overlay/select_list.rs, agent_prompt.rs — all long but cohesive with no parameter problem. action_registry.rs is a PRESENTATION CATALOGUE (ActionSpec/REGISTRY/palette_items) with no handler, no fn pointer, no execution path; it is coupled to the dispatcher only by the every_action_has_exactly_one_doc_home partition test, which is working drift prevention. run_action is a flat dispatch table (34 arms, avg 23 lines, 4 params) where adding an action is O(1). 'Retire run_action in favor of action_registry' is the WRONG prescription and is out of scope. The bodies of handle_server_frame and dispatch_input_events stay: the stages fix their SIGNATURES; splitting the ordered protocol dispatcher risks routing precedence (its own match_same_arms allow reason says so). All of phux-server/phux-protocol is a DIFFERENT epic.
acceptance_criteria: A decomposition plan exists as child beads with a chosen answer to the parameter-threading problem; driver.rs is materially smaller with the seams named in the plan; no behaviour change; the workspace suite is green at each landed step.
notes:
STAGE 1 LANDED 2026-08-17 (branch w5/jx39-chromectx, commit 5847faf6) — with THREE corrections to this epic's DESIGN that later stages must inherit.

CORRECTION 1, IMPORTANT: THE ONBOARDING BUG DOES NOT EXIST. The design said 21 paint sites vs 18 finish_return_onboarding_after_paint calls, implying three paint paths strand the onboarding claim. That was WRONG — counting statements in the original main_loop gives 19 paint and 19 finish. Every paint path finishes. The one structural asymmetry is DELIBERATE and correct: the onboarding INTRO overlay paint commits on out.flush() succeeding via finish_onboarding_claim (not on the return-notice being published), and the finish fed by a paint inside handle_server_frame pairs off with it. Stage 1 preserved this by leaving the intro paint outside the executor with a comment, and deliberately did NOT add the ExecuteFlags{finish_onboarding} the design called for — a bool false at exactly one site that also needs a DIFFERENT finish function would have been fiction. DO NOT file the discrepancy bug and do not re-derive this.

CORRECTION 2: the allow baseline was 23, not 14 — the design's number was measured differently. Stage 1 took it 23 -> 14 (paint.rs 4->0, driver/chrome.rs 3->0, driver/overlay_paint.rs 2->0), added none. Later stages must measure their own baseline and report against it.

CORRECTION 3: ChromeCtx could NOT live in attach/driver/ as the design assumed. attach/paint.rs is a SIBLING of driver, and a no_module_depends_on_attach_driver layering test enforces that. The struct lives in attach/chrome_ctx.rs; only the executor impl is in attach/driver/repaint_exec.rs because the overlay compositor is driver-private.

ACHIEVED: main_loop 2474 -> 2133 lines (target was <=2180); locals 77 -> 75; paint_active_overlay 13->4 params, refresh_fleet_if_open 19->6, refresh_window_chrome 10->4, paint_full_frame 10->5, paint_chrome_in_place 9->4. Snapshots byte-identical (0 .snap modified, 0 .snap.new), 3913/3913 workspace tests.

DESIGN LESSON CONFIRMED, worth carrying into every later stage: Stage 1's first cut bundled the session kernel into its PaneScene grouping and it immediately taxed refresh_window_chrome's unit tests with standing up a libghostty kernel they never read. A BUNDLE THAT TAXES ITS CHEAPEST CALLER *IS* THE CHANGE-AMPLIFIER this epic exists to remove. The kernel became an explicit param on the two functions that render pane interiors. Group by who READS the state, not by what looks related.

title: Attach never reflowed panes to the chrome-inset content rect
description:
The server sizes each pane's PTY from ATTACH.viewport (the client's OUTER terminal, chrome included) in apply_attach_viewport, and its own comment defers the off-by-one to 'the client's concern via the post-attach TERMINAL_RESIZE reflow path'. The client never had that path: nothing emitted TERMINAL_RESIZE between ATTACHED and the first SIGWINCH.

Symptom: with a status bar docked, the pane's libghostty mirror is one row taller than the content rect the client paints into, so the shell's bottom line lands on a row that is clipped away and the bar looks like it overwrote it. Self-heals on resize / split / sidebar toggle because those paths do reflow.

Second gap in the same family: the persisted-layout restore (MetadataValue) and the peer-broadcast (MetadataChanged) arms set layout_replaced but not reflow_panes, so a restored multi-pane layout kept the attach-time winsize on every leaf.
close_reason: Closed

title: Stage 2: Three-zone row model, hit-test and painter
description:
Stage 2 of 9 in the fleet-inbox sidebar chain (epic phux-k0cw).

COMMIT SUBJECT
  feat(client): rebuild the sidebar row model as three zones

FILES
  - crates/phux-client/src/render/chrome/sidebar.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/render/chrome/snapshots/phux_client__render__chrome__sidebar__tests__sectioned_layout_snapshot.snap
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/input_dispatch.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/rendered.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/snapshots/phux_client__attach__driver__tests__palette_over_sidebar.snap

VALIDATION
  cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'binary_id(phux-client)' && cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'package(phux-client)' && just ci
design: The allocator rewrite. sidebar.rs consts: add `pub const NEEDS_YOU_HEADER: &str = "needs you"`, `pub const HERE_HEADER: &str = "here"`, keep `SPACES_HEADER` for zone 3, add `pub const NEEDS_YOU_CAP: usize = 5` and `pub const HERE_FLOOR: usize = 3` (header + one two-row block); delete `AGENTS_HEADER` and `AGENTS_EMPTY` (zone 1 has no empty state by design). Add `#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)] pub struct SidebarCounts { pub needs_you: usize, pub windows: usize, pub roster: usize }`. Replace `SidebarRow`'s `AgentsHeader`/`Agent(usize)`/`AgentsEmpty` with `NeedsYouHeader`, `NeedsYou(usize)`, `NeedsYouOverflow`, `HereHeader`, `RosterEntry(usize)`, `RosterOverflow`; keep `WindowName`/`WindowBranch`/`SpacesHeader`/`Blank`/`NewWindow`/`Menu` and keep the enum `Copy`. Rewrite `row_model` to `#[must_use] pub fn row_model(counts: SidebarCounts, h: u16) -> Vec<SidebarRow>` preserving the documented 'derivable from counts alone' invariant at :232-234 and the non-saturating `body = h - footer` safety (footer is 2 exactly when `h >= MIN_FOOTER_HEIGHT`). New allocation order, inverting today's window-greedy order: (1) footer reserved as today; (2) zone 1 gets `min(counts.needs_you, NEEDS_YOU_CAP)` rows plus one `NeedsYouOverflow` when `counts.needs_you > NEEDS_YOU_CAP`, the whole reservation clamped to `body.saturating_sub(HERE_FLOOR)` so the focused session is never squeezed to nothing on a short strip, and contributing ZERO rows — no header, no gap, no placeholder — when `counts.needs_you == 0`; (3) `HereHeader` + the existing two-row `WindowName`/`WindowBranch` blocks with the same mid-block truncation; (4) zone 3 only when `rows.len() + 3 <= body` (gap + `SpacesHeader` + at least one row), `RosterEntry(j)` until `body` is exhausted with a trailing `RosterOverflow` when rows remain, and zero rows when `counts.roster == 0`; (5) `Blank` pad; (6) footer. Change `SidebarHit` to `Window(usize) | NeedsYou(usize) | Roster(usize) | Fleet | NewWindow | Menu | Collapse` — index-based so the enum stays `Copy`; `Fleet` is what both overflow rows commit. Rewrite `hit_test` to `#[must_use] pub fn hit_test(rect: Rect, counts: SidebarCounts, x: u16, y: u16) -> Option<SidebarHit>`, keeping the collapse-corner rule (:313-319) and the separator-column exclusion (:321-323) byte-for-byte. Painter: add fields `needs_you: Vec<AgentEntry>` and `roster: Vec<SessionRosterEntry>` with `pub fn set_needs_you(&mut self, ...) -> bool` / `pub fn set_roster(&mut self, ...) -> bool` following the same change-report contract as `set_windows`; CRITICALLY widen `last` (:350) to `(Rect, Vec<WindowInfo>, Vec<AgentEntry>, Vec<SessionRosterEntry>)` and update both the equality check (:408-414) and the store (:417) or the strip silently freezes. title: [epic] The fleet inbox: cross-session attention sidebar
description:
Turn the TUI sidebar from a session-local structural list into a bounded, cross-session ATTENTION INBOX. This is step 0 of the five-step fleet arc and the reframe the rest of the arc depends on: once the human has a ranked, bounded inbox, every later bead is queue economics (cost per item, then arrival rate, then removing the human for whole classes of item).

THE PROBLEM, BOTH ENDS. The competitor (herdr) paints every workspace x every agent whether or not any of it wants the human, so at ~9 agents it is a wall. phux paints only the attached session, so at ~6 sessions it is a keyhole. Both sidebars are STRUCTURAL: neither ranks. phux already owns the primitive that fixes it - attention_rank in crates/phux-client/src/render/chrome/sidebar.rs:163 (blocked > done-unvisited > working > settled > unknown, with seen decay) - but it is scoped to the attached session.

THE DESIGN (agreed 2026-08-15). Three zones instead of today's two:

  ZONE 1 'needs you' - cross-session attention queue, ranked by attention_rank, CAPPED to K rows with a '+N more' overflow row that opens the fleet dashboard. Rows carry the session name and commit switch-session { name, window, pane }. Renders ZERO rows and returns its height when nothing wants the human.

  ZONE 2 'here' - the focused session's windows at full detail (today's two-row blocks with the branch sub-line).

  ZONE 3 'spaces' - a roster, ONE line per other session, rolled up to a status dot plus a compact state histogram ('!1 *2'). Capped only by remaining strip height. Satellite sessions appear here as ordinary rows, which is the federation payoff delivered as a UI detail.

Plus: [sidebar] enabled flips to true (it is commented out at false in crates/phux-config/src/default.toml:450, so today none of this reaches anyone who does not go looking) and width rises from 20 to fit a nested tree.

FOUR RULES THAT MAKE IT SCALE.
1. Cap the queue, never cap the roster. The queue competes for the eye; the roster is one line per space and the human WANTS it complete - that is the 'I forget which sessions are on the line' need. 12 sessions = 12 lines, not 60.
2. Rollup carries counts, not just a worst-state colour. A dot says what; the count says how much.
3. Quiet when calm. The competitor's sidebar is the same wall at rest as under load; a sidebar that SHRINKS when you are calm is demoable and structurally unavailable to them.
4. Two surfaces, two jobs. Sidebar = ambient and bounded. The C-a A fleet dashboard = complete and on demand. This stops the sidebar trying to be the dashboard.

NO WIRE CHANGE (ADR-0030). Sessions are consumer projections; a richer client view earns no new wire surface. The live cross-session feed is enumerate-at-attach plus follow AgentEvent::PaneSpawned / PaneClosed on the server-wide event subscription the client ALREADY holds (driver.rs:1968 sends SubscribeEvents { terminal: None }; events.rs:19-21 documents EventScope::Server as every event for any observable Terminal). See phux-w7z2.20, whose 'this needs a wire change' conclusion is contested on exactly this evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The sidebar renders three zones; the queue is cross-session, ranked, capped, and empty-when-calm; the roster shows one rolled-up line per other session including satellites; peer state stays live via subscriptions rather than the attach-time snapshot; [sidebar] is on by default; docs/consumers/tui.md section 6.4 describes the shipped behaviour; just ci-full is green.

title: cell_grid content is invisible to the GPU packet fingerprint, so typed text is never re-encoded
description: ROOT CAUSE CANDIDATE for phux-cockpit-aht, found 2026-08-12 by a six-seam architectural trace and independently confirmed by an adversarial verifier. canvasGpuCommandFingerprint (SDK src/primitives/canvas/serialization.zig:1109-1221) decides whether a retained command must be re-encoded to the GPU host. It hashes kind, bounds, opacity, stroke_width, cap, id, clip, transform, shape, paint, image, text, effect - and NEVER reads command.cells. The cell_grid arm of gpu.zig:502-524 puts ALL terminal content into .cells and leaves shape/paint/text/image/effect empty, and CellGrid.bounds() is purely geometric. So a cell_grid row's packet fingerprint is INVARIANT under every possible content change. Downstream: canvas_frame.zig:1557 sets upserts[index]=false on a fingerprint match, :1719 skips re-encoding it, and appkit_host.m calls rasterCacheRemoveKey only for evicted/upserted keys - so the host re-blits the raster it already has. terminal_grid.zig:983 emits one cell_grid PER ROW under a stable key ids.at(0x60_0000+row), so a row's glyphs can never change on glass once a retained baseline exists. The cursor is a SEPARATE fill_rect (ids.at(0x61_0002)) whose bounds and paint ARE hashed, so it upserts every keystroke. Predicted appearance: a cursor advancing across untouched background leaving no glyphs - the owner's 'the text is see-through' and 'is the text color the same as the background'. It also explains why every previous diagnosis missed: the CPU reference renderer re-rasterizes from the content-aware display list (so screenshots always looked right), gpu_sample is frozen at the first non-blank frame, and a background config change alters a fill_rect PAINT which IS hashed and therefore does reach glass. CONFIRMED AT UNIT LEVEL, TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, both with positive and negative controls: a test asserting fingerprint(typed) != fingerprint(base) for a cluster change 'ab'->'xb' FAILS (exit 1) and flips to PASS under expectEqual; a second agent drove the real chain terminal_grid.paint -> DisplayList.renderPlan -> canvasGpuCommandFromRenderCommand -> canvasGpuCommandFingerprint and added a positive control (repaint at a different origin yields changed=1, proving the hash is live on cell_grid commands rather than inert) plus a check that the two painted states genuinely differ. NOT YET ESTABLISHED: that this produces the owner's symptom on glass. A live A/B by the parent - patched SDK vs pinned SDK, same p10k shell, same keystroke - gave 26 upserts/7066 bytes vs 27/7159, i.e. NO discriminating difference, because powerlevel10k repaints its whole prompt every keystroke and most of those commands are fill_rects that hash correctly either way. That measurement cannot separate the two builds and is not evidence either way. FIX: docs/sdk-patches/cell-grid-fingerprint.patch hashes the grid identity and std.mem.sliceAsBytes(grid.cells), mirroring render_fingerprints.zig:109 cellGridFingerprint which already does this over a full screen every frame. Applied to a sandbox copy, the SDK's own canvas-frame, canvas and platform suites are exit 0. docs/sdk-patches/cell-grid-fingerprint-test.patch is the regression test that would have caught it.

title: Token store is loaded once at startup; phux pair needs a server restart to take effect
description:
REPRODUCER:
  phux pair                      # mints a token, appends to remote-tokens
  <connect a device with it>     # REJECTED
  phux upgrade                   # re-exec reloads the store
  <connect again>                # accepted

Observed live: remote-tokens held 18 entries while the running server logged 'tokens=16' -- the two most recent, including the one the user was typing into the phux mobile app, were unknown to it. Presents as pairing silently not working.

CAUSE: crates/phux-server/src/runtime/mod.rs::build_ws_listener (~1248) calls auth::TokenStore::load once and moves the store into the listener. Nothing re-reads the file; there is no watch, no reload on connect, no invalidation. Same shape in the QUIC listener path (~1326).

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: ADR-0081 made the server auto-bind an overlay listener at startup precisely so that 'phux pair' would be a pure credential operation needing no restart -- 'the door is already there; pairing turns the lock'. That is only half true: the listener exists, but the credential SET is frozen at startup, so the lock cannot actually be turned. The one-command onboarding story does not work end to end as documented.

FIX OPTIONS:
  (a) Re-read the store per accepted connection. Simplest and correct; the file is tiny and connections are rare. Cost: a stat+read on the auth path.
  (b) Reload on mtime change (stat per connection, re-read only when changed).
  (c) Have 'phux pair' signal the running server to reload (needs a wire command or a signal handler).
(a) or (b) is preferred -- no protocol change, and revocation (deleting a line) starts working too, which today also requires a restart.

ALSO UPDATE ADR-0081, whose Decision section claims pairing needs no restart. Either the claim or the implementation has to move; the fix above makes the claim true.

WORKAROUND: 'phux upgrade' after pairing -- graceful re-exec (ADR-0032) reloads the store and preserves panes. Verified: tokens 16 -> 18 with both sessions intact.
close_reason: Closed

title: Creating a pane while attached kills the client (new-window and split-pane)
description:
REPRODUCER (deterministic, on 0.14.0 and at least back to 0.12.1):
  phux attach <session>
  press C-a c   (new-window)   -> client dies
  press C-a %   (split-pane)   -> client dies

Both fail identically:
  phux: attach failed: protocol error: frame is not valid from a server in the
  attached phase: Error { code: InternalError, message: "native history request
  failed: invalid snapshot handle or token" }

So ANY pane created while a client is attached tears the client down. This is the core interactive workflow.

NOT A REGRESSION from the 0.14.0 socket/attach work. Evidence: archive-20260809/client-52996.log (v0.12.1, 2026-08-07) ends at exactly the same point -- 'action=new-window', then one HistoryStatus Loading line for the new terminal, then nothing. The failure text goes to stderr, not the client log, which is why old logs merely stop rather than showing the error. 11 archived logs used new-window; none recorded the error, all consistent with the same silent death. It was unreachable for the reporter until the ATTACH_READY fix let attach succeed at all.

NARROWED TO: phux-server/src/terminal_actor/mod.rs::handle_native_history (~3497). It returns NativeStateError::InvalidHandle when self.native_cursor_owners.get(&owner) is missing, or when the binding's cursor/terminal_id/stream_id/bootstrap_id do not all match the request. Bindings are inserted only in finish_native_bootstrap (~3318), keyed by owner (client id) within one terminal actor.

Client log shows the new pane DOES get a bootstrap and a cursor (HistoryStatus Loading, next_cursor bytes: 32) before the request is refused -- so the failure is a mismatch or a missing binding for the newly created terminal's actor, not a missing bootstrap. Next step: determine which path bootstraps a pane created mid-attach (as opposed to the aggregate attach path in runtime/attach.rs::prepare_attach), and whether it registers the native cursor owner at all, or registers it under a different bootstrap_id/stream_id than the frames sent to the client.

WORKAROUND: create sessions from the CLI ('phux new --session NAME') and attach to them; multi-session attach works. Only in-TUI pane/window creation is affected.
close_reason: Closed

title: The Claude shim writes state:unknown on every hook, so agent wait exits 1 mid-turn
description:
REGRESSION introduced by the phux-w7z2.26 fix on this branch. Filed P0 because
it breaks the flagship orchestration loop (`agent send-keys` then `agent wait`)
on exactly the panes phux instruments most deeply, and nothing in the test
suite covers it — CI is green with the bug in place.

MECHANISM, every link verified in the tree:

1. crates/phux/src/commands/agent/shim.rs set_state now runs
   `phux agent set "$target" --name claude --kind claude` with NO --state, on
   the UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart and Stop hooks.
2. crates/phux/src/commands/agent/record.rs:47-49 —
   `state: state.map(...).unwrap_or_default()` is AgentMetaState::Unknown.
3. crates/phux-client/src/agent_meta.rs:118-119 — AgentRecord.state carries
   `#[serde(default)]` with NO `skip_serializing_if`, so it is serialized. The
   shim's literal bytes are {"name":"claude","kind":"claude","state":"unknown"}.
4. SET_METADATA replaces the record wholesale (record.rs:26-27, "last writer
   wins; no field merges"), so each hook clobbers the detector's live state
   back to unknown until the detector's next tick refills it.
5. crates/phux-client/src/agent_wait.rs:233-238 — EdgeTracker::observe returns
   Verdict::Departed{reason: WithdrewToUnknown} on ANY edge into Unknown.
6. crates/phux/src/commands/agent/wait.rs:123-145 maps Departed to
   codes::AGENT_DEPARTED and EXIT_FAILURE.

CONSEQUENCE: on any pane running the shim, the Stop hook fires an identity
write at the end of EVERY turn, producing a working -> unknown edge, so an
in-flight `phux agent wait` exits 1 (agent_departed) instead of 0. A mid-turn
PermissionRequest or Notification does the same, earlier. Before this branch
the Stop hook wrote --state done and the wait was satisfied.

WHY IT IS UNCOVERED: `grep -rln WithdrewToUnknown crates/` returns only
crates/phux-client/src/agent_wait.rs. No test anywhere exercises the generated
shim against `agent wait`. The shim's own tests assert on the rendered wrapper
STRING only.

PROPOSED FIX (~6 lines, entirely inside shim.rs, keeps the .26 ruling's
substance — still identity-only, still never a state): write identity ONCE at
session start instead of on every hook. Map SessionStart to a new `start` case,
make `blocked` fire only `run_phux ask`, drop the `done|idle|working` arm, and
point the inner launch path's `set_state working` at `start`. Identity never
changes mid-session, so nothing is lost, the record exists before any wait
would begin, and there is then no edge INTO unknown at all.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that drives the generated shim's hook sequence against a
live server while an `agent wait` is in flight, and asserts the wait is not
satisfied-or-departed by the hook write. A wrapper-string assertion is not
enough — that is the gap that let this ship.

Documented as a known divergence in docs/consumers/agents.md section 5.1 until
fixed; remove that callout when this closes.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/agent-detection-p1-bugs. The shim now writes identity exactly once, at SessionStart (SHIM_SCHEMA 2 -> 3): set_state gained a 'start' arm that is the sole 'agent set' caller, 'blocked' reaches only 'phux ask' (ADR-0035/0036, writes nothing to the record), and the UserPromptSubmit/Stop hooks are unwired since they would now write nothing and only cost a subprocess per turn. The inner launch path stamps 'start' instead of 'working'. Proven by commands::agent::shim::tests::only_the_start_arm_writes_the_record, which asserts structurally that exactly one line reaches 'agent set', that it is the 'start' arm, that the per-hook 'blocked' arm reaches 'ask' and never 'agent set', and that no write-nothing hook is wired. Three assertions in install_over_a_stale_shim_upgrades_it_and_uninstall_removes_exactly_its_own_files hardcoded schema 2 and now use SHIM_SCHEMA so they cannot rot on the next bump. The upgrade message distinguishes a schema-1 (declared state) from a schema-2 (per-turn clobber) predecessor. just ci green.

title: The asked-to-answer round trip: join detector blocked to ADR-0035 asked, then phux agent answer
description:
Completeness-critique F3, ranked third of nine and described as the differentiator no competitor can structurally reach. Large, and it is where the epic three ADRs compose into a loop instead of a loop that halts.

THE VERIFIED GAP. AgentEvent Asked, carrying id, question, suggestions and elapsed_seconds, SHIPS - ADR-0035, wire tag 0x09, field-tagged TLV. phux ask and phux_ask emit it. phux watch --json surfaces it. NOTHING ANYWHERE CONSUMES AN ANSWER. grep for answer across crates returns only doc prose and the word answered in unrelated comments. There is no verb, no frame and no client function.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW RATHER THAN LATER. phux agent wait --until blocked SHIPPED in wave 2. An orchestrator will land in blocked constantly and has nothing to do there but send-keys guesswork. That is WORSE than herdr, not better, because phux carries structured suggestions on the wire and will have taught the caller to expect structure. herdr entire blocked story is manual - its own skill says to inspect and then send esc and hope.

THE PREREQUISITE NOBODY NAMED, AND IT IS THE ACTUAL WORK: blocked, from the ADR-0046 detector screen rules, and asked, from the ADR-0035 OSC title sentinel, are TWO ENTIRELY INDEPENDENT CHANNELS. A pane in detector-blocked has no asked payload unless the agent also happened to set the sentinel title. JOINING THEM is the job, and it is the natural extension of ADR-0036 point 3, which was written for exactly this and never built.

That join requires a manifest-schema change the rule engine cannot express today, and the detection-parity audit section 5.2 spells out why: Predicate evaluates to bool, Regex is_match is used and never captures, and Evaluation carries a state, four flags and a rule id but NO TEXT. Capture-bearing rules with named groups for question and options are a NEW MANIFEST CONCEPT, plus a stable synthetic id so the equality-based coalescing in AskedDetector report does not re-fire every tick on a re-rendered spinner. A level-triggered scrape source also needs the blocker left the screen so clear, which has no representation today.

THEN the verb: phux agent answer TARGET --id ID --choice 2, or --text, resolving choice 2 through the SAME manifest that detected the block into a keystroke batch, delivered over APPLY_INPUT with an ADR-0053 operation id - so answering a question is acknowledged and cannot be double-submitted.

DEPENDS on agent prompt phux-w7z2.5 for the acknowledged write path, on the AskedSource work phux-w7z2.23, and on the sentinel-into-the-ladder refactor phux-w7z2.22 which the audit calls the cheap prerequisite. Also gated by the same capture-session constraint as phux-w7z2.28 - a rule that captures question text cannot be authored blind, and the existing 15 fixtures were captured to answer is this blocked, not what did it ask.

SECURITY BOUNDARY, from F2 and recorded here so it is not lost: this verb should exist on the CLI and should NOT get an MCP tool that auto-selects a suggestion. Expose read the question, not answer it.
acceptance_criteria: A shipped manifest carries a capture-bearing blocked rule with a committed fixture, agent show surfaces the question and options for a detector-blocked pane, and agent answer delivers a choice over APPLY_INPUT with an operation id.
notes:
PARTIAL IMPLEMENTATION landed: phux agent answer validates the exact live ask id and delivers a choice/text over acknowledged APPLY_INPUT, with CLI and MCP surfaces tested. Keep open: the acceptance criterion also requires capture-bearing detector rules that surface question/options, which this branch does not implement.
REPRICED 2026-08-15 (P2 -> P0), fleet-inbox sequencing.

Step 1 of the five-step arc: the cross-session attention sidebar turns phux into a bounded human inbox. Its value is CAPPED without this bead. The queue answers 'who is blocked'; without asked-to-answer the human still pays ~30s of context reconstruction per item (jump to pane, read back, reconstruct, type). Joining detector-blocked to ADR-0035 asked is what lets a queue row carry the question and take the answer in place.

Sequenced immediately after the attention-sidebar epic.
FINDING 2026-08-17 from phux-w7z2.22 (branch w2/ask-ladder, commit cc137456): nothing but an ANSWER or a REAP clears a HOOK-owned ask, so a pane whose hook fired once suppresses every lower rung (sentinel, and later scrape) until one of those happens. Pre-existing behavior, but the newly-real ADR-0036 ladder makes it visible and it lands squarely in this bead's asked-to-answer round trip. Note the arbiter now has a per-source retract primitive (AskedDetector::retract — a source takes back only what it asserted, so a clearing title cannot drop an ask a hook is standing behind), which is the mechanism this bead should use rather than inventing a second one.

title: cell_grid has no GPU encoder: terminal frames route to the CPU pixel path
description: The packed cell_grid command is marked unsupported in the packet layer, so terminal frames fall back to the CPU reference renderer on macOS and Windows. That is correct everywhere from day one and needed no wire-format bump, and it was a deliberate call: automation screenshots render through the reference path, so a host encoder cannot be validated in this environment and a wrong one would diverge silently on real hardware while every screenshot looked right. Consequence: frame performance is UNMEASURED against the previous CoreGraphics packet path, and matching Ghostty's responsiveness is an explicit product bar. Two follow-ups: (1) measure the CPU pixel path on a full dense screen using the automation snapshot fields gpu_frame_interval_ns, gpu_input_latency_ns, present_mode and present_fallback; (2) write the Metal host decoder plus a wire-format v6 section, using the reference renderer and CellDecoration as the spec it must match.
notes:
MEASURED on the running app (1100x640, automation snapshot), cell_grid vs the previous build:

  gpu_present_path   packet -> pixels
  present_fallback   none   -> unsupported_command
  present_mode       patch  -> none
  present_patch_bytes 1092/395 -> 0

The consequence is bigger than 'no GPU encoder'. Incremental dirty-region patching is DISABLED entirely: before the change a keystroke presented as a 395-byte patch with 1 upsert against a retained list; now every frame is a full-surface CPU pixel upload (~2.8 MB at 1x, ~11 MB at Retina 2x) because an unsupported command forces the whole view onto the reference renderer. gpu_input_latency_ns measured 19.4ms against a 16.67ms budget, budget_exceeded=1.

For a terminal that must be idle-quiet and keystroke-latency-sensitive this is not an acceptable steady state, which is why this is now P0 rather than P1. The correctness win it bought is real and should NOT be reverted (60/60 rows on a dense screen, stale columns fixed by construction, all SGR attributes carried) — the fix is forward: write the Metal host decoder for cell_grid plus the wire-format section, so terminals return to the packet+patch path.

Considered and rejected as an interim: emitting per-run commands for sparse screens and cell_grid only for dense ones. It would restore the fast path for a shell prompt, but it reintroduces the per-run retained-key class of bug that caused the stale-column artifact, and it means the common path and the correct path are different code. Not worth it.
close_reason: Fixed. The Metal/AppKit decoder for cell_grid landed with wire format v6, and terminal frames are back on the GPU packet path with incremental patching. Measured on the running app: gpu_present_path pixels->packet, present_mode none->patch, present_patch_bytes 0->789 (one upsert on a shell prompt), present_fallback unsupported_command->none, gpu_input_latency_ns 19.4ms->5.36ms against a 16.67ms budget (budget_exceeded 1->0). The structural key was emitting one grid command PER ROW rather than per screen, plus moving cluster interning per-row: with per-screen interning a single new character re-encoded the whole screen (31 upserts / 8449 bytes a frame), which per-row interning took to 1 upsert and ~400-800 bytes. Also returned the per-view command ceiling 4096->2048 (~45 MiB of address space) since a terminal now costs ~100 commands. Not verified: per-pixel equality with the reference rasterizer (host uses CoreText, geometry is identical, antialiasing is not, and that was already true of every draw_text), and the Windows Direct2D path (no device). One unreproducible startup transient was reported rather than assumed away; present_fallback_frames climbing at startup is the signal if it recurs.

title: Implement paired workload authentication and scoped Phux policy enforcement
description: Implement the phux-workload/v1 service pairing required by Blackbird ADR-0005. Authenticate a registered Blackbird workload key over a server-incarnation and transport-bound challenge, mint connection-bound effective scopes, enforce selectors/scopes in authoritative handlers, revoke active sessions, and replace permissive default policy for RC deployments. Secrets/key material travel only via vault/inherited FD/private IPC, never argv/env/logs.
design:
DECOMPOSITION PLAN 2026-08-16 (autonomous run; full detail in child beads pjc5.1-.6).

FIVE ADR DECISIONS (one ADR, ~ADR-0092, Stage 1), recommended answers:
1. Challenge format: in-band Ed25519 proof-of-possession between HELLO and HELLO_OK. AUTH_CHALLENGE (S->C, tag from 0x84..=0x8F) {proto:"phux-workload/v1", server_id: bytes16 incarnation, nonce: bytes32 CSPRNG single-use, channel_binding: TLS exporter or empty on UDS}; AUTH_RESPONSE (C->S, tag from 0x04..=0x0F) {key_id, requested_scopes, sig over domain-sep transcript}. Replay fails on nonce; restart-replay fails on incarnation; cross-transport relay fails on channel binding. Amends proto.md section 10's "no in-band auth" doctrine. No timestamps (server-stateful nonce = structural freshness). Crypto via ring (already in tree through rustls); ed25519-dalek fallback with dep justification.
2. Scope taxonomy: closed enum bitset of exactly the six verbs Inventory/Observe/Create/Bind/Input/Signal + selectors {terminals, groups, hosts, global} + expires_at. Normative total classification table in spec mapping EVERY client-originated frame to (verb, selector); unclassified frames are default-deny — that rule retires "handler bypass". Replaces the non-wire Capability struct in phux-protocol/src/policy.rs.
3. Key registry: <state-dir>/workload-keys file (pubkeys are not secrets), 0600, hot-reload via the ReloadingTokenStore stat-generation pattern from auth.rs. Provisioned by new `phux workload add-key|list|revoke` CLI (pubkey via stdin/file, never argv) and by Blackbird at RuntimeEndpointRegistration. Rejected: live Blackbird query at HELLO (couples admission to sidecar availability).
4. Revocation: registry-is-truth and LIVE — revoking a key refuses new connections AND cancels existing sessions minted from that key_id (per-connection CancellationToken, ERROR{PermissionDenied} flushed before close). Deliberately reverses ADR-0031's survive-until-drop for workload sessions; bearer WS consumers keep old semantics. expires_at also terminates live sessions.
5. Permissive-default replacement: [policy] mode = "local" (default; today's kernel-enforced UDS trust) | "paired" (phux-workload/v1 required on EVERY transport incl. same-UID UDS; ambient identity confers nothing). Fail-closed: paired+no-registry denies everything; routable listener or configured registry with mode unset refuses to START with a diagnostic. Operator CLI uses an auto-provisioned operator key in paired mode.

STAGES: .1 ADR+spec draft (docs-only) -> .2 wire types in phux-protocol (inert; PROTOCOL_VERSION 0.9.0) and .3 key registry+verifier+CLI (no wire; parallel with .2) -> .4 handshake integration (ScopedPolicy engine; stop discarding granted set at client.rs:1474) -> .5 scope enforcement at the single dispatch choke point (client.rs frame loop + handle_command entry before the satellite-relay branch, one enforce() call, never per-handler checks) -> .6 live revocation + RC fail-closed default + adversarial conformance sweep (every acceptance bullet a named test incl. the no-secret-in-argv/env/stdout/stderr/logs sweep).

SEAM FACTS (verified): every transport stamps PeerIdentity (transport.rs:69); authorize_hello consulted at client.rs:1439-1491 with placeholder caps, granted set DISCARDED at :1474; injection ServerConfig::policy_engine (runtime/mod.rs:174), None in binary (phux/src/commands/server.rs:258); tests/policy_deny.rs pins refusal+permissive-default; HELLO_OK.server_id is the 128-bit incarnation (lifecycle_state.rs:131); reserved tags 0x04..=0x0F / 0x84..=0x8F free; pattern donor auth.rs (constant-time compare, 0600, redacted Debug, hot reload).

BLACKBIRD COORDINATION: blackbird:docs/architecture/adr/0005-phux-runtime-binding.md DOES NOT EXIST (only cited in references.md) — phux ADR-0092 can define phux-workload/v1 unilaterally but stays Proposed until Blackbird ratifies its half. Blackbird moves: registry provisioning at RuntimeEndpointRegistration (soft dep; manual CLI unblocks phux), private-key delivery convention (PHUX_WORKLOAD_KEY_FD / key-file path — name must be agreed in the joint ADR). Incarnation semantics already aligned. Phux fully testable without Blackbird via testkit.
acceptance_criteria: Adversarial conformance proves same-UID UDS and bearer possession are insufficient; replay, wrong incarnation/connection, over-scope, revoked key, permissive fallback, and handler bypass all fail; inventory/observe/create/bind/input/signal scope matrix passes; no secret reaches argv/env/stdout/stderr/logs.
notes:
Linear mirror: https://linear.app/phall/issue/PHA-244/implement-paired-workload-authentication-and-scoped-phux-policy
Seam context (2026-08-07, ADR-0072): the authorization seam this feature must implement is PRESERVED and wired end to end -- every transport stamps a PeerIdentity, and crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs consults PolicyEngine::authorize_hello once per connection, sending ERROR{PermissionDenied} and closing on Err. What was pruned was the unreferenced vocabulary around it (13 pub types in phux-protocol; AuditSink/InputProvenance/PolicyBundle and 4 zero-caller authorize_* methods in phux-server), deliberately NOT pre-shaping this feature's scope taxonomy -- the deleted op enums matched neither the wire frame catalog nor this bead's inventory/observe/create/bind/input/signal matrix. ServerConfig::policy_engine is the injection point (Arc<dyn PolicyEngine>, None in the binary). crates/phux-server/tests/policy_deny.rs already proves a denying engine reaches the wire. Enforcing a granted capability set in authoritative handlers, revocation, and audit are explicitly left to this bead.
SEQUENCING NOTE 2026-08-15 (priority unchanged at P0).

Step 4 of the five-step fleet-inbox arc, and the only open P0 outside the epics. Named as the gate on every user who is not a solo dev: the moment agents spawn and answer other agents across satellites (step 3, phux-w7z2), 'who may drive what' is the question that decides whether anyone runs phux off their own laptop. Scoped policy is what lets a human hand an agent a rented box without handing it their machine.

This is the one item on the arc where being early is worth more than being polished, because nothing else in this product category has it.
COORDINATION WARNING 2026-08-16 (autonomous run): live UNCOMMITTED work exists in an opencode worktree at $TMPDIR/opencode/phux-provider-authority on branch feat/provider-authority (touches phux-protocol policy.rs/caps.rs/wire/frame.rs/decode.rs + phux-server; last modified Aug 16 03:24, 9 behind origin/main). Any implementation of this bead MUST first reconcile with that branch — do not start parallel implementation. A decomposition plan is being drafted separately.
ADR NUMBER CORRECTION 2026-08-17: this bead's DESIGN field names 'ADR-0092' twice for the phux-workload/v1 decision record. That number was taken the same day by external PR #487 (ADR/0092-durable-work-coordinator-authority.md). The workload-auth ADR must take the NEXT FREE number at authoring time, read fresh from ADR/ and ADR/README.md, with its index row added in the same commit — do not hard-code a replacement number into this plan. See phux-pjc5.1's note.

title: Create synchronous generic SessionKernel with fake-engine transcripts
description: Turn phux-client-core into a frontend-neutral synchronous SessionKernel<E> with EngineAdapter, normalized KernelInput/Action/Effect, reusable EffectBuffer, terminal staging/published replicas, canonical geometry, stream/bootstrap sequencing, and no transport/render/layout I/O. Normalize current synthesized bootstrap through it first so work can proceed before native bindings.
design:
Boundary: extend phux-client-core; do not create a second client-core crate. Generic synchronous core, no async trait/boxing and no transport/frontend dependencies.

Core shape:
- EngineAdapter associated Live, HistoryPage/Projection, Anchor, Error.
- push_bootstrap(live, opaque chunk) -> Pending|Ready|Finished; apply_pty; import/project history; create/resolve engine anchors; format selection; borrowed render access.
- SessionKernel<E> owns terminal map, connection state, staging/published replicas, bounded HistoryCache, viewport/selection/reconnect state.
- update(KernelInput, &mut reusable EffectBuffer) emits Send, Damage, Clipboard, ScheduleTimer, ConnectionChanged, HistoryJob, Fatal. It performs no I/O/frontend callback.
- KernelInput normalizes server events, explicit-terminal user actions, transport events, timers. Layout/plugin/theme/help remain outside.

Replica invariants:
- publish only after both phux BOOTSTRAP_READY and engine internal READY agree; mismatch is corruption/resync.
- apply only matching stream/bootstrap raw seq > base_seq, contiguous; wrong/stale/gap never reaches engine.
- keep last published replica while a replacement stages; atomically swap on dual READY.
- canonical live geometry equals BOOTSTRAP_BEGIN. Physical viewport/history projection never independently resizes it.
- engine synchronous effects are queued then drained after apply to prevent reentrancy.

History/anchors:
- opaque generation-scoped engine page handles, bounded by encoded/materialized bytes.
- newest-first pull; duplicates idempotent; gaps explicit; visible/prefetch/selection pages pinned; LRU otherwise.
- ViewportAnchor Tail or Pinned(engine DocumentAnchor + row bias). Tail follows; pinned stays and unread increments.
- selection endpoints are engine anchors across History(page)/Live segments. Missing pages defer copy and emit fetch; engine defines wraps/graphemes/join boundaries.
- historical projections cache by page,target_cols,engine generation; cooperative visible+neighbor slices. Live grid is not reflowed.

Allocation: borrow frame Bytes into adapter; reuse effects/engine-effects/decode/reflow/render scratch; no durable Canvas Grid/cell model; allocate selection text only at copy completion. Move predict::overlay stdout VT emission to Ratatui shell.

Migration: fake-engine transcript kernel -> Ratatui synthesized compatibility normalization -> native adapter dual READY -> bounded history -> semantic selection -> reconnect staging -> web compatibility reducer deletion -> native host. Delete old reducers/viewport-cell selection after both frontends migrate.
acceptance_criteria: Core compiles native+wasm without Ratatui/crossterm/tokio/web-sys/DOM; deterministic fake-engine transcripts enforce dual READY, chunk/raw order, attach barrier, stale generation rejection, and exact effects without allocation-heavy async traits.
notes: Implemented on isolated phux branch feat/session-kernel and integrated into feat/native-state-sync-wave1 through 229d053f. Added synchronous generic SessionKernel/EngineAdapter, explicit replica keys and canonical geometry, staging/published atomic dual READY, exact raw sequence and tombstone gates, aggregate ATTACH_READY barrier, StateSync generation ACKs, typed reusable effects, generation-buffered Status/Job, adapter-error retirement, and wasm-safe dependencies. Independent review found/fixed ACK, error atomicity, bootstrap effect, close-removal, and generation-key defects. Validation: cargo fmt clean; phux-client-core 169 tests passed; wasm32-unknown-unknown no-default-features check clean.

title: Specify protocol 0.7 bootstrap and history cutover
description: Finalize ADR and normative L1/proto 0.7 contract: retire TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT tag 0x91 permanently; define StreamId/BootstrapId, codec sets, BEGIN/CHUNK/READY, ATTACH_READY, HISTORY_REQUEST/PAGE, tombstones, actor cut sequence, mode matrix, bounds, resize, multi-pane fairness, and federation mapping. Prefer exact libghostty v2+Raw; synthesized VT+Raw/StateSync is compatibility.
design:
Protocol target: 0.7.0 clean cutover.

Discriminants:
- C→S HISTORY_REQUEST = 0x16.
- S→C ATTACH_READY = 0x83.
- S→C BOOTSTRAP_BEGIN = 0x93, BOOTSTRAP_CHUNK = 0x94, BOOTSTRAP_READY = 0x95, HISTORY_PAGE = 0x96, BOOTSTRAP_TOMBSTONE = 0x97.
- Withdraw TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT 0x91 permanently; never reuse it.

Types:
- nonzero StreamId(u64): one logical subscription.
- nonzero BootstrapId(u64): replaceable replica generation.
- BootstrapCodec values allocated only after Ghostty version decision: SynthesizedVtV1 and exact LibghosttyCheckpointV2+.
- BootstrapCodecSet additive bits; ClientCapabilities advertises set + max_chunk_bytes + max_history_page_bytes. HELLO_OK returns selected supported bounds/profile. OutputMode remains Raw|StateSync.
- Allowed profiles: exact native+Raw preferred; synth+Raw and synth+StateSync compatibility; native+StateSync rejected CodecUnavailable.
- TombstoneReason: RawReplayOverflow, OutboundGap, Resize, RelayReconnect, ExplicitReattach, CodecFailure, Other.

Frame fields / TLV ids:
BEGIN: terminal=1, stream=2, bootstrap=3, codec=4, cols=5, rows=6, output_mode=7, base_seq=8.
CHUNK: terminal=1, stream=2, bootstrap=3, chunk_seq=4, payload=5.
READY: terminal=1, stream=2, bootstrap=3, history_cursor=4 optional.
HISTORY_REQUEST: terminal=1, stream=2, bootstrap=3, cursor=4, max_bytes=5.
HISTORY_PAGE: terminal=1, stream=2, bootstrap=3, cursor=4, next_cursor=5 optional, payload=6. next_cursor=None means this payload ends the requested codec stream/FINISH.
TOMBSTONE: terminal=1, stream=2, bootstrap=3, reason=4, last_valid_seq=5.
ATTACH_READY: attach_id=1.
Append stream=4, bootstrap=5 to TERMINAL_OUTPUT; append stream=3, bootstrap=4 to FRAME_ACK. Add attach_id to ATTACH/ATTACHED.

No separate raw/bootstrap ACK gates server release: reliable ordering plus dual READY is sufficient and avoids one RTT. FRAME_ACK remains cumulative only for StateSync within (stream,bootstrap). Raw uses actor stream seq for gap/cut verification but does not ACK.

Ordering:
ATTACHED -> BEGIN for all panes in stable snapshot traversal -> round-robin bounded CHUNKs -> per-pane READY -> per-pane raw seq base_seq+1 immediately -> ATTACH_READY once all panes are READY/closed. History is client-pull and lower priority; at most one request outstanding per logical stream. Payloads are opaque engine bytes; phux never scans magic/tags/READY/FINISH.

Server cut:
actor stamps checked non-wrapping stream_seq before broadcast. Coordinator drains subscription, takes actor-turn cut, drops seq<=cut, queues bounded seq>cut, sends state through READY, then releases contiguous raw. Missing/gap/overflow/loss/resize produces TOMBSTONE before a new BEGIN. No old generation data is legal after tombstone.

Federation:
select profile per logical stream. Bijection downstream(client,stream)<->upstream(link,stream). Rewrite only phux IDs/envelope; payload/raw bytes unchanged. Distinct profiles use distinct subscriptions. Proxy history and StateSync ACK. Bounded return queues; raw overflow tombstones rather than silent try_send loss.
acceptance_criteria: Every field/discriminant/order/error is allocated; engine payload stays opaque; native+StateSync is rejected; raw native bytes are never color-rewritten; previous ADRs are explicitly superseded/constrained; implementation tasks require no semantic guesswork.
notes: Implemented on isolated branch feat/native-state-sync-wave1 through d29ff12a. ADR-0067 and normative L1/proto define the 0.7 clean cutover, explicit NativeState/SynthesizedVtRaw/SynthesizedVtStateSync profiles, actor-global inclusive cut, no raw ACK RTT, per-pane READY/global ATTACH_READY, opaque history/tombstone/federation and negotiated bounds. Protocol crate adds nonzero IDs, exact profiles/codecs/features, new discriminants/frames, required-field decoding, pre-copy negotiated limits, and permanently retires 0x91. title: Expose incremental checkpoint handles through C and WASM ABI
description: After the Zig incremental READY/history state machines land, expose callback-free opaque capture/decoder handles, caller buffers, sized options/events, capability metadata, structured codec errors, take-terminal-at-READY, history push/abort, and exact cleanup. Use the same linear-memory ABI for native C and the standalone ghostty-vt.wasm module.
design:
Engine API direction:
- Version enum with immutable v1 and exact v2+; CheckpointId is validated READY prefix digest.
- Capture::init is the pause-sensitive operation: serialize active prefix/continuation through READY and acquire bounded stable history lease/pins/COW. Capture::next writes exactly one non-advancing-on-short-buffer opaque chunk (READY, history manifest/page, FINISH), reports metadata, and releases on abort/deinit.
- Decoder buffers at most one bounded record, accepts arbitrary fragments, reports NeedInput/Ready/HistoryBegin/HistoryPage/Finish, and consumes nothing after FINISH. take_ready transfers a stable Terminal exactly once; serialized vt_write may run between later history pushes.
- HistoryImport tracks only imported old nodes. Post-READY corruption/FINISH failure rolls back imported history and invalidates pins into it while preserving active READY state and post-READY PTY writes. Retention pressure may report retained=false rather than evict newer live output.
- Pull history lease/cursor is generation-bound, newest-to-oldest, byte/page bounded, stale/pruned explicit. Never expose Page.memory, cloneBuf, compressed-page bytes, parser structs, allocator pointers, or native padding.
- Continuation is canonical replay-safe bytes only. Tracking starts before first vt_write. Disabled/unavailable capture fails explicitly.
- C ABI uses opaque handles, sized options/events, caller buffers, exact consumed counts, structured codec errors, and no callbacks/file descriptors. Rust typestate owns handles/terminal and makes pre-READY access/wrong-terminal history application unavailable.
- Source capture leaves compressed pages compressed and does not mutate terminal presentation/cache state.
acceptance_criteria: A pure C test and WASM smoke can fragment at every byte boundary, take a usable terminal only at verified READY, vt_write between history pages, finish or abort cleanly, distinguish version/corruption/limits/OOM, and never mix a decoder with the wrong terminal.
notes: Implemented native C and standalone wasm incremental snapshot/history ABI through 8f5b178d4: opaque capture/decoder/lease/cursor/importer handles, sized metadata/events, strict bounds, exact READY/consumed semantics, ownership/OOM cleanup, honest wasm capability gating, C contract and Node smoke. Independent review clear. Native test-lib-vt passed 5327 tests (34 skipped); wasm smoke and zig fmt checks pass.

title: Publish terminal at READY and resume history decoding incrementally
description: Refactor the synchronous complete-snapshot decoder/encoder into bounded incremental state machines. Encoder can stop after the authenticated active-state plus continuation READY prefix. Decoder returns a movable, renderable terminal and continuation exactly once at READY, then accepts validated HISTORY/PAGE records without blocking PTY writes or invalidating the published handle. FINISH authenticates a requested complete sequence but is not required for interactivity.
design:
Engine API direction:
- Version enum with immutable v1 and exact v2+; CheckpointId is validated READY prefix digest.
- Capture::init is the pause-sensitive operation: serialize active prefix/continuation through READY and acquire bounded stable history lease/pins/COW. Capture::next writes exactly one non-advancing-on-short-buffer opaque chunk (READY, history manifest/page, FINISH), reports metadata, and releases on abort/deinit.
- Decoder buffers at most one bounded record, accepts arbitrary fragments, reports NeedInput/Ready/HistoryBegin/HistoryPage/Finish, and consumes nothing after FINISH. take_ready transfers a stable Terminal exactly once; serialized vt_write may run between later history pushes.
- HistoryImport tracks only imported old nodes. Post-READY corruption/FINISH failure rolls back imported history and invalidates pins into it while preserving active READY state and post-READY PTY writes. Retention pressure may report retained=false rather than evict newer live output.
- Pull history lease/cursor is generation-bound, newest-to-oldest, byte/page bounded, stale/pruned explicit. Never expose Page.memory, cloneBuf, compressed-page bytes, parser structs, allocator pointers, or native padding.
- Continuation is canonical replay-safe bytes only. Tracking starts before first vt_write. Disabled/unavailable capture fails explicitly.
- C ABI uses opaque handles, sized options/events, caller buffers, exact consumed counts, structured codec errors, and no callbacks/file descriptors. Rust typestate owns handles/terminal and makes pre-READY access/wrong-terminal history application unavailable.
- Source capture leaves compressed pages compressed and does not mutate terminal presentation/cache state.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmented input at every byte boundary yields identical results; READY never exposes unauthenticated or incomplete active state; live vt_write may proceed while older pages import; malformed later history cannot corrupt active state; caller controls memory and per-step work.
