title: [epic] Native engine-state terminal synchronization and client-owned history
description: Build phux's next terminal substrate around exact, versioned libghostty state rather than VT-synthesized bootstrap: READY-before-history attach, raw PTY live fanout, canonical bounded server history, progressive client-owned history caches/viewports, queue tombstones and full resync, and one frontend-neutral client kernel shared by Ratatui, web, and future native UI. Preserve the invariant one PTY = one authoritative active-area geometry; independent client sizes mean projection, crop/letterbox, zoom, and deferred historical reflow, never multiple PTY winsizes. Upstream engine work stays on phall1 forks unless explicit upstream permission is granted.
design:
DECISION SUMMARY

Phux will preserve its existing distributed-terminal shape—one authoritative libghostty Terminal beside the PTY and one engine replica per client—but replace native clients' VT-synthesized bootstrap with exact, versioned libghostty checkpoint bytes. Live output remains raw PTY bytes. Historical state becomes a separate progressive, client-pull lane. Synthesized VT remains an explicitly negotiated compatibility codec for web/older-engine/agent consumers; it is not the native fidelity ceiling.

The engine owns terminal semantics and binary codecs. Phux owns connection negotiation, logical stream/bootstrap IDs, ordering/fences, resource bounds, cursor routing, tombstones, and frontend-independent policy. No cells, styles, Ghostty record tags, page layouts, parser structs, or compressed Page memory enter phux's protocol. CRC32C/BLAKE3 validation stays inside libghostty.

GEOMETRY INVARIANT

One process + one PTY = one authoritative active cell geometry and one PTY winsize. Multiple clients may have different physical surfaces, font sizes, zoom, crop/letterbox, layouts, scroll positions, cache budgets, and historical projections. They do not simultaneously turn the same live PTY into true 80x24 and 200x60 terminals. Existing server window-size policy selects the canonical geometry. Phase 1 history pages remain canonical-width. Deferred client-local historical reflow/disk paging is later engine work; it must never resize the live raw-PTY replica.

ENGINE FORMAT

Current Ghostty main already has portable field-wise snapshot records:
  envelope -> TERMINAL -> SCREEN/PAGE active suffix -> CONTINUATION -> READY(BLAKE3)
           -> HISTORY/PAGE newest-to-oldest -> FINISH(BLAKE3)

The current continuation branch changed v1 incompatibly and current v1 omits load-bearing state such as Kitty image payloads. Freeze complete-v1 bytes. Add an explicit v2 (or later) with replay-safe CONTINUATION and exact feature coverage. Native is advertised only when the engine can preserve all canonical state present in that terminal; otherwise choose synthesized compatibility before payload delivery. Raw Page.memory/cloneBuf/compression.Page bytes are process-local only and never portable.

The final engine API is incremental and callback-free:
- capture begin emits bounded prefix chunks through verified READY and returns a stable bounded history lease/cursor;
- decoder consumes arbitrary fragmentation, transfers one usable Terminal at internal READY, then applies history records newest-to-oldest while serialized vt_write continues;
- history failure after READY preserves active/live state and invalidates/rolls back only imported history;
- abort/drop frees pins/clones/handles exactly once;
- C sized structs/opaque handles and safe Rust typestate wrappers expose milestones/errors/capabilities;
- standalone ghostty-vt.wasm uses the same caller-buffer ABI.

The whole-blob C bridge is the first proven slice, not the final transport API: phall1/ghostty feat/terminal-snapshot-c-api commit e32f7169c.

PROTOCOL 0.7 CLEAN CUTOVER

Retire TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT and permanently reserve 0x91; no alias or shim. Both native and synthesized bootstrap use one generation-scoped lifecycle. Exact discriminants/fields are finalized in phux-slogic.2.1, with this semantic vocabulary:
- HELLO client codec set + limits; HELLO_OK selected codec/profile + limits.
- StreamId: one logical subscription. BootstrapId: replaceable replica generation.
- BOOTSTRAP_BEGIN {terminal, stream, bootstrap, codec, canonical cols/rows, output_mode, base_seq}
- BOOTSTRAP_CHUNK {terminal, stream, bootstrap, chunk_seq, opaque payload}
- BOOTSTRAP_READY {terminal, stream, bootstrap, optional history cursor}
- ATTACH_READY {attach_id} after all panes reached READY/closed.
- HISTORY_REQUEST {terminal, stream, bootstrap, cursor, max_bytes}
- HISTORY_PAGE {terminal, stream, bootstrap, cursor, next_cursor, opaque payload}
- BOOTSTRAP_TOMBSTONE/RESYNC_REQUIRED {old generation, reason, last valid seq}; then a new BEGIN.
- TERMINAL_OUTPUT and StateSync ACK carry stream/bootstrap identity.

Preferred profile: exact LibghosttyCheckpointV2+ + Raw. Compatibility profiles: SynthesizedVtV1 + Raw or StateSync. Native + StateSync is rejected until libghostty supplies an exact native delta. Native raw output is byte-identical and never color/image rewritten. Protocol version and engine codec version/build capabilities are independent.

CAPTURE/RAW ORDERING

TerminalActor owns checked non-wrapping u64 stream_seq and stamps every accepted raw PTY payload before broadcast. Runtime actively subscribes/drains before requesting capture. Capture runs in one actor turn and returns cut=last_stream_seq. The coordinator drops buffered seq <= cut (already represented by checkpoint), queues only seq > cut under a strict byte/count bound, sends BEGIN/CHUNK/READY, then sends cut+1, cut+2, ... exactly once. No client ACK gates raw release or adds a round trip: reliable phux frame order plus dual READY is the fence. BOOTSTRAP_ACK, if retained, is observational/resource accounting only.

Multi-pane attach sends BEGIN for all panes first, schedules bounded chunks round-robin, allows each ready pane's raw stream immediately, and sends ATTACH_READY after all pane outcomes. Large history never blocks READY, raw output, input, or another pane.

HISTORY

History is canonical, bounded, retained once by the server terminal, but replicated progressively into client-owned engine caches. One request may be outstanding per logical stream. A cursor is an opaque sequential lease token bound to bootstrap/history generation—not a byte offset and not a scroll position. The engine chooses complete payload boundaries; phux may fragment bytes but never parses them. Server clamps page bytes, prioritizes live output, and releases leases on completion/TTL/detach/tombstone. Stale/pruned cursors fail explicitly. Clients request newest pages first, prefetch older pages near a cache boundary, and own viewport/selection/search/prefetch/cache budgets. Server never stores “client is scrolled up N rows.”

RESYNC

Per stream: Absent -> Bootstrapping -> Ready -> Tombstoned -> Bootstrapping(new). Raw replay overflow, missing sequence, outbound loss, resize, relay reconnect, explicit reattach, or codec failure emits a tombstone before replacement. No old generation chunk/page/output/ACK applies afterward. Client keeps the last published replica visible while staging replacement and atomically swaps only when both phux BOOTSTRAP_READY and libghostty internal READY agree. Resize creates a new canonical generation. StateSync compatibility reference/ACK state is keyed by (client, stream, bootstrap).

CLIENT KERNEL

phux-client-core becomes a synchronous generic SessionKernel<E: EngineAdapter>, with no Ratatui, crossterm, tokio, web-sys, DOM, sockets, stdout writer, or async traits. It owns negotiation results, terminal staging/published replicas, dual READY, stream/bootstrap order, history cache, viewport/document anchors, selection/search, tombstones, reconnect state, and reusable effect buffers. It emits effects; transport/frontend shells execute them. Layout/chrome/theme/plugin policy remains outside.

EngineAdapter owns terminals/pages/tracked anchors/reflow/selection formatting and borrowed render access. The kernel stores no cells. HistoryCache stores bounded engine-owned opaque handles/materializations. ViewportAnchor is Tail or Pinned(engine document anchor); pinned views do not jump as raw/history arrives. Missing selection pages trigger fetch and deferred copy, never silent truncation. Historical projection may reflow cooperatively; live canonical geometry may not.

Migration order: fake-engine kernel -> native libghostty adapter -> bounded history/anchors -> selection/search -> reconnect staging -> Ratatui cutover -> web compatibility cutover -> native-sdk host bridge/UI -> optional native web codec. Delete duplicate Ratatui/web reducers and viewport-cell selection authority after migration.

FEDERATION

Codec/profile selection is per logical stream, not just HELLO connection. Hub maps (downstream client, stream) bijectively to satellite stream, rewrites only phux IDs/envelopes, and proxies history/ACK. Different downstream profiles use distinct upstream subscriptions. Native payload and raw bytes compare identical end-to-end; no hub transcoding. Replace return-leg try_send loss with bounded per-stream queues; overflow tombstones raw streams. Satellite reconnect tombstones all mapped generations.

ORCHESTRATION WAVES

Wave 0 (done/active): synchronize phall1 forks; whole-blob C checkpoint bridge e32f7169c; architecture issue graph.
Wave 1 (parallel): v1/v2/fidelity decision; complete whole-blob Rust wrapper; strict HELLO for every stateful constructor; protocol 0.7 ADR/spec; fake-engine SessionKernel.
Wave 2: incremental Ghostty capture/decoder/history lease; exact missing-state codec; incremental C/WASM ABI; protocol types/goldens.
Wave 3: safe Rust typestate wrappers and phux pin; actor raw sequence/cut; native kernel adapter.
Wave 4: fair runtime coordinator; pull history; tombstone replacement; HistoryCache/anchors; federation mapping.
Wave 5: Ratatui migration and web compatibility migration in parallel; native host bridge after native adapter; selection/search/reconnect.
Wave 6: production native UI; optional exact web/WASM native mode; remove obsolete TerminalSnapshot/PanesOutput::Resync paths.
Wave 7: cross-architecture compatibility, fuzz, deterministic race/fault proofs, benchmarks, browser/native/recording smoke, release soak.

VALIDATION/END STATE

Non-negotiable proof:
- READY authenticated/renderable before history; input/raw continue while history stalls.
- Arbitrary parser cut (UTF-8/CSI/OSC/APC/DCS) resumes identically.
- Every byte is in checkpoint or seq>cut raw exactly once.
- Tombstone recovery never accepts stale data and converges without blank/double content.
- Multiple physical client sizes share identical canonical live state/raw stream while local viewport/history state differs.
- Cross-language and macOS-arm64/Linux-x86_64 fixtures agree; v1 immutable, future versions explicit.
- Fuzz/malformed/OOM/drop paths have no panic/leak/unbounded allocation/partial pre-READY terminal.
- Ratatui, browser compatibility, portable recording, and real native multi-pane paths are artifact-backed.
- After warmup, raw payload fanout adds no payload copy per client; history/cache memory is formula-bounded.

Initial performance targets: 200x60 codec READY p95 <=25ms; warm UDS READY p95 <=100ms/p99<=250ms; 50k history changes READY <=10%; page import/reflow slices p95 <=4ms and <=256KiB; input-to-paint p99 <=50ms during paging; eight-client raw throughput >=90% current baseline with zero extra payload copies; local resync <=250ms. Establish pinned baselines before enforcing relative gates.

This program aims to surpass the disclosed Superlogical terminal architecture through measured exact-state fidelity plus phux's existing open protocol, browser/remote transports, federation, agent APIs, and shared frontend kernel. No “surpassed” claim is valid until these gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: A native client can attach, render exact current engine state before history finishes, type immediately, scroll/search/select locally through demand-paged history, survive dropped output via deterministic resync, and share the same client state machine as Ratatui/web; compatibility clients retain synthesized VT mode; focused fidelity, corruption, loss, performance, and end-to-end tests pass.

title: Wire: acknowledge idempotent atomic input operations
description: phux-mobile public-launch chaos testing found an unavoidable ambiguity at reconnect boundaries: the consumer can know that a pane was input-ready and that bytes entered its local queue, but cannot know whether the server accepted them before a WebSocket failure. Replaying may duplicate commands; not replaying may silently lose them. Define and implement a protocol-owned atomic input operation carrying a consumer operation ID, with server acknowledgment after acceptance by the pane input path and bounded deduplication across reconnect. Update the normative wire spec, changelog/version, protocol codec, server dispatch, and consumer APIs. Preserve structured key/mouse/focus semantics; do not infer delivery from terminal echo. This is a public-launch prerequisite for phux-mobile bead phux-q7e.24.
acceptance_criteria: A complete line/paste/key batch has one operation ID and is accepted atomically; the server ACKs acceptance and deduplicates retries of the same ID across reconnect; clients can classify each operation as accepted, refused, or unknown without claiming unacknowledged delivery; reconnect tests cut the socket before send, after send, and after server acceptance and prove no silent loss or duplicate PTY execution; docs/spec and docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md describe the compatibility/version behavior.
close_reason: Merged in PR #286 as f1a1306a: capability-gated atomic acknowledged input, PTY write/flush receipts, reconnect dedupe, server incarnations, bounds, tests, ADR, and normative spec.

title: Set up the release GitHub App (blocks release-please)
description:
release-please.yml (PR #215) fails closed until a GitHub App exists.

Why an App and not GITHUB_TOKEN: main's ruleset 'main automation guardrails' requires the check+test contexts with bypass_actors: [] and current_user_can_bypass: never. GitHub raises no workflow runs for GITHUB_TOKEN-triggered events, so a release PR opened with GITHUB_TOKEN would never get CI, those checks would never report, and the PR would be unmergeable BY ANYONE including the owner.

Setup:
1. Create a GitHub App on the phall1 account. Repo permissions: contents: write, pull requests: write.
2. Install it on phall1/phux.
3. Repo variable RELEASE_APP_ID = the App's numeric App ID
4. Repo secret RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY = the App's generated .pem

Both the release-please job and the sync-lockfile job use it. Do not merge PR #215 to main before this exists.

title: Implement QUIC transport for remote satellite connections
description:
Add QUIC as a transport option for federation, replacing SSH-stdio for remote satellites.

- Quinn-based QUIC server/client
- 0-RTT connection establishment
- Connection migration for network changes
- NAT traversal via hole punching
- Certificate management (mTLS or token-based)
- Fallback to TCP when UDP is blocked

QUIC gives us streams, multiplexing, and connection migration for free. This makes satellite deployment resilient to network changes.
notes: Remote-consumer relationship: native QUIC is Phase 2 of the remote-consumer transport sequence (Phase 1 = wss+token, phux-5vsr). A native consumer reuses quinn directly (wire-identical) for connection migration and no HOL blocking; wss stays the universal fallback for blocked-UDP networks; the browser equivalent is WebTransport (phux-0wmf); NAT traversal still needs the relay (phux-yx6y). Anti-sprawl: QUIC is NOT needed when a remote consumer connects over an overlay (Tailscale/Headscale/WireGuard) — the overlay already gives reachability + encryption + roaming, so QUIC's migration win is redundant and double-encryption is overhead. Mosh-class resilience = overlay path-roaming + app-level state resume (ADR-0018 StateSync). QUIC earns its keep only on the no-overlay/relay path and for federation/satellites (this bead's driver). Treat QUIC + WebTransport + relay as one coherent no-overlay bundle.
close_reason: Completed the launch-critical QUIC remote-attach slice by adding native WebSocket/TLS fallback for UDP-blocked networks, sharing the QUIC certificate pinning trust policy, wiring phux attach --ws, adding WS/WSS transport tests, and updating remote attach docs; nix develop -c just ci passed. NAT relay/hole punching remains tracked separately in phux-yx6y per the issue notes.

title: Implement hub-and-spoke federation with real satellite support
description:
Move federation from wire reservation (v0.1) to fully working hub-and-spoke architecture.

- Hub receives frames with Satellite IDs and relays to appropriate satellite connection
- Satellite enrollment protocol (token-based or mTLS)
- Connection management: satellites reconnect on drop, hub tracks active satellites
- Error handling: UnsupportedSatelliteRoute becomes a real routing decision
- Testing: 2-3 satellite end-to-end scenario

This is the foundation of the distributed C2 architecture. Without this, tradecraft is limited to single-host operations.

title: Upgrade must not kill a live server on a missing distro layer or stale service path
description:
## Why

2026-09-12 dogfood: `phux update --channel next` re-exec'd 0.34.0 into 0.35.0+next, the new image refused to start because ~/.config/phux/config.toml still extended distros/herdr/herdr.toml after the rename to distros/starter, and launchd's unit still pointed at /opt/homebrew/bin/phux which was gone. KeepAlive SuccessfulExit=false then left the Mini with no server. Panes died. The user had to talk over herdr from a laptop.

validate_binary only probes --version. Config load happens after execve, which is irreversible. reconcile_after_update only rewrites restart-policy keys, not ProgramArguments/ExecStart.

## What

1. Keep distros/herdr/herdr.toml as a compatibility alias of starter, and rewrite a missing distros/herdr/herdr.toml extends path to distros/starter/starter.toml when that file exists.
2. prepare_upgrade's binary validation must run `config check` on the pinned image and abort (old server keeps serving) if it fails.
3. phux update's automatic unit reconcile must rewrite the supervised binary path to current_exe when it drifted (brew leftover, missing Program).

## Acceptance

- A config that still extends the old herdr.toml path loads after the rename.
- An upgrade against a broken extends layer returns UpgradeError::Validation and leaves the old image serving.
- reconcile_after_update rewrites a launchd ProgramArguments / systemd ExecStart that names a missing or different phux binary to current_exe, without dropping --hub/--listen/--quic.
- Tests cover the three seams. just crate-check phux-config / phux-server / phux (or equivalent scoped tests) green.
acceptance_criteria: Broken extends cannot take a live server down; herdr.toml path still loads; service unit Program tracks the updated binary.
notes: Landed on fix/upgrade-config-preflight as c48b54b9; PR https://github.com/no-phux/phux/pull/603. Live Mini recovered: config extends retargeted to starter.toml, com.phux.server reinstalled at ~/.local/bin/phux, 0.35.0+next.c817cd3 serving pid 34386 with wss:8787 and quic:8788.

Exceptions require a new decision bead, not a drive-by "while we are here".

title: [epic] Elite docs pass: one story, honest maturity, page jobs
description:
Full quality pass over the public docs so a Hashimoto/Yegge/DHH-class reader would trust them.

Not a restructure. The 3-layer system stays. The failure is: four overlapping "what is phux" essays, a maturity line that disagrees with itself, indexes that re-teach CONCEPTS, and product pages that reprint generated reference.

Canonical facts for this checkout (main / this tree):
- phux is a terminal multiplexer. Shells live in a background server. Detach survives. Each pane is a real libghostty emulator on the server, so a person, Cockpit, a script, or an agent can hold the same live terminal.
- AgentSession is served here: the server advertises RESOURCE_KINDS; runtime calls new_agent_session; CLI has `phux agent session` / emit / log. Older brew/curl releases may not; `phux status --json` is the check. Pane detector (`phux agent show`/`explain`) is a different surface.
- Cockpit is the shipping macOS native client. Do not say "native GUI is designed but not wired."
- Hub-and-spoke federation is real and limited (host/@N, no session/window join). Do not say federation is unwired.
- CONCEPTS.md owns "what is phux" and the Status gap table. Other docs link; they do not restate.
- Wordmark is always lowercase `phux`. No slogans. No restated TL;DRs. No reprinting docs/reference/.
- Install: curl is the universal one-liner (matches phux.sh); Homebrew is the recommended day-to-day on supported platforms. Show both; do not pick a secret third.

title: Preserve keep-empty when explicit Close Tab ends its last resources
description: Discovered implementing B19 helper on 2f4be865. crates/phux-server/src/runtime/commands.rs handle_kill_terminals calls release_keep_empty_covered_by before close_resources. The explicit close batch FFI currently emits KillResources, so closing the final tab clears Cockpit keep-empty and reaps its named session, contradicting ADR0112. Add a correctly scoped explicit-close policy/path preserving keep-empty, while End Session remains terminal. Validate actual final-tab teardown leaves named session empty and other clients observe correct lifetime. Parent/runtime notified in Blackbird messages 01a0942e-2810-73b0-be6f-ce1c0b0d8c6e and 01a0943a-b67c-717a-a883-f52a2e1a3eea; writer assignment remains parent-owned.
notes:
DESIGN DECISION (parent, replaces cancelled review lane):
PROBLEM: handle_kill_terminals (commands.rs:2999+3062) releases keep-empty for ANY full-coverage KillResources batch (ADR-0105 group teardown). Cockpit final-tab Close Tab sends the batch FFI, so closing the last tab reaps the named session, contradicting ADR-0112 (Empty session view retains named session; End Session is terminal). Single KillResource path does NOT release (cascade stops at keep-empty, ADR-0105 §3) - only the batch path is wrong for GUI close.
DECISION - additive close path, not a policy field:
1. New additive Command::CloseTabResources { ids }, tag 0x0a (former CREATE_SESSION slot, same dissolved L2 family as 0x09; verify at impl). Identical atomic all-or-nothing close, but NEVER calls release_keep_empty_covered_by; keep-empty survives full-coverage; no SESSION_KEEP_EMPTY_KEY=false broadcast.
2. KillResources (0x09) keeps exact ADR-0105 semantics -> phux kill SESSION / End Session remain terminal; all existing clients / accepted B19 wire untouched.
3. Backend: shared single-lock close routine parameterized preserve_keep_empty:bool; handlers differ only in flag + debug label.
4. FFI: additive phux_client_queue_close_tab_resources(client,request_id,ids,count) mirroring queue_close_resources (same validations, same PendingClose batch completion: command Ok AND all authoritative ResourceClosed, either order; disconnect=unknown). queue_close_resources unchanged.
5. Frontend: Cockpit Close Tab (incl. final tab) emits the new command via batch entry (1-pane final tab = count 1, never single KillResource). Non-covering batches behaviorally identical to today. Future Cockpit End Session resolves session terminals -> KillResources (existing semantics).
6. Tests: final-tab teardown leaves named session listed + SESSION_KEEP_EMPTY_KEY true + no removal broadcast; second client observes retained empty session and removal after End Session; codec round-trip; existing KillResources/close-resource tests stay green (wire untouched).
SCOPE (writer, parent-owned, after gate): phux-protocol command+codec+tag; phux-server commands.rs shared routine+handler+tests; phux-client-ffi new entry+docs+tests; cockpit native Close Tab routing+test. No new ADR needed; ADR-0105 + ADR-0112 stand, this implements the seam.

description: Deterministic local failure on macOS (Darwin 25.5) at main 97cceb51, reproduced alone and in 'just e2e' (3/3 retries): crates/phux/tests/lifecycle_e2e/upgrade_e2e.rs:204 'the resumed server should accept connections again'. notes:
Hosted ci on main 97cceb51 is green (run 34476020216, Linux runners), so this reproduces only on the local macOS host so far; likely platform-specific (re-exec / socket rebind timing on Darwin).
Root cause confirmed: not Darwin-specific. The test shell is a pane (PHUX_TERMINAL_ID=4) of a phux server upgraded from '/Applications/Phux Cockpit.app/Contents/MacOS/phux'; the server leaked PHUX_UPGRADE_SOURCE_EXE and PHUX_UPGRADE_SNAPSHOT_DIR into pane child env, so any server launched from that shell re-execs into the older Cockpit binary on upgrade, which refuses the handshake. Hosted CI does not run inside a phux pane, hence green. Fix in flight on fix/upgrade-resume-macos: honor the var only on --resume, scrub it after use, and clear PHUX_UPGRADE_* from pane spawns.
close_reason: Landed e2723adb: PHUX_UPGRADE_* read only on --resume, removed from the server env on every start (resume consumes, cold start discards), stripped from pane spawns. Root cause: env leaked into panes of an upgraded server, not Darwin. Full bar on the validated tree with the leaked vars present: just ci 4614 pass, e2e 87/87 incl. upgrade test + perf 3/3, agents-fleet-smoke pass. title: W2: parent bindings and cascade close with CloseReason
description:
Server: parent bindings and cascade close (ADR-0104).

ServerState gains a binding graph (children: HashMap<ResourceId, Vec<ResourceId>>, parent on each ResourceDescriptor). Rules: set at spawn only; parent must be local, live, and Terminal kind; a resource with a parent cannot itself be a parent (v1). KILL_RESOURCE / KILL_RESOURCES / Terminal exit / server shutdown compute the closure (targets plus all children) under one lock and close every member, emitting RESOURCE_CLOSED with reason Killed for targets, ParentClosed for cascaded children, Exited for a PTY exit, ServerShutdown on shutdown. Closing a child never touches the parent. AgentEvent ResourceClosed (still named PaneClosed until W3) fires for each. Satellite: SPAWN with a satellite parent is forwarded to the owning satellite like any spawn; a hub retags parent ids in aggregate inventory and in relayed RESOURCE_CLOSED frames.

Tests: kill parent -> child closed with ParentClosed, both frames observed by a subscriber; PTY exit cascades; KILL_RESOURCES over a mixed set is all-or-nothing and never double-closes; killing a child leaves the parent attached and live; spawn with unknown parent -> ParentNotFound; with AgentSession parent -> ParentKindMismatch; hub relay test retags parent. title: W1: ADR-0104 Parent bindings are L1 lifecycle
description:
Write ADR-0104 "Parent bindings are L1 lifecycle" and its index row.

Decision content: a resource may name one parent at spawn (SPAWN_RESOURCE field 12); the binding is immutable and server-enforced. Closing a parent closes every child with CloseReason::ParentClosed (RESOURCE_CLOSED field 3: Exited=0, Killed=1, ParentClosed=2, ServerShutdown=3, Unknown), atomically under the single state lock, the same guarantee KILL_RESOURCES gives. Closing a child never affects the parent. One level only in v1 (a child cannot be a parent); AgentSession requires a Terminal parent; Terminal has no parent. Parent ids are federation-routable like any ResourceId; a hub retags parent ids in aggregate inventory exactly as it retags resource ids. ResourceInfo carries parent.

Why this earns an L1 op: ADR-0030 admitted exactly one irreducible group operation, atomic teardown, because a projection cannot make it atomic. A resource that lives inside another has the same problem in the lifecycle direction: no client can guarantee the child closes when the parent dies. The relation is therefore lifecycle, not metadata. ADR-0027's phux.link/v1 stays for advisory, client-defined relations (group links); the parent relation is not expressible there.

Relationships: amends ADR-0027 (parent relation leaves L3), amends ADR-0030 ("one irreducible op" becomes two: atomic teardown and parent cascade), builds on ADR-0102.

Alternatives: parent as an L3 link with client-side cascade (rejected: races, partial states observable by other clients); arbitrary DAG bindings (rejected for v1: cycles, cascade ordering, no consumer needs it); owner_terminal spawn field reuse (rejected: that is a placement hint for the TUI, ADR-0050, not lifecycle).

title: W1: ADR-0103 Agent session resource and producer-fed streams
description:
Write ADR-0103 "Agent session resource and producer-fed streams" and its index row.

Decision content: AgentSession is the second ResourceKind. Facet: provider (string), native_id (opaque, ADR-0068 bounds), derived state. Always has a Terminal parent (ADR-0104). Output codec AgentEventsJsonlV1: one JSON object per line, {"seq","ts_ms","type","data"}, server assigns seq/ts_ms, <= 16 KiB per record, closed v1 type set: session_start, prompt, tool_start, tool_end, notification, ask, stop, session_end, state, provider_raw. Producer-fed: APPEND_RESOURCE_OUTPUT { resource_id, bytes } (command tag 0x1a, <= 64 KiB per call, Error: WRONG_RESOURCE_KIND | NOT_PRODUCER | RECORD_INVALID | OVERFLOW). Bounded retention ring (defaults.agent-log-bytes, default 4 MiB, ADR-0094 pattern); bootstrap = replay of retained records; live RESOURCE_OUTPUT carries complete records; raw profile only, FRAME_ACK forbidden. Server derives state: prompt/tool_start -> working, ask/notification{permission,elicitation} -> blocked, stop -> done, session_end -> retract; idle stays detector-owned (ADR-0085). Detector precedence Stream > Hook > Process > Screen; while a live AgentSession child exists screen derivation runs only for idle/departure. REPORT_AGENT_STATE stays as the fallback and synthesizes a state record when a child exists. Feature bit RESOURCE_KINDS = 0x4000. The Claude shim reads hook stdin JSON and emits records; prompts carry length only by default; provider_raw is opt-in.

Relationships: amends ADR-0040 (the phux.agent/v1 record becomes a projection of the stream when present), ADR-0046 and ADR-0085 (detector demoted to fallback, hook path becomes a stream producer), gives ADR-0075 (%name) its production caller. Does not touch ADR-0092 (durable work stays on the coordinator endpoint; the stream is live, bounded, not evidence).

Alternatives to record: keep scraping as primary (rejected: 6.5k LOC to recover what the harness states); make the agent session the coordinator's WorkSession (rejected: different failure semantics, ADR-0092); put structured agent events on the wire as a typed frame family (rejected: ADR-0030 principle, opaque codec per kind instead); record transcripts (rejected for v1: privacy, size; provider_raw is opt-in).

title: W1: ADR-0102 Resources: the server serves kinds; Terminal is the first
description:
Write ADR-0102 "Resources: the server serves kinds; Terminal is the first" and its ADR/README.md index row.

Decision content (from the program brief): Resource = ResourceId + ResourceKind (open u8 enum: Terminal=0, AgentSession=1, Unknown on decode) + optional parent + lifecycle + ordered opaque output stream with per-stream negotiated codec + bootstrap (ADR-0070 shape) + kind-defined input + tagged event stream + L3 scope. Location (Local/Satellite) stays orthogonal to kind. Terminal-facet-only operations (input atoms, RESIZE, GET_SCREEN, GET_TERMINAL_STATE, HISTORY_*, input leases, SIGNAL, APPLY_INPUT, PUT_FILE, TRANSCRIBE) fail on other kinds with WRONG_RESOURCE_KIND. The wire primary renames TerminalId -> ResourceId (same tag bytes) in protocol 0.9.0; the reserved PROCESS_* / FORWARD_PORT discriminants are subsumed by kinds and stay unallocated.

Relationships to state in the ADR: supersedes ADR-0016 (wire primary); scopes ADR-0014 (the actor becomes the Terminal engine inside a generic resource core), ADR-0015 (L1 is the resource substrate), ADR-0022 (projections are per kind), ADR-0030 (engine delegation generalizes: every kind gets an opaque negotiated codec; the closed list becomes identity, lifecycle, transport, opaque bytes per kind, metadata). Names to avoid and why: Workload (ADR-0098 client), WorkSession (ADR-0092), Block, Surface.

Constraints: <= 150 lines; CONVENTIONS.md template exactly (Context / Decision / Why / Tradeoffs / Alternatives); Status: Proposed; TL;DR <= 75 words, no links; no emojis; no future tense about shipped behavior; frontmatter audience: contributors, stability: stable. Alternatives must include: keep TerminalId + add kind (rejected: vocabulary is the point); make AgentSession a metadata convention (rejected: no ordered stream, no bootstrap, no cascade); model kinds as separate frame families like the reserved PROCESS_* (rejected: N parallel lifecycles). Run just docs-check.

title: [epic] Resource model: the server serves kinds; Terminal is the first, AgentSession the second
description:
Goal: phux is shaped as a multiplexer for all work. The server serves *resources*; a PTY-plus-libghostty Terminal is the first ResourceKind, an AgentSession (the agent harness's structured event stream, producer-fed via hooks) is the second, and the server enforces a parent binding between them (kill the pane, the agent session closes). Vocabulary, wire, server, clients, and docs all say "resource". Protocol 0.8.0 -> 0.9.0 in exactly one break.

Why now: the server crate is ~26k LOC VT/PTY-bound out of ~80k and the rest never touches libghostty, but there is no trait, enum, or kind field anywhere that says what backs a served thing; satellite terminals are handled by eight open-coded is_local() bail-outs in runtime/commands.rs; agent_detect spends ~6.5k LOC scraping screens for state the harness already reports through hooks whose stdin payload the shim discards. The frame registry already reserves PROCESS_* and FORWARD_PORT discriminants for non-terminal served things that were never built. Superlogical (Mitchell Hashimoto, announced 2026-07-29) ships the same phase-1 architecture and names "multiplexer for all work" as its phase 2.

Canonical design: ADR-0102 Resources, ADR-0103 AgentSession and producer-fed streams, ADR-0104 parent bindings, once landed. Until then the lead's program brief governs.

Waves (children carry blocks deps):
- W1 no wire break: ADRs; core+server resource split; resolve_resource seam; protocol additive shapes; docs tooling and banner flips; memory prune.
- W2 features: AgentSession engine; bindings and cascade; detector precedence; hook shim; client/CLI/MCP; client-core/TUI; web/FFI tolerance; spec text; e2e.
- W3 rename and bump: TerminalId -> ResourceId workspace-wide, 0.9.0, FFI/cockpit/web/spec.
- W4 docs cascade: CONCEPTS rewrite, IN-FORCE view, supersession flips, architecture, consumers, positioning docs, ci-full, PR.

Out of scope, explicitly: coordinator/WorkSession (ADR-0092 stays a separate endpoint); structured cells on the wire (the ADR-0030 principle holds per kind); panes/layout on the wire; grandchildren bindings; recording AgentSession streams; renumbering or deleting any ADR.

title: Reverse enrollment: sandboxes dial out to the hub with a one-time credential
description:
Slice 3. Disposable agent VMs behind NAT with no dialable listener register themselves: the satellite server dials OUT to the hub over QUIC/WSS with a one-time enrollment credential minted on the hub, and the hub's link supervisor adopts the inbound connection as a satellite link (a link is a link regardless of who dialed). No cloud, no third-party relay.

Needs an ADR (auth direction, credential lifecycle, ADR-0098 alignment) and spec text. This is the differentiator; herdr's answer to this problem is a hosted cloud.

title: Fleet overlay and sidebar: every agent everywhere with live state (hub-side metadata mirror)
description:
Slice 2. Fleet overlay and sidebar list satellite terminals grouped by agent (not by machine) with a host badge and live agent state.

Requires a hub-side read-only mirror of a tiny allowlist of L3 keys per satellite terminal (phux.agent/v1, asked flag), retagged Local->Satellite for consumers. L3 stays server-local; this is one named carve-out and needs a short ADR plus a docs/spec/L3.md amendment. Not general L3 federation.

title: TUI: open satellite terminals as panes, split onto a host, host badge
description:
Slice 1. No wire change. A window may hold local and satellite panes side by side.

Add: open host/@N as a pane; split-onto-host (spawn with satellite: Some, owner_terminal: None per L1, then place the returned Satellite id in the layout); host badge on pane border and status bar; the driver must not install per-pane SUBSCRIBE_METADATA on satellite scopes (L3: refused on the wire) and must treat SatelliteUnreachable as a pane state (grey, layout slot kept, snapshot replay on return). Web and Cockpit inherit via the shared layout document (Satellite ids already serialize).

Acceptance: hub session window shows a local pane next to a devbox pane; input, resize, snapshot, kill all work; satellite link drop greys the pane without tearing the layout; multi-satellite e2e test; docs/consumers/tui.md updated.

title: Mixed-host workspace: place terminals across machines, no machine-first UI
description:
Product thesis: the user never thinks about machines; host is a placement attribute of a terminal, like cwd. Workspaces belong to the client, terminals belong to servers; satellites stay Terminal-scoped on the wire (ADR-0007) and the client workspace mixes hosts. One attach point (the always-on hub); SSH is bootstrap only; sandboxes phone home.

Reference point: herdr v0.9 'machines' (SSH-connected servers, one TUI, switch-machines UX). Phux does NOT integrate with herdr; this is native. Not building: mesh, satellite chaining, federated L2 session/window joins, hosted relay dependency.

Slices in ship order are the children of this epic.

title: Voice passthrough: TRANSCRIBE command pastes a PUT_FILE audio clip's transcription into a pane
description: Loop: phone records a 16kHz mono WAV -> PUT_FILE (ADR-0059 sandbox) -> COMMAND Transcribe { upload_id, terminal_id } -> server runs the operator-configured transcriber command ([voice] transcriber = [...] with {path} substituted; stdout is the text; wraps any local ASR server such as whisper.cpp/speaches/a Friday CLI via curl, so no HTTP client dependency enters phux-server) -> replies OkWith(Json { text }) so the client shows what was heard -> pastes the text into the pane as one acknowledged APPLY_INPUT (idempotent across reconnect, #486). Paste inserts without submitting so the client keeps a confirm step. Feature-bit gated like GET_PERF (new ServerFeature TRANSCRIBE), shipped as a 0.8.0 draft. Batch not streaming for v1. Bound the transcriber with a timeout and the upload cap; refuse when [voice] is unset with a remedy message. title: Lane 11: keep the PTY reader draining during the pane-kill grace window
description: Found by lane 4's own post-hoc trace: await_pane_group_exit never drains pty_rx, so with the new bounded reader channel (PTY_CHANNEL_DEPTH=128) a dying child that flushes more than ~128KiB to the terminal parks the reader, the kernel PTY accepts only 1024 bytes without a reader (measured), and the child stalls against its own PANE_KILL_GRACE and gets SIGKILLed mid-flush. Before the bounded channel the reader never stopped. Fix: drain-and-discard pty_rx on every grace poll tick (proposed diff in lane 4's analysis), plus a test that a child writing >256KiB in its SIGHUP handler finishes before the kill. Pre-existing and separate: those bytes are discarded rather than shown to an attached client; file as a follow-up if worth it.

description: release-drift correctly reports pi-extension-v0.2.0 and opencode-plugin-v0.2.0 as stranded drafts. 2026-09-02 BLOCKER found after #496 merged (6c025145): the new repository.url gate in agent-integration-release.yml's prepare step rejects all three stranded tags. The step checks out the TAG's tree, and pi-extension-v0.2.0, pi-extension-v0.2.1 and opencode-plugin-v0.2.0 all still carry "url": "https://github.com/phall1/phux.git" (the URL fix landed on main only). Expected is https://github.com/no-phux/phux.git, so every dry_run=false dispatch against those tags now fails at step one with "repository.url must be ... for npm trusted publishing".

The gate is CORRECT, not over-strict: npm requires a case-sensitive match between package.json repository and the repo publishing with provenance (docs.npmjs.com/generating-provenance-statements); redirect tolerance is undocumented, so relying on phall1 -> no-phux redirecting is unverified. Those tags are therefore not publishable with provenance as-is.

Options, none applied yet (another lane is mid-bootstrap; deliberately not re-tagging under it):

(b) Force-move the existing tags onto commits carrying the URL fix. Destructive and breaks the verifiable tag->tree chain #496 exists to guarantee.
(c) Relax the gate for legacy tags. Rejected: npm would likely still refuse provenance, moving the failure later and making it illegible again.

Independent of this, the npm first-publish blocker still stands: local npm CLI is unauthenticated (npm whoami fails) and @phux/pi and @phux/opencode are both still 404. Trusted publishing cannot do a first publish - a trusted publisher is configured against an already-existing package - so one human-authenticated npm publish per package is required before the automated lane can ever succeed. Documented in docs/RELEASING.md as of 51f9dc53.
2026-09-02 option A executed: PR #496 merged as 6c025145; OIDC docs correction landed as 51f9dc53. title: macOS: adhoc-signed binary + phux upgrade temp-exec make firewall allowlisting impossible
description:
On macOS with the Application Firewall enabled, phux is silently unreachable over any non-loopback interface, with no error on either end.

Mechanism: phux ships adhoc/linker-signed (Signature=adhoc). The firewall's 'automatically allow built-in signed software' covers Apple binaries but NOT adhoc-signed ones, so phux needs an explicit allowlist entry. With stealth mode on, unlisted apps are dropped silently: the kernel completes the TCP handshake, the client's connect() succeeds, and the server's accept() simply never fires. Client hangs forever; server logs nothing. UDS and loopback are unaffected (the firewall exempts them), so 'phux ls' and a loopback listener look perfectly healthy while the whole remote surface is dead.

Two things make this worse than a one-time setup step:
1. The allowlist entry is per-path and versioned (/opt/homebrew/Cellar/phux/<version>/bin/phux), so EVERY upgrade silently breaks remote access. Observed exactly this: an entry for 0.21.0 kept working until an upgrade to 0.23.0 moved the path.
2. 'phux upgrade' re-execs the server from a tempfile snapshot dir which it then deletes (runtime/upgrade.rs), so the running server's executable path is both ephemeral and already unlinked -- it can never be allowlisted at all.

Diagnosed by racing listeners on the same host/interface/instant: /usr/bin/python3 (Apple-signed) accepted the connection while phux got nothing.

Worth considering: sign+notarize release binaries, detect this in 'phux doctor' (probe the routable listener from off-loopback and report a firewall block distinctly from 'no server'), and document it. doctor currently reports the server fully healthy in this state -- see phux-kyna.

title: phux pair exits 0 when it fails to mint a token
description:
`phux pair --json` printed 'phux pair: failed to mint token: legacy token store requires explicit migration' on stdout and still exited 0.

Because the exit code said success, `phux host enroll` treated the human-readable error as its JSON mint document and reported 'remote `phux pair --json` emitted unparseable JSON: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0' -- hiding the actual, actionable cause (needs --migrate-legacy). A failed mint must exit non-zero, and on --json the error belongs on stderr as a JSON error object (the documented contract for the flag).
close_reason:
Invalid: measurement artifact, not a phux defect.

phux pair correctly exits 1 on a failed mint with stdout empty and the error on stderr. Verified on both machines against a real legacy-format store:

  remote_exit=1
  phux pair: failed to mint token: legacy token store requires explicit migration

The original 'EXIT:0' came from my own harness: 'ssh host "exit 7"' also reports 0 here, so the ssh exit status was never reaching the check. The downstream symptom the bead blamed on this -- 'phux host enroll' reporting 'unparseable JSON' -- has a different cause worth keeping in mind: enroll consumes 'phux pair --json' over ssh, so it needs the ssh exit status to survive. That part held up; only the claimed pair bug did not.

description: Docs-only. ADR stays Proposed until Blackbird ratifies its half (blackbird ADR-0005 does not exist yet). Gate: just docs-check + spec-version-sync.
notes:
ADR NUMBER COLLISION, CORRECTED 2026-08-17. This bead was written naming 'ADR-0092'. That number was taken later the same day by an EXTERNAL PR (#487, commit 3b418f24, ADR/0092-durable-work-coordinator-authority.md). DO NOT USE 0092.

AND DO NOT SUBSTITUTE A NEW HARD-CODED NUMBER HERE — that just re-arms the same trap for whoever implements this weeks from now. THE RULE: at authoring time, take the next free number by reading ADR/ and ADR/README.md, and add the index row in the SAME commit. The registry gate (phux-5xtz) enforces one row per ADR with unique, ascending numbers, so a same-number claim then becomes an ordinary textual conflict at integration rather than two files landing silently.

WHY THIS IS WORTH SPELLING OUT: the gate protects the TREE, not a PLAN. A bead that names a future ADR number is claiming an identifier with no reservation behind it — nothing stops another branch taking it in the interim, and nothing detects it until someone reads both. That is exactly what happened here.

title: TLS cert SANs omit the routable address phux pair advertises
description:
`phux pair` prints a connect link naming a routable overlay address (`phux://connect?url=wss://100.79.155.27:8787&fp=...`), but `ensure_self_signed` in crates/phux-server/src/transport/tls.rs mints the certificate with SANs `DNS:localhost, IP:127.0.0.1, IP:::1` only. Verified against a live server:

    openssl s_client -connect 100.79.155.27:8787 -verify_ip 100.79.155.27
    verify error:num=64:IP address mismatch

So the server hands out an address its own certificate does not claim. Any client that adds the phux certificate to its trust store and then validates the server name (curl --cacert, a browser with the cert trusted, openssl s_client -verify_ip) fails the handshake on a name mismatch it cannot work around.

NOT affected: phux's own dialer (phux-dial CertTrust is SkipVerify or Pinned; PinnedFingerprint::verify_server_cert ignores _server_name) and phux-mobile (its PinnedCert verifier likewise ignores the name). Fingerprint pinning is unaffected by SANs.

Fix: mint the certificate with the addresses phux actually advertises. Hard constraint: an existing complete cert/key pair must never be regenerated, because that rotates the fingerprint pinned on every paired device.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/tls-cert-routable-sans (955ccaaa/amended): SANs now cover the listener bind address and the pair link host + detected overlay addresses; existing certs are never widened (ADR-0091), coverage is reported by phux pair, the listener log, and phux doctor's remote-cert check.

title: [bug] beads DB is at schema v65, ahead of the supported bd 1.2.2 binary (v53)
description:
Hit 2026-08-15 at the end of the phux-k0cw session. Not caused by any phux code; it is a beads-tooling state.

SYMPTOM. Every bd command fails with:
  schema version mismatch: database is at v65, binary knows up to v53 (12 migrations ahead)

bd's own message says the database was migrated by the accidental, untested v1.2.0/v1.2.1 release, and that 1.2.2 (the installed Homebrew build) is the supported one — do NOT reinstall 1.2.1 to make the error go away.

WHEN IT APPEARED. Mid-session. Every bd read and write worked normally — bd prime at session start, and all the phux-k0cw creates/updates/closes — until a 'bd sync', after which reads began failing. The inference is that sync pulled a working set that a v1.2.x binary elsewhere (another machine or another clone) had already migrated forward, and the local binary cannot read that cursor.

DATA IS INTACT. Verified after the fact with --ignore-schema-skew: every bead written this session is present and correct (phux-k0cw and children, phux-jx39, phux-q7ks, phux-at0r closed, the retitled phux-w7z2.20, all labels and the gh-478 external ref). Nothing was lost and the sync push completed; refs/dolt/data on origin is at 091fc7bf.

WORKAROUND, per bd's own message (it states this is verified safe for this schema range; audit-event versioning is paused until recovery):
  BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1 bd <command>
  bd --ignore-schema-skew <command>

FIX. Follow the official recovery, which rolls the schema cursor back to v53 in about two minutes:
  https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/v1.2.2/docs/RECOVERY-1.2.1.md

WHY P1. Every agent session in this repo opens with a bd prime hook. While this is unrecovered, each one starts against a tracker whose plain commands error out, and the natural 'fix' an agent or a human reaches for — reinstalling the version that appears to work — is the one thing the tool explicitly warns against, and would migrate the database further forward.
acceptance_criteria: The recovery guide has been run, bd commands succeed with no BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW and no skew warning, and any other clone that syncs this repo is checked for the same forward cursor.
notes:
LOCAL RECOVERY DONE 2026-08-16 (this machine, /Users/phall/workspace/phux).

Diagnosis refinement: bd runs in EMBEDDED mode on .beads/embeddeddolt/phux. A stray 'dolt sql-server -H 127.0.0.1 -P 53736' (pid 39297) holds .beads/dolt — a DIFFERENT, leftover server-mode directory that bd is not using. It did not need stopping for the recovery and was left running.

Steps run, per the v1.2.2 recovery guide:
1. Verified binary is bd 1.2.2 (Homebrew) and dolt 2.3.0 present.
2. Backup taken OUTSIDE the repo at /Users/phall/workspace/phux-beads-backup-pre-recovery (498M). Deliberately not .beads.backup-pre-recovery: .beads/.gitignore ignores embeddeddolt/ but a repo-root sibling would show up untracked in every worktree's git status.
3. Cursor was confirmed at 63 rows, max version 65.
4. dolt sql -q "DELETE FROM schema_migrations WHERE version > 53; CALL DOLT_ADD(...); CALL DOLT_COMMIT(...)" in .beads/embeddeddolt/phux. Dolt commit lb4rft1cauebli3n2ql8lpvpl7mcv8r8.
5. Verified: bd stats and bd ready run with NO BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW and no skew warning. 955 issues, 882 closed, counts unchanged from pre-recovery.

STILL OPEN, and why this bead is not closed:
(a) The recovered cursor has NOT been pushed. The guide is explicit that the migrated cursor replicates, so until this is pushed, any clone that pulls can carry v65 back and regress the fix. Held because CLAUDE.md sets a conservative profile: no dolt remote sync without explicit authority. Command when authorized: bd dolt push
(b) No other clone has been checked for the forward cursor, which the acceptance criteria requires.
(c) Optional and skipped on purpose: the guide's audit-event re-track (DELETE FROM dolt_ignore WHERE pattern='events'; DOLT_ADD -f events). It changes what syncs, so it should be a decision, not a side effect. Until it runs, the 1.1 line writes audit events unversioned and unsynced; everything else syncs normally.
close_reason:
Recovered and pushed 2026-08-16. Cursor rolled back to v53 on this machine (dolt commit lb4rft1cauebli3n2ql8lpvpl7mcv8r8), verified by bd stats/ready running with no BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW and no warning, 955 issues intact. Pushed with bd dolt push: refs/dolt/data 091fc7bf -> 5ebffe36, so the v53 cursor is now the one any clone pulls.

Residual, deliberately not held open for: the acceptance line 'any other clone that syncs this repo is checked' cannot be verified from here. Pulling clones now get v53; the only remaining regression path is a clone that still holds v65 locally AND pushes. If that happens the symptom is identical and this recovery re-runs the same way. Full step-by-step is in the notes.

Also not done, on purpose: the guide's optional audit-event re-track. It changes what syncs, so it stays a deliberate decision. Until then the 1.1 line writes audit events unversioned and unsynced; everything else syncs normally.

title: The layout audit never sets chrome_top, so it has never audited the titlebar-riding chrome
description:
chrome_register_tests.zig's auditAt() builds and solves the tree for each sweep size but leaves Workspace.chrome_top at its default 0. tabsRideTitlebarIn() therefore returns false in every state the audit sweeps, so every audit run lays out the FULLSCREEN fallback header band -- never the hidden-inset titlebar arrangement that actually ships, where the 78pt traffic-light reserve and the two 8pt gaps are spent.

comments.author: phall
comments.text:
FIXED on branch fix/tab-label-identity (worktree .claude/worktrees/rosy-purring-pretzel/tablabel), 6 commits, tip 3c8d968. NOT pushed.

REPRODUCED first, exactly as reported. Sandbox pty ceiling + composite patches applied to a copy of the pinned SDK; real bundle via scripts/dev-run.sh --automation --detach --fresh; 15x cmd+t. publisher_pid=33405 matched the pid dev-run.sh launched, gpu_present_path=packet, present_fallback=none. Snapshot bounds matched the report byte for byte (51.428574x17.5 at 123.428574 pitch) and the composited texture showed seven tabs each reading "Termi...".

FIX: elideTitleMiddleInto in workspace_projection.zig grows the TAIL first, so the app hands the renderer a string that already fits. Two consequences beyond the pixels: the accessibility snapshot now reports what is painted (it reported the full "Terminal 10" before, which is why nothing but a GPU capture could see the bug), and TabLabelIdentity gives the app an instrument for "is the strip still naming anything", in the shape Legibility already has.

SECOND ROUND, worth remembering: middle elision alone was not enough. A greedy fit always stops at the EDGE of the box, so a sub-one-percent disagreement between the view builder's estimator and CoreText decided the last character -- 3 of 7 tabs came back "Ter...l...". Measured: estimator priced "Ter...l 12" at 50.932, "Ter...l 14" at 51.156, "Ter...l 16" at 51.002 in a 51.428574 box and CoreText refused all three, while 11/13/15 at 47.642/50.848/51.030 survived. Not monotone. labelFitBudget holds back one ellipsis advance -- derived, not tuned: it is exactly what the backstop must reclaim to append its own marker.

VERIFIED on real composited pixels after the fix, same conditions, publisher_pid=138, packet path, no fallback: "Te... 10" "Te...l 11" "Te... 12" "Te... 13" "Te... 14" "Te... 15" "Te... 16". Seven tabs, seven different words.

Two guards, both watched red: tab-label-keeps-its-tail and tab-label-fits-its-box. All eight guards in the ledger re-proved red at b2d8a15.

NOT VERIFIED: fullscreen at 1920pt on the glass. The cmd+ctrl+f chord landed (the strip moved to the fallback band, tab y 29.25 -> 51.25) but the window never widened past 1100 in the snapshot, so there is no real-pixel evidence at the 14-tab / 48.2857pt box. The suite pins that geometry and its distinctness instead.

title: Tabs vanish from the top strip with no cue anywhere - not in the pixels, not in the AX tree
description:
visibleTabWindowIn draws a contiguous run around the selection and omits the rest, and nothing marks the omission: no chevron, no count, no edge fade, no partial tab.

title: [bug] main is red: wrapper_never_relaunches_claude_after_a_mid_session_crash fails at 41c032ca
description:
Discovered 2026-08-15 while validating the phux-k0cw sidebar chain.

crates/phux/src/commands/agent/shim.rs:1034 fails on a CLEAN checkout of main at 41c032ca — verified in a throwaway worktree with no local changes, so it is not caused by the sidebar work.

FAILING ASSERTION (scenario B, the phux-t2g bug):
  assert!(output.contains('phux session ended abnormally'))
after run_on_pty(&wrapper, [('FAKE_CLAUDE_EXIT', '17')]).

The status assertion above it (status == 17) passes, so the exit code propagates correctly; it is the operator-facing message that is missing from the PTY output. Either the wrapper stopped printing it, or the PTY capture is racing the message (the test drives a real PTY, which puts it in scope for the phux-5wxp load-dependent flake family — but it reproduced on the first run at base, which is not flake-shaped).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TEST: 'just ci-full green before pushing' is the ONLY gate protecting main (CONTRIBUTING.md 'How work reaches main' — a maintainer push has no PR CI). A test that is already red on main silently converts that gate into 'green except the one that was already failing', which is how a second failure gets waved through.

REPRO:
  git worktree add --detach /tmp/check 41c032ca
  cd /tmp/check
  cargo nextest run -E 'test(wrapper_never_relaunches_claude_after_a_mid_session_crash)'
acceptance_criteria: Either the wrapper emits 'phux session ended abnormally' on a mid-session crash again and the test passes on main, or the assertion is corrected to match intended behaviour with the change explained. main runs 'cargo nextest run --workspace' clean.
notes:
NARROWING 2026-08-15, from the feat/fleet-inbox-sidebar branch (this bug is NOT caused by that branch — confirmed against a clean 41c032ca worktree).

Ruled OUT: the launch-sentinel primitive itself. `marker=$(mktemp); sh -c 'printf started > "$1"' _ "$marker"; [ -s "$marker" ]` is TRUE on this machine, so neither mktemp nor the stamp nor the -s test is the failure. The outer wrapper's argument math is also correct: the fake phux does 'shift 4' over 'new -c <cwd> --', leaving '<shim> --phux-inner <marker> ...' for exec, so the inner shim IS reached with the sentinel as $1.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS, unverified — the test's fake phux is too thin. crates/phux/src/commands/agent/shim.rs:1003-1006 models ONLY 'phux new':

  #!/bin/sh
  set -u
  if [ "${FAKE_PHUX_LAUNCH_FAIL:-0}" = "1" ]; then exit 3; fi
  shift 4
  exec "$@"

But the inner branch also calls set_state (shim.rs:449 'set_state start', and a 'set_state clear' EXIT trap), which invokes the same fake binary as 'phux agent set ...'. That input hits the same 'shift 4; exec "$@"' path, so the fixture execs whatever four-args-in is left of an 'agent set' command line — an arbitrary side effect in the middle of the scenario, and a plausible route to the sentinel or the wrapper's state being disturbed before the assertion reads it.

NEXT STEP: make the fake phux dispatch on $1 — model 'new' as today, and make 'agent' a no-op exit 0 — then re-run. If the test goes green, the bug was fixture fidelity rather than wrapper behaviour, and the fix is the fixture plus a comment saying why the fake must dispatch. If it stays red, the wrapper's started-detection is genuinely broken and the next thing to instrument is whether the EXIT trap's set_state runs before the outer wrapper reads the sentinel.

Priority unchanged at P1: while this is red, 'just ci-full green before pushing' — the only gate protecting main — cannot be satisfied by anyone.
close_reason: Fixed upstream on main by 90613b90 'fix(agent): stop the shim pty test inheriting the phux env it tests' — CommandBuilder inherited PHUX_TERMINAL_ID, so the wrapper took its inner branch, never ran 'phux new', and never stamped the launch sentinel. Verified green after rebasing feat/fleet-inbox-sidebar onto current main: 3818/3818.
