title: Converge TUI help and command palette into one fuzzy action finder
description:
Why: phux currently maintains two overlapping discovery overlays. The help modal is a scroll-only keybinding table while the command palette is the fuzzy, executable action catalog with live chords. Users should not have to remember which discovery surface answers which question, and help should support the same type-to-find flow.

What: make show-help and command-palette open the same fuzzy action finder, backed by the canonical action registry and live keybindings/plugin rows. Keep both action names and user bindings as entry aliases, but remove recursive/noise rows from inside the finder. Retire duplicated help-only presentation code when no longer referenced.

Acceptance: C-a ? and C-a : (including rebound equivalents) open the same filterable overlay; typing searches action descriptions and displayed chords with existing scored fuzzy ranking; Enter executes through run_action; Esc dismisses; neither show-help nor command-palette appears as a recursive row; generated action docs explain both aliases; TUI docs describe one discovery surface; stale help-only code/tests are removed or migrated; just ci-full passes.
design: Treat help and palette as two entry aliases to one SelectList, not stacked overlays or one opening the other. Keep ACTION_NAMES stable for config compatibility. Move show-help into NON_PALETTE_ACTIONS beside command-palette with an explicit alias reason.
close_reason: Landed on main as 72fca3ce after rebasing onto current main. show-help and command-palette now open one fuzzy executable finder; both aliases are excluded from recursive rows; the old HelpOverlay and duplicate tests/docs were removed; generated references were refreshed. just ci-full passed on the exact landed commit: 3,794 workspace tests, 60 real-server/agent E2Es, 3 performance tests, and fleet smoke.

title: Move the focused pane across sessions from one fuzzy TUI picker
description:
Why: cross-session movement already exists in the canonical CLI (phux move-pane) and MCP (phux_move_pane), but a human in the TUI must leave the attach surface, discover selectors, and type a two-target command. That defeats the zero-thought workflow the command palette and all-session pickers are meant to provide.

What: add one palette/context-menu action for moving the focused pane. It opens a fuzzy destination picker spanning panes in every cached session/window, clearly identifies session/window/pane and excludes the source. Choosing a target performs the existing ADR-0056 ownership+layout operation without restarting the process or changing TerminalId. Use the same action dispatch and SelectList primitives as other TUI discovery surfaces; do not fork selector or movement semantics. Preserve existing phux move-pane CLI and phux_move_pane MCP behavior as the headless canonical surfaces.

Acceptance: the action is discoverable by fuzzy search in the command surface and from the pane context menu; one selection moves the focused pane beside an exact local destination in the same or another session; process, scrollback, metadata, agent record, subscriptions, and id survive; source/destination layout failure and rollback are visible rather than silent; source/self/satellite/partial-cache cases are safely refused; tests cover same-session, cross-session, last-pane source reaping, destination-layout failure, and picker filtering; generated action/reference docs and TUI docs are updated; just ci-full passes.
design: Reuse SelectList and run_action. The TUI implementation should factor or reuse the spatial operation below crates/phux/src/commands/spatial.rs rather than shelling out to phux. Default placement should be a documented single choice (likely side-by-side at 0.5); directional variants can be separate palette rows only if that remains one selection.
notes: Implemented fuzzy TUI destination picker and pane context-menu action backed by shared phux_client::pane_move transaction. Preserves TerminalId, follows server-confirmed focus/layout, supports current/cross-session fully cached destinations, and refuses source/self/satellite/uncached/no-target without mutation; errors remain visible. Landed on main as 3fdbe6df, ancestor of current 675b4959. Post-rebase validation: pane_move 4 pass, TUI move_pane 2 pass, spatial 10 pass, fmt pass, and full just ci-full green (5,067 tests, 95 skipped; 93 fast E2E; 3 perf E2E; fleet smoke). Rendered picker verified unclipped.
close_reason: Cross-session destination picker implemented, fully validated, and landed on main as 3fdbe6df

title: Stage 9: Docs and the ADR
description:
Stage 9 of 9 in the fleet-inbox sidebar chain (epic phux-k0cw).

COMMIT SUBJECT
  docs(tui): document the three-zone sidebar and live peer metadata

FILES
  - docs/consumers/tui.md
  - docs/CONFIG.md
  - ADR/0089-three-zone-sidebar.md
  - ADR/README.md

VALIDATION
  just docs-check && bash scripts/check-docs.sh --only=impl-status && just ci
design: docs/consumers/tui.md §6.4 (1733-1855) is the main rewrite. Keep the `<!-- impl-status: shipped; probe: toggle-sidebar -->` marker at :1735 immediately above the `> **Status:**` callout — check-docs gate 7 fails on either without the other — and if any zone ships incomplete give it its own subsection with its own marker and a probe symbol that is a real, unique identifier in non-comment crate source (`needs_you_queue` and `session_roster` from Stage 6 are good probes; avoid generic words like `roster`, which will match unrelated code). Replace 'laid out herdr-style in two labelled sections' (:1751-1752) with the three zones; recast the `spaces` block (:1753-1765) as zone 2 'here'; recast the `agents` block (:1766-1805) as zone 1 'needs you' keeping the attention-ladder text at :1795-1798 VERBATIM (it is the agreed ordering) and adding the `NEEDS_YOU_CAP` cap and the `+N more` row committing `agent-fleet`; add zone 3 'spaces' as the one-line-per-peer roster with dot + `!1 *2` histogram, an overflow line, and an explicit statement that a satellite row shows unknown state because L3 does not federate (docs/spec/L3.md:122-133) rather than a fabricated zero. REPLACE the empty-state paragraph at :1806-1812 — it currently asserts the exact opposite of zone 1's contract ('still renders its header with a quiet `no agents` empty-state line … rather than vanishing'). Extend the click-target table at :1837-1847 with `switch-session { name, window, pane }` and `agent-fleet`; the surrounding 'Every sidebar click commits the same ResolvedAction a keybinding or palette row would' sentence stays true. Also: §4.4 theme rows :1216-1220 (retitle sidebar_section to the three zone headers); §4.5 :1290-1297 (recompute the yield example for the new width, and say that yielding is now the DEFAULT narrow-terminal behaviour, keeping the 'turning the strip off is always allowed' escape hatch that makes default-on safe); §4.3 :1180-1182 (be explicit that `[sidebar]` GEOMETRY is attach-time while zone CONTENT is push-driven, mirrored into docs/CONFIG.md:84); §5.5 :1505-1513 and §5.6 :1548-1556 (both are the doc-of-record for the retired attach-time-snapshot staleness — rewrite for live subscriptions and KEEP the ADR-0030 citation, extending it to say the sidebar's cross-session zones add no wire surface either); §7 mouse table :1899-1906 and §7.1 context-menu table :1954-1965 (a zone-1/zone-3 row switches sessions, and its right-click menu cannot offer same-session window verbs for a session this client is not attached to); §13 :2630-2635 (flip 'off by default', in lockstep with help.rs from Stage 8) and :2604-2612 (a fresh `phux` now paints a strip). Bump the frontmatter `last-reviewed` at :4 from 2026-08-09. New `ADR/0089-three-zone-sidebar.md` using the strict template (docs/CONVENTIONS.md:169-204): `Status: Accepted`, ~150-line cap, frontmatter, `**TL;DR.**` block; the decision it closes off is cross-session attention as always-on chrome versus an on-demand overlay, and live peer state via existing L3 verbs versus a new projection frame — cite ADR-0030 for the no-new-wire constraint and ADR-0018 for the lazy L3 reads, and record the two accepted degradations (satellite state unavailable; session rename is poll-only because the server returns before `metadata_set`). Add its row to the hand-curated ADR/README.md index table.
close_reason: ADR-0089 accepted and registered; tui.md 6.4 rewritten for three zones; docs-check green.

title: Stage 8: Sidebar on by default, wider
description:
Stage 8 of 9 in the fleet-inbox sidebar chain (epic phux-k0cw).

COMMIT SUBJECT
  feat(config): turn the sidebar on by default and widen the strip

FILES
  - crates/phux-config/src/schema.rs
  - crates/phux-config/src/default.toml
  - crates/phux-config/tests/parse.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/render/overlay/help.rs
  - crates/phux/src/refdocs/config.rs
  - docs/reference/config.md
  - crates/phux-client/tests/sidebar_branch_e2e.rs

VALIDATION
  just docs-gen && cargo nextest run --workspace && just ci-full
design: Highest blast radius of the whole change; keep it as its own commit so a revert is one hop. schema.rs:445-447 — `enabled` uses bare `#[serde(default)]`, which resolves to `bool::default()` = false, NOT to `SidebarCfg::default()`. Flipping only the `impl Default` at :459 creates a silent split where an empty config gets `enabled: true` but `[sidebar]\nwidth = 30` gets `enabled: false`. Add `const fn default_sidebar_enabled() -> bool { true }` and `#[serde(default = "default_sidebar_enabled")]`, and flip the Default impl in the same edit. Raise `default_sidebar_width()` (:466-468) from 20 to 28 (28 + the shipped `min_pane_cols` 40 puts the yield threshold at 68 columns, just above the 64-column compact breakpoint — pick deliberately and state the arithmetic in the doc comment). Update the struct doc at :436-441 ('Off by default') and the two field docs. default.toml:435-452 — rewrite the prose for three zones and on-by-default, update `# enabled = false` -> `# enabled = true` and `# width = 20` -> `# width = 28`, keep every value COMMENTED (an uncommented value that disagrees with the schema trips `the_embedded_defaults_agree_with_the_schema_defaults`, refdocs/config.rs:321), and retitle the `sidebar_section` comment at :429 to the three zone headers. parse.rs:122/136-138 — flip `assert!(!cfg.sidebar.enabled, "sidebar is off by default")` and the width assertion INCLUDING their messages, and ADD `a_partial_sidebar_table_keeps_the_enabled_default` covering exactly the serde split above (nothing guards it today: parse.rs:336 sets all three keys). driver.rs:1749 — the third hardcoded 20, `sidebar_cfg.as_ref().map_or(20, |c| c.width)`; make it call `default_sidebar_width()` so there is one source. help.rs:457/464 — 'toggle-sidebar (window sidebar; off by default)' becomes user-visible fiction the moment the default flips, and its unit tests at :578-601 pin the string. refdocs/config.rs:67 summary and the pinned literal row `"| `sidebar.width` | `20` |"` at :369. Then run `just docs-gen` and commit the regenerated docs/reference/config.md — it is byte-compared by `generated_reference_docs_match_the_tree` (refdocs/mod.rs:164) on every `just test`, and docs-gen runs the COMPILED binary so it must be re-run after the schema change builds. sidebar_branch_e2e.rs:49-51/71 — widen the 20-column read window and update the const doc; keep the explicit `enabled = true` config write at :81-86 even though it is now a no-op, so the test still states its own precondition. This is the stage where `just ci-full` is mandatory rather than nice-to-have: a default-on, wider sidebar changes the pane geometry every PTY-backed e2e client sees, and `just e2e` is NOT inside `just ci`.
close_reason: Sidebar on by default at width 28; defaults, refdocs, and help text moved with it. Closed ahead of phux-k0cw.7, which was deliberately re-sequenced behind stages 8-9 (see its notes).

title: Stage 7: Session-graph poll for roster membership
description:
Stage 7 of 9 in the fleet-inbox sidebar chain (epic phux-k0cw).

COMMIT SUBJECT
  feat(client): poll the server session graph so the roster tracks new and renamed sessions

FILES
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs

VALIDATION
  cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'binary_id(phux-client) & test(session_graph)' && just ci
design: Closes the one liveness gap named in the verdict, with an existing verb. Today `sessions` (driver.rs:1816) is refreshed ONLY from `outcome.sessions`, which only the `FrameKind::Attached` arm sets (server_frame.rs:831), so the roster is frozen for the life of one attach. Add `async fn refresh_session_graph(conn, next_request_id, pending: &mut HashSet<u32>)` sending `FrameKind::Command { request_id, command: Command::GetState { scope: StateScope::Server } }`, and intercept `FrameKind::CommandResult { request_id, result: CommandResult::OkWith(CommandValue::State(snapshot)) }` in the batch loop alongside the existing MetadataValue intercepts (:2560-2632) — `handle_server_frame` has no CommandResult arm at all today, so the reply would otherwise fall through and be dropped. Fold the snapshot into `sessions` / `focused_session` and re-run `sync_foreign_layout_subscriptions`. Trigger it (a) after the ATTACHED fold, (b) edge-triggered when Stage 3's `foreign_pane_set_dirty` fires or an event names a TerminalId absent from both `panes` and the known foreign leaf set, and (c) on a slow floor timer (a `SESSION_GRAPH_POLL: Duration = 10s` arm in the existing `select!`) — a rename emits nothing at all, so poll is the only answer. Note in the fn doc that `build_session_snapshot` synthesizes window names as `window-{index}` and ships `layout: None` (phux-server/src/state/snapshot.rs:78-82), so GET_STATE is the roster's SPINE (membership + pane inventory, which is all zone 3 needs) and the peer's `phux.tui.layout/v1/<session>` key is an optional enrichment for real window names — the inverse of today's foreign_layouts-first ordering. Keep the poll edge-triggered with a slow floor: `handle_get_state_federated` (phux-server/src/runtime/commands.rs:2328) fans out to every dialed satellite, so a per-second poll from an attached TUI becomes per-second satellite fan-out. Tests: `a_session_created_after_attach_reaches_the_roster`, `the_graph_poll_is_edge_triggered_not_per_frame`.
notes:
UNCLAIMED and re-sequenced 2026-08-15, after stages 1-6 landed.

Deferred behind stages 8 and 9 deliberately, not forgotten. Rationale: this is the only stage in the chain that is pure refinement — the roster is live for every session that exists at attach, and this stage extends that to sessions CREATED or RENAMED mid-attach. Stages 8 (on by default) and 9 (docs + ADR) are what make the feature reach a user at all, so they go first.

Scope discovered while sequencing: the attach loop has NO GET_STATE handling today (grep for GetState/StateScope in driver.rs and server_frame.rs returns nothing). So this is not a small addition to an existing path — it needs the command send, a correlated reply intercept, SessionSnapshot decode, and a re-run of the peer sweep against the fresh graph. Price it as such.

Coverage this stage buys, from the recon:
- Session CREATE surfaces only indirectly today (create_named_session broadcasts nothing, so a headlessly-created session appears only when its seed pane first emits Dirty).
- Session RENAME surfaces to nobody: crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs returns BEFORE metadata_set, so no subscriber is notified.
- Session DEATH is already covered — PaneClosed reaches every server-scope subscriber.
COORDINATION 2026-08-16 (autonomous run): phux-q7ks (server-side METADATA_CHANGED on rename) is in flight on branch w1/rename-notify. When it lands, this stage's poll narrows per the bead's own note: rename gets covered by broadcast; the poll's remaining job is CREATE coverage + membership floor. Keep the edge-trigger + slow-floor design; the 10s floor may be relaxable.
UPDATE 2026-08-16: phux-q7ks is implemented (w1/rename-notify, commit 21db19c4, awaiting merge): renames now reach subscribers of (Global, phux.session.name/v1) push-style with a current\0new payload the roster can apply directly. This stage's poll shrinks to CREATE-only coverage + safety floor. If phux-8uly (seed-pane PaneSpawned) also lands, the poll becomes a pure lossy-notification safety floor and its interval can be long.
DEMOTED 2026-08-17 — this stage is now a PURE SAFETY FLOOR, not a liveness mechanism. Its design premise ('a rename emits nothing at all, so poll is the only answer') is false twice over: rename pushes METADATA_CHANGED (phux-q7ks, landed), and create pushes PaneSpawned (phux-8uly, branch w4/seed-pane-spawned commit 279ab12e). Death was already covered by PaneClosed. So all three legs of session lifecycle now PUSH. Better still, this stage's trigger (b) is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED: crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame/handler.rs:1116 sets foreign_pane_set_dirty on a PaneSpawned for a Terminal outside the client's pane set — the client hook exists and now actually fires for newly created sessions. REMAINING JUSTIFICATION for any poll at all: fanout is best-effort (broadcast_event uses try_send and DROPS on a full mailbox), so a slow floor guards against a lost notification, not against a silent transition. The 10s floor can therefore be relaxed considerably, and the GET_STATE enumerate half is only needed on attach. RESCOPE THIS BEAD ACCORDINGLY BEFORE IMPLEMENTING — it is materially smaller than when it was written.
close_reason: Original poll is no longer required: rename pushes METADATA_CHANGED (phux-q7ks), create pushes PaneSpawned (phux-8uly), death already pushes PaneClosed, and foreign_pane_set_dirty already edges the peer sweep. Remaining long-interval lossy-notification floor is optional follow-up, not inbox-epic scope.

title: Stage 6: Cross-session projection into the three zones
description:
Stage 6 of 9 in the fleet-inbox sidebar chain (epic phux-k0cw).

COMMIT SUBJECT
  feat(client): project the cross-session attention queue and session roster

FILES
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/sidebar_zones.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/mod.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/fleet.rs

VALIDATION
  cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'binary_id(phux-client) & (test(sidebar_zones) | test(roster) | test(needs_you))' && just ci
design: The stage that actually fills zones 1 and 3. New module `crates/phux-client/src/attach/sidebar_zones.rs` holding `pub(super) struct ChromeInputs<'a>` (workspace, panes, focused_pane, zoomed, own_client_id, agent_meta, vcs, sessions, focused_session, foreign_layouts, foreign_agents, foreign_attention) — `refresh_window_chrome` (driver.rs:166) already carries a `too_many_arguments` allow at 9 args, so this is the point to introduce the struct rather than grow the list. Add `pub(super) fn needs_you_queue(inputs: &ChromeInputs) -> Vec<AgentEntry>`: local rows exactly as today's `agent_entries` (:4160) produces them with `session: None`, merged with foreign rows projected from `foreign_layouts` leaves + `foreign_agents` records + the Stage-3 `foreign_attention` set carrying `session: Some(name)` and `pane: Some(dfs_ordinal)`; sort by `attention_rank(state, attention, seen)` descending, tiebreaking local rows by `agent_meta.change_at` (:4177) and foreign rows by stable declaration order below the local ones — the `change_at` map is keyed by local TerminalId only, so document that degradation in the fn doc rather than pretending it is ordered. Foreign rows default `seen: false` (a peer's done-unvisited agent cannot become seen without switching there — correct, but it means the queue never self-clears from a distance; say so in the doc). Return the FULL ranked list; `row_model` owns the `NEEDS_YOU_CAP` truncation so `+N more` counts honestly. Add `pub(super) fn session_roster(inputs: &ChromeInputs) -> Vec<SessionRosterEntry>`: one entry per non-focused session in the `sessions` cache, histogram rolled up from that session's cached leaves, `satellite: true` when any leaf is `!id.is_local()` — a satellite row reports `unknown` for every pane and MUST NOT report `blocked: 0`, which would be an attention queue lying by omission. Rewrite `refresh_window_chrome` to take `ChromeInputs` and drive `set_windows` / `set_needs_you(needs_you_queue(..))` / `set_roster(session_roster(..))`; update all eleven call sites (driver.rs:2020, 2122, 2407, 2792, 2979, 3043, 3356, 4435 `handle_config_reload`, and tests 6155/6175/6213) plus the headless composite path at :974-977 — decide there explicitly whether `phux capture` does a one-shot peer sweep or renders zones 1/3 empty, and encode the choice in a comment. Extract `pub(super) fn switch_session_args(name: &str, window: usize, pane: usize) -> BTreeMap<String, toml::Value>` out of `fleet.rs::foreign_pane_row` (:378-396) so the sidebar and the fleet dashboard cannot drift on how a cross-session target is addressed. Guard the repaint budget: the projection must compare EQUAL when nothing user-visible changed, or `refresh_window_chrome`'s `changed` return lies and the strip repaints forever against the ADR-0029 accumulator. Tests in sidebar_zones.rs: `a_peers_blocked_agent_outranks_a_local_working_one`, `the_roster_rolls_a_peer_session_into_one_histogram`, `a_satellite_session_reports_unknown_not_zero`, `an_unchanged_projection_does_not_report_a_change`.
close_reason: Landed; cross-session queue + roster projected and wired through the chrome refresh.

title: Stage 5: Live peer layout and agent subscriptions
description:
Stage 5 of 9 in the fleet-inbox sidebar chain (epic phux-k0cw).

COMMIT SUBJECT
  feat(client): keep peer session layout and agent records live

FILES
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/fleet.rs

VALIDATION
  cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'binary_id(phux-client) & (test(foreign) | test(peer))' && just ci
design: Zero new wire surface — two existing verbs on keys the client already reads. Rename `request_foreign_layouts` (:3766) to `sync_foreign_layout_subscriptions(conn, sessions, focused, next_request_id, pending, subscribed: &mut HashSet<SessionId>)`: keep the per-peer `GetMetadata { Scope::Group(DEFAULT_GROUP_ID), layout_key(s.id) }` and add `SubscribeMetadata { same scope, same key }` once per session, guarded by `subscribed` (there is no UNSUBSCRIBE_METADATA verb — docs/spec/L3.md:103 — so this is send-once bookkeeping, not teardown). Send the SUBSCRIBE even when the GET answers `None`: a peer that has not persisted a layout yet is exactly the one whose first SET matters. Rename `request_foreign_agents` (:3825) to `sync_foreign_agent_subscriptions`: keep the per-leaf GET, add `SubscribeMetadata { Scope::Terminal(id), TERMINAL_AGENT_KEY }`, add the `if !id.is_local() { continue; }` satellite skip that `sync_agent_meta_subscriptions` already has at :4283-4285 (without it every sweep earns UNSUPPORTED_SATELLITE_ROUTE refusals that the :2620-2632 intercept silently swallows), and track `foreign_agent_subscribed: HashSet<TerminalId>`. Extend `prune_foreign_agents` (:3885) to also prune `foreign_agent_subscribed` and the Stage-3 `foreign_attention` set to the live foreign-leaf union, and call it on the push-shaped folds as well as the GET-reply intercept at :2572. Move the peer sweep to AFTER the first paint at bootstrap (:1953) so a session switch — which tears down every server-side subscription (`crates/phux-server/src/state/client.rs:305`) and rebuilds every driver local from empty — does not put N session + M pane frames on the critical path of the switch. Update fleet.rs's module doc (:11-34), which currently states the retired design verbatim ("No subscription — a one-shot read", "Foreign rows therefore carry no asked flag"); the asked-flag half is now available, branch/cwd still are not (no foreign PaneSlot, and CwdChanged is dropped for unknown terminals). Tests, built on Stage 4: `peer_layout_keys_are_subscribed_not_just_read` (assert `ScriptedServer::run()`'s returned frame list contains `SubscribeMetadata { Group(1), "phux.tui.layout/v1/<peer>" }` and a per-foreign-leaf Terminal subscribe), `a_pushed_peer_layout_refolds_the_foreign_cache`, `satellite_panes_are_never_subscribed`.
close_reason: Landed; peer layout + agent keys subscribed, satellites skipped, bookkeeping pruned.

title: Stage 4: Key-targeted pushes in the scripted server
description:
Stage 4 of 9 in the fleet-inbox sidebar chain (epic phux-k0cw).

COMMIT SUBJECT
  test(client): let the scripted server gate a push on its own subscription key

FILES
  - crates/phux-client/src/testkit.rs

VALIDATION
  cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'binary_id(phux-client) & test(testkit)' && just check
design: Stage 5's assertions are untestable without this. `ScriptedServer::run` (:427) currently releases the whole pushed script on the FIRST `SubscribeMetadata` frame regardless of key (`script_needs_metadata_subscription`, :371, consumed at :445-449) — a test written against it would pass against a client that subscribed to the WRONG key. Add `pub fn push_after_subscribe(self, scope: Scope, key: impl Into<String>, frames: Vec<FrameKind>) -> Self` to the script builder and a `HashSet<(Scope, String)>` of satisfied subscriptions in `run()`'s send loop; a keyed push is released only once its exact (scope, key) pair has been seen. Keep the existing unkeyed behaviour for every current script so no in-tree test changes. Preserve the module's stated contract (:1-19): the harness owns frame order, the test supplies payloads — do not let this become a per-test fake. New test: `a_keyed_push_waits_for_its_own_subscription`.
close_reason: Landed as d135c3a7 plus lint follow-up; keyed pushes proven by a_keyed_push_waits_for_its_own_subscription.

title: Stage 3: Foreign metadata routing guard (blocking prerequisite)
description:
Stage 3 of 9 in the fleet-inbox sidebar chain (epic phux-k0cw).

COMMIT SUBJECT
  fix(client): route peer layout and agent metadata away from local state

FILES
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs
  - crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs

VALIDATION
  cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'binary_id(phux-client) & (test(layout_key) | test(foreign))' && just ci
design: Behaviour-neutral today (nothing subscribes a peer key yet) and mandatory before Stage 5. server_frame.rs: replace `fn is_layout_key(scope, key) -> bool` (:1777) with `fn layout_key_session(scope: &Scope, key: &str) -> Option<Option<SessionId>>` returning `Some(None)` for the bare legacy `phux.tui.layout/v1` and `Some(Some(id))` for a `/<session>` suffix; thread the client's own `focused_session: Option<SessionId>` into `handle_server_frame` and adopt the payload through `reconcile_loaded_workspace_checked` (:1265-1290) ONLY when the parsed session is the own session or the key is the bare legacy form. Add `FrameOutcome` fields `foreign_layout: Option<(SessionId, Option<Vec<u8>>)>`, `foreign_agent: Option<(TerminalId, Option<Vec<u8>>)>`, `foreign_attention: Option<TerminalId>`, `foreign_pane_set_dirty: bool`, and emit a non-matching layout broadcast through `foreign_layout` instead of adopting it. Gate the `MetadataChanged` agent branch (:1238-1252) and the `MetadataValue` agent branch (:1177-1188) on `panes.contains_key(&terminal)`; route the miss to `foreign_agent` so a foreign record never enters the LOCAL `AgentMetaIndex` (where `sync_agent_meta_subscriptions`'s `records.retain(|id,_| pane_ids.contains(id))` at driver.rs:4267 would silently evict it). Route the `AgentEvent::Asked` else-branch (:1594-1615) to `foreign_attention`, and split `PaneSpawned`/`PaneClosed` for an unknown `TerminalId` out of the catch-all Event arm (:1659) into `foreign_pane_set_dirty`. driver.rs: add a `foreign_attention: HashSet<TerminalId>` local beside the four caches at :1824-1836 and fold the four new outcome fields in the batch loop using the existing, already-correct `apply_foreign_layout_reply` (:3791) and `apply_foreign_agent_reply` folds; raise BOTH `repaint.raise_chrome()` and `repaint.raise_fleet()` (today lines 2588/2605 raise fleet only, so a foreign push repaints nothing unless the fleet modal is open — `refresh_fleet_if_open` returns `NotPublished` at :3941). Tests in server_frame.rs: `a_peer_layout_broadcast_leaves_the_local_workspace_untouched` (a `MetadataChanged { Group(1), "phux.tui.layout/v1/<other>" }` must leave `*workspace` and `*focused_pane` byte-identical and set `foreign_layout`), `the_bare_legacy_layout_key_is_still_adopted`, and `a_foreign_agent_record_push_stays_out_of_the_local_index`.
close_reason: Landed as 7af503ef; 1013/1013 phux-client.

title: Correct current capability documentation drift

title: Build provider-neutral session inspector
description: Unify lifecycle, search, history, notices/signals, transcript evidence, reconnect state, and provider metadata behind a progressively disclosed session inspector. Resting chrome remains calm.
acceptance_criteria: One inspector presents provider-neutral state without leaking internal structs; keyboard and accessibility paths work; absent capabilities are represented honestly.

title: Preserve completed-run terminal evidence
description: Preserve completed-run terminal transcript and replay evidence as artifacts in the durable event/evidence plane. Do not reuse the Native SDK record/replay test journal as the product store. Ordinary process exit may close presentation without destroying bounded inspectable evidence.
design: Live ingestion and historical projection are separate from side-effect replay. Evidence has schema version, provenance, integrity, retention, redaction, crash recovery, and migration semantics. Dead panes are not retained as permanent husks.
acceptance_criteria: Completed work leaves bounded inspectable evidence linked to stable lineage; replay integrity and cleanup are tested; terminal exit behavior stays immediate.
notes: Blocked after Phux ADR-0092 and Cockpit #51 until the corresponding phux-ajxq coordinator protocol, event authority, terminal binding, evidence, and client/FFI contracts ship. Cockpit may implement only the projection/interaction side; do not recreate authoritative IDs, evidence, Signals, policy state, or execution.

title: Two sessions shared one git worktree; branch flipped mid-build
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-12 while doing phux-cockpit-2ml.2.

The worktree .claude/worktrees/rosy-purring-pretzel was handed to this session as 'your own git worktree'. It was not. Over roughly one hour it was observed on four different states without this session touching git: feat/osc8-hyperlinks (dirty, with a fix commented out and a 'RED RUN' marker left in src/cockpit/update.zig), fix/phux-extension-write-deadline at 5bccbd2, then feat/osc8-hyperlinks-clean at 4a7f6eb.

Two concrete harms, both measured:

1. A guard-red-run.sh invocation started at 5bccbd2 and finished at 4a7f6eb. The run was internally consistent - green baseline, break applied, named test red, restored - and it recorded 'red: at 4a7f6eb', a commit whose tree it had only partly used. Test totals differed between the two trees (382 vs 396), so the runs genuinely straddled two codebases.

2. The recording step captured 'git diff' for the whole tree and swept up a build.zig.zon edit repointing native_sdk at .zig-cache/pinned-sdk-patched - the OTHER session's local SDK pin. The subsequent restore ('git checkout -- .') then discarded it.

This is the same failure class as phux-cockpit-2ml.11 (a build that ran in a sibling worktree) but worse: the exit code, the source-root line, AND the working directory were all correct. Only the commit moved.

Mitigations landed in ff16fa2: guard-red-run.sh re-reads HEAD at the end and records nothing if it moved; --record takes explicit paths; every restore is narrowed to the patch's own paths instead of 'git checkout -- .'.

What is NOT fixed: whatever hands out worktrees can hand the same one to two sessions. Work for phux-cockpit-2ml.2 was completed in a private worktree created by hand at scratchpad/guards-exclusive.

comments.author: phall
comments.text:
Hit again on 2026-08-15, same shape, from a fresh subagent's point of view.

Given .claude/worktrees/rosy-purring-pretzel, on integrate/render-instruments with a clean tree at session start. Partway in, `git status` showed ~1200 lines of tracked modifications across 9 files I had never touched (theme overrides, settings tests, tab_strip_tests), mtimes 55 seconds old, and `git worktree list` reported the worktree's branch as fix/settings-fg-override -- another session had run `checkout -b` inside it. Four `.dev-run-*` homes (b3l, fgover, tabfix, tabstrip) and two nested worktrees (iso-readonly-config, later verify-readonly) had appeared under it.

Cost: nothing was lost, but committing was impossible (a per-path commit would have swept up a neighbour's work) and `guard-red-run.sh` refuses a dirty tree by design, so the whole guard ritual was blocked. Worked around by creating a private nested worktree at .../rosy-purring-pretzel/tablabel on my own branch.

Two smaller symptoms of the same thing, both already predicted by phux-cockpit-2ml.10 and worth adding to it:
- `dev_app_wait_named` correctly refused to proceed because `pgrep -x phux-cockpit-dev` resolved to two pids (mine and a neighbour's). The automation dropbox is fine -- it resolves against the app CWD, so it is per-worktree -- only ACTIVATION BY NAME is ambiguous. Driving by `System Events ... first process whose unix id is <pid>` is a working alternative that does not disturb the neighbour.
- A detached dev app was terminated mid-run by something outside the session (graceful "stop"/"window_closed" in app.log, ~2s after the last frame), losing an in-progress capture.

title: Another swarm wrote source and ran the dev app inside a sibling's worktree
description: Observed 2026-08-12 from .claude/worktrees/rosy-purring-pretzel while working phux-cockpit-ix6. This is phux-cockpit-2ml.11's failure class in the OPPOSITE direction: not my build running in someone else's tree, but someone else's edits landing in mine. Sequence, all verifiable from the logs: (1) 'zig build test' at 18:1x returned exit=0 with 'source root:' correctly naming this worktree; (2) after committing a docs-only change (fe05793, two .md files, git diff --name-only confirms), the SAME command returned exit=1 with 'src/terminal/palette.zig:94:9: error: use of undeclared identifier probeLowContrast' and, on two other steps, 'src/terminal/palette.zig:1:1: error: file contents changed during update'. git status then showed 'M src/terminal/palette.zig' - a file this session never opened for writing - plus untracked .dev-run/, scripts/dev-run.sh, scripts/lib/ and scripts/zon-dep-url.sh. WHY IT MATTERS: the exit code and the source-root line were both TRUE and still described work this session did not do. The verdict block added for 2ml.11 does not catch this, because the tree it names IS the right tree - it is the tree's CONTENTS that are foreign. 'file contents changed during update' is the only signal, and it only appears when the race is tight enough to land mid-compile; a foreign edit that settles before the build starts is completely silent and would be attributed to whoever runs the gate next. ALSO: .dev-run/ is untracked rather than gitignored, so it dirties any status in the tree it lands in. WANTED: agents must not write into a worktree they were not assigned; and consider whether the verdict block can additionally report whether the tree is dirty and in which paths, so a run states not just WHICH tree but WHAT STATE of it produced the exit code.

title: One command to build and run the app without clashing with the installed one
description: The owner spent three days reporting a rendering bug against /Applications/Phux Cockpit.app (0.7.1, built 2026-08-09) while main was 0.8.0: nothing merged in three days had ever been in front of them. Wanted: scripts/dev-run.sh, one command, builds and launches the app with a distinct bundle identity, a distinct PROCESS NAME (pgrep -x and System Events target by name - see phux-cockpit-2ml.10), and isolated config/state/automation dropbox.
notes:
LANDED (not closed; parent verifies). scripts/dev-run.sh, scripts/lib/dev-app.sh, scripts/dev-isolation-check.sh, README + AGENTS.md. Commits 6d98e00, a76dbdf, 9b28bc0, b2bec7b on work/next.

MECHANISMS (all measured, not reasoned): bundle id and executable name come from app.zon via zig build package, and the pinned SDK has no bundle-id build option, so dev_app_stage rewrites the packaged bundle's Info.plist and renames Contents/MacOS/phux-cockpit to phux-cockpit-dev. That moves LaunchServices (lsappinfo reports dev.phux.cockpit.dev), the Dock/menu name, pgrep -x and System Events. Config and state are the PHUX_COCKPIT_CONFIG/STATE seams; the automation dropbox has no env seam at all (SDK opens .zig-cache/native-sdk-automation relative to CWD) so the run chdirs into .dev-run/.

EVIDENCE: dev-isolation-check.sh runs the installed 0.7.1 and the dev build simultaneously - pgrep -x resolves each name to exactly the pid launched, lsappinfo reports two bundle ids, System Events lists both names. Red run with the rewrite disabled: 5 failures including 'pgrep -x phux-cockpit -> 85900 85901' and 'System Events sees: phux-cockpit phux-cockpit'.

STILL SHARED, documented in README: ~/Library/Application Support/dev.phux.cockpit/State/windows.zon and ~/Library/Logs/dev.phux.cockpit/native-sdk.jsonl, because the SDK keys those off the bundle id COMPILED IN from app.zon, which a plist rewrite cannot reach. Nothing reads windows.zon back (restore_state=false).

OBSERVED DURING THE WORK: the user's real ~/Library/Application Support/Phux Cockpit/State/workspace.state changed during one run while an unexplained third phux-cockpit pid, which this session did not launch, was live. Not reproduced in four later runs. Consistent with a concurrent unisolated launch from another session in the same worktree - i.e. the exact hazard this work removes.
close_reason: Already completed on main or pinned dependency; reconciled against commits, guards, and current source on 2026-08-18

title: A subagent build can silently run in another worktree
description: Discovered 2026-08-12. A subagent working in its own git worktree had a 'zig build test' run SILENTLY EXECUTE in the parent session's worktree (.claude/worktrees/rosy-purring-pretzel) instead of its own. The exit code was real; it just described someone else's code. The agent only noticed because a LATER run was starved for 30 minutes by an orphaned build runner holding the Zig cache lock, which made it look closely - so the failure mode is silent by default and was caught by luck. This is the same class as an assertion that cannot fail: a green result that does not describe the thing you changed. It is worse than that class in one way, because nothing about the output distinguishes it - a correct-looking exit 0 from the wrong tree is indistinguishable from a correct one. WANTED: a build-level guard, so this cannot depend on discipline. Options to weigh: have build.zig record and print the resolved source root in the verdict block that phux-cockpit-2ml.1 already added, so every test run states which tree it compiled; and/or give each worktree an isolated Zig global cache so a shared cache lock cannot make one worktree's build starve or serve another's. The verdict block is the cheap half and it already exists - printing the source root there costs nothing and makes the failure visible in every future log. ALSO SEEN alongside: orphaned zig build runners outliving their session and holding the cache lock for 30+ minutes.
notes:
ISOLATED CACHE HALF LANDED on branch fix/2ml11-isolated-zig-cache (bc21754,
6810ba4), worktree .../scratchpad/wt-a. NOT pushed, no PR.

MECHANISM, measured rather than assumed. Zig 0.16 already materializes
dependency SOURCE per build root into zig-pkg/ (528-693 MB, per worktree,
today). What the global cache still holds for a full `zig build test` here is
45 MB - b 28K, h 132K, o 3.1M (one libcompiler_rt.a), z 41M - plus p/, the
793 MB package download cache. So the choice is not "private everything vs
share everything": it is which of those two to share. Design picked: private
b/h/o/z/tmp per worktree, p/ shared by symlink. p/ is immutable,
content-addressed, hash-verified, written once by an atomic rename, never
produced under a long-held lock. Cost measured with `zig build --fetch=all`
into a fresh worktree: fully private 16s + 172 MB downloaded; private with p/
shared 7s + 0 bytes. An offline machine cannot make the first one at all.

STARVATION REPRODUCED (this was the guess that needed testing). A cache entry
is guarded by an exclusive flock on <global cache>/h/<hash>.txt. Those
manifests are project-independent: a hello-world and this repo write the SAME
one, h/19941dd10bf085611a6d575c4f038f22.txt. With a sleeping process holding
that lock:
  shared cache, lock held      blocked, killed at 45s (exit 124)
  isolated cache, lock held    exit 0 in 3s
  shared cache, lock released  exit 0 in 1s
The third line is what makes the first two mean anything.

CORRECTION TO THE BEAD: ordinary concurrency does NOT starve on its own. Two
worktrees built concurrently on the SHARED cache and both finished normally
(A 46s exit 0, B 17s exit 1). Isolation removes the CHANNEL; the channel only
bites when something is stuck holding the lock - i.e. an orphaned runner.
Saying "two worktrees on one cache starve each other" would overclaim.

THE OUTSTANDING DEMONSTRATION IS DONE. Two worktrees, isolated caches, same
second start (both t0=1786580645), overlapping windows:
  wt-a  exit 0  47s  verdict: source root .../wt-a, global cache
        .../wt-a/.zig-global-cache (worktree-private)
  wt-b  exit 1  20s  compile error in src/tests/wtb_marker_tests.zig, a file
        that exists only in wt-b
They DISAGREED while running at the same time, which is the point: a served
result could not have disagreed. Sequential cold baseline was 51s, so wt-a's
47s under concurrency shows no starvation either.

ORPHANS. Real specimen found live while working: pid 65004, ppid 1, now 2h51m
old, a build runner in .claude/worktrees/agent-a022f379ec5728412 whose session
is gone, with a child test binary spinning 100% CPU inside
terminal_registry_tests.zig:171. Nothing is left to read its exit code.
`./scripts/zig-build.sh --list-orphans` reports it. NOT killed - the tool
reports other trees' orphans and only reaps its own, on purpose. Someone with
authority over that worktree should kill 65004.

ALSO FOUND, worth its own bead: .claude/worktrees/rosy-purring-pretzel is
being mutated by more than one session at once. During this work its branch
moved (feat/osc8-hyperlinks -> feat/osc8-hyperlinks-clean), its dirty file
changed from src/cockpit/update.zig to src/terminal/session.zig a minute
later, scripts/ gained and lost files, and a git worktree got created INSIDE
its .zig-cache. A build there produced an error referencing
src/tests/flattened_probe_tests.zig, a file present in no commit and on no
disk. I nearly reported that as "the private global cache breaks the build";
it was a concurrent edit. No A/B taken in that tree is trustworthy, which is
why everything above was measured in fresh worktrees.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not PREVENT a wrong-tree run for someone typing
plain `zig build test`. The wrapper refuses when your shell is in a different
checkout than the tree it would build, and build.zig now prints the resolved
global cache beside the source root so a non-wrapper run still says in its own
log that it was exposed - but the cwd mistake itself is only made visible, not
impossible.
close_reason: Integrated onto main in the sweep at caea926

title: Raise the pty ceiling: cockpit is capped at 4 concurrent shells by the SDK
description:
phux-cockpit-pg1 traced the empty-pane bug to a hard capacity mismatch: the pinned SDK's effects layer keeps ONE fixed pty table for the whole process, native_sdk.max_effect_ptys = 4 (.zig-cache/pinned-sdk/src/runtime/effects.zig:942, 'One live terminal surface plus a background job or two is the realistic shape; a fifth spawn is refused loudly'). Cockpit is a MULTIPLEXER. Its UI advertises 16 tabs x 16 panes x 5 windows.

pg1's fix makes the refusal honest (cmd+T/cmd+D/cmd+N now refuse at the ceiling with a visible '4 SHELL LIMIT' badge instead of opening a permanently blank pane). It does NOT raise the ceiling, because the ceiling lives in the SDK.

Consequences shipped by that fix, all deliberate:
- 5 windows (max_windows) is now unreachable - the 5th cmd+N has no shell to put in it, so it does not open.
- A restored workspace snapshot with more than 4 local leaves is refused whole and falls back to a fresh single-terminal workspace.

The real fix is upstream in the SDK fork (phall1/native): raise max_effect_ptys, or make the pty table per-window / dynamically sized. Verified 2026-08-12 against the shipped bundle: four cmd+T from a fresh workspace leave Terminal 5 at SPAWN REJECTED.
notes: Committed d50e816 on worktree branch worktree-agent-a022f379ec5728412 (worktree: .claude/worktrees/agent-a022f379ec5728412), on top of cherry-picked 80e97ca (pg1). SDK patch: docs/sdk-patches/raise-pty-ceiling.patch (max_effect_ptys 4->32 + comptime pty-table budget). build.zig.zon still pins the tarball, so the two capability tests (registry-to-max_tabs, sixth-window) SKIP via support.requireLiveShells until the pin moves; both were watched failing against the unpatched pin (355 pass, 5 skip, 2 fail). Proof: scripts/drive-shell-ceiling.sh --want 16 -> exit 1 stopped at 4 unpatched (badge reads 4), exit 0 with 16 tabs and 0 SPAWN REJECTED patched. Nothing committed to the SDK fork; no PR opened. NOT closing - needs the fork pushed and the pin bumped.

title: GPU composite mode refuses cell_grid, degrading Cockpit to the reference renderer
description:
NATIVE_SDK_GPU_SHOT_DIR is the SDK's only path from real GPU pixels to a PNG (appkit_host.m:5132-5155, a getBytes readback of the composited canvas texture). It needs no TCC, no focus and no visible window, so it is the natural basis for a real-frame capture in CI.

It is unreachable for this app. The dump only fires from the GPU composite pass (appkit_host.m:5030), gated on NATIVE_SDK_GPU_COMPOSITE=1, and that pass refuses any command whose kind is not in its known-kind list at appkit_host.m:4714-4716. cell_grid is not in that list, and a Cockpit terminal frame is nothing but cell_grid commands.

Measured, same pane both runs:
  composite unset -> gpu_present_path=packet
  composite=1     -> gpu_present_path=pixels, present_fallback=missing_service, present_fallback_frames=147, shots written 0

So composite mode does not capture the real rasterizer, it REPLACES it: every packet present is refused and the runtime falls back to the CPU pixels path, which is the deterministic reference renderer. An app running with composite on looks exactly like its own screenshots.

Fix is in the SDK fork (phall1/native, branch cockpit/v0.8.4): add cell_grid to the composite known-kind list, and make the composite scratch path handle it the way the CPU raster cache already does (cell_grid is already raster-cacheable per appkit_host.m:3198). That would both fix the degradation and unlock NATIVE_SDK_GPU_SHOT_DIR as a TCC-free real-pixel capture for CI.

Guard added meanwhile: scripts/automate-smoke.sh now asserts gpu_present_path=packet. Verified failing (exit=1) under composite=1 and passing otherwise.

See docs/RENDER_FIDELITY.md section 2.
close_reason: Integrated on local main with pinned Native 87917c4; full Cockpit gate passed with Phux provider compiled

comments.author: phall
comments.text:
CONFIRMED as filed, then fixed in a sandbox and demonstrated.

Reproduction (packaged bundle, publisher_pid checked against the launched pid
both runs, isolated config/state):
  composite unset  gpu_present_path=packet  present_fallback=none
  composite=1      gpu_present_path=pixels  present_fallback=missing_service  shots=0

Mechanism confirmed by removing exactly one condition. Patch:
docs/sdk-patches/composite-cell-grid.patch, on branch
feat/composite-cell-grid-capture, commit 1f57a50.

Hunk 1: cell_grid joins the composite pass's known-kind list
(appkit_host.m:4714-4716). Nothing else was needed - both CG paths the pass
uses (rasterCacheBuildEntryForCommand:, compositeScratchTextureForCommand:)
already dispatch through NativeSdkPacketDrawCommandBody, whose cell_grid branch
has existed since the kind did, and NativeSdkPacketCommandRasterCacheable
already returns YES for it. The bead's "make the composite scratch path handle
it" turned out to be already true. With only the gate changed:
  composite=1, patched  gpu_present_path=packet  present_fallback=none  shots=3

Hunk 2 (not in the bead, measured into scope): the dump's fixed every-30th-
present cadence becomes NATIVE_SDK_GPU_SHOT_EVERY (default 30, unchanged when
unset). NATIVE_SDK_GPU_DRAW_TRACE=1 measures three composite presents in
thirty seconds on a settled pane, so present 30 never arrives and present 1 is
the empty first frame: the stock cadence writes one blank PNG per run. Watched

title: phux extension.zig tests have never run; rooting them hangs forever
description:
DISCOVERED 2026-08-12 while wiring phux-cockpit-2ml.1 (zig build test now roots the phux modules as test artifacts).

Zig runs tests only from a compilation's ROOT module. src/providers/phux/extension.zig has only ever been IMPORTED (by provider.zig, via the phux_extension module), never rooted. So its 6 tests have never executed anywhere - not locally, not in CI, not under -Dphux-enabled=true. The same was true of transport.zig (5 tests), provider.zig (4) and pointer.zig (4); build.zig only ever added a test artifact for host.zig.

transport, provider and pointer are now rooted and pass. extension is NOT, because rooting it hangs the build indefinitely.

MEASURED: phux-extension-tests, pid 13993, ran 11m28s at 0.0% CPU in state S before being killed. macOS `sample` of the hung process:

  main (start.zig:663)
    test_runner.mainServer (test_runner.zig:140)
      extension.test.a non-reading peer cannot hold one frame writer forever (extension.zig:486)
        extension.writeExact (extension.zig:239)

extension.zig:239 is `const rc = std.c.send(fd, input[offset..].ptr, input.len - offset, flags);`

DIAGNOSIS. writeExact has a 1-second deadline, but it is evaluated at the TOP of the send loop only:

    if (elapsed_ns >= std.time.ns_per_s) return false;
    ...
    const rc = std.c.send(fd, ..., flags);

The deadline is therefore never reached if send() itself blocks. flags include MSG.DONTWAIT (Darwin 0x80, present as a decl so the `comptime @hasDecl` guard passes), but macOS does not honour MSG_DONTWAIT on an AF_UNIX socketpair - only O_NONBLOCK on the fd does. The test creates a socketPair(), shrinks SNDBUF to 4096, and sends 16MB with nobody reading, so send() blocks forever and the deadline code is unreachable.

The test's name states the invariant it is checking: 'a non-reading peer cannot hold one frame writer forever'. On macOS that invariant is FALSE, and this is the first time anything has evaluated it. Note the neighbouring test at extension.zig:469 calls configureSocket() first, but configureSocket only sets SO_NOSIGPIPE - it does not set O_NONBLOCK either.

This is a production concern for the extension lane, not only a test bug: any writeExact against a blocking fd whose peer stops reading blocks the caller forever despite the deadline.

TO REPRODUCE: add extension back to the `rooted` list in addPhuxGraphTests in build.zig (and to phux_test_module_names beside it), then run zig build test with the phux client FFI discoverable.

FIX DIRECTION: either set O_NONBLOCK in configureSocket and call it from every writeExact path, or make the deadline enforceable by poll()ing for POLLOUT with a computed remaining-time timeout before each send rather than after.
notes:
VERIFIED AND FIXED (not closed; parent verifies). Commit 8273b93 on branch
fix/phux-extension-write-deadline-iwf, based on origin/main 5bccbd2.

DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY, not taken on faith. scripts/measure-send-blocking.c
(added in this commit) on macOS 25.5/arm64, AF_UNIX socketpair, SNDBUF 4096,
16 MiB payload, peer never reads:

  blocking fd + MSG_DONTWAIT    still inside send() when a 5s alarm fired
  O_NONBLOCK fd                 EAGAIN after 0.000s, 4096 bytes written
  blocking fd + SO_SNDTIMEO=1s  EAGAIN after 2.004s

Rooting extension.zig unfixed reproduced the hang exactly as described:
"5 pass, 1 crash", crash = 'a non-reading peer cannot hold one frame writer
forever', killed at 180s, build exit 137, no verdict line. sample(1) of the
hung pid: 1608/1608 samples in __sendto under extension.writeExact, 0.0% CPU,
state S -- the same stack recorded on this bead.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FIX DIRECTIONS ON THIS BEAD.

1. "poll() for POLLOUT with a computed remaining-time timeout BEFORE each send"
   would NOT have fixed this on its own. POLLOUT means "there is some room",
   not "room for all of it", and a blocking SOCK_STREAM send() does not return
   until the whole buffer is handed over. Measured: with an EMPTY 4096-byte
   send buffer, poll reports POLLOUT set, and the following blocking 16 MiB
   send() still sat in the kernel until the 5s alarm fired.

2. SO_SNDTIMEO was measured and REJECTED, not merely unchosen. Darwin overshoots
   it by a consistent 2.00x: 250ms -> 0.503s, 500ms -> 1.004s, 1s -> 2.004s,
   2s -> 4.004s. It would have turned writeExact's one-second budget into two
   seconds silently.

Also declined "set O_NONBLOCK in configureSocket": configureSocket is called on
only one path, and a descriptor left non-blocking leaks into readExact, which
treats any read error as a dead connection -- a benign EAGAIN would then tear
down a healthy session. writeExact now forces O_NONBLOCK for the duration of
the write and restores the mode it was handed; a new test pins that both ways.

RED PROOF for each new assertion (each disabled, observed failing, restored):
  - O_NONBLOCK forcing removed   -> hang, killed at 120s, exit 137
  - EAGAIN treated as fatal      -> lower bound fails at extension.zig:548, exit 1
  - mode restore removed         -> "expected false, found true" at :561, exit 1
Green with all three in place: exit 0, verdict "COMPILED AND TESTED (transport,
host, provider, pointer, extension)".

ENVIRONMENT GAP worth recording: /Users/phall/workspace/phux/target/ffi-release/
libphux_client_ffi.a did not exist, so the documented test command failed at
build.zig's FFI lookup before running anything. Built it with
`cargo build --locked --profile ffi-release -p phux-client-ffi` (45s, gitignored
target/ only, no source touched in that repo).
close_reason: Integrated onto main in the sweep at caea926; both build graphs, both executables, and a live app run are green

title: %name selectors resolve to nothing, but two consumer docs and ADR-0071 point 6 describe them as live surface
description:
VERIFIED IN THE TREE at origin/main 3c7a838a. Found by the phux-w7z2.1 ratification brief; I re-verified every claim below independently before filing.

crates/phux-client/src/selector.rs:320 --

    // Singular selector, set-valued seam: see this function's docs. Never
    // let `%name` reach `pick_target_pane`.
    Selector::Agent(_) => Vec::new(),

That arm is DELIBERATE and correct in isolation: %name is singular and must not flow through the set-valued path, because a partial AgentIndex would turn a real ambiguity into a confident single match. The intended path is resolve_agent (read-only verbs) / resolve_agent_for_input (send-keys, paste, signal, run), both of which are written, documented and unit-tested, and both of which correctly refuse a partial index.

THE DEFECT: nothing calls them. 'grep -rn resolve_agent crates' outside their own module returns exactly three hits and ALL THREE ARE COMMENTS --

  crates/phux/src/commands/mod.rs:2441   (a comment saying it resolves through resolve_agent)
  crates/phux/src/selector.rs:17         (a doc comment)
  crates/phux/src/selector.rs:18         (a doc comment)

So every %name on every verb falls to the Vec::new() arm and is reported as an ordinary selector miss. The machinery exists, is tested, and is unreachable.

WHY THIS IS A 1.0 BLOCKER RATHER THAN AN ORDINARY GAP -- three published surfaces already promise it:

  docs/consumers/agents.md:714 -- lists %name in the selector grammar and documents its semantics ('never matches detector-default kind names and refuses ambiguity rather than choosing among duplicate declarations')
  docs/consumers/mcp.md:131 -- lists %name among the TARGET forms
  ADR-0071 point 6 -- freezes '%name selectors over explicit names only' as part of the agent surface the 1.0 release commits to

Freezing a surface that returns nothing is the worst of both: consumers script against a documented form, get a miss, and the contract says the behaviour is now stable.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF A KNOWN CLASS in this repo -- an ADR documents a mechanism that was never wired up. phux-0d92 (ADR-0081 claimed pairing needed no restart; the credential set was frozen at startup) and phux-pimp (ADR-0080 claimed a deliberate stop stays stopped; there was no stop verb) were the same shape and both shipped as P0/P1 bugs. The difference here is that this one is inside the 1.0 freeze list.

RESOLUTION -- exactly one of:
  (a) land phux-w7z2.3 (Implement ADR-0075: %name agent addressing in the selector grammar) before the freeze, wiring the verbs to resolve_agent / resolve_agent_for_input; or
  (b) remove %name from docs/consumers/agents.md, docs/consumers/mcp.md and ADR-0071 point 6 until it works.

Do NOT freeze it as-is. Note phux-w7z2.3 is currently blocked on phux-w7z2.1 (ratification), so if ratification slips, (b) is the honest fallback and must not be forgotten.

RELATED, from the same brief and not yet independently verified by me: fetch_agent_index returns a bare HashMap with no complete/partial bit, so ADR-0075 point 3's exit-3 refusal has no source of truth; and the shipped Claude shim writes --name claude --kind claude, which would make ZERO panes %-addressable out of the box even once (a) lands, because %name deliberately never matches detector-default kind names.
notes: Taking the bead-approved honest fallback while ADR-0075 remains Proposed: remove %name from shipped working-surface promises and mark it reserved/fail-closed; keep parser/resolver machinery dormant for later ratification.
close_reason: Removed %name from active CLI/MCP/root-help/skill/1.0 promises; documented it as parser-reserved and fail-closed until proposed ADR-0075 is accepted; kept dormant resolver machinery.

title: Accept or reject ADR-0071: 1.0 cannot be cut against a Proposed commitment
description:
ADR-0071 'What phux 1.0 commits to' has been Status: Proposed since 2026-08-07. It is the only written definition of what a phux 1.0 means, and every other 1.0 gate in the tracker derives from it — yet nothing tracks ratifying it, so the release definition has no owner and no close condition.

Backwards derivation from the ADR's own text shows most of its hard preconditions are ALREADY MET:

- Point 3, one-command update path: shipped (phux update, phux-1c51 closed).
- Point 3, unbypassable HELLO version gate: shipped (crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs:1080; phux-0vp and phux-j4on closed).
- Point 4, overdue deprecated-spelling removals: done. crates/phux/src/deprecations.rs DEPRECATED is empty; the rows went in v0.12.1.
- Point 4, dead pub surface in the publishable phux-protocol crate: done by ADR-0072. policy.rs is down to PeerIdentity, TransportType and Capability, all three live.
- Point 7(b), phux_agent multiplexer frozen as ten distinct MCP tools: done. crates/phux-mcp/src/agent_tools.rs, with a test asserting bare phux_agent is now an unknown tool.
- Point 7(a), every stable error code in commands::json_err::codes: met in practice — 81 codes, and no call site outside json_err.rs invents a literal.

What is NOT met is the decision layer, and it is the whole remaining blocker:

- This ADR itself is Proposed.
- ADR-0075, ADR-0076 and ADR-0078 are Proposed (0077 is Accepted), so point 6's enumerated freeze cannot close and point 7(c) has nothing to amend into.

ACCEPTANCE: ADR-0071 reaches a terminal Status. If Accepted, point 6 is amended to whatever ADR-0075/0076/0078 ratification yields (see phux-w7z2.1, phux-w7z2.2), and the six already-met preconditions above are recorded as met in the ADR rather than left to be re-derived.
notes:
SEQUENCING NOTE 2026-08-15 (priority unchanged at P1).

Step 5 of the five-step fleet-inbox arc, and the adoption gate. Third parties cannot build against phux while nothing here is safe to build against; the competitor is iterating in the open at v0.8.0 with a plugin marketplace. Being first to a FROZEN, spec'd agent surface makes the durable moat the ecosystem rather than the feature set, because features get copied in a weekend and an integrated contract does not.

HARD DEPENDENCY, added today: do not cut the freeze while phux-w7z2.20 still claims a fleet-wide agent-state stream needs a wire change. That claim is contested (see that bead's notes) and the freeze must not be taken against a phantom wire requirement.

title: Cockpit uses none of the SDK's automation harness
description:
FINDING 2026-08-12. Before building anything: the harness we were about to invent already exists upstream, and it is good.

vercel-labs/native ships 'native automate' - a runtime control surface built for agents to drive:
- assert with POLLING regex, --timeout-ms and --absent, so no sleeps and failures print the missing pattern plus the snapshot tail
- widget-click / -hold / -context-press / -drag / -wheel / -key (modifier chords, real key_down+key_up) / -pinch
- snapshot, list, wait, reload, tray-action, bridge round-trips
- screenshot through the deterministic CPU reference renderer
- profile on/off, publishing rolling p50/p90/max per pipeline stage: rebuild, layout, reconcile, emit, a11y, plan, patch, encode, present, host_decode, host_draw
It is documented in skill-data/automation/SKILL.md as an agent-facing SKILL, 251 lines. There is also evals/ - 24 cases, scaffolded workspaces, sandboxed microVMs, deterministic graders plus an LLM judge - but that grades AGENTS AUTHORING APPS, not the SDK's or Cockpit's own internals.

Cockpit uses NONE of it. scripts/build-automation-cli.sh exists (it must build 'native' from the PINNED fork, because the automation dropbox is guarded by a protocol fingerprint that our fork's epoch bumps) - but CI never invokes it. CI today: null-platform tests, the phux-enabled graph, then package + soak launch/terminate cycles. No snapshot assertions, no widget driving, no profile capture.

That is why several beads are stuck on 'needs a human at the machine' when the tooling to answer them already exists:
- phux-cockpit-jw4 wants host_draw p50/p90 under load. 'native automate profile on' publishes exactly that.
- phux-cockpit-pg1 wants a snapshot taken while a LOCAL pane is visibly broken - pane rect, cols/rows, and the screen text the model holds. 'native automate snapshot' is that evidence.
- phux-cockpit-5cu wants a fullscreen transition actually observed against a bundled app that can take focus.

WANTED: a smoke lane in cockpit that builds the CLI from the pin, launches the app with -Dautomation=true, waits, asserts a known-good snapshot, drives a few chords, captures a profile, and fails loudly. Then wire the subset that survives without a GUI session into CI.

Caveat to design around, not ignore: widget-key silently no-ops when the app is not frontmost, which already produced one confidently wrong bisect (retracted in PR #22).

title: The reference renderer is structurally blind to the GPU path
description:
THE most expensive gap in this repo, measured in wasted diagnoses.

phux-cockpit-aht (all terminal text renders ~35% thin) survived THREE confident diagnoses over several days. The reason is structural, not incidental: automation screenshots render through the deterministic CPU reference renderer, which never touches CoreText and blends coverage itself. The defect lived in the AppKit host's CGBitmapContext configuration. No reference screenshot could ever show it - by construction.

The same blind spot is why the ligature decision (docs/DECISIONS.md) refuses per-renderer shaping: a divergence would be invisible in every screenshot while being wrong on real glass.

So the harness needs a THIRD thing, between 'reference screenshot' and 'look at it with your eyes':

A rasterizer-fidelity suite that exercises the REAL CoreText path headlessly, in the exact context configuration the host uses, and asserts on measured pixel statistics. scripts/measure-glyph-smoothing.m is the working prototype - it found the bug three greps could not. Generalize it:
- a small ObjC/Zig harness that renders known glyphs through the host's actual context setup
- asserts coverage/stem statistics against pinned values
- runs in CI, no window, no screen recording, no focus

This would have caught the smoothing regression the day it was introduced, and would catch its reintroduction.

Related: phux-cockpit-aht's own note says the fix is still unconfirmed ON GLASS, blocked on the macOS Screen Recording TCC gate.
notes:
Research + implementation landed as 6bc9f80 (worktree agent-aca5365bdb4f8942c). Full write-up: docs/RENDER_FIDELITY.md.

CONFIRMED the blindness, with file:line. automate screenshot -> flow.zig:944 -> publishAutomationScreenshot (flow.zig:1043) -> renderCanvasScreenshot (canvas_frame.zig:801, body :819) -> canvas.ReferenceRenderSurface (:843-849). Glyphs come from primitives/canvas/font_ttf.zig, a std-only TrueType outline parser, filled by a vector rasterizer in per-thread scratch (reference.zig:61-79). CoreText never runs on that path. Cockpit's real frames run gpu_present_path=packet, where appkit_host.m rasterizes with CoreText into CGBitmapContexts (:5256 cached raster, :5473 direct, :4569 composite scratch), all three setting CGContextSetShouldSmoothFonts.

Proof, not argument: rebuilt the app against a copy of the pinned SDK with the aht defect reintroduced. Different binaries (57ba94b9 defect / 8ed94141 fixed), byte-identical reference screenshot (sha256 6b4f3b582a7bbf926d0605f44bf9b7af1f07c84c86b61c6f84c4acba66fcd3d2), twice per run, on a fixed screen.

NO TCC-FREE CAPTURE OF THE APP'S REAL FRAMES EXISTS TODAY. CGWindowListCreateImage / CGDisplayCreateImage / ScreenCaptureKit / screencapture are all TCC-gated. cacheDisplayInRect and renderInContext do not read a Metal drawable. gpu_sample in the snapshot IS a real drawable readback (appkit_host.m:6337-6344) but is one centre pixel. NATIVE_SDK_GPU_SHOT_DIR (appkit_host.m:5132-5155) is the only real-pixel-to-PNG path and needs no TCC, but only fires from the composite pass, which refuses any kind outside appkit_host.m:4714-4716 - cell_grid is not there. Measured: composite=1 gives gpu_present_path=pixels, present_fallback=missing_service, 147 fallback frames, 0 shots. Filed phux-cockpit-g1z; fixing it there would unlock real-frame capture in CI.

BUILT scripts/host-raster-check.sh + scripts/measure-host-raster.m: #includes the pinned SDK's own appkit_host.m and rasterizes a terminal row through its real rasterCacheBuildEntryForCommand. Not a replica. Catches the defect the screenshot misses: cell_grid solid 4179 -> 3081 (-26.3%), exit 1 against --min-solid 4000, exit 0 on the pin. Baseline pinned in docs/RENDER_FIDELITY.md section 3.

STILL UNVERIFIED: the aht fix on glass. That needs a human to grant Screen Recording once; docs/RENDER_FIDELITY.md section 5 says what would then be automatable. The harness proves the rasterizer, not the composited frame.

CI wiring left open as phux-cockpit-9v1.
