title: Ratify ADR-0075/0076/0077/0078 as one agent-surface batch, with one owner for the overlaps
description:
ADR/0075-agent-name-addressing.md, ADR/0076-agent-prompt-and-lifecycle-wait.md and
ADR/0077-agent-read-surface.md were written in one run by three agents who did not
read each other. All three are Status: Proposed. They all add to the same `agent`
verb surface, and each names the others as an unresolved conflict. One owner has to
accept or reject them as a batch, because the overlaps are real:

- 0075 point 7 constrains input-delivering verbs against a `%name` target
  ("re-verify the pane still hosts the agent before writing bytes"); 0076 point 4
  specifies the same rule for `agent prompt` in different words. One owner, one
  wording, one place.
- 0075 conflict 2: it deliberately does NOT narrow docs/spec/L3.md 3.7's record
  `name` ("REQUIRED, non-empty", no charset), so `%`-addressability is a strictly
  smaller set than valid records. Narrowing the spec instead is a normative change
  plus a docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md entry, and it invalidates display names like
  "Claude Code". Decide which.
- 0076 conflict 2: `phux send-keys host/@N` works via ROUTE_INPUT relay but
  `agent prompt host/@N` cannot (APPLY_INPUT is local-only, ADR-0053). Accept the
  documented hole in ADR-0066's host namespace, or schedule federated acknowledged
  input (bead phux-2en already exists for that).
- 0076 conflict 3: `phux wait` already exists with Condition::{Contains, Idle}.
  `phux agent wait` is a second wait verb with a different data source. Confirm the
  split against ADR-0065's one-grammar principle, or fold it into
  `phux wait --until-agent-state`.
- 0077 conflict 1: the alternate-screen harvest contradicts docs/spec/L1.md 6.1's
  normative "no side effects" claim for GET_SCREEN. Accepting 0077 commits to a
  normative spec change.
- 0077 conflict 3: ADR-0046 point 8 (an explicit SET_METADATA outranks the
  detector) vs. 0077's idle gate for the harvest. 0077 chose to read the published
  record; confirm that over gating on the detector's own derivation.
- 0077 conflict 6: exit code for a refused harvest. crates/phux/src/exit_codes.rs
  defines EXIT_PARTIAL_VIEW = 3 narrowly as "resolved against a partial view of the
  fleet"; 0077 chose 2 (EXIT_USAGE, "or the server refused the request"). Confirm.

ACCEPTANCE: each ADR moves to Accepted or Rejected with the conflicts above
resolved in the text; ADR/README.md index rows updated (they were hand-added and
already carry curated annotations); the combined CLI delta handed to the ADR-0071
carve-out bead.
design:
RATIFICATION DECISIONS 2026-08-17 (autonomous run, evidence-backed). SPLIT THE BATCH THREE WAYS — do not ratify as one. Batching 0078 with the rest repeats exactly the mistake wave 2 corrected when it split 0078 out of 0077.

FIRST, A CORRECTION: ADR-0077 is ALREADY Accepted (ADR/0077:15). This is a three-ADR decision, not four. A 482-line ratification brief already exists at ADR/RATIFICATION-BRIEF-agent-surface.md.

VERDICTS
- ADR-0077: already Accepted, no action.
- ADR-0075: ACCEPT with three edits. It is a COMMITMENT TO BUILD, not a record of shipped behaviour — %name parses and is fully unit-tested, then resolves to nothing (selector.rs:317-319 returns Vec::new() with the comment 'Never let %name reach pick_target_pane'); resolve_agent, resolve_agent_for_input, AgentIndex and AgentResolveError have ZERO production callers and are not re-exported.
- ADR-0076: ACCEPT with two corrections. Its subject matter is entirely shipped and already carved into ADR-0071 point 6.
- ADR-0078: DEFER, leave Proposed.

CONFLICT 1 (duplicated re-verify rule) — KEEP THE SPLIT, do not merge. They stopped being duplicates in wave 2: 0075 point 5 is a SAFETY GATE reading the level (refuse when kind present and state unknown); 0076 point 4 is an IDENTITY COMPARISON (the shipped --expect-agent/--expect-kind check). The doctrine is already single-sourced and normative in docs/spec/L3.md 3.7 ('a safety gate MAY read the level, a completion gate MUST require an observed transition'). 0076 point 4 ALREADY cites 0075 point 5 by name and already states the circularity — the bead's open item 1 is stale. Merging would destroy the distinction that a safety gate may fire on a corpse while an identity comparison may not. EDITS: name the concrete verb set (agent send-keys, agent prompt, agent answer) instead of 'any ADR-0053 acknowledged-batch verb'; and ADD A SENTENCE saying the guard has no caller, because as written point 5 reads as a description of behaviour when it is a commitment.

CONFLICT 2 (name charset) — OPTION A, keep two grammars. Shipped-manifest evidence is decisive but NOT in the assumed direction: all five manifests (claude/codex/opencode/pi/omp) use bare lowercase single-word names that all satisfy the addressable grammar, so option B breaks no manifest — BUT every one of those names EQUALS ITS OWN KIND, which is exactly what 0075 point 4 refuses as AgentResolveError::KindConstant, and the Claude shim writes that shape explicitly (shim.rs:407 --name claude --kind claude). CONSEQUENCE: phux's own flagship integration yields ZERO %-addressable panes; %name is inert until a human runs 'phux agent set @N --name <chosen>'. Option B was rejected because it costs a THIRD thing nobody priced: a new refusal on 'phux agent set --name' (record.rs:38-41 validates non-empty-after-trim and nothing else), which is stable CLI surface owed a deprecations.rs cycle, spent immediately before the ADR-0071 freeze, to buy tidiness. SPEND THE DIFFERENCE ON THE ERROR MESSAGE instead: before reporting Unknown, scan for a live record differing only in excluded characters and name it. That is a message, not a field, so it adds nothing to the frozen document surface. ALSO write into point 7(a) that the Claude integration produces zero addressable panes. DEFECT TO FOLD IN: the addressable grammar is stated THREE times unsynchronized — selector.rs:237 (bound via AGENT_NAME_MAX_LEN:222), start.rs:214 (bound HARDCODED as 32), and the display string NAME_GRAMMAR at start.rs:124.

CONFLICT 3 (federation hole) — OPTION A, accept, but WIDEN the statement. The premise is one wave stale: as of 9b61a3c5 both verbs give a clean typed refusal. 'agent prompt host/@N' exits 2 with code satellite_target and a remedy, refused CLIENT-SIDE before a socket opens (agent_prompt.rs:847-851; test deliberately passes a nonexistent socket to prove it). 'agent wait host/@N' likewise (wait.rs:86-101). The brief's 'dangerous one' finding is stale. Option B rejected: phux-2en is P3/post-1.0/other-owner, and ADR-0053 point 7 already declined federated acknowledged input because it needs destination capability negotiation, destination-owned dedupe and server_id incarnation semantics across the hop — buying uniformity costs the idempotency guarantee that is the verb's entire point. THE FIX: 0076 point 1 states the narrow version; make it state the WIDE one — the hole is the whole agent surface, not one verb. send-keys/paste/signal/run reach host/@N; agent prompt/wait/show/explain/set/clear/list and %name are hub-local by construction. Filed separately: an e2e test for both verbs against a real relay, plus a satellite guard on handle_get_metadata (client.rs:2059 still silently returns value:None where handle_subscribe_metadata gained refuse_satellite_metadata_scope), so the lie is unreachable even if a CLI guard is removed.

CONFLICT 4 (two wait verbs) — KEEP THE SPLIT. ADR-0065 does not ask for folding: all seven of its decision points are about FLAG SPELLING, none about verb count, and its own remedy for a collision is a disambiguating noun, which 'agent' is. The verbs differ on every axis a caller branches on: data source (GET_SCREEN poll vs SUBSCRIBE_METADATA push + poll floor), condition domain (Contains/Matches/Idle vs closed idle|working|blocked|done), PREDICATE (level match vs observed-transition-only via EdgeTracker, which L3.md 3.7 REQUIRES of a completion gate and 13 tests pin), and exit codes. Shared code is ONE constant. DECISIVE on phux-w7z2.20: that bead's verdict is no-wire-change for 'agent wait --any', implemented as EdgeTracker becoming HashMap<TerminalId,EdgeTracker> — a fan-out of the edge tracker, which has NO analogue in phux wait. Folding would ACTIVELY COMPLICATE --any. Folding also costs a deprecation cycle on shipped surface immediately before the freeze and would break ADR-0071 point 7(b)'s ten-tool MCP freeze, which names phux_agent_wait. CORRECTIONS OWED TO 0076: --timeout is SECS not MS (agent/mod.rs:149-152, Duration::from_secs; ADR-0071 point 6 already says SECS, so the ADR is the wrong one). AND CLOSE bead item 3: the 'no shipped done writer' objection is DEAD — ADR-0085 (Accepted 2026-08-14) shipped REPORT_AGENT_STATE with a ServerFeature bit and the report-state verb, so done has a real producer. KEEP done in the default --until set.

CONFLICT 5 (GET_SCREEN side effects) — DEFER 0078, and there is NO live contradiction today. Wave 2 moved the harvest out of 0077 into 0078; 0077 as it stands makes no spec claim, no wire change and no PTY write, and request_transcript appears NOWHERE in crates/ or docs/ — only in 0078's prose. L1.md 6.1's 'no side effects' is CURRENTLY TRUE. Accepting 0078 commits to a FUTURE normative change (three sentences, one CHANGELOG row, no PROTOCOL_VERSION bump since the feature bit is additive per ADR-0061). A separate HARVEST_TRANSCRIPT verb would preserve the sentence but is REJECTED per 0078's own Alternatives: no retry identity, result is a screen not a receipt, and it needs its own role policy, capability bit, relay arm and CLI verb — a flag plus a PRIMARY clause buys the identical guarantee for one line. DEFER FOR THREE REASONS: (1) 0078's own Context says to capture live viewports before accepting, and that is UNDISCHARGED — rows per wheel notch, repaint settle time, merge seam; ADR-0046's Tradeoffs record what writing against an imagined TUI cost last time. (2) Point 6's freeze mechanism is NEW mechanism, not the reuse it claims: skip_state_update is a per-rule boolean on a main-screen text rule (rules.rs:190, claude.toml:174); there is no alternate-screen bit and no actor-assertable duration-scoped freeze. That belongs in the wording and in the 1760-line estimate. (3) NOTHING depends on it — 0077 says so at :35-36. When accepted, make the spec amendment IN THE PR THAT SHIPS THE FIRST HARVESTING CODE so the spec never describes behaviour the server lacks.

CONFLICT 6(a) (ADR-0046 point 8 vs the idle gate) — CONFIRM 0077/0078's choice: read the published record, do not gate on the detector's own derivation. L3.md 3.7, made normative in wave 2, expressly settles it and names this exact case: a safety gate MAY read the level, and 'a crashed or unidentified pane reading as do-not-disturb errs in the conservative direction'. Residual: a consumer can declare idle on a busy agent and unlock a harvest. THERE IS NO STRUCTURAL FIX — 3.7 states a consumer 'neither can nor needs to distinguish' declared from derived; the record carries no provenance field and minting one adds a field to a document ADR-0071 freezes. Accept it rather than inventing provenance. ADR-0085 narrowed the hazard anyway: hook evidence now feeds the DETECTOR rather than declaring metadata state.

CONFLICT 6(b) (exit code for a refused harvest) — OVERTURN BOTH 2 AND 3; the answer is EXIT 0 with a named reason on the payload. 3 is wrong on meaning: no satellite is involved and 3's published contract is 'retry is correct once the link is back', but of 0078 point 4's reasons only agent_not_idle is retryable — no_detector, not_local and a missing capability bit are PERMANENT. 2 is wrong on mechanism AND breaks an existing contract: ADR-0065 point 4 fixes the JSON error shape as one line on stderr WITH STDOUT EMPTY, but a refused harvest still produced a perfectly good viewport read — exiting 2 forces discarding it or emitting a success payload alongside a non-zero exit; and 'snapshot --transcript' on an ordinary main-screen pane would exit 2, making every '|| handle_error' treat a good read as failure. Precedent for exit 0: 0077 point 4's truncated/truncated_reason. NAME THE COST in the ADR: a script that asked for a transcript and got none now succeeds silently, so callers must branch on transcript.status — a genuinely new exit-code semantic with no precedent in exit_codes.rs. Carve it into ADR-0071 point 6 so it cannot be discovered post-freeze.

CLI/JSON DELTA OWED IF 0075 RATIFIES (0076 owes NOTHING but the SECS correction): %<agent-name> as a TARGET token on every targeted verb AND the MCP tools' target argument (note resolve_one is duplicated byte-identically at phux-mcp/src/tools.rs:743 and ask_tool.rs:63 — a migration must touch both); the grammar as a parse-time refusal exit 2; four refusals with statuses (Unknown->1, Ambiguous->2, KindConstant->2, Withdrawn->2, PartialIndex->3); error codes in commands::json_err::codes for each (none exists today; ADR-0071 point 7(a) requires them); AND A COLLISION ADR-0071 POINT 6 MUST RESOLVE IN THE SAME EDIT — point 6 says agent wait/send-keys return 1 with partial_view in error.code, but %name's partial-index refusal is 3, and the two rules meet on 'phux agent send-keys %foo'. DECISION: 3 wins for %name and point 6 is amended to say so — a partial FLEET is a server-side gap the client infers; a partial INDEX is the client knowing it did not finish looking, and %name is the one selector whose entire contract is singularity. PRECONDITION, not a delta: fetch_agent_index (agent/record.rs:216-219) returns a bare HashMap and swallows every transport failure into silent truncation via three early returns, so the exit-3 refusal HAS NO SOURCE OF TRUTH TODAY; it must return AgentIndex with a real completeness bit, and three production callers take the raw map.

TWO ITEMS STILL NEEDING A CALL: (i) whether 0075 point 5's guard covers attach and kill — my read is NO: attach writes no bytes, and refusing to kill a pane whose record was withdrawn strands the panes a user most wants gone. (ii) the ~150-line convention overrun (0076 is 224 lines, 0078 is 214); no CI gate enforces it and CONVENTIONS.md prescribes a companion page under docs/architecture/.
notes:
WAVE-2 UPDATE. All four ADRs were revised or written in wave 2 and ALL FOUR ARE STILL Status Proposed - nothing was ratified. ADR/README.md index rows were corrected for the retitles. The scope of this bead grew by one file: ADR/0078-alternate-screen-history.md is NEW, split out of 0077.

CONFLICTS FROM THE ORIGINAL LIST THAT WAVE 2 CLOSED, so do not re-litigate them:
- 0077 conflict 1, the alt-screen harvest versus L1.md 6.1 side-effect-free. Moved to ADR-0078, which names the L1.md 6.1 and 6.2 sentences and commits to amending them in the same PR with a PRIMARY clause on the gate. 0077 now has no wire change and no spec change at all.
- 0077 conflict 3, ADR-0046 point 8 versus the harvest idle gate. ADR-0078 declares it a SAFETY gate taking the LEVEL, per the new normative docs/spec/L3.md 3.7, and ACCEPTS the crashed-pane consequence rather than hedging.
- 0077 conflict 6, exit code for a refused harvest. Resolved to EXIT 0 with a named reason on the payload, on the ground that the read genuinely succeeded, just passively.
- 0075 point 7 versus 0076 point 4, the two wordings of re-verify before writing. 0075 now owns a SAFETY gate on the withdrawn record shape reading the level. 0076 owns a COMPLETION gate requiring an observed transition. They are different gates with different predicates and both are now anchored to docs/spec/L3.md 3.7, which was made normative in wave 2 with a 0.7.0-draft.2 CHANGELOG row and NO PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.

STILL OPEN, AND EACH NEEDS THIS OWNER TO DECIDE:
1. 0075 versus 0076 CIRCULARITY, flagged by the 0076 author and written into neither ADR: 0076 ownership re-verification is TAUTOLOGICAL for a percent-name target, because the name came from the record it re-reads. The gate is only meaningful for at-N targets, and 0076 still does not cite 0075. One of the two must own it.
2. ADR-VERSUS-CODE DIVERGENCE, live in the tree right now. ADR-0076 point 5 permits a narrowed fast path - the wait may satisfy on a POSITIVELY ASSERTED level, blocked or done, on the argument that neither is reachable by fallthrough. The SHIPPED EdgeTracker in crates/phux-client/src/agent_wait.rs implements the strict rule with NO fast path ever, and has two tests pinning it. Either the ADR loses the fast path or the code gains it. The code author says it is a three-line change in EdgeTracker::new. Note that on today manifests the fast path would be inert for blocked-only-by-screen panes anyway - see phux-w7z2.28.
3. 0076 default --until set still contains done, which no shipped manifest can emit. Completeness-critique F1 option 1 was to drop it. See phux-w7z2.28.
4. WHETHER percent-name SHIPS BEFORE OR AFTER the ADR-0046 occupant-change guard, ADR-0075 point 7b. The ADR states what is true either way and deliberately does not choose. Shipping before means an occupant swap inside a surviving pane silently retargets input. Filed as phux-w7z2.27.
5. The percent-name exit-3 asymmetry against hash-tag degrade-to-miss, at the same resolution seam. Defensible - a name claims singularity, a tag does not - but it is a second behaviour at one seam.
6. Whether the ADR-0075 point 5 guard also covers attach and kill.
7. LINE BUDGET. ADR-0076 is 198 lines and ADR-0078 is 201, against the roughly-150 cap in docs/CONVENTIONS.md. No CI gate enforces it - check-docs.sh checks frontmatter, status vocabulary and links only. The convention own remedy is a companion page under docs/architecture. 0076 natural split is decision points 2 and 7. 0078 is points 1, 6 and 7.
8. ADR-0036 needs two corrections the detection-parity audit found while this batch was being written: its three-tier ladder claims a phux-ask sentinel tier that is not in AskedSource at all, and its closing line about waiting for libghostty to expose OSC 9 is now false because phux has its own raw-byte OSC scanner. Filed as phux-w7z2.22 and phux-w7z2.16 respectively, but the ADR text is this owner call.

title: Chrome redesign: tab strip and split focus
description:
Owner picked 'redesign the chrome properly' on 2026-08-08. Three directions mocked and pitched at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/f0efab35-68e7-469f-96b2-39f4c014f4e8 - awaiting a pick.

The constraint that decides it: any chrome that changes HEIGHT resizes a live PTY. header_height is 50pt over a ~17.5pt cell, so a reveal costs every terminal in the tab three rows and a SIGWINCH, and the retraction costs another. Directions A (tabs in the existing 66pt hidden_inset_tall titlebar) and C (summoned overlay) delete that problem rather than manage it; B (permanent 44pt rail) moves the cost to the columns axis, which TUIs reflow far more cheaply.

Also in scope, and independent of which direction wins:

  view.dimScrim returns tokens.colors.background at alpha 0.36 and paints it over panes whose background is the same colour. Compositing a colour over itself is a no-op at any alpha, so the unfocused-pane scrim draws NOTHING and the only focus signal in a 4-way split is a solid-vs-hollow cursor. Confirmed both analytically and in a 4-pane screenshot. Fix: dim toward black rather than toward the window ground (so it survives a configured 'background' and an application OSC 11), plus a 1pt accent edge on the focused pane for the OLED-black case where a dim has nothing left to take.

Recommendation on record: A, with C's palette behind it.
close_reason: Built: titlebar tabs (direction A), side rail kept as the tab-placement option (B), summoned switcher on cmd+shift+P (C), and the split focus fix. All three shipped rather than one - the owner wanted top/side as an option and the palette as well. Verified in the running app with screenshots. Suite 329 pass / 5 skip / 0 fail.

title: [bug] host_draw p90 is 21ms against a 16.7ms frame budget
description:
Measured live on 2026-08-08 via 'profile on' against the running app (v0.6.0, 1100x640, 4 panes, ordinary split/close interaction):

  host_draw   p50 2417us  p90 21147us  max 21147us
  present     p50 3085us  p90  7576us  max 21171us
  plan        p50  214us  p90   297us  max   314us
  a11y        p50    3us  p90   359us  max   445us
  encode      p50    7us  p90    14us  max    24us

host_draw p90 alone exceeds a whole 16.67ms frame, so the app drops frames during normal interaction. That is the measured half of the owner's 'laggy and shit'.

host_draw and host_decode are SDK/AppKit-side (Metal decode + draw of the canvas packet), so this likely needs profiling inside native-sdk rather than in cockpit. plan at 214us p50 is the most expensive stage cockpit controls directly - it is the retained-diff planner over the packed cell grid.

Next step: re-run 'profile on' under a sustained repaint load (a full-screen TUI, not idle) and split host_draw by pane count to find whether it scales with panes or with dirty area.
notes: MEASURED IN THE RECORDED CONDITION 2026-08-12, and jw4's headline no longer reproduces. Driven by scripts/automate-smoke.sh --profile: real bundle, automation-enabled, 1100x640, FOUR panes in the selected tab (asserted, the script refuses to profile below 4), continuous full-screen repaint in every pane, n=204 host_draw samples (the script now waits for >=200 and refuses to print percentiles otherwise). host_draw p50 377us p90 428us (was p50 2417us p90 21147us on v0.6.0); present p50 402us p90 453us (was p50 3085us p90 7576us); plan p50 275us p90 280us n=216 (was p50 214us p90 297us); rebuild p50 60us p90 89us n=2541; host_decode p50 19us p90 22us; encode p50 3us p90 3us; a11y p50 5us p90 697us n=5082. host_draw p90 is now 428us against a 16670us budget - 39x under, where it used to exceed a whole frame on its own. Summing every stage's p90 gives ~1275us, under 8 percent of the budget. NOT CLAIMING THE BEAD IS FULLY ANSWERED, for two reasons stated plainly. (1) CONDITION MISMATCH: the original was recorded under 'ordinary split/close interaction', which is layout CHURN; my load is steady-state repaint with only three splits at setup. Churn is exactly where plan/rebuild spike, so the worst case may still be unmeasured. (2) FRAMES ARE STILL BEING MISSED, and the frame work does not explain it: interval p50 16968us is a clean ~59Hz, but interval p90 36222us is two frame intervals - a dropped frame - while every stage stays under half a millisecond. Something outside the measured pipeline is costing those frames. Also worth a look on its own: a11y p50 5us against p90 697us is a 140x spread over 5082 samples, the widest of any stage.

title: agent-to-agent orchestration: herdr parity and beyond
description:
Bring phux's agent-to-agent orchestration surface to herdr parity and past it:
addressable agent names, acknowledged prompting, event-driven waiting, a read
surface that survives soft wrap and the alternate screen, and the detection-layer
fixes an audit against herdr surfaced.

What already landed this run (uncommitted in the worktree at the time of filing,
so it is context, not work):

- `phux watch` now carries `agent_state` lines. crates/phux-client/src/watch.rs
  subscribes to SUBSCRIBE_METADATA on `phux.agent/v1` alongside SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS;
  crates/phux/src/commands/watch.rs renders them. No wire change.
- The server-side fanout was relaxed so an L3 metadata subscriber no longer has
  to be attached (ClientTable::broadcast_metadata_changed falls back to a
  captured `metadata_mailboxes` entry). See the review bead under this epic.
- `phux agent explain --file PATH --kind KIND` — offline manifest explainer
  (crates/phux-server/src/agent_explain.rs, crates/phux/src/commands/agent/offline.rs).
- Three proposed ADRs: 0075 (agent-name addressing), 0076 (prompt + lifecycle
  wait), 0077 (agent read surface). All Status: Proposed, none implemented.
- `nix develop -c just ci` was green at the end of the run. Nothing was left
  failing; every bead here is new work, not breakage.

SCHEDULING CONSTRAINT (real, not a nicety): ADR-0071 is Proposed and freezes the
CLI JSON surface for 1.0. Every verb and JSON document under this epic must land
BEFORE that freeze or be explicitly carved into it. That already applies to two
SHIPPED things ADR-0071 does not name: the AgentExplainJson document and the
`agent_state` watch event name. See the ADR-0071 carve-out bead.

Source material: the three ADRs in ADR/, and a read-only detection-parity audit
against herdr (10 ranked findings; its top items are filed individually here,
including the two correctness findings, which are NOT polish).
notes:
WAVE-2 STATUS, 2026-08-08. Everything below is UNCOMMITTED in the worktree. Verified green in that state: cargo nextest run --workspace 3246 of 3246 passed with 72 skipped, just docs-check 142 files 0 violations, refdocs::tests::generated_reference_docs_match_the_tree PASS, fmt and clippy -D warnings clean, cargo deny clean.

CLOSED THIS WAVE: phux-w7z2.8 read surface, phux-w7z2.9 wait soft-wrap bug plus --regex, phux-w7z2.4 agent wait, phux-w7z2.7 agent send-keys. Two carry recorded deviations - agent wait has NO level fast path, and agent send-keys shipped on ROUTE_INPUT rather than APPLY_INPUT. Read their close reasons before assuming the ADRs describe the code.

THE RULING THAT GOVERNED THE WAVE, now normative in docs/spec/L3.md 3.7 with a 0.7.0-draft.2 CHANGELOG row and NO PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. The five shipped manifests contain exactly ten state-bearing rules - five working, five blocked - and ZERO idle and ZERO done. idle is the fail-safe fallthrough at agent_detect/mod.rs:424-428 and is equally true of a finished agent, a half-painted TUI, a crashed agent and a pane running less. So state is read two ways depending on the shape of the gate. A LEVEL asserts only that no state-bearing rule currently matches - absence of contrary evidence. An EDGE asserts that whatever was asserting the old value stopped. SAFETY gates take the level: do not scroll a repainting screen, do not write into a pane whose occupant may have changed. COMPLETION gates take the edge: agent wait and prompt --wait must be satisfied only by an observed transition, never by a level read, which is what stops a wait returning success on a corpse. A quiescent open-enum value was CONSIDERED AND REJECTED - it would have no producer, because the only thing that could emit it is a positive idle rule in a manifest, and none can be honestly authored until real viewports are captured. Do not introduce it.

ADR-0071 SCHEDULING CONSTRAINT, RESTATED AND NOW URGENT. ADR-0071 is Status Proposed and freezes the CLI JSON surface AND the MCP tool names and arguments for 1.0. Wave 2 shipped four CLI surface changes, three JSON documents and four error codes BEFORE the carve-out was written - which is the failure this epic flagged from the start, happening. Every verb and JSON document under this epic must land before that freeze or be explicitly carved into it. Two beads own that and both are P1: phux-w7z2.2 for the CLI and JSON surface, and phux-w7z2.30 for splitting the phux_agent MCP action multiplexer before its argument union freezes around a shape designed for five read verbs. Neither is optional and neither is reversible after 1.0.

FOUR ADRs NOW, NOT THREE. ADR-0077 was split - it keeps the additive read decisions and the alternate-screen harvest moved to the NEW ADR/0078-alternate-screen-history.md. ALL FOUR ARE STILL Status Proposed. Nothing was ratified. phux-w7z2.1 owns all four.

title: Seven --json surfaces ship unversioned, days before the ADR-0071 schema freeze
acceptance_criteria: Every --json document either carries a top-level schema_version or has a written, referenced reason it does not; the streaming watch surface has an explicit documented decision; docs/consumers/agents.md and the generated reference describe each shape; tests pin the emitted documents.
close_reason: Six documents versioned additively (new, spawn, ask, pair, play, rec), each factored into a pure builder with a pinning test; matched the majority inline-literal convention. watch deliberately NOT per-line versioned: a per-line field is repeated overhead on a hot path and a header line is invisible to a consumer that reconnects or tails mid-stream, so the stream is versioned by the binary with the event-name vocabulary as the compatibility unit -- decision documented on run_watch and in docs/consumers/agents.md. phux-mcp needed no change (it passes parsed values through). Real binary output captured for four verbs.

title: Remove the deprecated CLI spellings whose v0.12.0 removal window has passed
description: crates/phux/src/deprecations.rs pins 12 deprecated spellings (phux remote/satellite/enroll verbs and the --horizontal/--vertical booleans) all scheduled removed_in=v0.12.0. The shipped version is 0.12.1, so the published removal window has passed. ADR-0071 makes removing them a pre-1.0 obligation: after 1.0 freezes the CLI grammar, dropping a spelling costs a major bump.
acceptance_criteria: All 12 rows removed from deprecations.rs and the clap tree; the bidirectional pin test still passes; docs/reference/deprecations.md regenerated via just docs-gen; no hidden alias remains; CHANGELOG-worthy breaking change noted in the commit body.
close_reason: All 12 deprecated spellings removed with their clap surface; DEPRECATED is now an empty table with the mechanism and the bidirectional pin test intact (still fails if a hidden alias appears without a row or a row outlives its alias). refdocs generator fixed to render an empty table instead of panicking on DEPRECATED[0]. Found and fixed a REAL consumer still using the removed flags: integrations/pi/src/adapter.ts built --horizontal/--vertical for insertPane/movePane, now --split. Docs prose and examples updated; docs/reference regenerated. Breaking change, conventional-commit body lists every spelling and its replacement.

title: Stale glyphs remain in columns a widening pane newly exposes
description: Reproduced in the running app: split a pane, close the split so the survivor widens, and the widened pane keeps stale glyphs — a duplicated prompt line and a hostname truncated at the narrower width. Ruled out: the emulator and the app-side projection are provably correct (80 to 40 to 80 with wrapped content reflows cleanly, RenderState forces a full redraw on any dimension change). One real SDK cause was found and fixed (the render planner erases clip commands into a per-command field, so a GROWING clip left the revealed pixels unnamed in the retained packet baseline) but the symptom still reproduces, so that was not the whole story. Next lead: per-row text runs are keyed by start column, so a row that loses a run emits nothing for that id. NATIVE_SDK_GPU_VERIFY_INCREMENTAL=1 with NATIVE_SDK_GPU_DRAW_TRACE=1 byte-compares a from-scratch redraw against the patched backing and will localize engine vs host in one run.
close_reason: Fixed by construction and verified in the running app. The packed cell grid makes a terminal one retained key replaced wholesale, so a row that loses a run can no longer orphan a per-run command keyed by start column - which was the mechanism leaving a duplicated prompt line and a truncated hostname in columns a widening pane exposed. Confirmed by driving split then close-split in the real app and reading the screenshot: the survivor widens clean. A separate real bug was found and fixed on the way: the render planner erases clip commands into a per-command field, so a GROWING clip left the newly revealed pixels unnamed in the retained packet baseline.

title: Max-density truecolor still truncates: needs the packed cell-grid command
description: The SDK renders a terminal as per-run fill_rect and draw_text commands. Raising the per-view ceiling 2048 to 4096 took a realistic 200x60 styled screen from 34 to 60 of 60 rows, but a distinct truecolor fg AND bg per cell needs ~2 commands per cell (~24000 for 200x60) at ~696 bytes per slot across the view mirrors, so no constant fixes it — 8192 was measured to segfault runtime construction at 255 MB. Truncation is now reported rather than silent. The real fix is one CanvasCommand carrying a packed cell array that the host renderers expand. Touches: CanvasCommand union, equality, hash/render_fingerprints, retained diffing, packet baseline, the reference CPU renderer, the Metal and Direct2D encoders, wire format version, canvas_limits, and snapshot/automation. Work is on the phall1/native fork.
close_reason: Built. CanvasCommand.cell_grid is a packed lattice of 20-byte cells that each renderer expands, emitted one command PER ROW. A 200x60 screen with a distinct truecolor fg and bg per cell went from 9 of 60 rows in ~1600 commands to 60 of 60; 300x100 fits in 585 KB and was previously unreachable at any budget. Cluster bytes are interned per row, so text cost tracks the alphabet rather than the cell count. Command count is now a constant function of ROWS rather than of styling. Truncation, where a budget genuinely binds, is reported through paintReport (rows_total/rows_painted/stopped_by) and a DisplayListDegradation on the builder instead of being silent.

title: No scrollback search (cmd+F / cmd+G)
description: libghostty-vt ships a complete search and highlight API (vt.search.PageList plus RenderState.updateHighlightsFlattened) and only the remote phux provider uses it. Local terminals have no search at all. A daily driver needs cmd+F to open a search field, cmd+G / cmd+shift+G to step matches, highlighted hits projected into the grid snapshot, and escape to dismiss. The projection needs an extra highlight channel through row.highlights.
close_reason: Landed and verified in the running app. cmd+F opens a search band, typing filters live, cmd+G / cmd+shift+G step, Escape dismisses and restores the prior scroll position. Matches wash amber, the current match washes in the accent, and the foreground is picked by perceived luminance against the terminal's own colours rather than forced to black or white. Search state lives on the Session rather than the Model, so per-terminal locality is structural instead of a lookup a tab switch can get wrong - confirmed visually: the unfocused pane containing the same text showed zero washes. Screenshot verified: magnifier, needle with caret, '6 of 6' counter, live filtering from 14 matches down to 6, and 'No matches' in warning yellow when the needle stopped matching. Two hazards handled: leaving the alternate screen DESTROYS it and its pin pool, so the engine records a screen key and generation; and the printable-text arm needed its own modal gate or the needle would also have reached the shell. Known limits recorded separately: local search is always case-insensitive (the engine exposes no option) while the phux provider takes a case_sensitive flag, and searchAll runs synchronously on the dispatch thread so a full 50 MB history will stutter while typing.

title: Session restore is implemented but never called
description: Model.topologySnapshot() and restoreModel() are complete and covered by topology_persistence_tests, but nothing in the executable calls either one. The app therefore never persists or restores tabs, splits, selection, focus, or divider positions across a relaunch. A daily-driver terminal has to come back the way you left it. Wire a save on shutdown/state-change and a load at startup, and decide the storage location (the SDK's app_dirs state dir). The snapshot deliberately carries no PID or process-survival claim, so restore means recreating shells in the same layout, not resurrecting processes.
close_reason: Wired end to end. Layout persists to the app_dirs STATE directory (not config) on a debounced 750ms timer, edge-triggered off a shape fingerprint that deliberately excludes cwd so a plain cd is not a disk write, plus a synchronous flush on the shutdown lifecycle. Restore runs before the default terminal is created so the window opens INTO the layout. Schema v3 adds per-terminal working directories as a side table keyed by registry offset. Format is a flat line-oriented text file with an explicit end terminator: chosen over ZON/JSON because a startup-read, user-editable, possibly half-written file must never crash, and a non-nesting grammar is structurally incapable of stack overflow or unbounded recursion. Verified live: opened two tabs and a split, pkill -KILL to model a crash rather than a clean quit, relaunched, and the layout came back identically with fresh shells. Corrupt, empty, truncated-at-every-line-boundary and 400 random-byte files all fall back to a normal launch.

title: Add Blackbird-compatible Phux agent probe contract
description: Expose the additive machine contract required by Blackbird ADR-0005: phux agent probe --json returns schema_version phux.agent.probe/v1, binary_version, build_id, selected_protocol, opaque HELLO server_id as base64url, stable named server capabilities, inventory completeness, and workload auth methods. Current status JSON and probe_hello discard required HELLO_OK identity/capability evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Golden JSON schema and CLI tests prove exact server_id/capability preservation, bounded output, unknown additive fields, typed incompatibility, no terminal content or credentials, and Blackbird conformance fixtures pass.
notes:
Linear mirror: https://linear.app/phall/issue/PHA-243/add-blackbird-compatible-phux-agent-probe-contract

Independent verification 2026-09-13 of commit dbedea6c: do not close/land as-is. The implementation is additive and content-free, preserves the negotiated HELLO_OK server_id and named capability bits, and targeted probe unit/e2e success plus no-server failure tests pass. However full acceptance is not met: (1) accepted phux ADR-0095 and Blackbird ADR-0001 explicitly say Blackbird does not read phux agent probe and retire the phantom Blackbird ADR-0005 requirement; that referenced ADR/file and Blackbird conformance fixtures do not exist, so this cannot be called Blackbird-conformant without an explicit architecture decision change; (2) tests do not exercise malformed/unsupported HELLO_OK protocol/profile/limit mismatch, despite acceptance requiring typed incompatibility; (3) cargo nextest run -p phux --lib fails because the new command was not added to EXPECTED_INVENTORY or skills/phux/SKILL.md. Scoped probe tests, docs freshness/docs-check, fmt, and workspace rustdoc pass. Targeted clippy is blocked by pre-existing unrelated test lint failures in config_init_distro.rs and automation_e2e/common/mod.rs. Commit dbedea6c was preserved; no correction added because doing so would entrench a surface forbidden by current accepted architecture rather than resolve the governing contradiction.
close_reason: Superseded by accepted ADR-0095: Blackbird consumes AgentSession/resources rather than phux agent probe; candidate commit intentionally not landed after verification found architectural conflict and failing command inventory/skill tests

title: Phase 1: extract ServerConfig (8 immutable-after-boot fields)
description:
term, shell, history_limit, cwd_inheritance, window_size, session_root, server_socket_path, policy_bundle are each written exactly once (setters in registry.rs L270-341) and read 79 times combined. They are boot config living inside the live-state mutex, indistinguishable from mutable state at the type level.

title: Initialize login environment for service-spawned panes
description: A server installed with 'phux service install' runs under launchd's minimal PATH. New panes spawn the configured shell as a plain interactive shell rather than a login shell, so macOS profile initialization never runs. Users get their normal prompt and .zshrc but commands installed through Homebrew or Nix profiles are absent (for example, nvim and brew both report command not found). Environment markers such as NIX_PROFILES may still be inherited, making common profile guards incorrectly believe initialization already happened.
design: Define and document service-backed pane environment semantics. Prefer invoking the user's shell in the platform-correct login mode or another shell-native initialization path rather than baking the installer's transient PATH into the service unit. Preserve explicit defaults.shell behavior and avoid assuming zsh. The solution must cover launchd and systemd without double-sourcing profiles in ordinary terminal-launched servers.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A launchd server started with only the macOS default service PATH spawns a pane that receives the user's normal login PATH. 2. Homebrew and Nix profile commands are discoverable in service-backed panes when their standard profile initialization provides them. 3. bash, zsh, fish, explicit defaults.shell, and fallback /bin/sh behavior are defined and tested. 4. Service installation never captures a transient nix develop/direnv PATH. 5. An end-to-end regression starts the service under a minimal environment and proves a profile-provided command resolves. 6. Existing direct/server-in-terminal pane startup remains regression-free.
close_reason: Detection is knowledge not heuristic: phux service install stamps PHUX_SERVICE_MANAGED=1 into both the launchd plist and the systemd unit, and phux server reads it at startup. Login invocation per shell: bash/zsh/sh take -l, fish takes --login, unrecognized defaults.shell gets no flag (deliberate: an unknown program's flag semantics are unknown, and a fatal exec is worse than an unsourced profile). All 6 acceptance criteria satisfied. Criterion 4 was already correct -- resolve_plan never reads PATH -- and is now locked in by a test that reads the test process's own ambient nix develop PATH and asserts it appears in neither unit. Criterion 5/6 proven by a real e2e that runs the compiled binary with env_clear plus a launchd-shaped minimal PATH against a real profile fixture and a real PTY; only the init system itself is simulated. ADR-0073 records the decision.

title: [epic] Decompose ServerState: 51 fields into 8 cohesive concerns
description:
ServerState carries 51 fields and 61 methods across ~1450 production lines in state/mod.rs + state/registry.rs. Roughly eleven unrelated concerns share one struct behind one mutex: wire ID interning, immutable boot config, terminal lifecycle, clients, sessions, leases, metadata, agents, federation, upgrade, attach-seeding.

This is a legibility problem, not a correctness or performance one. The runtime is current-thread and the mutex is uncontended by construction (see the clippy::arc_with_non_send_sync allow in state/mod.rs). SharedState's 4-method API (new/lock/with/with_mut) and the 20 lock sites across 5 files are the GOOD part and must survive unchanged.

The cost of the status quo is that adding a 52nd field is free, and no subsystem boundary is expressed in the type system.

Also: state/registry.rs is 69KB containing a single 'impl ServerState' block and no type named Registry. The filename describes something that does not exist.
acceptance_criteria: ServerState holds 8 named sub-structs instead of 51 flat fields. SharedState's public API is byte-identical. just ci green at every phase boundary. No behavior change.
close_reason: 7/7 children complete and the acceptance criterion is met on the current tree: ServerState is 11 fields, 10 of them named sub-structs (SessionTable, ClientTable, TerminalTable, LeaseTable, IdSpace, MetadataStore, AgentState, ServerConfig, HubState, Lifecycle) plus hook_dispatcher, down from 51 flat fields. state/registry.rs is gone, replaced by 29 focused modules under state/. Verified 2026-08-07; the epic was left open after 294a7e6c 'finish the ServerState decomposition' landed.

title: Add first-class self-update with live server handoff
description: Today, 'phux upgrade' only asks a running server to re-exec whatever binary is already on disk. It does not discover, download, verify, or install a newer Phux release, leaving users to understand Homebrew, direct release archives, NixOS, and the subsequent live-server handoff themselves. Add a first-class update workflow that detects the installation source, checks available versions, safely updates supported mutable installs, and invokes the existing graceful upgrade so panes survive. Package-managed or immutable installations must fail safely with an exact actionable native update command rather than attempting to mutate their store.
design: Prefer a user-facing 'phux update' command, retaining 'phux upgrade' as the low-level live-server re-exec primitive. Verify release checksums before an atomic binary replacement. Detect direct-release, Homebrew, Cargo, Nix/NixOS, and unsupported installs; either perform the safe update or print/optionally execute the correct package-manager path. Support check-only, dry-run, explicit version/channel, non-interactive output, and clear rollback/error behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 1. One documented command checks current versus latest Phux and identifies the install source. 2. Direct release installs download the matching platform archive, verify the published checksum, atomically replace binaries, and preserve permissions. 3. A running local server is handed off through the existing graceful upgrade path without losing live panes. 4. Homebrew/Cargo/package-managed installs use or print the correct native update path. 5. Nix/NixOS and other immutable-store installs are never mutated and receive an exact actionable rebuild/update instruction. 6. Check-only, dry-run, explicit-version, machine-readable output, failure, and rollback paths have tests. 7. Documentation covers macOS, Linux, Homebrew, direct archives, and NixOS.
close_reason: phux update shipped: --check, --dry-run, --version, --json, --rollback, --no-restart. Install-source detection from the symlink-resolved current_exe as a pure testable function, most-specific-first: Nix store (NixOS vs profile), Homebrew (Cellar component or prefix), Cargo bin, direct-release allowlist, unknown. Only direct-release is mutable; unknown is refused with a hint rather than best-effort overwritten. Artifact naming and the sha256 sidecar format were read out of release.yml, not assumed; the digest is computed in-process and compared BEFORE tar is invoked, with the sidecar filename cross-checked so crossed assets are caught, then a tar member allowlist and an extracted-tree revalidation. Staging happens inside the target bin dir so rename(2) is atomic; mode is copied from the existing binary, which also strips any setuid the tarball carried; phux-mcp and phux are replaced in an order that rolls back on partial failure. Rollback keeps one generation as plain files plus a JSON manifest, deliberately recoverable with mv if you downgrade past the verb. Priorities 1-5 done; --channel (6) CUT and the flag does not exist, since only stable releases are published and adding it later is additive. One dependency, sha2, already in the workspace: zero new Cargo.lock rows. ADR-0074 records the trust boundary honestly -- the sidecar shares a host and TLS channel with the archive, so it catches truncation, corruption, crossed assets and a mid-flight proxy but NOT a compromised release host; signing is named as the successor.

title: Adopt a live server into service supervision without killing panes
description:
## Problem

Running `phux service install` while an unsupervised Phux server already owns the configured Unix socket creates a restart loop: the launchd/systemd process exits because the socket is live, while stopping the existing server would kill every pane and its in-flight shells, agents, and subagents. This occurred with a long-lived server containing active OMP sessions when enabling persistent service supervision and new QUIC/WebSocket listeners.

A user should be able to move a live Phux server under service supervision without losing terminal processes, rather than waiting for all work to finish or accepting that conversation resume cannot restore killed subprocesses.

## Desired behavior

Provide an explicit adoption/handoff path, potentially `phux service install --adopt`, that transitions a running unsupervised server to the native service manager while preserving live sessions and pane processes. The transition must also reconcile listener configuration instead of leaving the old server on stale transports.
design: launchd and systemd generally cannot adopt an arbitrary existing PID. Treat this as a server-to-server handoff, not process reparenting: start the supervised replacement, transfer or re-adopt live PTY/session file descriptors and state using the existing graceful-upgrade machinery where possible, atomically transfer socket/listener ownership, then retire the old server. Clients may briefly reconnect but pane process identities and execution must survive. If a platform cannot support safe adoption, detect that before installing a restart-looping unit and print a precise recovery path.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Installing service supervision over a live unsupervised server does not kill pane processes or their descendants. 2. The resulting server is owned and restart-managed by launchd on macOS and systemd --user on Linux. 3. Existing attached clients reconnect or receive a clear transient handoff, while detached sessions remain intact. 4. Unix socket and requested QUIC/WebSocket listeners transfer atomically without a prolonged bind conflict. 5. Pane child PIDs and observable terminal contents survive an integration test across handoff. 6. A failed or unsupported handoff leaves the original server running and does not install a crash-looping service.
notes:
SCOPING (2026-08-11, from a code audit): the design note's 'reuse the graceful-upgrade machinery' direction is sound but requires NET-NEW MECHANISM, not reuse. Four confirmed blockers:

1. THE ONLY FD TRANSPORT IS execve INHERITANCE. There is no SCM_RIGHTS anywhere in the codebase -- grep for SCM_RIGHTS|sendmsg|recvmsg|ScmRights|send_fd|pass_fd across all crates returns zero hits. blob.listener_fd and PaneBlob::master_fd are RAW INTEGERS meaningful only inside the exec'd image's own fd table. A process launchd/systemd spawned independently has an unrelated fd table; the blob is literally uninterpretable to it.

2. NO SOCKET ACTIVATION. render_launchd_plist emits no Sockets key; there is no LISTEN_FDS handling. The only mentions of 'socket activation' in the tree are prose analogies.

3. THE BLOB NEVER CROSSES THE WIRE, BY EXPLICIT DESIGN. Command::Upgrade is documented as 'A bare trigger -- the handoff state blob is built and passed entirely server-side (it never crosses the wire)' (phux-protocol/src/wire/frame.rs:1601-1608).

4. execve PRESERVES PROCESS IDENTITY AND PARENT, which is exactly the problem this bead names. The trigger IS externally requestable (phux upgrade sends Command::Upgrade), but the DESTINATION is hardcoded to std::env::current_exe() (runtime/upgrade.rs:106). An external process can say 're-exec yourself'; it cannot say 'hand off to me'. After the re-exec it is still the same PID with the same parent, so launchd/systemd still does not own it.

TWO FURTHER GAPS blocking this bead's stated acceptance criteria:
- LISTENER CONFIG CANNOT CHANGE ACROSS THE HANDOFF. resume_args (runtime/upgrade.rs:140-177) reconstructs argv from RuntimeFlags captured at the OLD server's startup, and Command::Upgrade carries no payload. There is no way to request 'upgrade AND now also serve --quic 0.0.0.0:8788'. An adopted server would come back on the old transports.
- ENVIRONMENT DOES NOT SUBSTITUTE. UpgradePlan::exec uses std::process::Command, which inherits the current environment, so a re-exec of an unsupervised server keeps the unsupervised env -- it would NOT pick up the unit's PHUX_WS_TOKENS / PHUX_WS_TLS_* / PHUX_SERVICE_MANAGED. Note login_shell is derived from PHUX_SERVICE_MANAGED (commands/server.rs:200), so an 'adopted' server would still spawn non-login panes.

MINIMUM MISSING PIECES: (a) an fd-passing channel (SCM_RIGHTS over the UDS, or socket activation), (b) a handoff REQUEST verb with a target, (c) a parameterized upgrade command so listener config can change, (d) an env-substitution story. Only (a) has any partial analogue today, and it is the execve path -- precisely the one that cannot cross process boundaries.

RECOMMENDATION: do phux-67wg (refuse to install over a live server, with a precise recovery message) first. It removes the user-facing damage cheaply. This bead is a multi-week design item and should get an ADR before any code.
close_reason: Shipped as phux service install --adopt on army/w3-service-adopt (commit f30644cb), with ADR-0088. Numbered 0086 at first, renumbered after army/w3-render-newtype minted 0086 and army/w3-chrome-config 0087 concurrently in the same wave (see phux-254o). Adoption transfers the supervision, not the process: no supervisor can restart-manage a pid it did not start, so the unit is armed rather than loaded and the auto-spawn path completes the hand-over. ACs 1, 4 and 6 met; ACs 2, 3 and 5 (live pane transfer between two processes) remain blocked on an SCM_RIGHTS channel and are recorded as post-1.0 in ADR-0088.

title: Local dev shell cannot build libghostty since the Zig 0.16 re-pin: nmedit missing from nix apple-sdk
description: Since 40fcf5e0 (Zig 0.16 + libghostty re-pin to 98ad1db), the vendored build runs ghostty-src/src/build/libsystem_override.sh which invokes nmedit. Inside nix develop, DEVELOPER_DIR=/nix/store/...-apple-sdk-14.4 and SDKROOT point at the nix SDK, whose toolchain lacks nmedit, so the /usr/bin/nmedit shim fails with "error: tool 'nmedit' not found" and every local cargo build of the workspace fails on macOS. GitHub CI passes (runner has full Xcode active). Reproduced 2026-08-02 in a fresh worktree; unsetting DEVELOPER_DIR/SDKROOT inside the shell and clearing the sys-crate build dir do not clear it (zig build plan re-resolves the nix SDK). Fix candidates: add an nmedit-bearing toolchain to the dev shell PATH ahead of the shim, patch libsystem_override.sh via the -sys crate, or upstream a fallback to llvm-objcopy. Until fixed, local heavy gates on macOS are degraded; branch verification leans on the required GitHub checks.
notes: WORKAROUND FOUND (wave-10 implementer, 2026-08-02): exporting DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer inside nix develop makes the libghostty zig build succeed — full Xcode's toolchain carries nmedit, overriding the nix apple-sdk's DEVELOPER_DIR. Candidate permanent fix: have the dev shell prefer the host Xcode DEVELOPER_DIR when present, or patch libsystem_override.sh.
close_reason: 4xdh: flake.nix now prefers a host Xcode whose toolchain actually contains nmedit (checked, not assumed), falling back to nix's DEVELOPER_DIR with a loud actionable warning. Root cause pinned down precisely: the nix apple-sdk ships an nmedit specification plist but not the binary, and a CLT-only DEVELOPER_DIR is rejected because zig then reports DarwinSdkNotFound. t2g: the shim fix landed in d2946e3f and was never closed; nothing pinned it, so added a pty-driven behavioral test running the rendered wrapper against fake phux and claude binaries across all three paths -- clean exit, mid-session crash (status propagates, no relaunch), and pre-launch failure (direct fallback exactly once).

comments.author: phall
comments.text: Workaround found (wave 10): the nmedit failure is the nix apple-sdk DEVELOPER_DIR hiding the real toolchain -- nmedit exists at /Applications/Xcode.app/.../usr/bin/nmedit and in the CLT. Overriding inside the dev shell makes the full build green on macOS: nix develop -c bash -c 'DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer cargo check -p phux'. CLT alone is NOT enough (zig reports DarwinSdkNotFound); full Xcode works. zig 0.15 (ambient) is refused by vendored ghostty (needs 0.16), so the override inside the 0.16 shell is the working combination.

comments.author: phall
comments.text:
G3 gate record (phux-i0e8.13.2) -- run against ux/g3 (base decde8631 = waves 5-11, plus the in-gate fix 83bc1eae).

== 1. just ci + just e2e ==

- just ci: GREEN on the final run with the in-gate fix (2840/2840 unit tests,
  fmt/lint/docs-check/formula-check/font-check/e2e-lane-check/deny/doc all
  pass). An earlier run failed once on phux-server::agent_detect
  deleting_the_record_hands_it_back_to_the_detector ("precondition: the
  detector published `blocked`" -- got "idle") under heavy sibling-agent CPU
  load; passes in isolation and on every rerun. Contention flake, not a
  regression. Not filed; refile if it recurs on an idle box.
- just e2e: IN FLIGHT at agent handoff (forced return): 4/48 e2e tests passed,
  zero failures at cutoff; the run continues in the worktree. Verify the tail
  of the run before closing this bead.

== 2. Completion leak loop ==

FINDING (fixed in-gate, commit 83bc1eae): `phux completion zsh|bash` offered
the three hidden ADR-0066 deprecation aliases (remote, satellite, enroll) and
the hidden gen-reference-docs next to `host`:
- zsh: root `_phux_commands` descriptor list carried
  'remote:Deprecated alias...', 'satellite:...', 'enroll:...'.
- bash: root opts= word list carried them, plus full
  `cmd="phux__subcmd__satellite"` completion machinery.
- Root cause: clap_complete 4.6.7's AOT generators copy every subcommand;
  is_hide_set is only consulted for possible values.
- The in-tree guard test (completions_carry_host_and_not_the_deprecated_verbs)
  passed VACUOUSLY: it grepped `phux__remote`, a marker 4.6.7 never emits
  (paths join as `phux__subcmd__remote`). Born vacuous -- 4.6.7 was in
  Cargo.lock before the aliases were hidden.

Fix: completion.rs now generates from a pruned tree (real root args/version,
visible verbs only); guard test greps the real markers + "Deprecated alias"
help text; new unit test pins the pruned tree to the visible half of the
parser. After the fix the scripted loop is CLEAN for zsh and bash:
no phux__subcmd__{remote,satellite,enroll}, no "Deprecated alias" text,
no gen-reference-docs; `host` offered in both.

Recorded drift, filed:
- phux-06nn (P2): phux-i0e8.12.5 is closed ("stdio-bridge hidden, shadowing
  documented, agent args doc'd") but NO deliverable exists in the tree or in
  any commit in history. stdio-bridge is visible in --help and completions;
  attach help says nothing about name-shadowing; AgentAction args undocumented.
- phux-c1ry (P3): hidden per-verb flags (--horizontal/--vertical) still leak
  into completion option lists; needs arg-level pruning or upstream fix.

== 3. Grammar sweep table ==

Cells: plain ls | ls --json | --socket root position | --socket verb position.
DEAD = socket nobody listens on. All cells PASS.

| registry    | ls                  | --json                         | --socket (root)      | --socket (verb)      |
|-------------|---------------------|--------------------------------|----------------------|----------------------|
| ls (root)   | exit 1 (no server)  | jq -e OK, no_server, stdout "" | exit 1, dials DEAD   | identical            |
| tag ls .    | exit 1 (no server)  | jq -e OK, no_server, stdout "" | exit 1, dials DEAD   | identical            |
| worktree ls | exit 0 (by design:  | jq -e OK on stdout             | exit 0, binding      | identical            |
|             | local git listing)  |                                | degrades to "-"      |                      |
| host ls     | exit 0 (registry)   | jq -e OK on stdout             | exit 2 teaching      | identical refusal,   |
|             |                     |                                | refusal (socketless) | byte-identical text  |
| plugin ls   | exit 0 (registry)   | jq -e OK on stdout             | exit 2 teaching      | identical refusal,   |
|             |                     |                                | refusal (socketless) | byte-identical text  |

Hidden aliases: `phux remote ls` and `phux satellite ls` parse (exit 0) and
print the one-line deprecation warning; absent from root --help; `host` listed.

Split-direction spellings (insert-pane AND move-pane, all cells PASS):
--split vertical | v | horizontal | h all parse (dead-socket exit 1, never a
usage error); deprecated --horizontal/--vertical parse with exactly one
warning line teaching --split; --split v + --horizontal refused at clap (exit 2).

== 4. Dead-socket --json documents under jq -e ==

- query (phux --socket DEAD ls --json): exit 1, stdout empty, one-line stderr
  doc parses under jq -e; schema_version=1, error.code=no_server, remedy
  present, exit_code=1.
- mutation (phux --socket DEAD insert-pane @1 @2 --json): same contract,
  jq -e OK. (`new --json` is NOT usable as the dead-socket mutation probe:
  it auto-spawns a server at the socket -- by design.)
- status (phux --socket DEAD status --json): running:false answer document on
  stdout, jq -e OK, exit 1.

Full transcript: scripted check (57 PASS / 0 FAIL / 3 DRIFT lines, drift =
stdio-bridge, filed as phux-06nn). Reference-drift regeneration deferred to
G4 per this bead; the in-gate fix changes no generated reference page
(completions are not checked in; refdocs already omits hidden verbs).
