title: Automate Ratatui, browser, recording, and native surface smoke
description: Turn tui-probe into bounded assertion-bearing scenarios with artifacts; extend browser Chrome/WebSocket tests for explicit compatibility; prove native adapter against a real server; ensure native sessions still record portable VT casts and never serialize engine checkpoint bytes into asciicast.
acceptance_criteria: Marker paints before delayed history, typing works during paging, PageUp does not jump, resize/split/resync stays exact, host terminal restores, browser compatibility remains green, native multi-pane is usable, and interrupted/complete recordings replay.

title: [epic] Ratatui, web, and native frontend adapters
description: Migrate the existing Ratatui client onto the shared kernel first, retain the web client on negotiated synthesized-VT compatibility until exact wasm codec support is proven, and complete a native renderer/input adapter using the validated native-sdk terminal-grid path. All frontends share session/history/recovery semantics while retaining platform-specific painting, input, clipboard, font, zoom, and window integration.
acceptance_criteria: Ratatui behavior is preserved with READY-before-history and visible recovery; web remains interoperable without weakening native fidelity; a native app attaches to a real phux server, renders multiple panes, accepts input, scrolls/searches local history, and recovers from tombstones through the same kernel.

title: PTY writer dies permanently on any io error, and its Drop injects newline+VEOF into the pane
description: spawn.rs:401-415 breaks the writer loop on ANY io::Error with no errno discrimination, no retry, no partial-write accounting. Compounding: the receiver drops (discarding up to 64 queued requests), nothing ever restarts the thread (writer_thread is only taken in shutdown_pty), and self.pty_tx stays Some so every later send hits TrySendError::Closed and is discarded at debug! level while ROUTE_INPUT keeps acking Ok -- pane looks alive, all input goes nowhere. Additionally portable-pty's Drop for UnixMasterWriter writes newline + VEOF into the master on thread exit (unix.rs:392-405), which in canonical mode commits a truncated partial line as if complete. EIO asymmetry is the realistic trigger: portable-pty maps EIO to EOF on the read half (unix.rs:94-97) but not the write half (unix.rs:407-412). Split out of phux-6b6t.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #318 (4bbe113e). Writer now classifies errno: EIO/EPIPE are routine child teardown, EINTR/EAGAIN retry under a bounded budget, only unexpected errnos end the loop and they log the partial-write count. write_all replaced by a resuming loop. portable-pty's VEOF-injecting Drop now fires on clean shutdown only (ManuallyDrop), so a failed write can no longer commit a truncated line to a canonical-mode shell. Drop sites raised to warn!/error!.

title: Add cache-preserving phux context awareness to Pi and OpenCode
description: Implement dynamic phux fleet awareness in the Pi and OpenCode integrations without rewriting the stable prompt prefix. Emit bounded sequenced checkpoints/deltas only when fleet state changes, preserve current state across compaction/session lifecycle, avoid terminal-content leakage, document semantics and configuration, and add focused unit/runtime tests for both hosts.
acceptance_criteria: Pi and OpenCode receive bounded current phux metadata context with exact-prefix-cache-friendly append semantics; unchanged state emits nothing; state changes produce sequenced deltas/checkpoints; compaction/session recovery preserves a canonical current checkpoint; no screen contents are injected automatically; tests and consumer docs cover behavior and safety.
close_reason: Implemented cache-preserving sequenced phux fleet checkpoints/deltas for Pi and OpenCode, compaction recovery, bounded/untrusted metadata projection, docs/ADR, unit/package/runtime smoke coverage, and full CI validation.

title: phux config reload silently resets status.position to bottom
description: reload.rs:91 (phux-client/src/attach/reload.rs): StatusBarPainter::new(bar, Position::default()) — the reload path hardcodes default position while the startup path uses cfg.status.position (driver.rs:4245). A user with position = "top" who runs phux config reload gets the bar jumping to bottom, silently, unrecoverable without detach/re-attach. tui.md:1124-1126 enumerates reload's documented non-coverage; status.position is not on that list, so this is a bug, not a limit.
design:
---

**Design resolution (stream A, 2026-08-01).** Verified: reload.rs:88 constructs StatusBarPainter::new(bar, Position::default()) while startup uses cfg.status.position.into() (driver.rs:4244-4246). Additional divergence found: reload composes the bar BEFORE loading plugin manifests, whereas startup runs plugin::merge_widget_contributions first (driver.rs:4233-4240) — reload appears to drop plugin-contributed status widgets; same bug class, in scope. Decomposed into A7: fix position, fix/verify widget-contribution parity, extract a shared compose_status_bar helper used by both paths, add a startup-vs-reload parity regression test.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: reload parity fix landed (wave 3).

title: [umbrella] Log discoverability: one canonical server log, phux logs verb, doctor path reporting
description:
Three log files exist; no command or doc ever prints any of their paths:

- Auto-spawned server: <socket_dir>/phux-server.log (server.rs:302-314) — in zero docs, printed by nothing.
- Service-installed server: $XDG_STATE_HOME/phux/server.log (service.rs:367,705). `phux service logs` tails only THIS file, so it errors for every auto-spawn user.
- Client: $XDG_STATE_HOME/phux/client-<pid>.log (phux-server/src/telemetry.rs:210-223); the doc comment admits "Public so a future phux subcommand can report the path" — no caller exists. Client panics are durable but unreachable.

docs/operations.md:80-84 concedes: no server status, no logs discovery verb. docs/architecture/process-model.md:24-30 flatly contradicts tui.md:558-563 about whether the state dir even exists (tui.md is right; process-model.md is stale).

Fix: (a) a `phux logs` verb (or `phux doctor --logs` section) that names every live log path and which process writes it; (b) doctor gains a check/section reporting log + state paths (doctor.rs:104-109 currently runs four checks, none mention logs); (c) every fatal client/attach error prints where the log went; (d) reconcile the two server log locations or teach service logs about both; (e) surface phux doctor in README.md and docs/QUICKSTART.md — it currently appears only in tui.md (grep-verified).
design: DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream C, 2026-08-01). Resolved: (1) canonical server log is $XDG_STATE_HOME/phux/server.log for BOTH spawn paths — auto-spawn (currently <socket_dir>/phux-server.log, server.rs:305-314) moves to the file the service unit already uses (service.rs:367, 705), via a single phux_server::telemetry::server_log_path() helper so service logs / phux logs / doctor can never disagree; startup line gains pid+version+socket. (2) phux logs is a new top-level verb: bare invocation prints the path inventory, --server/--client tail with -f/-n, --json for machines; phux service logs delegates. (3) doctor gains a logs check (doctor.rs:104-109 has four checks today, none names logs). (4) doctor and logs get surfaced in README and QUICKSTART (grep-verified zero doctor mentions today). (5) Stale process-model.md:22-34 state-dir/stderr claims fixed inside C1 (owner; stream F's F6 defers to it). Fatal-error log pointers implemented in C6 to keep the error-remedy pass in one place. Decomposed into C1, C2, C3; umbrella.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: canonical log, phux logs verb, doctor path reporting all landed.

title: Dead config keys: implement or delete defaults.shell / refresh-rate / log-filter; honor or drop the widget style promise
description:
Keys that parse, validate clean, echo back in config show, and do nothing:

- defaults.shell (schema.rs:96): consumed NOWHERE — server unconditionally uses $SHELL (phux-server/src/terminal_actor/spawn.rs:123,266). It is the FIRST LINE of the documented minimal config (tui.md:578) and tests/loader.rs:110 green-lights it.
- defaults.refresh-rate (tui.md:580): dead.
- defaults.log-filter: dead, undocumented, and its doc-comment claims $PHUX_LOG overrides it when PHUX_LOG is actually a log file path (main.rs:132).
- Widget `style` table: tui.md:1923-1925 promises every widget accepts style {fg,bg,bold,...}; NO factory reads it (time.rs:74-89, session_name.rs:65-99, cwd.rs:104-139, exit_status.rs, exec.rs). Opts are an open BTreeMap so it parses and renders unstyled. Only help-hints rejects unknown opts (help_hints.rs:33-38) — the inconsistency is itself a trap.
- session-name widget: tui.md:1911 documents a `format` opt that does not exist (session_name.rs:68-93 reads prefix/max-len).
- defaults.mouse works but is documented nowhere.

Fix: each key either gets implemented or deleted (with docs updated); widget opts move to closed structs or a per-factory unknown-opt warning surfaced via config check. Guiding rule: if `phux config check` says ok, the key must do something.
design:
---

**Design resolution (stream A, 2026-08-01) — per-key verdicts** (note: widget factories live in crates/phux-config/src/widget/widgets/, not phux-client; substance of every audit claim holds): defaults.shell (schema.rs:93-96) IMPLEMENT via a resolve_shell seam mirroring the defaults.term/apply_term precedent, threaded from the server's single config load. defaults.refresh-rate DELETE (no consumer exists; with deny_unknown_fields a stale config fails loudly with a located finding — the epic's contract). defaults.log-filter DELETE (zero consumers; its $PHUX_LOG doc claim is false — PHUX_LOG is a log-file path; filtering is RUST_LOG). defaults.mouse works — DOCUMENT in tui.md §12. Widget style table (tui.md:1927-1929 promise) IMPLEMENT UNIVERSALLY by hoisting style extraction into the registry build path (CellStyle already exists). session-name `format` opt IMPLEMENT. Widget opts CLOSE: generalize help_hints' unknown-opt rejection to every factory with did-you-mean; surface widget composition errors through config check. Decomposed into A8 (defaults truth) and A9 (widget closure + style). Umbrella.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: defaults truth (wave 3) + widget closure/style (wave 4).

title: [umbrella] Validate what parses: vocab registry, config check semantics, lenient resolver, honest error lines
description:
Everything that parses is assumed valid; three independent silent-no-op traps:

1. Typo'd action name: "x" = "kill-pain" parses (Action::Bare, schema.rs:369), passes config check, and the key does nothing — logged at tracing::debug only (input_dispatch.rs:2560-2562). The canonical 36-name list ACTION_NAMES already exists (input_dispatch.rs:1727) and is CI-enforced against the palette, but is not exposed to the validator.

2. One malformed chord disables EVERY keybinding including detach: driver.rs:3709-3716 — Resolver::new fails on first bad chord -> tracing::warn -> None -> no binding resolves. config check cannot catch it because chords are BTreeMap string keys.

3. Hooks fail open three ways (check.rs:329-334 asserts free-form hook keys are never flagged): typo'd event name ([[hooks.pane-exited]] vs real pane-exit, phux-server/src/hooks.rs:56) never fires; unknown `when` key never matches (hooks.rs:528); non-server-executable matched action consumes the event at debug level (hooks.rs:435-440). The six valid event names are consts at hooks.rs:54-64, surfaced nowhere.

Fix: teach phux config check (and resolver-build error paths) the action-name list, chord grammar, and hook event-name list; a bad chord must degrade to "this one binding is dead, loudly" not "all bindings are dead, silently". Also fix the on-screen config error (driver.rs:4259) to recommend `phux config check` instead of `phux config show`, and stop printing the fabricated 1:1 position (lib.rs:143) that check.rs:19-21 itself calls "worse than reporting none".
design:
---

**Design resolution (stream A, 2026-08-01).** Evidence verified: ACTION_NAMES at input_dispatch.rs:1726 (36 names, CI-synced); silent unhandled-action arm at input_dispatch.rs:2560-2562; Resolver::new fails whole on first bad chord and driver.rs:3709-3716 degrades to None = every binding dead including detach; unknown hook `when` key silently never matches (hooks.rs:519-530); non-`run` matched hook action consumes the event at debug! (hooks.rs:435-440); fabricated (1,1) span at lib.rs:130-131; wrong remedy `phux config show` at driver.rs:4256-4260. Architecture decision: **phux-config owns the validation vocabulary** (new crates/phux-config/src/vocab.rs). ACTION_NAMES moves INTO phux-config and is re-exported from input_dispatch.rs; hook event names move in from phux-server hooks.rs with re-exports; CI sync tests pin dispatch to vocab. No new crate, no codegen; did-you-mean is a ~25-line in-crate Levenshtein, no new dependency. Resolver policy: attach-time builds become lenient per-binding (new_lenient + diagnostics surfaced on the status bar); strict new stays for config check and reload (reload keeps all-or-nothing per tui.md:1119-1122). Decomposed into A2 (vocab), A3 (chords+actions in check), A4 (hooks in check + loud runtime warnings), A5 (lenient resolver), A6 (remedy + span honesty). Umbrella. Cross-stream: vocab is also consumed by stream F's generated action/widget/hook references (F3/F4).
close_reason: Umbrella complete: all five children (vocab, check semantics, hooks, lenient resolver, honest errors) landed across waves 1-3.

title: TUI failure surface: pane exit status, last-pane death, live reconnect indicator
description:
Three silent failure paths in the attach TUI, all evidence-verified:

1. Pane death is invisible. server_frame.rs:1169-1215 (phux-client): TerminalClosed receives exit_status, logs at tracing::info (file only), removes the PaneSlot, folds the layout. No toast, no "[exited 137]" placeholder, no status-bar line. When the last pane dies (1211-1216) the whole client exits with zero explanation — an OOM-killed shell looks like phux crashed.

2. Server crash = ~10 seconds of blank terminal. attach.rs:272 RECONNECT_DEADLINE=10s; attach.rs:335-341 prints "server restarted; re-attaching" only AFTER a successful reconnect; the alt screen is already torn down. No "reconnecting..." indicator during the window, and on failure the user gets the generic "connection closed by server before DETACHED" arm (mod.rs:2095-2097) with no log path, no doctor pointer.

3. The status-bar error_line mechanism exists (status_bar.rs:526-534) but is called for config errors only (driver.rs:4224,4251). Disconnect, reconnect-in-progress, pane death, degraded federation, take/give authority changes all have no user-facing representation.

Fix: exit-status toast + optional dead-pane placeholder; a reconnecting state that is visible while it happens; route lifecycle events through the existing error_line/toast machinery. docs/consumers/tui.md:28-40 calls the TUI the adoption wedge — the wire is the differentiator and the wire is precisely what has no failure UI.
design:
DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream B, 2026-08-01) — decomposed into B1/B2/B3; umbrella. Resolved: (1) Pane-death UX is a transient STATUS-BAR NOTICE, not a modal and not a dead-pane placeholder (placeholder rejected: layout is a shared metadata envelope — a client-local dead leaf desyncs siblings and PTY winsizes; a server-side dead leaf is a wire change out of scope). Text 'pane <label>: exited N' / 'killed (signal or unknown)'; suppressed for exit 0 and client-initiated kill-pane; 7 s newest-wins slot. (2) Last-pane death: run_* entry points return Result<AttachEnd, AttachError> (Detached | LastPaneClosed { exit_status }); the CLI prints a one-line explanation on the cooked terminal after teardown; process exit stays 0. (3) Reconnect: NO alt-screen re-entry — RawModeGuard drops on unwind (driver.rs:1258), so the 10 s wait (attach.rs:318-344) runs cooked; honest design is a live stderr countdown plus a post-reconnect status-bar notice inside the next attach (the current eprintln at attach.rs:337 is instantly alt-screened over). Failure distinguishes socket-unlinked vs timeout and names phux doctor. (4) General mechanism: StatusBarPainter gains a transient Notice slot riding the existing 1 s status_tick; persistent error_line outranks it; FrameOutcome gains notices: Vec<Notice>; first consumer is input-authority transitions. No wire changes — TERMINAL_CLOSED already carries exit_status (frame.rs:2105-2110).

FINALIZER AMENDMENT (2026-08-01): the bead's five enumerated lifecycle events must ALL map to a surface. Degraded federation was orphaned; B1 now carries it as the Notice slot's second consumer (degraded-federation transitions push a Warn notice, server_frame-tested). C5's phux status degradation line remains the CLI view, not a substitute for the in-TUI representation.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: notice mechanism, pane death, reconnect window all landed (waves 1,2,6).

title: Server silently swallows a broken config.toml and reverts to defaults
description:
crates/phux/src/commands/server.rs:113-148 reads history-limit, cwd-inheritance, term, window-size, and the entire hook catalog via five consecutive config_loader::load().map_or_else(|_| default, ...) calls. A single typo in config.toml silently disables every configured hook and reverts scrollback/TERM/window-size policy, then the server prints its normal "listening on ..." banner. Contrast server.rs:153-158 where connector registry failure correctly aborts loudly, and the client attach path which at least prints one line (attach.rs:110-113).

Also: config is read from disk five separate times in ~35 lines, so an edit mid-startup yields a torn read.

Fix: load once, bind once. On failure, print the config-check-style error to stderr (and the server log) and state explicitly which defaults are in effect. Never revert silently.
design:
---

**Design resolution (stream A, 2026-08-01).** Audit correction: a malformed config.toml already kills the server today via the fatal connector-registry read (server.rs:153-158) with a misattributed error; the five earlier reads (server.rs:113-148) silently default and misattribute every config error to the connector registry. Resolved design: load config exactly once; a broken config is fatal at server start with the real error and the remedy `run: phux config check`, written to both stderr and the server log via tracing::error (auto-spawn nulls stdio, so the log line is the durable trace). Missing file stays fine (loader.rs:71-77 returns defaults on NotFound). Degrade-and-continue rejected: the connector security stance already makes any parse error fatal, and one load cannot scope an error to a section. Decomposed into A1 (single load + loud fatal) and A8 (defaults.shell rides A1's struct). This bead is now an umbrella.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: single child 1.1 landed (wave 1).

title: [epic] UX: it just works — never silent, one grammar, visible at the moment of need
description:
Full-surface UX audit (2026-08-01, three parallel deep audits: CLI ergonomics, config surface, onboarding/visibility) found that phux's UX foundations are genuinely excellent but exist as islands: phux doctor, phux config check, config layering with provenance, output_hygiene.rs, the broken-pipe discipline, the first-run overlay. The product-level failures are four systemic patterns, not missing features:

1. SILENCE. Errors, dead keys, typos, and pane death all no-op invisibly: server swallows a broken config.toml with zero output (server.rs:113-148); a typo'd action name logs at debug (input_dispatch.rs:2560); one malformed chord disables ALL keybindings including detach (driver.rs:3709); a dying pane discards its exit status (server_frame.rs:1169-1216); server crash = 10s blank screen (attach.rs:272-341).

2. INVISIBILITY. The good tools are never pointed to at the moment of need: doctor appears in zero READMEs/quickstarts; three different log files exist and no command or doc ever prints any path; the on-screen config error names the wrong recovery command (driver.rs:4259 says "phux config show", the diagnostic tool is "config check").

3. INCONSISTENCY. 89 invocation paths with per-command grammar: --socket copy-pasted 36 times and not global; --json on ~32 verbs with no shorthand and no error-path contract; ls/list/rm/remove alias roulette across 8 registries; two split-direction flag styles (one of which is parsed and discarded, main.rs:364); four near-duplicate concept pairs (enroll vs satellite enroll, remote vs satellite, pair vs relay pair, workspace vs worktree).

4. DOCS DRIFT. CONFIG.md says reload does not exist (it ships); tui.md promises a widget style table no factory reads; README claims scrollback search that has no action; defaults.shell is the first line of the documented minimal config and is consumed nowhere.

Design principle for every child issue: the failure path IS the product. Simplicity means one grammar, and every error names its own remedy. Builds on phux-q9wj (CLI and API surface polish, 3/4 done); supersedes its altitude.

Full audit reports preserved in the three child-issue descriptions and session transcript 3bedc523.
design:
---

**Stream G landing sequence (planning resolution, 2026-08-01).** The epic lands in dependency waves closed by stream-G integration gates: never-silent failure surface (.1-.6) gated by G2; one-grammar + host namespace (.7 .8 .12) gated by G3; help/discoverability/docs+generated reference (.9 .10 .11) gated by G4. After the grammar wave, a deprecation-alias audit test (crates/phux/tests/deprecated_aliases.rs) pins every hidden alias, its deprecation note, and its absence from help/completions, bidirectionally against the clap tree. A scripted failure-UX dogfood lands as crates/phux/tests/failure_ux_e2e.rs in the `just e2e` PR lane (per scripts/check-e2e-lanes.sh), so the new failure UX is CI-enforced, not a release ritual. Release is a release-please minor bump (0.6.0 -> 0.7.0, automatic from feat commits under bump-minor-pre-major): run scripts/release-preflight.sh, undraft the release PR to run CI, merge; then `gh release edit` prepends the UX story + deprecation table (release.yml only uploads assets, never rewrites the body). Epic close: bd close sweep, bd remember entries (vocab location, reference-generation mechanism, alias contract, failure-UX lane), vision.md remaining-work reality check. Merge protocol throughout: branch per slice, rebase + ff-only, conventional commits, `just ci` green before every merge.
notes: EXECUTION IN PROGRESS (2026-08-01, session 3bedc523): user ordered full autonomous execution to completion. Wave-by-wave workflow loop; playbook + graph at scratchpad ux-epic/ (execution-playbook.md). Wave 1 = phux-i0e8.1.1, .3.1, .3.4, .2.1 branching from origin/main 6770f366.
close_reason: EPIC COMPLETE (v0.11.0, 2026-08-03): 52 tasks, 13 umbrellas, 14 merged PRs. Never silent: config/actions/chords/hooks validated with did-you-mean, pane death + reconnect visible, every error names its remedy, failure-UX e2e lane in CI. One grammar: global --socket, JSON error contract, alias parity, --split, phux host namespace with audited deprecations. Visible: status/logs/doctor triad. Zero drift: all reference docs generated from the binary with byte-exact CI gates.

title: Fix PR 316 federation test failure
description: PR 316 fails CI in phux-server::hub_relay_federation::aggregated_list_merges_local_and_satellite_terminals_and_degrades. Reproduce the failure, correct the test or implementation, run relevant quality gates, update the PR branch, and enable merge queue/automerge.
close_reason: PR 316 CI repaired, validated locally and remotely, and merged

title: Snapshot replay drops mouse-reporting DEC modes, breaking scroll in TUIs after attach
description: The TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT epilogue replayed bracketed paste, focus events and the alt-screen bits but never the mouse-reporting modes (9/1000/1002/1003, 1005/1006/1015/1016, 1007). The client gates wheel handling on its own libghostty mirror, so a mirror seeded from such a snapshot believes no program wants the mouse and downgrades the wheel to arrow keys. Repro: opencode in a phux pane -- scrolling moved the editor cursor instead of the message list.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #314: snapshot epilogue now replays the mouse-reporting DEC modes (9/1000/1002/1003, 1005/1006/1015/1016, 1007), and ReferenceCursorMode tracks the same bits so the per-tick diff path re-emits on a bare mouse-mode toggle.

title: Headless geometry: agents cannot set a pane size without a real PTY
description:
There is no way to set a pane's size without attaching a real terminal. phux new has no size flag, phux snapshot --rendered --cols/--rows does not persist (verified: pane stayed 80x24 after a 120x40 rendered read), and there is no phux resize verb.

This bit twice building phux rec: the demo asset is stuck at 80x24, and the non-resize regression test has to stand up a full portable-pty attach purely to obtain a pane whose size differs from the 80x24 a mistaken attach would impose -- otherwise the test resizes an 80x24 pane to 80x24 and passes vacuously.

For a project whose pitch is that agents are first-class users, agents cannot set a terminal's size. Proposed: a phux resize TARGET COLSxROWS verb and/or --cols/--rows on phux new, with the interaction against the attached-client WindowSize policy (schema.rs WindowSize::Smallest) thought through and specced -- that policy is why this is a design question and not a one-line flag.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: Conformance test: the three libghostty cell projections must agree
description:
The libghostty snapshot -> RenderedFrame projection now exists three times: crates/phux-client/src/attach/render.rs, crates/phux-server/src/grid/synthesizer.rs, and crates/phux-record/src/replay.rs.

The duplication is a DELIBERATE, documented tradeoff (a shared home would force phux-core to depend on libghostty, which is worse), so this issue is not 'deduplicate them'. It is that three copies which must agree cell-for-cell have nothing enforcing it, and divergence surfaces as 'the recording does not match the screen' or 'the agent sees different cells than the human' -- the bug class nobody notices for months.

Work: a conformance test that feeds one corpus of VT bytes (SGR truecolor and palette, wide CJK plus spacer tails, combining marks, alt screen, scroll regions, DECAWM wrap, cursor states) through all three projections and asserts identical output. Where they cannot be identical, assert the difference explicitly so it is a decision rather than a drift.

Consider afterwards whether a thin phux-vt-project crate between phux-core and libghostty is worth the refactor; the test is valuable either way and is the cheap half.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: Shared scripted-server test harness so fakes cannot lie about frame order
description:
Unit-test fake servers are hand-written per module, so each one encodes what its author believed the protocol does. That is the same belief that produces the bug, so the fake cannot catch it.

Evidence: 17 phux rec unit tests passed against a completely non-functional feature because the fake answered COMMAND_RESULT before the priming snapshot, while the real server does the opposite.

Work, cheapest first:
1. Extract one shared scripted_server into a test-support module, with the reference server's frame ORDER encoded once (snapshot before ack on ATTACH_TERMINAL, etc.).
2. Migrate the per-module fakes to it.
3. Consider golden frame traces: capture real server responses once into fixtures and replay them, so a fake that diverges from the reference implementation fails. Bigger lift; decide after 1 and 2.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: Add Connection::request so COMMAND callers cannot swallow interleaved frames
description:
Connection exposes send()/recv() only, so every COMMAND caller hand-rolls 'loop until my request_id returns'. The server legitimately interleaves: handle_attach_terminal pushes TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT before the COMMAND_RESULT ack. A caller that discards non-matching frames loses data that is never re-sent.

This is not hypothetical. It shipped as a bug in phux rec (fixed in PR #306): captures came back as a 0x0 grid with no opening screen, and all 17 unit tests passed because the scripted fake answered ack-first.

Work:
1. Add Connection::request(cmd) -> Result<(CommandResult, Vec<FrameKind>)> that returns interleaved frames instead of eating them. Callers physically cannot forget what they did not ask to drop.
2. AUDIT every existing COMMAND caller for the same swallow: GetScreen, GetTerminalState, AcquireInput, ReleaseInput, SignalTerminal, KillTerminal(s), DetachClients, PutFile, SubscribeTerminalEvents. Report which ones discard frames and whether the server can interleave on that path. This audit is the point of the issue; the helper is the easy half.
3. Migrate callers, and document the interleave contract on Connection itself.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: BUG: PTY input writer corrupts or dies under large paste load
description: Live phux-mobile image-upload experiments over INPUT_PASTE reproduced nondeterministic byte corruption in tiny 1.8 KiB base64 payloads (first divergence around byte 1150/1450) and the server log 'pty writer: write failed; pane input is now dead' under load. A 1.9 MiB JPEG also remained in canonical-mode ingest after 24s. ADR-0059 PutFile bypasses this path for file upload, but large interactive pastes still traverse the PTY input writer and may corrupt or permanently kill pane input. Reproduce with repeated multi-KiB trusted INPUT_PASTE / APPLY_INPUT batches against a checksum-reading fixture; fix write/flush/backpressure ownership so bytes are ordered and the writer survives transient pressure.
close_reason:
Resolved by decomposition (option A). RCA split this into three distinct defects; every part is now fixed or tracked separately.

1. 'dies under load' -> REAL BUG, fixed. Writer broke on any io::Error with no errno discrimination and never restarted, so a routine child exit permanently killed pane input. Fixed in phux-oxd7 / PR #318 (4bbe113e).

2. 'corrupts' -> WORKS AS SPECIFIED. A single INPUT_PASTE event is already atomic (one contiguous Vec, one write_all). Corruption only appears when a consumer splits ONE logical payload across MULTIPLE fire-and-forget events, and L1 SPEC section 9 explicitly makes those droppable ('a full mailbox drops the event but still acks OK'). The spec never promised cross-event delivery or ordering. ADR-0053 APPLY_INPUT (acknowledged, reconnect-safe) and ADR-0059 PutFile exist for exactly this; the original reporter, phux-mobile image upload, has already moved to PutFile. Making fire-and-forget atomic would put backpressure on the hot keystroke path -- a latency regression for phux's core purpose -- to buy correctness a different verb already provides. The defensible complaint was the SILENCE, not the semantics: both drop sites were raised to warn!/error! in PR #318.

3. 'canonical-mode ingest stuck after 24s' -> separate mechanism, tracked as phux-mjmc (P2). Empirically reproduced: MAX_CANON wedge, a hang rather than corruption.

Residual guidance gap filed separately.

title: send-keys TARGET "text" Enter does not submit in codex; Enter must be a separate call
description:
Observed while capturing codex detection fixtures. 'phux send-keys --socket S cx "prompt text" Enter' places the text in codex's composer but does NOT submit — the composer still shows the text and no turn starts. Sending 'phux send-keys --socket S cx Enter' as its own call immediately submits.

Likely the same class herdr hit (their 0.7.5 notes: 'Named agent prompts now honor live bracketed-paste mode before sending Enter'). Probable cause: the text is delivered as a paste/bracketed run and the trailing Enter is coalesced into it, so codex sees a literal newline inside the paste rather than a submit key.

Matters because it is the documented one-liner for driving an agent from a script, and it silently half-works: the text lands, so a caller sees no error and waits forever for a turn that never started. Worth an e2e test against a real agent TUI.

title: Native agent-session restore: persist and replay agent resume identity across pane restart
description: A phux-launched agent may carry a provider-native resume identity. Persist that identity with exact Terminal and integration provenance, include it in workspace archives, and reconstruct the provider's safe structured argv when workspace restore recreates the pane. Provider semantics remain client/plugin-owned L3 policy; the server only transports and atomically stores bounded opaque record bytes, without interpreting native identities.
design: Use a dedicated terminal-scoped, versioned L3 restore record rather than overloading `phux.agent/v1.session` (a free-form fleet label) or plugin-global link state. The record contains exact plugin/integration ownership plus an opaque, bounded native identity. The launch client carries the encoded record in additive optional `SPAWN_TERMINAL` field 9 so the server can install it atomically in the same state transaction that creates the local Terminal; ordinary metadata GET/SET remains the durable readback surface and the server never interprets provider semantics. Create-without-attach carries the same bytes in its nonce-correlated `phux.session.create/v1` request and installs them while seeding the pane. Workspace save copies only validated records read from exact local TerminalIds and verifies the terminal set did not change across collection. Restore re-resolves a unique enabled plugin/integration owner before reconstructing structured argv. Archive format advances to schema v2 while parsing schema v1 through an explicit compatibility path.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Integration templates expose a typed, validated native-session policy with a bounded identity source and structured fresh/resume argv; the placeholder occupies exactly one whole argv element, substitution never invokes a shell, and option-shaped identities are rejected.
2. `phux launch` captures a non-empty provider-native identity only from the integration's declared source and carries a bounded, versioned Terminal-scoped record atomically with the exact local `SPAWN_TERMINAL`; it never guesses from focused state or a global link.
3. `phux workspace save` collects each local pane's valid restore record into archive schema v2 and refuses an inconsistent snapshot if the local Terminal set changes during collection. Schema-v1 archives remain readable only through the explicit compatibility path; v2 fails closed for older readers.
4. `phux workspace restore` selects the archived preferred pane, re-resolves exactly one current enabled `(plugin_id, integration_id)` owner, validates provenance and bounds, uses the current integration working-directory policy, and replays the native identity as structured argv. Existing session names remain skipped without launching anything.
5. Missing records preserve non-agent restore behavior. Malformed, oversized, ambiguous-owner, unavailable-integration, option-shaped, stale, and ownership-mismatched data fail clearly before that session is spawned; there is no silent fresh-agent fallback or cross-pane/session identity reuse.
6. Protocol compatibility is additive: no new frame type/tag or protocol-version break; optional `SPAWN_TERMINAL` field 9 is ignored by older servers, and the versioned L3 metadata convention remains the durable consumer surface. Satellite spawns reject local provenance.
7. Session creation results are nonce-correlated and one-shot; failed/competing creates cannot reuse another caller's TerminalId. Provenance is installed in the same server state transaction that creates/interns the pane and is removed by normal Terminal reaping.
8. Deterministic tests cover template validation/substitution, unique owner resolution, wire compatibility, exact-Terminal atomic persistence and bounds, archive v1 compatibility/v2 round-trip, restart/replay argv, existing-session skip, stale ownership, and snapshot consistency. The real restore smoke observes resumed argv after server restart.
9. Formatting, focused tests, full `just ci`, docs checks, and required repository gates pass; review findings and CI failures are fixed before merge.
notes: Implementation complete: Terminal-scoped versioned native resume records, schema-v2 archives, current-policy argv/env/cwd reconstruction, atomic spawn provenance, owner-only bounded nonce results, batch preflight for older servers, rollback/confirmation, and stale/ambiguous ownership rejection. Validation: focused restart/replay E2E passed; focused security tests passed; just ci passed (3079/3079 tests, fmt, clippy, docs, deny). Independent correctness and security re-reviews report no remaining actionable findings.

title: watch consumers are starved of dirty/idle events unless a StateSync consumer exists

Repro: 'phux watch --json' on a fresh pane, drive output with send-keys — bell/title_changed/pane_closed flow, dirty arrives at most once, idle never. Either tick_emit should maintain the dirty/idle bookkeeping independently of StateSync negotiation, or agents.md must stop advertising dirty/idle as generally available — any wait/watch consumer hoping to observe quiescence without polling is affected. title: Mouse input never reaches pane apps: encoder emits zero bytes without EncoderSize; scrolling dead in phux
description: User-visible: cannot scroll inside phux panes at all; worst in mouse-tracking apps (Claude Code sets ?1000h/?1002h/?1003h/?1006h — probed 2026-07-14) which never receive wheel events. Root cause chain: (1) PerTerminalMouseEncoder::encode never configures libghostty mouse EncoderSize; ghostty's encoder emits ZERO bytes for every event when cell geometry is unset (proven by probe test: click and wheel encode to empty against a full-tracking terminal; with EncoderSize set the same events encode to correct SGR). service_input then drops them at the 'encoded to zero bytes' branch — so ALL mouse input (clicks included) is silently discarded server-side, violating docs/spec/input.md §3.2 which mandates setting EncoderSize from Terminal/cell geometry. (2) The TUI client sends pane-local CELL indices in INPUT_MOUSE but spec §3.1 defines wire positions as Terminal-local surface PIXELS (cell_index x cell_size for cell-quantized clients) — must convert at the send boundary or fixed server quantization mis-lands clicks. (3) Alt-screen apps WITHOUT mouse tracking (less, vim) get a local scroll_viewport that no-ops (alt screen has no scrollback); needs xterm alternate-scroll: wheel -> arrow keys when alt screen + mode 1007 (libghostty defaults 1007 ON, probed). Primary-screen local scrollback path (input_dispatch.rs:683) is sound. Fix: server sets EncoderSize (cell_px from actor, cols/rows from terminal); client converts cells->pixels using host cell geometry (fallback 8x16 == server DEFAULT_CELL_PX); client synthesizes Up/Down INPUT_KEY x3 for alt-screen+1007 non-tracking wheel.
close_reason: Closed

title: Server does not inject PHUX_SOCKET into spawned panes; in-pane phux CLI silently hits the default server
description:
The server injects PHUX_TERMINAL_ID into every pane it spawns (crates/phux-server/src/terminal_actor/spawn.rs:170 apply_terminal_id) so an in-pane process can 'self-target on the phux wire with zero configuration'. But it does not inject the socket it is listening on. So an in-pane 'phux <verb>' on a server bound to a non-default socket resolves default_socket_path() and talks to a DIFFERENT server.

Observed live: a pane spawned by a server on /tmp/pvfy.sock ran a bare 'phux agent set --name reviewer'; the write landed on the default-socket server's @1 -- a live pane in an unrelated session -- with no error. The pane's own server never saw it.

Zero-config self-targeting is only true on the default socket. PHUX_TERMINAL_ID names WHICH pane but not WHICH server, and the pair is what identifies a pane.

Fix: inject PHUX_SOCKET=<the server's listening socket> alongside PHUX_TERMINAL_ID at both spawn sites (crates/phux-server/src/runtime/commands.rs:101 and :181). Blocker: ServerState/SharedState does not currently carry the socket path (crates/phux-server/src/state/mod.rs:96), so it needs threading through seed_session_with_pty{,_and_colors} / spawn_pane_with_pty{,_and_colors} or storing on state at startup. Also update the apply_terminal_id doc comment, which currently overclaims 'zero configuration'.
close_reason: Landed on main via integration train PR #255 (rebase-merge, commits 8a4097e4..b5f72d15)

title: TUI: attention indicator + jump-to-next-attention
description:
The human half of 'pop over to it': you are working in one pane, an agent elsewhere gets blocked, you see it, you press a key, you are there. Then you press another key and you are back (which is why the '=' / last-focused bug matters).

There is more to build on here than you would expect: 'phux agent list' already infers per-pane agent state (working / blocked / idle, with a confidence score and a reason -- verified live: it correctly identified a blocked Claude in pane 22). There is already a focus-pane action addressing (window index, DFS leaf ordinal), described in the code as being 'used by the agent-fleet dashboard' (input_dispatch.rs:2029). Find that dashboard and build on it rather than beside it.
design:
Files: the action table -- actions are STRING-NAMED, not an enum: ACTION_NAMES at attach/input_dispatch.rs:1502-1534, dispatch is 'match resolved.action.as_str()' in run_action (:1548), and the palette/help metadata registry is attach/action_registry.rs:139-292. Default keybindings live in crates/phux-config/src/default.toml (prefix C-a, :82; existing pane bindings :96-116). Status bar is the natural home for the indicator -- note a recent commit already moved the status bar out of the sidebar's columns, so look at how it composes today.

Keep the jump ADVISORY (the human presses the key) unless ADR-0044's opt-in directed-focus config is on. The whole point of the ADR's focus/attention distinction is that the human stays in control of their own viewport by default.
acceptance_criteria: With an agent blocked in another pane, the status bar shows it, one keybinding jumps there, and one jumps back. Works with several agents blocked at once (cycle). Bindings documented in docs/consumers/tui.md:429-438 and defaulted in default.toml.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed.

title: Attention channel: an agent raises 'I need you, at pane N'
description:
The mechanism behind 'hey, pop over to it.' Per ADR-0044, this is a notification with an actionable target -- NOT shared focus, NOT a viewport yank.

Most of this may already exist. AgentEvent::Asked ships today (ADR-0035/0036), carries {id, question, suggestions, elapsed_seconds}, is emitted both from the REPORT_ASKED command (runtime/commands.rs:2098) and from an OSC-title sentinel (terminal_actor/mod.rs:1460-1470), and the TUI ALREADY handles it (server_frame.rs:1203). 'phux ask' is already a CLI verb and 'phux_ask' is already an MCP tool. So the honest first question for this bead is: is 'agent wants attention' just Asked, or is it genuinely a different event? ADR-0044 decides; implement what it says.
design:
If a new AgentEvent tag is needed, next free is 0x0b (frame.rs:424-458). Files: the AgentEvent enum (frame.rs:1373), EVENT_TAG_* const, encode_agent_event (:3610), decode_agent_event (:3702), the proptest roundtrip + insta golden-byte snapshot (crates/phux-protocol/tests/), an emitter, and the hub relay forward path (hub/relay.rs:956-965).

TWO TRAPS:
1. There are TWO parallel event fan-out paths and they are NOT unified. Path A (SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS -> broadcast_event, runtime/client.rs:1227) carries Bell/Asked/TitleChanged. Path B (SUBSCRIBE_TERMINAL_EVENTS -> the actor's own subscriber list, terminal_actor/mod.rs:1546) carries TerminalControl. A new event must pick one, or wire both -- pick wrong and the TUI never sees it.
2. Consumers match AgentEvent non-exhaustively, so a new variant compiles everywhere and is SILENTLY IGNORED. The three places that must actually learn about it: phux-client/src/watch.rs:72, phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs:1171-1255 (the TUI), phux-mcp/src/tools.rs:412-441 (the JSON projection agents read).
NOTE: adding an AgentEvent tag IS a wire change (spec + CHANGELOG + version bump), unlike the layout work. If ADR-0044 lets us reuse Asked instead, this bead gets much cheaper -- prefer that if it is honest.
acceptance_criteria: An agent can raise attention against a pane and an attached TUI learns about it. Old clients skip an unknown tag rather than breaking (AgentEvent::Unknown, frame.rs:1481). If the wire changed: docs/spec updated, CHANGELOG appended, PROTOCOL_VERSION bumped, golden snapshots regenerated.
close_reason: Already implemented by AgentEvent::Asked across CLI, MCP, shared client, wire, and TUI attention fold; ADR-0049 selects this advisory channel without new wire.

title: MCP parity: expose the full control surface, not a subset
description:
The MCP adapter exposes 11 tools; the CLI exposes 26 verbs. MCP is missing, among others: launch (the agent launcher -- the single most important verb for this epic), spawn, signal, take/give (input lease), tag, rename, agent (identity/state inference), and the new spatial verbs from this epic (focus, split, move).

Net effect today: an LLM connected over MCP is strictly WEAKER than the same LLM shelling out to the CLI through Bash. That is backwards -- ADR-0022 says the CLI is the stable contract and MCP is 'a thin adapter over the same structured surface', so the adapter should not be a lossy subset of it.

Deliberately ONE bead, not several: every MCP tool edits the same json! catalog array (tools.rs:64-172), the same dispatch match (:184-197), AND a test asserting the EXACT ORDERED vec of tool names (:717-729). Parallel beads here are a guaranteed three-way conflict on one array. Do them all in one coherent pass.
design:
Per-tool recipe (from the anatomy inventory): catalog entry in the json! array; dispatch arm; handler fn (or its own module with schema()/call(), mirroring ask_tool.rs -- preferred for anything non-trivial, and then a mod decl in main.rs:37-42); add the name to the ORDERED test vec at :717-729; extend the required-args test at :781-823.

CRITICAL: the handler must call the SHARED phux-client fn, not re-implement the CLI's logic. The adapter has already drifted by duplicating: MCP's phux_kill (tools.rs:346) omits the CLI's per-pane KILL_TERMINAL fallback and never fetches the tag index; MCP's create_session duplicates the SESSION_CREATE_KEY metadata dance; run_nonce() is a copy-paste 'matching phux run's run_nonce'. Do not add nine more copies. Depends on the get_state de-duplication bead for the same reason.

Docs: docs/consumers/mcp.md:102 hardcodes the tool count IN PROSE ('Eleven tools') -- bump it. Add a section 3.N per tool (model: 3.7 phux_kill at :219-231). Update the name-for-name CLI mapping at :352-364.

Also fix the two known CLI/MCP divergences while you are in here (docs/consumers/mcp.md:116-121, :178-185): phux_ls returns raw wire fields (window_count/attached_client_count) where the CLI projects to windows/attached, and on run timeout MCP returns {outcome:'timed_out'} in the body where the CLI emits no JSON and exits 125. Parsers are currently not portable between the two surfaces, which defeats the point of a 'thin adapter'.
acceptance_criteria: Every CLI control verb has an MCP tool, or a documented reason it does not (attach and server are legitimately TUI/daemon-only). Handlers share phux-client fns with the CLI -- no new duplication, and the existing kill/create_session/run_nonce duplication is retired. Tool count in mcp.md prose is correct. An LLM on MCP is no longer weaker than the same LLM on Bash.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed.

title: Placement on spawn and launch: put the agent's pane where the caller asked
description:
The payoff bead for the whole epic. 'phux launch claude-code --target . --split vertical --ratio 0.3' -- go get an agent, put it beside me.

Today launch/spawn have zero placement control and land the new pane by horizontally splitting whatever pane happens to have been created first in the window (see the spawn-placement bug). Fixing that bug makes the default sane; this bead makes placement explicit and callable.
design:
Depends on the spawn-placement bug fix and on layout_ops. Per the epic's thesis and that bug's design note, STRONGLY prefer keeping SPAWN_TERMINAL geometry-free on the wire and doing placement as a follow-up L3 layout write from the caller -- that keeps this epic at zero wire changes. If you conclude the wire genuinely needs placement fields, that is a spec change (docs/spec/L1.md + docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md + PROTOCOL_VERSION bump + the 5 silent '_' match arms including relay.rs:1407 route_to_satellite) and it needs its own ADR -- do not do it quietly inside this bead.

Files: crates/phux/src/commands/launch.rs and the spawn path. Note launch resolves an integration template from an enabled plugin (examples/plugins/agent-tools/ has claude-code/codex/gemini-cli) and routes the agent through an identity wrapper so the pane self-declares its phux.agent/v1 identity (ADR-0040) -- do not break that; it is what makes 'phux agent list' able to say 'pane 22 is a blocked claude'.
acceptance_criteria: phux launch claude-code --target . --split vertical lands the agent pane exactly where asked. The launched pane still self-declares its agent identity (phux agent list shows it). Same for phux spawn. e2e test.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed. Remaining dependency beads track broader/general follow-up, not this delivered scope.

title: phux-client/src/layout_ops.rs -- shared L3 layout envelope read/mutate/write
description:
THE load-bearing module of this epic. Every spatial verb (focus, split, move, swap, and placement on spawn/launch) is a wrapper over it, and both the CLI and MCP call it -- so it must land before the verb fan-out.

What it does: read phux.tui.layout/v1/<session> via GET_METADATA, decode the v2 envelope ({version, windows:[{name, root: LayoutNode, focused_terminal}], focused_window_index} -- phux-client-core/src/layout/mod.rs:15-17), apply a mutation to the binary split tree, re-encode, write back via SET_METADATA. The server broadcasts METADATA_CHANGED and attached clients re-render. Zero wire change.

The tree operations mostly EXIST ALREADY and must be reused, not reinvented: phux-client-core/src/layout/mod.rs has the envelope + set_ratio_at (:621); phux-core/src/window.rs has split/kill_pane/seed_layout/focus_direction (:281-304, a genuinely good directional-navigation walk). NOTE the phux-core copy is near-dead (the server populates Window.layout but never runs it in response to user splits -- the live tree is the client's), so read it for the algorithm and be deliberate about which crate the shared logic should live in. Also note phux-core/src/window.rs:12-23 explicitly warns 'do not reintroduce a parallel implementation' of tiling -- honor that; do not add a fourth LayoutNode.

Envelope v1 ({version, root, focus}) is still decoded for back-compat (layout/mod.rs:51-54) -- preserve that.
design: Design the mutation API around what the verbs need: focus(target), split(target, dir, ratio) -> new leaf slot, move/swap(a, b), close(target). Read-modify-write on shared metadata is a lost-update race if two writers interleave; state the concurrency story explicitly (last-write-wins is probably fine and is what the TUI does today, but SAY so rather than discovering it). Decide up front whether these live in phux-client (alongside snapshot/send_keys/run/wait/watch -- the de-facto shared surface both consumers use) or phux-client-core (where the tree types already are). Do NOT put them on the Agent facade; it is being deleted.
acceptance_criteria: One module, unit-tested against envelope fixtures (v1 and v2), that both a CLI verb and an MCP tool can call. No new LayoutNode type. No wire change.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed.

title: ADR-0049: agent-directed navigation and attention
description:
The decision that unblocks everything spatial in this epic. It must settle, in the ADR's own controlled vocabulary:

1. FOCUS STAYS CLIENT-LOCAL. Reaffirm ADR-0019 section 6. The server does not track which pane a human looks at. This ADR must not be read as reopening it.

2. ATTENTION IS A NEW, DISTINCT CONCEPT. An agent raising 'I am blocked, look at pane 7' is a notification with an actionable target, not shared focus. ADR-0019 rejected CONVERGENT focus (all clients yanked to the same pane, tmate-mirror-style); it never considered advisory attention. Name that distinction explicitly so the next reader does not think we snuck focus back in.

3. WHAT CARRIES ATTENTION? Two candidates, pick one and say why:
   (a) A new AgentEvent tag (next free is 0x0b). This is the ONLY extension seam with a real, tested forward-compat story: unknown tags decode to AgentEvent::Unknown and are skipped by old clients (frame.rs:1481). Delivery is already gated by opt-in subscription (SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS), which IS the de facto capability negotiation -- there is no ServerFeature bit mechanism, it is spec'd vapor with zero Rust. The attached TUI already subscribes server-wide (driver.rs:1821). Precedent: ADR-0035/0036 Asked did exactly this.
   (b) Reuse AgentEvent::Asked, which already ships, already carries a question + suggestions, and which the TUI ALREADY renders (server_frame.rs:1203). Cheapest possible path; the question is whether 'blocked on a question' and 'wants attention' are really the same event.

4. DIRECTED FOCUS: opt-in or not at all. If an agent can move a human's viewport, that must be config-gated (e.g. focus-follows-agent = false by default), never the default. NOTE: depending on the spike's answer, an agent may ALREADY be able to do this today by writing phux.tui.layout/v1 metadata -- if so, that is a latent capability that this ADR must either bless with a gate or explicitly close.

5. NO WIRE CHANGE FOR LAYOUT. Record the finding that split/focus/move ride L3 metadata (ADR-0019's own mechanism), so this epic does not touch docs/spec, does not bump PROTOCOL_VERSION, and does not need capability negotiation. That is a load-bearing constraint and it should be written down, because the obvious instinct (add a FOCUS_PANE command) is both a wire change AND a re-litigation of ADR-0019.
design:
Follow the strict template in docs/CONVENTIONS.md: controlled Status vocabulary, ~150-line cap. Cite ADR-0019 (the constraint), ADR-0012 (the split tree), ADR-0035/0036 (the Asked precedent), ADR-0033 (input authority -- the existing precedent for the server arbitrating between a human and an agent contending over one pane, and a good model for how the loser learns the world changed).

RECOMMENDATION going in (the ADR may overturn it, but argue against it explicitly): attention is advisory by default -- agent raises a flag, the TUI shows an indicator, the human presses a key to jump. Directed focus is opt-in config. This is ADR-0019-compatible, it is better UX than having your viewport yanked while you are mid-thought in another pane, and it degrades gracefully when nobody is attached.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-0044 merged, passing just docs-check, with a Status line. Answers all five questions above. Every downstream bead in this epic can cite it instead of re-deriving the constraint.
notes: 2026-07-15: ADR number corrected after duplicate ADR-0035 audit. Drag-to-resize is now ADR-0048; client-local focus/advisory attention is ADR-0049. ADR-0049 reuses terminal-scoped AgentEvent::Asked for the evidenced blocked-question attention case, keeps directed focus default-off, and leaves layout operations on L3 metadata with no wire change.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green foundation train PR #243 (combined CI passed).

title: Every spawn hardcodes a horizontal 0.5 split of Window.active -- agent panes land in the wrong place
description:
crates/phux-core/src/registry.rs:139: new_terminal() unconditionally does w.split(t, terminal_id, SplitDir::Horizontal, 0.5) against Window.active. SplitDir::Vertical is unreachable from any spawn; there is no wire path to it. There is no window/geometry/position argument on SPAWN_TERMINAL at all (frame.rs:1958-1998 -- no window id, no direction, no ratio, no anchor).

Worse: Window.active is NEVER updated by client focus. Nothing in phux-server ever writes Session.active / Window.active except structural create/remove in phux-core::Registry plus the upgrade-blob restore. So 'the active pane being split' is effectively THE FIRST PANE EVER CREATED IN THAT WINDOW -- not the pane the human is looking at, which is client-local state the server does not have.

Consequence for this epic: 'phux launch claude-code' drops the new agent pane by splitting some arbitrary first-created pane, horizontally, at 0.5, regardless of where you are or what you asked for. This is THE bug that makes agent orchestration feel wrong today, and it is a prerequisite for placement args on spawn/launch.
design:
Do NOT fix by teaching the server about focus -- ADR-0019 section 6 killed server-tracked focus and this bead must not re-litigate it. The server has no business knowing which pane a human is looking at.

The right shape follows from the epic's key fact: layout is client-owned. So the CALLER (who does know the target) should tell spawn where to put it. Two options for the ADR/design to settle: (a) SPAWN_TERMINAL stays geometry-free and the caller does a follow-up layout metadata write to place the new pane (pure L3, no wire change -- consistent with the epic's zero-wire-change thesis); or (b) add optional placement fields to SPAWN_TERMINAL (wire change, needs spec + CHANGELOG + version bump). Strongly prefer (a). Under (a) this bead's job is to make the DEFAULT placement sane and to stop pretending Window.active means anything.

TRAP: if you do touch the Command enum, note that adding a variant breaks NOTHING at compile time outside phux-protocol -- there are 5 silent '_' fallback arms across phux-server/src/runtime/commands.rs and phux-server/src/hub/relay.rs. relay.rs:1407 route_to_satellite is the one people miss, and missing it means the command silently does not route in federation.
acceptance_criteria: A pane spawned with an explicit placement lands where the caller asked. Default placement is documented and deliberate. Regression test. No re-litigation of server-side focus.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed.

title: SPIKE: does the TUI adopt a sibling's focused_terminal from a layout METADATA_CHANGED?
description:
Blocks ADR-0044. The layout envelope v2 ALREADY carries focus: {version, windows:[{name, root, focused_terminal}], focused_window_index} (phux-client-core/src/layout/mod.rs:15-17, LAYOUT_ENVELOPE_VERSION=2 at :49). And the client already subscribes to layout metadata and re-renders on a sibling's write (attach/server_frame.rs:894 MetadataChanged arm, gated by is_layout_key at :1334).

So the question that decides how much client work ADR-0044 needs: when client B decodes a layout blob that client A wrote, does B ADOPT the focused_terminal / focused_window_index, or does B preserve its own local focus and take only the tree?

Evidence it may NOT adopt: layout/mod.rs:311-315 says the active-window index 'is serialized as focused_window_index but a bare window switch does not broadcast it', and focus-changing actions set effects.layout_mutated + effects.set_focus but NOT effects.set_metadata (input_dispatch.rs:1846-1849), whereas resize-pane DOES set set_metadata (:1866-1867). That asymmetry is deliberate and smells like 'focus rides along in the blob but is not honored on read.'

If B DOES adopt: phux focus is a pure metadata write, near-zero client work, and directed focus is basically free (which makes the ADR's opt-in question urgent -- an agent could yank a human's view today by writing layout).
If B does NOT adopt: we need an explicit client-side opt-in path, and the ADR must specify it.
design: Method: run two attached clients on one session (phux attach in two terminals). In client A, change focus (C-a o) then force a layout broadcast (resize a divider, which DOES set_metadata). Observe whether B's focused pane moves. Then read the MetadataChanged arm at server_frame.rs:894 and the layout decode path to confirm from source. Write the answer into this bead's notes -- ADR-0044 depends on it.
acceptance_criteria: A definitive yes/no, cited to source, recorded in bd notes. If yes, also answer: can an agent writing phux.tui.layout/v1 today already move an attached human's viewport? (That is a latent capability -- and arguably a latent security/UX surprise -- either way it must be stated in the ADR.)
notes: 2026-07-15 source evidence: MetadataValue and MetadataChanged both decoded the full Workspace and replaced local state, including focused_window_index and focused_terminal, so a sibling layout write could yank a human viewport. Fixed in crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs: reconciliation now adopts topology while preserving valid local active index and per-window focus, with deterministic repair. Regression tests cover initial loads, sibling broadcasts, tombstones, topology changes, and foreign layouts. Decision recorded in ADR-0049.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green foundation train PR #243 (combined CI passed).

title: Agent workspace: programmatic layout, attention routing, and CLI/MCP parity
description:
phux ships a complete agent CONTROL surface (observe/drive/spawn/signal) and a complete human SPATIAL surface (binary split tree, focus-direction, zoom, drag-resize dividers). The two do not meet. An agent can spawn a pane and read it, but cannot place it, cannot arrange it, and cannot get the human to look at it. A human can arrange panes beautifully but has no way to be told 'the agent in pane 7 is blocked on you.'

This epic closes that seam so phux becomes a workspace an agent can orchestrate and a human can supervise: an agent launches work into a placed pane, raises a flag when it needs you, and you jump to it.

KEY ARCHITECTURAL FACT (drives the whole decomposition): the layout tree is NOT server state. It is a client-owned CBOR blob in L3 metadata under phux.tui.layout/v1/<session> (ADR-0019). Clients mutate locally, push SET_METADATA, server broadcasts METADATA_CHANGED to siblings; the server never parses it. phux rename already works exactly this way. Therefore split/focus/move can be built as L3 metadata edits with ZERO wire-protocol changes: no new frame types, no PROTOCOL_VERSION bump, no capability negotiation. That last point matters because ServerFeature/AGENT_HOOKS capability bits are spec'd in docs/spec/proto.md 6.2 but have ZERO lines of Rust behind them (caps.rs ServerCapabilities has exactly one field: layers). There is no per-feature gate to build on.

THE ADR-0019 CONSTRAINT: ADR-0019 section 6 explicitly REJECTED server-tracked focus, names the exact FOCUS_CHANGED frame, and marks it 'Killed.' Convergent focus was rejected as 'a different product (a la tmate view-only mirror).' Do not re-litigate it. The resolution is a distinction ADR-0019 did not consider: FOCUS (which pane this client looks at; client-local; ADR-0019 is right) is different from ATTENTION (an agent raising a flag with an actionable target). Attention is a notification, not shared focus. phux already has the primitive: AgentEvent::Asked ships, the TUI already renders it (server_frame.rs:1203), and phux agent list already infers working/blocked/idle. Build on that. Directed focus, if we ship it at all, is opt-in config -- never the default.
design:
WAVE STRUCTURE (dependency edges are wired; run bd ready to get parallel work):

Wave 0 -- foundations, all parallel, no deps: the spike, three bugs that make agent panes misbehave today, the get_state triplication, the dead Agent facade, and the missing MCP registration doc.
Wave 1 -- ADR-0044 (blocked on the spike; blocks everything spatial).
Wave 2 -- phux-client/src/layout_ops.rs, the shared L3 layout envelope module. Load-bearing; every verb wraps it.
Wave 3 -- CLI verbs fan out in parallel (focus/split/move), each with real logic in NEW files.
Wave 3b -- ONE bead for ALL MCP tools (see conflict note).
Wave 4 -- attention routing (event + TUI indicator + opt-in directed focus).
Wave 5 -- docs, skill, worked example.

SWARM CONFLICT NOTE (read before fanning out): every new CLI verb edits three shared registry files -- crates/phux/src/commands/mod.rs (the Command enum), crates/phux/src/main.rs (dispatch arm AND the curated long_about inventory), and crates/phux/src/help_inventory.rs (EXPECTED_INVENTORY, an order-sensitive pinned list). Parallel verb beads WILL conflict on those three lines each; that is a trivial rebase, and the tests command_inventory_matches_snapshot / top_level_help_lists_every_subcommand will catch a miss. By contrast, every new MCP tool edits ONE json! array in crates/phux-mcp/src/tools.rs plus a test asserting the EXACT ORDERED tool-name vec (tools.rs:717-729) -- parallel MCP beads are a guaranteed painful conflict, so all MCP tool work is deliberately ONE bead. Per CONTRIBUTING.md, fan-out uses self-managed worktrees.
acceptance_criteria: An agent (Claude, via MCP or CLI) can, in one session: launch a sub-agent into a pane placed where it asked; watch it; snapshot it; be told when it is blocked; and surface to the human a way to jump straight to that pane. The human can supervise a fleet without hand-navigating. just ci green; docs/spec untouched (no wire change); ADR-0044 landed.
close_reason: All orchestration children are closed; delivered and merged via #223, #231, #243, and #246 with green combined CI and live dogfood.

title: User rename-window must outrank agent/OSC title in tab + sidebar labels
description: Window display label resolves as agent_label.or(osc_title).unwrap_or(stored_name) (crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:3608), so an explicit rename-window is invisible whenever the focused pane has a phux.agent/v1 record or any non-empty OSC 0/2 title. Root cause: WindowState.name is overloaded — it is both the auto default ("1","2") and the user's name, so the resolver cannot distinguish deliberate intent from a placeholder. Fix: split user_name: Option<String> from the auto name; user_name outranks agent record and title; agent/title remain the default when unset.
close_reason: Split WindowState.user_name (human's rename) from the auto name; label ranking is now user_name > phux.agent/v1 record > OSC title > auto name. Blank rename clears the name and restores automatic labelling (required making the rename-window prompt commit an empty buffer, which previously cancelled). Verified live in the TUI: tab strip + sidebar spaces + sidebar agents rows all honor the rename over an agent record AND an OSC title; name persists across client restart via the L3 layout blob.

title: Prevent multi-agent attach screen flicker
description: Routine agent metadata, title, lease, and attention updates currently trigger ED2 full-screen repaint transactions. Under several concurrent agents this repeatedly exposes blank or partially rebuilt frames. Make repaint transactions visually coherent and avoid destructive redraws for chrome-only updates where safe; add focused regression coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent chrome updates do not expose full-screen clear flicker; full-frame redraws are emitted as coherent transactions; cursor visibility remains correct; focused tests and repository CI pass.
close_reason: Already fixed and never closed; verified with evidence. cb69d00c wrapped paint_full_frame in DEC 2026 synchronized output so clear+rebuild is one atomic terminal transaction; 4c5fa6da/b841868f added RepaintLevel None/Chrome/Full plus paint_chrome_in_place and routed every metadata, title, lease and attention trigger to chrome-only repaint. The guard test paint_chrome_in_place_never_clears_the_viewport_or_repaints_a_pane was proven load-bearing by reintroducing ED2 and watching it fail. Black-box proof on a live attach: 12 rapid agent state transitions produced 11912 output events with ZERO ED2, correct status bar, cursor in a sane in-pane position.

title: Resume exit watchers so killed sessions are reaped
description: After a graceful server upgrade, rebuilt pane actors are registered without respawning their terminal-exit watchers. Killing or naturally exiting a resumed pane therefore drops the actor but leaves its pane/window/session in the authoritative registry, so phux kill reports success while phux ls and TUI pickers retain a ghost session. Return rebuilt exit receivers to the runtime, install watchers, and cover kill-after-upgrade.
acceptance_criteria: After phux upgrade, killing the only pane/session reaps it and allows the empty server to self-exit; ordinary non-upgrade lifecycle behavior remains covered.
close_reason: Restored exit watchers for every pane rebuilt after graceful upgrade and added a real upgrade/kill/reap regression test; just ci and targeted upgrade e2e pass.

title: SelectList overlays clip instead of scrolling: selection can leave the viewport
description: The command palette and every picker built on SelectList (window picker, agent fleet) build a Line for every filtered row and hand them all to a Paragraph, which clips at the modal's bottom edge. There is no scroll viewport, no offset, and no position indicator, so navigating past the last visible row moves the selection off-screen with no way to see where you are. Fix: window the rows around the selection, add a scrollbar on the modal border, and support PageUp/PageDown/Home/End and wheel.
close_reason: Closed

title: Honor synchronized-output mode across phux repaint boundaries
description: Why: Codex wraps each complete TUI redraw in DEC private mode 2026 (synchronized output). phux applies each raw TerminalOutput chunk to libghostty and immediately paints unless another frame is already buffered in the same socket wakeup; it never checks Mode::SYNC_OUTPUT. PTY coalescing is bounded/arbitrary and snapshot requests can interleave, so fast scroll and bottom-of-screen redraws expose the application's intermediate clear/scroll/paint states as flicker. What: make repaint scheduling transaction-aware across transport wakeups and define safe snapshot behavior while a synchronized update is open.
acceptance_criteria: No pane paint is emitted while its mirror remains in Mode::SYNC_OUTPUT; the transition out paints the final state once; a bounded watchdog prevents a stuck application from freezing the pane; existing ordinary-frame coalescing remains; tests split begin/body/end across distinct TerminalOutput frames and exercise attach/snapshot behavior mid-update; black-box fast-scroll capture shows no intermediate blank/stale frame.
close_reason: Closed

title: Propagate host default colors and answer OSC 10/11 queries
description: Why: Codex 0.144.1 probes OSC 10/11 for terminal foreground/background and only paints its gray composer surface when both replies arrive. In phux, the canonical libghostty Terminal installs on_pty_write but has no default fg/bg configured, while ClientCapabilities carries color depth only. A live phux Codex snapshot (67x29, 238 styled cells) contained zero non-default backgrounds, proving the app took its no-color-query fallback rather than the renderer dropping painted cells. What: query the outer terminal while the client is still cooked, propagate optional default fg/bg to the server, define terminal-global authority/fallback behavior for multiple/headless clients, configure server and client mirrors, and return correct OSC color reports to PTY applications.
acceptance_criteria: A Codex-like OSC 10/11 startup probe receives both configured host colors through phux and renders a non-default composer background; light and dark host themes work; unsupported/headless and multi-client authority behavior is explicit; wire, actor, and black-box tests cover the response path.

title: Preserve TUI cell styling and eliminate attach flicker
description: Why: TUI applications such as Codex render differently through phux than in a native Ghostty split: row background styling is lost, and fast movement or scrolling at the bottom produces visible flicker. What: reproduce both failures, identify whether loss occurs in PTY byte forwarding, client libghostty state, layout composition, or stdout paint ordering, then add regression coverage and fix the responsible render/state paths.
acceptance_criteria: Codex-like background rows retain their source background through phux; fast cursor movement and bottom scrolling do not expose partial or stale frames; a black-box or integration regression test covers each confirmed cause.
notes: Diagnosis 2026-07-09: two independent bugs confirmed. Styling: live installed phux is 0.0.2, but current main is also affected. Side-effect-free snapshot of the live 67x29 Codex pane returned 238 styled cells and zero non-default backgrounds. Codex rust-v0.144.1 probes OSC 10 and OSC 11 for default fg/bg at startup; style::user_message_style_for returns default style when the probe is absent. phux TerminalActor installs on_pty_write and on_size but constructs libghostty Terminal with no default colors; ClientCapabilities has color depth only. Track fix in phux-dpop.1. Flicker: Codex wraps draw in CSI ? 2026 h/l. phux client applies every TerminalOutput then paints immediately unless a later same-pane frame is already buffered in the current recv drain. No production path reads Mode::SYNC_OUTPUT, and TerminalActor PTY coalescing boundaries are arbitrary/bounded; snapshot and screen requests can interleave. Track transaction-aware repaint plus watchdog and snapshot consistency in phux-dpop.2. No source edits made during diagnosis.
close_reason: Closed

title: Seed pane inherits daemon CWD, not client cwd — breaks claude --resume
description: A claude (Claude Code) session started inside a phux shell can't be resumed: 'claude --resume' from the project dir finds no history. Root cause: the seed/initial pane never sets a cwd and inherits the daemon's cwd. Claude keys its transcript at HOME/.claude/projects/<cwd-hash>/*.jsonl on the pane's actual cwd (= daemon cwd), so the transcript IS written and flushed, just under the hash of the wrong directory. The session NAME is derived from the client cwd basename, so it looks like it's in the project dir while the pane runs in the daemon dir. HOME/env inherited correctly (not the cause); data not lost, just filed under wrong project hash. Fix: client should send its real cwd (not None) for the initial attach, and resolve_create_if_missing must apply it, mirroring the split path's resolve_inherited_cwd. Likely warrants an ADR. Verified against code: resolve_create_if_missing ignores _cwd (phux-server/src/runtime/attach.rs:159, doc-comment :140-142); client sends cwd:None (phux/src/commands/attach.rs:177); seed_session_with_pty sets no .cwd() (phux-server/src/runtime/commands.rs:63-94); split path DOES honor cwd (attach.rs:496-500). Secondary (lower prio): TerminalSignal::Kill group-SIGKILLs via killpg (terminal_actor/mod.rs:1324-1344), so killing a pane while claude is foreground gives no chance to flush; clean shell-exit reaps gracefully. Reported via phux-mobile bead phux-mobile-3ru. See SEED_CWD_BUG.md.

Consumer ready: phux-mobile-kfa.8 (client) closed/inert. aps-environment is 'development' on the client until this ships. Coordinate the push payload key names with phux-mobile RelayPush.
UNDEFERRED + REPRICED 2026-08-15 (deferred to 2026-09-30 / P3 -> open / P1), fleet-inbox sequencing.

Step 2 of the five-step arc: a bounded human inbox only pays if it reaches the human when they are NOT at the terminal. The phux-mobile client half is already DONE and inert (phux-mobile-kfa.8 closed; aps-environment still 'development' pending this), so this bead is the only thing standing between the fleet and a phone.

'Your agents run on a box you rent and ping your phone when they are stuck' is the competitor's own advertised pitch and we have the better substrate for it plus a finished client.

title: Decide the agent-asked wire mechanism (new AgentEvent vs TERMINAL_EVENT vs RUN_HOOK)
description: The emission mechanism is genuinely unsettled (a real protocol decision, not readable from source). Candidates: (a) a new additive AgentEvent variant Asked{ id, question, suggestions?, ... } on the existing 0xB3 stream -- cheapest, forward-compatible; (b) implement the spec-only TERMINAL_EVENT 0xB1 frame + TerminalEventBody::USER_NOTIFICATION (OSC 9 / OSC 777) at docs/spec/L1.md:183-194; (c) implement the spec-only RUN_HOOK command (L1.md:436, tag 0x06 reserved in frame.rs:403-410) as an agent-hook dispatch point. The downstream Swift consumer already expects agentAsked(terminalID, AgentQuestion{ id, text, suggestions[], waitingSeconds }) (phux-mobile Packages/PhuxKit/Sources/PhuxProtocol/Model.swift:22-45) -- the chosen payload must carry that shape. Resolve whether OSC 9/777 are currently parsed-and-dropped (L1.md:228 "server does not forward every OSC type") or forwardable.
design: Read docs/spec/proto.md:203-213 (versioning), L1.md sec 3.3 and 5.1. Prefer the additive AgentEvent variant unless USER_NOTIFICATION/OSC reuse is clearly superior.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR is written and merged in phux choosing exactly one mechanism with rationale, defining the wire payload (fields + tags) and the minor-version bump, AND this spike FILES the downstream implementation beads (the protocol-type bead and, if 0xB1/RUN_HOOK is chosen, the frame-implementation bead) under this epic with the decided shape.
notes:
Bead-that-creates-beads for the wire shape. Do not pre-write the impl beads here; emit them once the mechanism is chosen.
DECISION MADE + IMPLEMENTED (not yet written as a formal phux ADR): chose the additive AgentEvent::Asked variant on the 0xB3 EVENT stream (tag 0x08) over TERMINAL_EVENT/RUN_HOOK. Shipped in bdb64f6 (feat/agent-asked-wire). Remaining: write the ADR doc to close the spike formally.
