title: Determine how the server detects an agent has entered ASKED
description: Independent of the wire mechanism, the server must DECIDE that an agent is asking. Three clean-room-reusable patterns from herdr (AGPL-3.0 -- PATTERN ONLY, NO source copy): (a) opt-in agent lifecycle hooks reporting state over a channel (authoritative when live), (b) per-agent screen-scrape manifests (evidence gates over OSC title + bottom grid lines), (c) OSC title/progress. phux already owns the PTYs server-side via libghostty, so scrape is feasible. This needs a build/run to confirm what OSC sequences real agents (Claude Code, Codex, pi) actually emit when blocking on input, and which detection layer phux wants to own first. Requires an ADR because it closes off a design space (hook contract vs manifest authority vs both).
design: Clean-room: reuse only the design pattern (hook-authority-wins, scrape-fallback, suppress-on-exit). Author phux own manifests/contract from scratch.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR is written and merged in phux choosing the detection source(s) and (if hooks) the namespaced hook/OSC contract agents implement, with an explicit clean-room note that no AGPL herdr source/manifests/hook scripts are copied. The spike empirically records what at least Claude Code and one other agent emit on block, AND FILES the implementation bead(s) for the chosen detection module under this epic.
notes:

title: Client pane mirror frozen at attach size: resize-grow (kill/window-enlarge) leaves freed space blank
description: phux-wurs removed the paint-path mirror resize (to fix alt-screen ghost cells on shrink), leaving safe_resize ONLY in the client's TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT arm. But the server's post-resize resync (broadcast_resync_after_resize, phux-8v1) is delivered via the raw output_tx broadcast -> TERMINAL_OUTPUT, which the client applies with vt_write WITHOUT resizing the mirror. Net: the client libghostty mirror is frozen at its attach-time size and never grows on ANY resize. Shrink looks fine (render clips mirror->rect); GROW cannot fill. Repro: stacked split (C-a "), nvim in bottom, kill top (C-a k, C-a x) -> survivor stays ~19 rows tall at top, rows 20-38 blank. Server grid is correct (snapshot shows 120x39); the client mirror is the problem. Verified via pyte independent-emulator capture of the composited client frame. Fix: deliver the resize-resync as a TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT (carries cols/rows) instead of raw TERMINAL_OUTPUT, by making the actor output broadcast carry an enum {Output(Bytes) | Resync{cols,rows,bytes}}; pumps map Resync -> FrameKind::TerminalSnapshot. Client TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT arm already resizes+resets+repaints. Keeps server-authoritative mirror dims (phux-wurs principle) and fixes the GENERAL resize-grow case, not just kill.
close_reason: Fixed in 870c679: resize resync delivered as TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT via PaneOutput::{Live,Resync} enum so the client mirror resizes to post-reflow dims. Verified via pyte (kill-survivor fills, window-grow fills, alt-screen shrink no ghost) + full nextest green (1400).

title: Graceful server upgrade: sessions survive a binary update (ADR-0032)
description:
Per ADR-0032 (Proposed). Today a binary upgrade requires 'phux kill' -> restart, which closes every PTY master and SIGHUPs the children (shells, editors, the Claude agent session) — the maintainer hit this directly (installing a fix killed the session hosting the work). tmux has the same hole; phux can close it because it ALREADY emits a replayable per-pane snapshot (vt_replay_bytes + scrollback_bytes via SnapshotSynthesizer, ADR-0013).

APPROACH (ADR-0032): graceful in-place upgrade via execve re-exec + fd inheritance + VT snapshot replay. On 'phux upgrade' the running server (1) snapshots every pane + serializes the session/window/pane tree + an fd->pane manifest into an inherited state fd; (2) clears FD_CLOEXEC on the PTY masters + the UnixListener and execve's the new binary as 'phux server --resume <fd>' (fds survive exec -> children stay alive, socket stays bound); (3) the new server adopts the fds and rebuilds each pane's Terminal by vt_write-ing its snapshot ('attach to yourself'). Clients blink-reconnect (v1); passing live client sockets for flicker-free swap is v2.

PHASES: v1 = explicit 'phux upgrade' command (the dev-iteration + agent-session win). v2 = auto-detect a newer on-disk binary after cargo install / brew upgrade (the non-dev 'just works' win) + pass client sockets for seamless. Rejected alts: kill+restart (status quo, loses sessions); separate fd-keeper daemon (cleaner crash-isolation but a permanent 2nd process + IPC seam — recorded as v2 hardening); serialize libghostty engine state (not feasible / drifts — replay the VT snapshot instead).

IMPLEMENTATION SLICES (file beads as children): (a) state-blob format (versioned — old<->new server versions straddle it) + ser/de; (b) fd manifest + CLOEXEC clearing + the --resume server mode that adopts inherited PTY masters + listener; (c) the snapshot-all-panes + quiesce (a pane mid-SPAWN / in-flight input must quiesce before snapshot); (d) the re-exec orchestration with a SAFE FALLBACK (validate the new binary via --version / dry --resume probe BEFORE committing; on failure keep serving on the old image — must never strand children); (e) client reconnect-on-swap; (f) 'phux upgrade' command + tests (incl. a child-survives-upgrade integration test: spawn a sleep/echo, upgrade, assert the same child + scrollback survived). SHARP EDGES: scrollback fidelity bounded by the snapshot (styled-scrollback still plain pending phux-q0x7); OSC8/graphics registries deferred same as attach; the state format is a maintained compatibility boundary across releases.
notes:
SCOPED (session 2026-06-10): ADR-0032 = execve re-exec + fd inheritance + VT-snapshot replay (NOT fd-keeper daemon, NOT engine serialization). HARD CONSTRAINT (not in ADR): portable_pty 0.9 exposes MasterPty::as_raw_fd() (read) but NO constructor to rebuild MasterPty/Child from an inherited fd+PID. => Approach A: on resume, bypass PtyOwned with an adopted-PTY backing wrapping File::from_raw_fd(master) + waitpid(pid); keep portable_pty for SPAWN only. ~1100-1500 LOC across ~9 files. Phases: P0 spike (open PTY, clear FD_CLOEXEC, execve, confirm child alive + bytes flow). P1 versioned state blob (phux-server/src/upgrade/{mod,blob}.rs): per-pane {core/wire ids, child_pid, master_raw_fd, dims, cell_px, term, title, cwd, vt_replay_bytes+scrollback_bytes via SnapshotSynthesizer::synthesize_with_scrollback synthesizer.rs:252} + listener fd + next_wire_id counters (registry.rs:51-54); expose raw fd+PID via a new TerminalHandle request channel (mirror ScreenRequest, terminal_actor/mod.rs:148). P2 perform_upgrade: quiesce panes, collect manifest, clear FD_CLOEXEC on masters+UnixListener (rustix), write blob to memfd/temp fd, std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::exec current_exe as 'server --resume <fd>'; PRE-COMMIT validate new binary; GATE the unconditional socket unlink (runtime/mod.rs:392-397). P3 --resume runtime: UnixListener::from_raw_fd, rebuild registry+wire maps, spawn adopted-PTY actors, vt_write snapshot into fresh Terminal (new_with_seed). P4 wire Command::Upgrade (frame.rs:824, #[non_exhaustive] => additive) + handle_command + phux upgrade CLI. P5 client blink-reconnect (ABSENT today: driver.rs:1148 breaks on Disconnected): outer reconnect loop around main_loop, distinguish detach(exit) vs server-vanished(reconnect); ATTACH already resyncs via TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT (reconnect_scenario.rs:105). RISKS: fd adoption (#1), FD_CLOEXEC miss kills a child, exec-in-place (NOT Command::spawn/fork), quiesce ordering, blob version skew, snapshot fidelity (styled scrollback plain-text). Needs manual upgrade DRILL for acceptance. Update ADR-0032 with the fd-adoption gap + cross-platform blob carrier (macOS has no memfd).
DECISION + SPIKE GREEN (session 2026-06-10): going with re-exec v1 (execve + fd inheritance + snapshot replay), framed as STAGE-1 of substrate/projection separation (NOT the end state). Custodian/fd-keeper stays the planned v2 whose real prize is CRASH-durability (surviving our own panics), which re-exec cannot give. CORRECTION to the earlier SCOPED note: the fd-adoption 'real constraint' is NOT ~1100-1500 LOC and does NOT need to bypass PtyOwned. portable_pty's MasterPty/Child are PUBLIC traits and PtyOwned already stores them as trait objects, so the adopted backing is ~250 LOC of two trait impls over (raw_fd, pid) — no portable_pty fork, no library patch, no new direct dep (Downcast is blanket-impl'd; libc already a dep). The 1100-1500 figure is the WHOLE feature; fd-adoption is its CHEAPEST slice, not the blocker. Built it as a standalone, extractable workspace crate: crates/portable-pty-adopt (AdoptedMaster/AdoptedChild; README has TODO(extract) to split to its own repo + crates.io — it fills a genuine upstream gap). TWO proofs pass (clippy -D warnings + fmt clean): (1) tests/adopt_inprocess.rs — adopt a real PTY from (raw_fd,pid) alone and drive read/write/resize/reap; (2) tests/execve_roundtrip.rs — a PTY master fd (CLOEXEC cleared) + its child survive a REAL execve of the parent, and the post-exec image re-adopts via the crate. Core ADR-0032 bet is de-risked. Remaining work is ordinary feature eng (children a-f): the genuinely hard slices are quiesce-ordering and the never-strand-a-child fallback, NOT fd adoption. Next: phux-server depends on portable-pty-adopt in the --resume path (P3).
STAGE-1 LANDED on main 2026-06-11: crate portable-pty-adopt (AdoptedMaster/AdoptedChild) merged via PR #111, commit c2dd990 (rebased, linear). Full just ci green + Linux CI green. fd-adoption bet de-risked; remaining = blob/quiesce/--resume/reconnect/CLI (children a-f). Next consumer hook: phux-server --resume path depends on portable-pty-adopt.
SHIPPED v1 (2026-06-11). Graceful upgrade complete across 9 PRs merged to main: #111 portable-pty-adopt crate (fd re-adoption, execve-survival proof) | #112 versioned StateBlob format | #114 per-pane upgrade-handle actor request | #118 build_upgrade_blob producer | #121 new_with_adopted_pty (resumed actor) | #122 rebuild_from_blob consumer | #123 server --resume mode (adopt listener + rebuild) | #125 UPGRADE wire command (tag 0x0e, spec 0.5.0-draft.4) | #126 perform_upgrade re-exec orchestration + handle_upgrade + phux upgrade CLI + child-survives acceptance drill (PASSES) | #127 client blink-reconnect | #128 ADR-0032 -> Accepted. KEY FINDING: the 'real constraint' (portable_pty can't re-adopt) was shallow — MasterPty/Child are PUBLIC traits, so ~250 LOC of impls (no fork), extracted as portable-pty-adopt crate (TODO: split to own repo + crates.io). Blob carrier = anonymous tempfile (not memfd; macOS has none). Acceptance: server PID unchanged across upgrade (in-place execve), pane child alive, scrollback survives. REMAINING (v2, not blocking): flicker-free client-socket handoff; crash-surviving fd-keeper daemon; styled-scrollback fidelity (phux-q0x7); auto-detect newer on-disk binary. Suggest closing this bead; open v2 follow-ups separately.

title: Client incremental paint leaves stale ghost cells after a coalesced redraw burst (nvim 'fucked up')
description:
REPRODUCED + SEEN (rendered the client's actual output through pyte, an independent non-libghostty emulator, to a PNG and looked at it). Symptom: scrolling/jumping in neovim (e.g. G in a long file) under the user's real config leaves STALE 'ghost' cells on the right half of rows — fragments of the previous screen (e.g. top-of-file doc-comment text) overlapping the new content. This is the user-reported 'neovim weird and fucked up'.

LOCALIZED (evidence chain, all rendered to images):
 1. Server authoritative grid (phux snapshot --cells) = CLEAN.
 2. Client output captured from a real 'phux attach' via PTY, parsed by pyte = GHOST TEXT.
 3. After a forced full redraw (terminal resize -> server resync + render_at_full) = CLEAN again.
 => The server is right, the client's libghostty MIRROR is right (a full repaint from it is clean), pyte is honest. The corruption is in the client's INCREMENTAL paint. NOT broadcast lag (server log had no Lagged warnings during the repro). NOT the SGR-fidelity bugs fixed on main today (those were color; this is erase/stale-cell). NOT a static-attach issue (a fresh attach re-synthesizes a clean snapshot, which is why round-trip tests + static captures never saw it).

MECHANISM (leading): render_at_inner's Dirty::Partial path repaints only rows whose libghostty per-row row.dirty() bit is set (crates/phux-client/src/attach/render.rs:282-366). Under the phux-jhv8 frame-coalescing (crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:936 coalesce_defer_flags + server_frame.rs:464 defer_paint), a burst applies all vt_writes but paints ONCE on the pane's final frame via render_at (Partial). The final partial paint misses rows that actually changed across the burst — while render_at_full (paints every row) is clean. So either libghostty's row.dirty() under-reports after a scroll/big-redraw (content-dirty-per-cell vs paint-dirty-per-absolute-position mismatch: a viewport scroll moves rows whose cells didn't 'change' but whose absolute screen position now needs repainting, and the client repaints in place rather than scrolling the outer terminal), or dirty state is lost across the coalesced batch.

FIX DIRECTIONS (need hands-on debugging): (a) when libghostty reports a scroll / Dirty implies viewport shift, force render_at_full for that pane; (b) track a per-row content signature of what was last PAINTED to the outer terminal and repaint on mismatch (decouples paint-dirty from libghostty content-dirty); (c) on a coalesced burst whose accumulated change is large, fall back to a full repaint. (a)/(c) are cheapest; (b) is most correct.

REPRO HARNESS (reusable to verify a fix): /tmp/phux-diag/cap_big.py drives 'phux attach' in a PTY, opens nvim on a long file, jumps with G; /tmp/phux-diag/render_big.py renders the captured client bytes via pyte to PNG. Server-grid cross-check: /tmp/phux-diag/render_srv.py over 'snapshot --cells --json'. Needs: pip install --break-system-packages pyte pillow.

SEVERITY: high — it's the headline visible defect for the primary use case (human in neovim). Distinct bead from phux-ahk/emdv/the SGR fixes.
notes: FIXED on main (commit 74b1a81), just ci green (1397 tests) + visually confirmed via pyte. ROOT CAUSE (workflow disproved the original scroll/dirty hypothesis — libghostty correctly re-dirties scrolled rows and render_at was faithful): the client resized its libghostty MIRROR to its own layout rect in the paint hot path (safe_resize in paint_focused_pane / paint_full_frame loop / the TerminalOutput arm). On the ALT SCREEN (neovim) libghostty resize() does NOT reflow, so a SIGWINCH repaint at the new smaller viewport_dims BEFORE the server's resized output arrived shrank a server-authored width-N mirror to width M<N, stranding the previous screen's content in columns >=M; render_at then painted the divergent mirror and (clipping only rows, never cols) never repainted M..N -> the right-side ghost that persisted through scrolling until a server resync. The 'forced full redraw heals it' clue was contaminated: a resize also triggers a TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT resync that overwrites the mirror. FIX: drop the per-paint safe_resize (mirror sized only by the server-authoritative TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT resync); add clip:(cols,rows) to render_at clamping BOTH axes to min(mirror,rect). Steady state clip==grid so Dirty::Partial perf is preserved. VERIFIED with an independent emulator (pyte, not libghostty): the attach-resize+G-jump repro that was ghost-ridden is now clean, as are pure-scroll and live-shrink. Tests added: render_at_clips_columns/rows_to_rect, paint_focused_pane_does_not_resize_server_authoritative_mirror (red->green).

title: Split+resize leaves dead space: three divergent layout algorithms
description:
Live repro: with a split, resizing the terminal leaves dead/unfilled space (reported at the bottom).

Verified structural root cause — phux has THREE different pane-rect computations that must agree but don't:
1. phux-client-core/src/layout.rs:729 fill_rects/pane_rects — used by REFLOW (compute_reflow) to decide the size to TELL the server (TERMINAL_RESIZE → TIOCSWINSZ). Subtracts dividers GLOBALLY up front: compute_reflow does content = (cols - total_h_dividers, rows - total_v_dividers), then fill_rects splits with NO per-node gap (left_w + right_w == bounds.w).
2. phux-client-core/src/multi_pane.rs:335 walk_layout/compute_layout — used by PAINT (paint_full_frame, snapshot/output arms) to decide WHERE TO DRAW. Subtracts ONE divider per split node LOCALLY: content_w = bounds.w - 1 at each interior node, recursively.
3. phux-core/src/window.rs:390 pane_rects — the SERVER's own layout (sizes PTYs / builds snapshots).

In the SIGWINCH path (driver.rs:1159-1217): prev_rects come from compute_layout (walk_layout), new_rects from compute_reflow->pane_rects (fill_rects). The diff that drives TERMINAL_RESIZE emission compares rects produced by TWO DIFFERENT algorithms. For a SINGLE split they happen to agree (both use content=dim-1, split_dim(content,ratio)); for NESTED splits the per-node-vs-global divider subtraction and split_dim float rounding diverge at different recursion depths -> the size phux tells the server to make a PTY (fill_rects) != the rect it draws into (walk_layout) -> gaps/overlap. The 'changed' detection can also miss/spurious-fire because it compares incompatible sources.

Secondary contributor (single-split case): resize is async — SIGWINCH emits TERMINAL_RESIZE then immediately paint_full_frame's the NEW geometry, but the reflowed PTY output arrives later, so a pane's libghostty mirror is briefly shorter than its new rect and render_at leaves the extra rows blank (dead space at the bottom) until the reflowed output repaints.

Also note split geometry is RATIO-based (ratio: f32 per split, recomputed via split_dim each resize) rather than tmux's authoritative integer sizes + remainder distribution — float re-derivation is inherently lossy.

FIX DIRECTION (the tmux lesson): collapse to ONE client layout algorithm with an exact-tiling invariant (sum of child sizes + dividers == parent, remainder distributed one cell at a time per tmux layout_spread_cell/layout_fix_offsets), used by BOTH reflow-emit and paint so PTY size == draw rect by construction. Add a property test: for any tree + viewport, rects tile (0,0,W,H_pane) with zero gap and zero overlap. Reconcile the server-side window.rs::pane_rects with it too. Best nailed with a live resize trace once Slice-1 observability lands.

Found during live copilot session 2026-06-05.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #55 (merged, e824f9e): unified client pane tiling — reflow/paint share multi_pane::pane_rects; exact-tiling property test added.

title: Split + re-attach renders blank panes (typable but no content)
description:
Live-session repro: re-attach to a session with a split -> all panes render blank/wiped, but input still routes to the shells (can type).

Root cause (confirmed in code):
1. crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs:279 - the TerminalSnapshot paint block is gated behind `if is_focused`. VT bytes are written to every pane's mirror (:277), but render_at (:298) only runs for the focused pane, so non-focused split panes never paint.
2. The recovery full-repaint (paint_full_frame) only fires on `layout_replaced`, which depends on the server returning a persisted layout under LAYOUT_KEY; the Attached arm seeds a single-pane bootstrap first and requests layout after (driver.rs:761-781). If layout metadata is absent/slow, the split is never reconstructed.
3. Stacked with phux-jhv8 frame-coalescing: the focused pane's snapshot paint is defer_paint-suppressed (:291) expecting a later full repaint that (per #2) never lands -> even the focused pane blanks.

Fix direction (needs care - render hot path): paint every pane's snapshot into its layout rect (the `origin` at server_frame.rs:246-255 is already computed), not just the focused one; and/or trigger an unconditional full repaint once attach snapshots land, independent of the LAYOUT_KEY metadata round-trip. Subtlety: if workspace layout isn't known yet, origin falls back to (0,0) for all panes -> they'd overlap; the fix must ensure layout is known (or defer the full repaint until it is) rather than naively ungating the per-pane render.

Found during live copilot session 2026-06-05; server was at INFO so per-pane snapshot/paint detail wasn't captured - itself motivation for the agent-observability work (self-narration + debug-on-reattach).
close_reason: Done: non-focused-pane snapshot paint present in attach/server_frame.rs (~L348) with regression tests (~L1404,L1445) guarding the focused path; split+reattach renders content.

title: Multi-pane/window re-attach wedges the client (screen freezes, Ctrl-C/detach dead); panes die as collateral
description:
USER REPORT: re-attaching to a session with multiple panes/windows -> screen freezes (no updates), client fully wedged (Ctrl-C and C-a d don't work), and the pane shells die. Single-pane re-attach is fine. Triggers on (re)attach to an EXISTING multi-pane OR multi-window session, both layouts.

NOT YET REPRODUCED headlessly: with a fast pty sink, multi-pane build + hard-detach + re-attach works (B renders + responds, panes survive, reaps delta 0). The 'code 1' pane exit also happens on NORMAL teardown kill in repro, so pane-death is likely COLLATERAL: the user force-kills the wedged terminal -> session EOF/kill -> panes reaped. PRIMARY bug = the WEDGE.

HYPOTHESIS (strong): same class as phux-jhv8 (synchronous render blocking the biased select! loop on a slow host-terminal sink), scaled by N panes. On multi-pane re-attach the server sends ATTACHED + a TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT per pane + layout metadata -> layout_replaced=true -> paint_full_frame() renders ALL panes synchronously inside the frame-processing loop (driver.rs ~891), emitting a large burst. On a real terminal that flush blocks; while blocked the select! loop never polls the stdin arm -> Ctrl-C/detach unprocessed = wedge. If the panes are also producing output, repeated full repaints keep the loop blocked = permanent wedge. A fast pty drains instantly so it never blocks locally.

SECONDARY (real but probably not the wedge cause): compute_reflow (phux-client-core/src/multi_pane.rs ~112-129) can emit degenerate w=0/h=0 rects as TERMINAL_RESIZE on re-attach; server clamps to 1x1 in terminal_actor handle_resize (cols.max(1)) so unlikely to kill the child directly, but emitting 0-dim resizes is wrong and worth fixing.

REPRO PLAN: multi-pane session with panes that continuously output, re-attach client B with a THROTTLED reader (simulate slow terminal, as in the jhv8 repro /tmp/phux_pty_capture.py SLOW_READ), then send B a detach keystroke DURING the re-attach paint and check it never responds = wedge confirmed. Suspect paths: driver.rs select! loop (paint_full_frame synchronous; biased frame arm starves stdin), and whether multi-pane makes the emitted-byte burst big enough to block. FIX direction: don't block the input loop on render (offload stdout writes / make the sink non-blocking) -- the option-2 'non-blocking sink' deferred on jhv8. Confirm with the throttled repro before fixing.
notes:
SECOND BUG (the 'still can't type after re-attach' the user hit while testing #51). DISTINCT from the render wedge: my #51 off-loop-writer fix made the prompts RENDER on re-attach, but input to the re-attached panes was still dropped. User clue: a NEW window accepted typing, existing re-attached panes did not.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via server WARN log 'client not subscribed to pane; dropping input wire_terminal_id=Local{id:3} INPUT_KEY'): ServerState::attach (state.rs ~975) subscribed the attaching client to ONLY the session's active pane. The input gate handle_terminal_input (runtime.rs ~3434) DROPS any keystroke to a pane the client isn't subscribed to. So on (re-)attach to a multi-pane session the client could only ever type into the one active pane (and after a focus move, none). Fresh panes worked because handle_spawn_terminal (runtime.rs ~1930) auto-subscribes the spawning client.

FIX (on the fix/fysb-nonblocking-stdout-sink branch, state.rs attach): subscribe the client to EVERY pane in the session (iterate session.windows -> window.panes), mirroring attach_snapshot_panes (which already snapshots all of them) and the spawn auto-subscribe. Also lets each pane's actor fan out live output to the client, so non-focused panes stay live too. VALIDATED: server 'dropping input' WARN count 0 after fix (was 5+ per keystroke); typed `echo MARKER` into the re-attached focused split pane @3 -> output appears in @3's snapshot (before: dropped).
RESOLVED. Both documented bugs were already fixed on main; this session verified and locked in the fix.

PRIMARY (re-attach wedge): fixed by #51 (8fdb4dd) off-loop writer + non-blocking stdout sink (crates/phux-client/src/attach/stdout_writer.rs). The synchronous paint-on-the-select!-loop that the hypothesis blamed no longer blocks the input arm.

SECOND (can't type into re-attached non-active panes): ServerState::attach now subscribes the attaching client to EVERY pane across the session's windows (crates/phux-server/src/state/registry.rs:412-442). This landed on main not via a dedicated phux-fysb PR but folded into the state.rs module split (f305f94) — which is why the bead was never closed. The companion commit c3643a7 on the local fix/fysb-nonblocking-stdout-sink branch (committed 07:53, after #51 merged 03:46) was the stranded original.

SECONDARY (degenerate 0-dim TERMINAL_RESIZE on reflow): now a deliberate design after phux-islu (#55) — compute_reflow tiles exactly and surfaces ReflowDiff::too_small as a WARNING; the server clamps cols/rows to 1x1. Not a bug; closed off by design, no action.

GAP CLOSED this session: the SECOND fix had only a ServerState unit test (the subscriber map) and was nearly lost in the module-split refactor. Added a wire-level regression (#59, 270f75e -> main 4fb0af1): crates/phux-server/tests/reattach_multipane_input.rs builds a two-pane cat session, drops the builder, re-attaches a fresh client, and INPUT_KEYs into the NON-active pane; a side observer reads the pane mirror via GET_SCREEN to prove the keystroke reached the PTY. Proven to bite: reverting attach to active-pane-only fails the non-active assertion. just ci + Linux PR CI + main CI all green.
close_reason: Closed

title: PTY-heavy e2e tests starve each other -> WIRE_RECV_TIMEOUT flakes (attach_detach_churn quarantined)
description: Fresh-session task. attach_detach_churn_keeps_pane_alive (and latently reconnect_after_detach, already retry-pinned) fail under e2e-lane parallelism: a fresh attach's snapshot render misses WIRE_RECV_TIMEOUT when PTY-backed tests compete for CPU; harness recv_framed (common/mod.rs:258 .expect) then panics with core::result::unwrap_failed. Failed 3/3 even with retries=2, so retries are insufficient. ROOT CAUSE is concurrency, not correctness (passes in isolation / at low -j). FIX: add a nextest test-group with max-threads (e.g. 1-2) covering the PTY-heavy timing-sensitive tests (stress_attach_churn::attach_detach_churn, reconnect_after_detach, likely the perf_* gates) so they don't oversubscribe, instead of retry-roulette. Then REMOVE the quarantine: drop the '-E not test(=attach_detach_churn_keeps_pane_alive)' filter in justfile e2e recipe (added under this bead id). Validate by running just e2e 5-10x green. Context: discovered while consolidating CI from 6 jobs to 2 (separate PR).
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTION (verified by flaky-e2e investigation 2026-06-06): the bead's stated root cause (CPU oversubscription; 'passes in isolation/low -j; concurrency not correctness') is FALSIFIED. attach_detach_churn_keeps_pane_alive fails DETERMINISTICALLY 3/3 in pure isolation on a fast 10+ core Mac, always ~15.0-15.8s at common/mod.rs:258 (.expect on recv timeout in ClientHandle::attach), AND also at near-creation commit 8fdb4dd. So it's a real liveness/deadlock bug in the transient-attach path on the shared current-thread runtime (server fails to deliver ATTACHED/TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT to a fresh transient client while an anchor + idle PTY sleep are live), NOT scheduling starvation. A nextest max-threads test-group CANNOT fix a test that deadlocks in isolation; dropping the quarantine as-written would turn the e2e lane RED. CORRECT SCOPE: (1) fix the actual hang first (instrument builder.rs:322 ATTACHED vs :348 SNAPSHOT recv), (2) THEN optionally add the test-group as hardening for the LATENT sibling reconnect_after_detach (which runs in the parallel default pool, masked today by the .config/nextest.toml retries=2 override), (3) drop ONLY the attach_detach_churn term from justfile:70 -E filter — LEAVE multi_mb_no_newline_burst quarantined (that's phux-fheq, not this bead).
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-06-06, supersedes both the bead's 'oversubscription' premise AND the flaky-e2e investigation's 'liveness deadlock' framing — it is NEITHER). Reproduced deterministically on current main (26437d0). Instrumented handle_attach + writer_task + stack-sampled the hung process:

- The server side is FAST and CORRECT: for the wedging transient client, handle_attach completes promptly (Attached SENT + SnapshotRequest sent + got snapshot reply ok=true at t=7s) and writer_task writes both frames (0x81 ATTACHED, 0x91 SNAPSHOT) to the socket. The runtime is HEALTHY — stack sample shows it parked in tokio::runtime::io::driver::Driver::turn (kqueue), not busy-looping, not blocked on a syscall. No deadlock.

- The panic is at builder.rs:491 (ClientHandle::wait_until), called from stress_attach_churn.rs:73 — NOT in ClientHandle::attach. The transient ATTACHES FINE; it then hangs in wait_until(|s| s.contains('CHURNMARKER')) for 15s and recv_framed's internal WIRE_RECV_TIMEOUT .expect (common/mod.rs:258) fires.

- WHY: the transient's TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT does NOT reconstruct CHURNMARKER. Instrumented snap.bytes: 80x24, ~2149 bytes, has_marker=FALSE for BOTH the anchor and the transient. The anchor passes anyway because it saw CHURNMARKER as a LIVE broadcast delta (it attached before the marker was printed). The transient attaches AFTER the marker and must reconstruct it from the snapshot — but synthesize() yields a blank grid. The seed is 'printf CHURNMARKER; sleep 30' => a single line with NO trailing newline; synthesize()/libghostty grid export does not capture that current-row, no-newline content.

REAL FIX (server-side, in TerminalActor::synthesize / libghostty grid->VT export): ensure the snapshot reconstructs the live grid including the current cursor row written without a trailing newline. This is a fresh bounded sub-investigation in the synthesize path (terminal_actor/mod.rs synthesize + the libghostty export bridge). It is a genuine user-facing bug: any client re-attaching to a pane whose last output had no trailing newline (e.g. a shell prompt with no newline, a partial line) would see it missing from the reconstructed screen until the next live output.

NOT the fix: nextest max-threads test-group (the bead's suggestion) — would only mask it by changing scheduling; the snapshot is wrong regardless of parallelism. Do NOT de-quarantine until synthesize is fixed.

Also note: this same snapshot-content bug is why a flooding-seed contract test added for phux-7w1j (#63) flaked on CI and was removed.
FIXED + merged (#64, commit on main 214f60c). Root cause was the snapshot synthesizer reusing a RenderState whose libghostty per-row dirty-bit cache went stale across consumers (register_consumer's per-consumer reference consumed the Terminal dirty bits before the full snapshot ran), so synthesize() emitted stale/blank rows for a re-attach. Fix: synthesize() builds a fresh RenderState per call (full observation, immune to cross-consumer dirty consumption). attach_detach_churn de-quarantined; passes ~0.5s (was 15s hang); validated on the 2-core CI runner (e2e lane green in #64). NOT oversubscription, NOT a deadlock — both prior diagnoses were wrong; runtime parks healthily.
close_reason: Closed

title: e2e stress_resize_extremes::both_axes_shrink_storm_under_output hangs (pre-existing, blocks CI e2e lane)
description: PRE-EXISTING (not phux-jhv8/PR#48). both_axes_shrink_storm_under_output_does_not_panic in crates/phux-server/tests/stress_resize_extremes.rs hangs indefinitely: CI gave it >6000s then cancelled; reproduces locally on BOTH main and any branch (timeout rc=124 at 150s). main CI has been cancelled/failing on the e2e lane for many commits as a result. The sibling stress_output_extremes passes 10/10 and all non-stress attach e2e (attach_lifecycle, byc_6_1_attach_snapshot, attach_viewport_resize, concurrent_attach_no_lag, route_input_no_resize, concurrent_attach_l2 = 41 tests) pass, so the hang is specific to the resize-storm-under-output path. Test does a monotonic both-axes shrink to 1x1 + boundary churn while /bin/sh emits 'row-N' at 200/s, then resize(100,30) and wait_until(contains 'row-'); the wait never resolves => actor wedged or client never re-renders after the 1x1 clamp churn. Likely a server-side resize/reflow wedge at the 1x1 boundary, OR the harness client. Needs: bisect on main to find the introducing commit, then fix the wedge. Unblocks the CI e2e gate.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (not a deadlock, not a server bug, NOT related to phux-jhv8). The test harness ClientHandle::screenshot() (builder.rs) drains TERMINAL_OUTPUT 'until 20ms of quiet' (timeout(20ms, recv_typed) loop). The both_axes test's seed emits every 5ms forever (printf;sleep 0.005), so screenshot() at the end (cap.attach_screen(client.screenshot()...)) NEVER sees a 20ms gap and loops forever => the >6000s CI hang. Flaky because occasionally scheduler jitter yields a >20ms gap and it breaks. Confirmed by stack sample: runtime thread stuck 148 samples in ClientHandle::screenshot builder.rs:430; pty-reader blocked in PtyFd::read (seed throttled by the unread output, but that was a side effect). My earlier client-read/backpressure hypotheses were WRONG (draining the client did not help; the hang is purely the screenshot drain loop).

FIX: added ClientHandle::snapshot_text() (non-draining oracle read) + drain_output_bounded(max_frames) (count-bounded drain, safe vs infinite seeds). Replaced the final screenshot() in both both_axes_shrink_storm and resize_degenerate (same file, 20ms stty-size seed = same borderline hang) with drain_output_bounded(32)+snapshot_text(). Storm loops left untouched (they never deadlocked; resize_raw is send-only and always reached the final screenshot). Validation: both_axes 25/25 pass slowest 1s (was 100min hang).

FOLLOW-UP (separate, lower priority): the same screenshot()-on-a-fast-continuous-seed anti-pattern exists in other test files (stress_resize_storm.rs stty-size, stress_lifecycle_churn.rs tick loop). They are NOT currently failing CI (timing/seed cadence differs) but are latent. Consider either fixing each call site or making screenshot() itself count-bounded (it has 20 call sites incl perf_latency.rs, so a global change needs care).
RESOLVED — fix already on main, just never closed (fysb pattern). Landed as a1c6b18 'fix(test): stop stress_resize_extremes hanging CI forever (phux-s2iw) (#49)'. Live on main: builder.rs:445 snapshot_text() + builder.rs:459 drain_output_bounded(max_frames); stress_resize_extremes.rs both_axes_shrink_storm + resize_degenerate now use drain_output_bounded(32)+snapshot_text() instead of the infinite screenshot() 20ms-quiet drain. Verified: nextest --run-ignored ignored-only both_axes_shrink_storm PASS 0.351s (was >6000s hang). FOLLOW-UP latent siblings remain (screenshot()-on-fast-seed in stress_resize_storm.rs, stress_lifecycle_churn.rs) — not currently failing; track separately if they flake.

title: client freezes ~0.5s when opening neovim (alt-screen / full-paint burst)
description:
Client-side ~0.5s freeze when opening neovim in a phux attach. Diagnosis (code-read, not yet measured):

RANKED SUSPECTS:
1. Per-frame FULL repaint not coalesced. Each TERMINAL_OUTPUT/TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT triggers render_at_inner (render.rs:229-332) which walks every row/cell -> CUP+SGR+glyph then out.flush() (render.rs:330). nvim startup = burst of frames = N full repaints + N flushes. TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT forces Dirty::Full.
2. Synchronous scrollback replay: server_frame.rs:265-268 vt_write(scrollback_bytes)+vt_write(vt_replay_bytes) inline before render; up to 10k lines (driver.rs:432) = 100KB+ parsed on the hot path.
3. paint_full_frame (paint.rs:90-193) on SIGWINCH/alt-screen: ED2 clear + render_at_full (forced, ignores dirty bits) for every pane; not debounced (driver.rs:989-1047). Prime one-time-stall suspect on alt-screen enter.
4. predict reconcile (only if predictive-echo enabled): reconcile.rs:124-129 read_grapheme_string_at is O(row*col) per pending prediction.

Existing client tracing spans to confirm WHICH: handle_server_frame, vt_apply (bytes=N), paint_trigger (rows=N), paint_full_frame. 

CAPTURE (on a machine where it reproduces): RUST_LOG=phux=debug PHUX_LOG_FORMAT=json PHUX_LOG=/tmp/phux-client.jsonl phux attach <session>, open nvim, then: jq 'select(.fields."time.busy")|{span:.span.name,busy:.fields."time.busy"}' /tmp/phux-client.jsonl | sort — the span with ~500ms busy is the culprit. Fix follows the measurement (coalesce renders / debounce paint_full_frame / lazy scrollback). DO NOT fix blind.
notes: PR #48 opened: https://github.com/phall1/phux/pull/48 (branch fix/jhv8-output-coalesce). 2 commits: the coalescing fix + a pre-existing runtime.rs doc-link fix. just ci green locally.
close_reason: Fix landed on main via PR #48 (commit 624c305): per-pane frame coalescing in attach driver, FrameReader buffered try_recv, defer_paint seam. Measured -38% bytes / -66% paint+flush under the nvim startup burst. Tests included in the PR. e2e is green on main.

title: split spawns into new spawn-N session instead of current session's window
description: Reported from live use: splitting a window in the TUI makes 'phux ls' show two sessions (default + spawn-1). Also breaks reattach: the split pane lives in a different session, so reattaching to the original shows nothing. title: Separate FRAME_ACK semantics for raw broadcast vs synthesized tick output
description: Audit finding from phux-zh01: client acks every TERMINAL_OUTPUT, but raw broadcast pump seq numbers are local to the pump and unrelated to TerminalActor consumer state seq/emit_instants. handle_frame_ack still forwards these acks to ConsumerSyncState even when consumer_tick_emits is false. Today this is mostly wasted bookkeeping, but if output modes become negotiable or switch mid-session, raw-pump ACKs can poison state-sync RTT/last_acked accounting. Fix by gating FRAME_ACK handling on output mode, or adding an emitter/source id so ACKs only update the matching emitter.

title: In-process session re-attach (switch-session effect)
description:
Wire the phux-4li.20 `switch-session` effect to an actual in-process re-attach so `<leader> a` can be bound.

CURRENT STATE (phux-4li.20):
- The client caches the server session graph from the ATTACHED SessionSnapshot (crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs: FrameOutcome.sessions, set in the Attached arm; cached in driver.rs main_loop as `sessions`/`focused_session`).
- `session-picker` action (crates/phux-client/src/attach/input_dispatch.rs run_action) opens a SelectList of peer sessions; selecting commits `switch-session { name }` through run_action — the single dispatch path.
- `switch-session` sets ActionEffects.switch_session = Some(name); apply_action_effects (input_dispatch.rs ~line 384) currently only logs + bells. `<leader> a` is LEFT UNBOUND in crates/phux-config/src/default.toml.

WHY RE-ATTACH WAS SCOPED OUT:
main_loop (crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:360+, run_with_stdout_predict at ~242) is single-session by construction. It constructs ~15 session-scoped locals up front: panes: HashMap<TerminalId,PaneSlot>, workspace, focused_pane, predict (PredictionState), pending_splits, pending_windows, layout_get_request_id, status_bar, overlays, session_name, sessions cache, etc. The ATTACH handshake (send_attach + wait_for_attached, driver.rs:301-339) runs once before main_loop. There is no entry point to re-run the handshake against a new AttachTarget without tearing down and rebuilding all of that state.

PLUMBING REQUIRED:
1. Detach from the current session: send FrameKind::Detach, await DETACHED (the detach path already exists via ActionEffects.detach in apply_action_effects, input_dispatch.rs ~365).
2. Re-run the ATTACH handshake against AttachTarget::ByName(name) (resolve_* in phux-server runtime.rs ~1249-1320 already supports ByName/ById). send_attach + wait_for_attached are reusable but currently private to run_with_stdout_predict.
3. Reset session-scoped state for the new SessionSnapshot: clear panes, rebuild workspace from the new bootstrap (handle_server_frame Attached arm already does Workspace::single + seeds focused_pane + session_name + sessions), drop the prediction queue, re-issue GET_METADATA/SUBSCRIBE_METADATA for the new collection's layout key, repaint.
4. Decide the control-flow shape: either (a) main_loop returns a 'switch to target X' signal up to run_with_stdout_predict which loops the handshake+main_loop, or (b) an in-loop re-attach helper that rebuilds the locals in place. Option (a) is cleaner — main_loop returns an enum { Detached, SwitchTo(AttachTarget) }; the outer fn loops while keeping the RawModeGuard installed (no flicker between sessions).
5. Once it works end-to-end, bind `a` = "session-picker" in crates/phux-config/src/default.toml prefix-table (the comment there documents this) and add an integration test that a client switches sessions and sees the new session's terminal.

TESTS: integration test under crates/phux-client (or the server integration harness) that two sessions exist, client attaches to one, commits switch-session, and observes the other session's snapshot/output.
close_reason: In-process re-attach: main_loop returns LoopExit{Detached,SwitchTo(name)}; outer loop reuses RawModeGuard+Connection, detach_and_drain frees server per-consumer state, re-ATTACH ByName rebuilds all session-scoped locals + flicker-free clear. Wire test phux_eb0_in_process_reattach proves same-connection re-attach. Landed 4c3dc26.

title: audit: snapshot/diff epilogue drops alt-screen modes 1049 and 1047 (only re-emits 47)
description:
CONFIRMED. grid.rs emit_epilogue() (crates/phux-server/src/grid.rs:937-942) re-emits only DEC mode 47 (ALT_SCREEN_LEGACY) when reproducing terminal state in TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT and in the per-tick reference diff. Real full-screen programs use mode 1049 (ALT_SCREEN_SAVE: vim, less, man, htop, tmux) or occasionally 1047 (ALT_SCREEN). libghostty tracks 47/1047/1049 as three independent mode bits (libghostty terminal.rs lines ~840-858; verified: after '?1049h', Mode::ALT_SCREEN_LEGACY reads false).

IMPACT: When a client attaches to (or a resize-resync fires for) a pane running vim/less, the synthesized snapshot paints the alt-screen CONTENT but the receiving mirror Terminal stays on the PRIMARY screen. Worse, because the live 47 bit is off, the epilogue actively emits '?47l', forcing the primary screen. The per-tick diff epilogue (synthesize_against_reference -> emit_epilogue) has the same defect, so the divergence persists for the whole attach. ReferenceCursorMode::capture (grid.rs:716-732) and LastAckedCursorMode::capture (terminal_actor.rs:107-124) likewise only track alt_screen_legacy, so a 47<->1049 transition mid-session may also be missed by the diff trigger.

REPRO: see pinning test crates/phux-server/src/grid.rs::audit_snapshot_drops_alt_screen_1049_mode (passes today, documenting the gap; flip its assertions when fixed).

FIX SKETCH: emit_mode for Mode::ALT_SCREEN (1047) and Mode::ALT_SCREEN_SAVE (1049) in emit_epilogue, and add both bits to ReferenceCursorMode + LastAckedCursorMode. Note ordering: 1049 also saves cursor/clears, so it should be emitted before the cursor-position re-establishment, not after. Parent: phux-ahk.
close_reason: Alt-screen modes 47/1047/1049 now emitted independently in the paint PROLOGUE (before row walk + cursor re-establishment, so 1049 clear-on-entry can't wipe content); per-consumer diff toggles only on actual transition. ReferenceCursorMode + LastAckedCursorMode track all 3 bits. Landed 38fe7a2.

title: main CI red: spawn_terminal_inherits_focused_pane_live_cwd fails on Linux (exec of a shell builtin)
description:
main has been RED on the last 5+ consecutive CI runs (incl. commits unrelated to this test: 'blinking block cursor', beads syncs, docs/web #37). All fail on the SAME assertion: crates/phux-server/tests/spawn_terminal.rs:572 'expected ATTACHED' — the first frame after ATTACH is not TYPE_ATTACHED.

Evidence:
- Passes 5/5 locally on macOS /bin/sh.
- Fails deterministically on Linux CI (GitHub Actions, nix devshell) across multiple unrelated commits → NOT load flakiness; Linux-specific.

Leading hypothesis: the seed command is sh -c "cd '<dir>' && exec read _" (line 563). On Linux /bin/sh is dash, whose 'exec' rejects the 'read' builtin ('exec: read: not found'), so the seed shell dies, the pre-seeded 'focused' pane fails to spawn, and ATTACH ByName('focused') returns an ERROR frame instead of ATTACHED — tripping the line-572 assert. macOS /bin/sh tolerates it, hence green locally.

Suggested fix (to verify): drop 'exec' so the builtin runs in-shell: "cd '<dir>' && read _" (and ensure the pane stays alive without a tty stdin race). Confirm against dash before closing.

Impact: blocks merge on every PR (incl. phux-e0d / PR #38, whose own tests are green). This is the gating item for restoring a green main.
notes:
CORRECTION: the 'exec of read builtin' hypothesis is DISPROVEN. dash -c 'cd /tmp && exec read _' exits 0 — dash execs the builtin fine. Root cause is NOT shell portability of exec.

Verified facts only:
- Deterministic on Linux CI (GitHub Actions, nix devshell) across 5+ unrelated main commits.
- Green 5/5 on macOS /bin/sh locally.
- Failure is: first frame after ATTACH ByName('focused') != TYPE_ATTACHED (spawn_terminal.rs:572).
- Could not reproduce from macOS (platform=darwin); needs a Linux repro to identify what frame is actually received (likely an ERROR from a failed seed-pane spawn, but unconfirmed).

Root cause: UNKNOWN pending Linux repro. Do NOT apply a blind fix. Next step: reproduce on Linux (or add a one-shot CI debug commit logging the actual first frame type/payload) before changing the seed command or the spawn path.
close_reason: Fixed by commit 5a261db (#39): dropped 'exec' so the 'read' builtin blocks the seed/spawn shell on the PTY, keeping the focused pane alive past ATTACH. Main CI green for 2+ consecutive runs.

title: Replay-equivalence property test: snapshot + output stream reconstructs server grid (totality keystone)
description: Audit (this session) confirmed the server output stream is COMPLETE but found no test asserting full replay equivalence. Add that property test via PumpHarness (src/test_support.rs). This is the self-auditing invariant that catches any future side channel automatically. Includes a resize variant: assert replay equivalence holds ACROSS a resize, which probes the known ordering gap (resize mutates grid state via resize_rx with no representation in the byte stream, reconciled only by a post-reflow resync snapshot in terminal_actor.rs:~1565). If the resize variant diverges, file the gap as a follow-up rather than papering over it.

title: Splitting a pane blanks the original (source) pane's content
description: Repro (tmux-free, via crates/phux/examples/pty_screen.rs): attach, type 'echo MARKER' so the pane has content, then split (C-a | OR C-a -). The NEW pane shows a fresh shell prompt correctly, but the ORIGINAL pane you split from goes completely BLANK — its prior content (MARKER + prompt) disappears. Happens for both vertical (| , cols shrink) and horizontal (-, rows shrink) splits, so it is not cols-shrink-specific. PRE-EXISTING: reproduced on commit 706fc41 (before phux-tnh), so the phux-tnh pane-close reflow fix did not introduce it. Same family as phux-8v1 (libghostty reflow content-loss on the resized mirror + a state-sync gap), BUT notably phux-tnh's TerminalSpawned resync (which now emits TERMINAL_RESIZE for the shrunk original leaf on split) does NOT restore the content — so there is an additional mechanism beyond the resize resync: either the original pane's server Terminal loses content on its split reflow (so the resync snapshot is itself blank), or the split's SPAWN racing the original-pane resize leaves the resync capturing an empty grid. ONLY visible without tmux — tmux retains/reflows the byte stream and masks it. Verification rig: crates/phux/examples/pty_screen.rs (raw PTY + libghostty oracle, NO tmux). Investigate the local split action path (input_dispatch/actions split-pane), the original pane's client mirror reflow in paint_full_frame, and whether/what the server resyncs for the original leaf on split.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed tmux-free via pty_screen + focus-back experiment): the original pane's content is NOT lost permanently. Chain: (1) on split, paint_full_frame's safe_resize reflows the original pane's CLIENT mirror, which is lossy on shrink (same libghostty reflow issue as phux-8v1) so render_at_full paints it blank; (2) the server resync (phux-8v1/phux-tnh, ~50ms later) restores the mirror content via TERMINAL_OUTPUT vt_write, BUT non-focused panes are never repainted (server_frame.rs TerminalOutput/TerminalSnapshot handlers render only the FOCUSED pane), so the restored content is invisible; (3) focusing the pane (C-a h) triggers paint_full_frame which renders it via paint_focused_pane -> content reappears. PROOF: 'echo LEFTMARK999; C-a |; C-a h' shows LEFTMARK999 in the left pane. BIGGER BUG EXPOSED: non-focused panes are visually FROZEN — output to an unfocused pane updates its mirror but never repaints to screen until focus/full-repaint. FIX: repaint non-focused panes (cheap dirty-tracked render_at at their rect) when they receive TERMINAL_OUTPUT/SNAPSHOT, restoring the focused pane's cursor afterward. This fixes both the split-blank and the frozen-non-focused-pane class.
close_reason: Fixed in edb3c17. Root cause: non-focused panes were never repainted on TERMINAL_OUTPUT/SNAPSHOT (only the focused pane rendered), so the post-split resync that restores the original pane's mirror content was invisible until focus-switch. Fix: TERMINAL_OUTPUT handler now repaints non-focused panes at their rect (dirty-tracked render_at) + restores focused cursor. Also fixes the general frozen-non-focused-pane bug. Verified tmux-free via pty_screen for both | and - splits.

title: Client/server crash on terminal resize: libghostty PageList.resizeCols integer overflow when cols AND rows both shrink in one resize() call
description:
REPRO (verified via isolated tmux + resize-window): start phux attach at 100x30, resize terminal smaller in BOTH dimensions (e.g. 60x20) -> phux client panics with 'panic: integer overflow' inside libghostty Zig: PageList.resizeCols <- PageList.resize <- Terminal.resize <- ghostty_terminal_resize, called from phux_client::attach::paint::paint_full_frame (driver.rs:734 SIGWINCH branch). Process dies.

MATRIX (single pane, from 100x30):
- shrink cols only (->60x30): OK
- shrink rows only (->100x20): OK
- grow (->larger): OK
- shrink cols AND rows together (->60x20): CRASH
Splits crash the same way; not split-specific.

ROOT CAUSE: libghostty's PageList.resizeCols overflows when both dimensions decrease in a single resize() call (Zig integer-overflow safety check; debug build). phux depends on libghostty-vt as a pinned git rev, so the upstream Zig fix is out of this repo.

SERVER EXPOSURE: the same both-shrink hits the server too — on SIGWINCH the client sends TerminalResize(cols,rows) and terminal_actor.rs:1022 calls terminal.resize(cols,rows,...). A both-shrink there crashes the server.

FIX (phux-side workaround): a safe_resize(terminal, cols, rows) that, when both axes shrink vs the Terminal's current cols()/rows(), decomposes into two single-axis resize() calls (shrink rows first, then cols) — each individually safe. Apply at all libghostty resize call sites: client paint.rs (x2), client server_frame.rs:161, server terminal_actor.rs:1022. Long-term: fix/upstream PageList.resizeCols and drop the workaround.
close_reason: Fixed in 4afee05 via safe_resize decomposition (client paint.rs + server terminal_actor.rs): a both-axis shrink is split into two single-axis resize() calls, each safe. Verified single-pane + split both-shrink no longer crashes and redraws cleanly. Root cause is upstream ghostty PageList.resizeCols (self.rows - c.y - 1 underflow); fixing there separately. Workaround stays since phux pins a libghostty-vt git rev.

title: Auto-spawned server not daemonized: shares client controlling terminal, dies when terminal closes -> sessions vanish
notes: FIXED + verified. maybe_auto_spawn_server (crates/phux/src/main.rs) spawned the server as a plain child sharing the client's process group + controlling terminal (code even admitted 'good enough for demo'). Closing that terminal SIGHUP'd the server -> sessions vanished. FIX: auto-spawn now passes a hidden --daemonize flag; run_server calls rustix::process::setsid() before binding so the server lands in its own session with no controlling terminal (verified ps: PGID==PID, SESS=0). stderr redirected to phux-server.log beside the socket for debuggability. Added rustix 'process' feature to phux/Cargo.toml (same crate already used by phux-client; no new workspace dep). Verified: destroyed the originating terminal while attached -> server SURVIVED, session reattachable from a fresh terminal with content intact. Note: the zombie-client fix [[phux-bln]] also independently helped, but daemonization is the robust decoupling.

title: Detach never exits client: tokio::io::stdin reader thread hangs runtime teardown -> zombie steals first post-detach line (reattach 'does nothing')
notes: FIXED + verified. Root cause: detach returned Ok(()) and relied on unwinding, but tokio::io::stdin() (driver.rs) parks an UNCANCELLABLE blocking read on a helper thread; the RawModeGuard Drop restored termios fine, but the subsequent tokio runtime drop blocked forever waiting for that stuck read(). Result: a zombie client (confirmed alive 3s+ after detach) that kept a reader on the shared PTY and stole the FIRST line the user typed next -- typically the reattach command, so reattach appeared to do nothing. FIX: exit_after_detach() in driver.rs restores the terminal (mirrors terminal_reset_on_signal) and process::exit(0) at all three outcome.exit / detach-disconnect sites, bypassing the hung teardown. Verified via tmux harness: client gone <1s after detach, first post-detach command executes, reattach from the SAME shell works.

title: Split/resize leaves the surviving pane blank: paint_full_frame clears screen but render_at honors incremental dirty tracking
notes: paint_full_frame emits ED2 (\x1b[2J) then re-renders each pane via render_at. render_at early-returns on Dirty::Clean and only paints per-row-dirty rows. The pane that SURVIVES a split/resize has unchanged grid content, so libghostty reports it Clean -> render_at paints nothing -> the just-cleared screen leaves it BLANK. (Symptom looked like 'old pane shows stale content' but that stale content was actually the NEW pane's own fresh-shell zsh-init output; the original pane was simply empty.) FIX: added TerminalRenderer::render_at_full (forces Dirty::Full) and a force_full param on paint_focused_pane; paint_full_frame now forces a full redraw of every pane while the hot incremental TERMINAL_OUTPUT path stays dirty-tracked. Verified via tmux harness: SHORT-01..05 survive a '|' split into the left 40-col pane.
close_reason: Fixed: render_at_full + force_full on paint_focused_pane (committed b98a2c1, render.rs:174/paint.rs). paint_full_frame forces full redraw of every pane; hot incremental path stays dirty-tracked. Verified via tmux harness.

title: Split direction inverted: '|' produced stacked panes (horizontal divider) instead of side-by-side
notes: split_dir_arg in crates/phux-client/src/attach/input_dispatch.rs mapped the config 'direction' string straight to the same-named SplitDir variant. But the config string names the DIVIDER orientation (tmux model, documented in default.toml: '|' = vertical divider = side-by-side panes) while SplitDir names the SPLIT AXIS (Horizontal = splits width = side-by-side; Vertical = splits height = stacked, per layout::fill_rects). So 'vertical' was mapping to SplitDir::Vertical (stacked) when it should be SplitDir::Horizontal (side-by-side). FIX: crossed the mapping (horizontal->Vertical, vertical->Horizontal) + updated the unit test. Verified via scripts/tui-probe.sh: '|' now yields a vertical divider with side-by-side panes.
close_reason: Fixed: split_dir_arg mapping crossed in input_dispatch.rs:582-583 ('horizontal' divider->SplitDir::Vertical, 'vertical' divider->SplitDir::Horizontal) + unit test updated. '|' now yields side-by-side panes.

title: Live phux session: leader key inert, can't split, status bar shows only time, cursor stranded bottom-right
description:
Reported live by phall1 on main @ 2460eeb (2026-05-27 evening).

## Symptoms

- Cursor parks at bottom-right of host terminal for the entire session.
- Status bar shows only the time widget on the right; left (session-name) is blank.
- Prefix key (C-a) does nothing.
- Cannot split (C-a |, C-a -, all inert).

## Hypothesis (composite or single root?)

Two plausible root causes — possibly the same one, possibly two:

1. **Config path issue**: if phux_config::loader::load() degraded silently, both the resolver and status bar are disabled. Counter-evidence: time widget renders, so SOME status config is built — would expect a totally blank bar if config failed. Maybe only the session-name widget is failing (empty session_name string), in which case the resolver should still work.

2. **focused_pane is None when paint_full_frame runs**: see crates/phux-client/src/attach/paint.rs:100-117. paint_bar_after_pane is called with fallback_origin=None, and the focused-pane render is skipped when focused is None. The cursor stays at the status bar's tail (bottom-right). This explains the cursor symptom, but not the leader-key symptom unless the resolver path is also gated on focused_pane being Some.

3. **Input not reaching resolver**: c0_or_ascii_to_key(0x01) does emit KeyEvent { mods: CTRL, key: A }, and the resolver build was verified to produce Feed::Partial → Feed::Resolved("split-pane") for "C-a |". So the resolver itself is fine. Either the parser path is not feeding bytes, or consume_chord is not being called.

## Repro capture needed

User to run:
  RUST_LOG=trace,phux_client=trace ./target/debug/phux attach 2>/tmp/phux.log
  # press C-a once
  # press |
  # press C-a d to detach
Then attach /tmp/phux.log to this issue.

## Refs

- Last code commit: 034f37e (fix clippy in input dispatch)
- Default config: crates/phux-config/src/default.toml (prefix=C-a, prefix-table |/-/h/j/k/l/x/n/p/d, [status] left=[session-name], right=[time])
- Resolver verified via smoke test: produces Partial then Resolved("split-pane") for C-a |.
- Paint cursor restoration: phux-9xn, phux-dca, phux-b9n landed restore-on-bar-repaint.

LABELS: area:client, area:input, area:tui, crate:phux-client, regression
notes: REOPENED 2026-05-28: prior 'fix' (CUP-restore band-aids in paint.rs) never worked live. Real root cause: every paint path computes the correct cursor-restore CUP but NEVER FLUSHES it. stdout is a LineWriter; the restore CUP has no trailing newline, and dropping the StdoutLock guard does not flush the global buffer. render_at() flushes mid-frame BEFORE the restore CUP is written; the bar paint + restore CUP that follow sit in the buffer until the next pane output. At an idle prompt no output arrives, so the host cursor strands at the bar's tail = bottom-right. The phux-gxy unit tests passed because they assert on the in-memory Vec buffer, which never exercises the flush. FIX: flush stdout after the final cursor write in paint_bar_after_pane() and paint_full_frame(). Verified empirically via new scripts/tui-probe.sh harness: cursor now lands at the shell prompt (2,22) instead of (80,23).
close_reason: Resolved by commits since the 2460eeb report. Verified end-to-end via scripts/tui-probe.sh (80x24): C-a | splits into side-by-side panes (leader live, k2a direction correct), both panes paint (d69 force-full redraw), cursor lands in the new right pane's prompt at 43,22 (NOT stranded bottom-right 79,23), status bar time widget renders. Residual: status-bar LEFT (session-name) still blank — that is phux-17u (session-name not wired through ATTACHED), tracked separately.

title: BUG: vim renders only half the screen — pane area smaller than host viewport
description:
User-reported: opening vim under phux shows the buffer occupying roughly half the host terminal's vertical space.

## Possible root causes (need investigation)
1. **Server PTY sized smaller than host viewport.** ATTACH carries `viewport: ViewportInfo` (driver.rs:300) but the server may apply only a default 80x24 to the spawned PTY on first attach, ignoring the ATTACH viewport. Confirm by reading the server-side ATTACH handler in crates/phux-server/ and the spawn-on-attach path.

2. **Pane area computed at half-viewport on the CLIENT.** If `multi_pane::compute_layout` returns a Rect with h=viewport.rows/2 for the single-pane case, the client-side libghostty mirror would be resized smaller than the server's PTY, so visible cells are only the top half. Check default LayoutState single-pane case + compute_layout in multi_pane.rs.

3. **Stale split.** User may have accidentally triggered a vertical/horizontal split via the new `|` or `-` chord (phux-9fu) and there's a hidden invisible second pane taking half. Check by attaching and inspecting layout state; if there are 2 leaves with one of dim 0 or one blank, the split-on-action path has a bug.

4. **Status bar reserves the wrong number of rows.** pane_viewport reserves 1 row (paint.rs:151-157). If it reserves N rows incorrectly, vim sees a shrunken viewport. Unlikely (subtraction is just 1) but worth checking when status bar wraps.

## Reproduction
`phux attach` then `vim` — observe buffer height vs host terminal height.

## Acceptance
- vim opens at the full available height (host_rows - 1 for status bar).
- The server's PTY for the focused pane matches the client's pane Rect dimensions.
- No invisible second pane in default single-pane attach.

References:
- crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:298-313 (send_attach)
- crates/phux-client/src/attach/multi_pane.rs (compute_layout)
- crates/phux-server/src/runtime.rs (ATTACH handler)
- ADR-0013 (wire is VT bytes — server PTY size IS the canonical size)
close_reason: Landed on main as 248b5da (cherry-picked from fanout/phux-2lj-vim-half). Root cause: server's handle_attach in runtime.rs had _viewport prefixed with underscore — the ATTACH viewport was literally dropped on the floor. Panes spawned at hardcoded 80x24 and stayed there until first SIGWINCH. Fix: un-underscore + new apply_attach_viewport helper that mirrors handle_viewport_resize's per-actor resize fan-out. New regression test attach_viewport_resize.rs uses 'stty size' loop in PTY to verify post-ATTACH winsize; stash-verified to catch the bug (88 consecutive '24 80' readings without the fix).

title: BUG: cursor pinned at bottom-right of screen after fresh attach (paint sequence strands cursor when last_cursor is None)
description:
User-reported regression observed after phux-5ke + phux-b9n landed.

## Symptom
Cursor sits at the bottom-right corner of the host terminal after `phux attach`. Does not move with the focused pane's cursor.

## Hypothesised root cause (paint.rs:140-144)
`paint_bar_after_pane` only restores the cursor when `restore_cursor: Option<(u16,u16)>` is `Some`. `restore_cursor` traces back to `slot.renderer.last_cursor()` which returns `None` whenever libghostty's `Snapshot::cursor_viewport()` returns None — which happens on fresh attach (no PTY output yet), during alt-screen transitions, and any frame where the cursor sits outside the viewport.

In those None cases, the previous `StatusBarPainter::paint` writes to the bottom-row cells and naturally leaves the terminal cursor at the end of the bar (bottom-right). The phux-b9n fix made the cursor visible but did not give it a fallback landing position.

## Fix sketch
When `restore_cursor` is None, fall back to positioning at the focused pane's origin + (0,0) (or last known position). Two reasonable options:
1. Cache the last non-None cursor per slot; reuse when current is None.
2. Position cursor at focused pane's (rect.x, rect.y) — guaranteed to be inside the pane and away from the bar.

Option 2 is simpler and matches user expectation (cursor inside the visible pane).

## Acceptance
- `phux attach` shows the cursor inside the focused pane immediately, not at bottom-right.
- vim, less, htop, nvim cursor positioning still correct (they emit their own CUP).
- Regression test: extend an existing paint test or add a new one asserting cursor position is inside pane rect after `paint_full_frame` with a freshly-created pane (no PTY output).

References:
- crates/phux-client/src/attach/paint.rs:116-145 (paint_bar_after_pane)
- crates/phux-client/src/attach/render.rs:73-74 (last_cursor doc)
- commit 138c772 (phux-b9n cursor-invisible fix)
close_reason: Landed on main as 78b316c (cherry-picked from fanout/phux-9xn-dca-cursor-bar). paint_bar_after_pane now plumbs the focused pane's Rect origin as a fallback; when last_cursor is None it emits CSI {y+1};{x+1}H + ESC[?25l so the cursor lands inside the pane area (hidden) rather than stranded at bottom-right after the bar paint. 3 new regression tests in attach/paint.rs::tests. 264 phux-client tests + integrated workspace 786/786 green.

title: Cursor invisible on fresh attach (status bar ?25l strands cursor)
description:
Surfaced immediately after phux-5ke landed on main (2026-05-27).
User reports cursor not visible on `phux attach`.

## Root cause

`render::chrome::status_bar::write_buffer` emitted `\x1b[?25l` (hide
cursor) at the start of every bar paint with the comment "Cursor stays
hidden — caller restores at the focused pane." The caller
(`attach::paint::paint_bar_after_pane`) only restored visibility when
`restore_cursor.is_some()`.

`restore_cursor` traces to `slot.renderer.last_cursor()`, which is
None whenever `libghostty_vt::Snapshot::cursor_viewport()` returns None
(per libghostty docs: "if it is currently visible within the viewport").
On a fresh attach with no PTY output yet, libghostty has no viewport
cursor and returns None — so the bar's `?25l` strands the cursor
invisible until the first pane render with a visible cursor.

Pre-existed wave-2 (the OLD hand-painted status_bar.rs also emitted
`?25l`), but went unnoticed because the older paint paths happened to
re-emit `?25h` more often. Wave-2's collapsed paint sequence
(`paint_full_frame` calls bar LAST with no following pane render) makes
the bug consistently visible on fresh attach.

## Fix landed

`crates/phux-client/src/render/chrome/status_bar.rs::write_buffer` no
longer emits `\x1b[?25l`. The flicker concern from the original comment
is sub-millisecond on modern terminals; the bug it created was visible
on every fresh attach.

`crates/phux-client/src/attach/paint.rs::paint_full_frame` reordered:
focused pane now paints LAST (after dividers and status bar) so its
`render_at` is the final cursor-positioning + DECTCEM emit. This
matches the comment in `render::chrome::dividers` that already claimed
"the focused-pane render runs after dividers."

Incremental path (`server_frame::handle_server_frame`) unchanged —
still emits `?25h` via `paint_bar_after_pane`'s restore branch when
`focused_cursor.is_some()`.

## Acceptance

- `phux attach` shows the cursor immediately, before any PTY output.
- `just ci` green (721 tests).
- No regression in vim/less cursor-hide behavior (focused pane render
  still owns DECTCEM via `snapshot.cursor_visible()`).
notes: Landed in #31 (138c772).

title: [epic] Lazy state synchronization wire — server-side implementation per ADR-0018
description:
Implement ADR-0018 (Lazy state synchronization). Wire shape is unchanged; semantics of TERMINAL_OUTPUT.bytes shift from "PTY pass-through" to "minimum VT to transition consumer's last-acked state to canonical's current state".

Scope per ADR-0018 addendum (2026-05-26 revision): the per-consumer cache primitive is libghostty RenderState, already used in-tree. The work is lifecycle (per-attached-consumer RenderState ownership in TerminalActor) + incremental synthesis (extend SnapshotSynthesizer) + tick scheduler + ack-driven dirty reset. Estimated ~200-400 LOC of new code plus per-consumer cache management.

Blocked on phux-28f (TerminalActor placement) for the lifecycle piece. The synthesis extension can proceed in parallel against the existing SnapshotSynthesizer.

References:
- ADR-0018 (Lazy state synchronization) + 2026-05-26 addendum
- research/2026-05-26-state-sync-algorithm.md (revised Dependencies §)
- bd memory: renderstate-as-cache, mosh-decomposition (updated)

Plus phux-l0t (libghostty FFI bug diagnosis #5) and phux-6jb (tracking ticket for upstream fix revisit). Only q0e.5 (RTT-adaptive tick) remains, deferred per its description. title: client: attach failure wedges terminal (alt-screen + cursor hidden); graceful failure UX
description:
Repro: \`phux attach <session>\` when no server is running, or when the session doesn't exist, or when the client gets signal-killed mid-attach. Terminal is left in alt-screen mode + cursor hidden + sometimes raw mode. User has to type \`reset\` blind.

Root causes:
1. \`attach::run\` installs RawModeGuard (alt-screen + raw mode + hide cursor) BEFORE the UDS connect + handshake. Any pre-handshake failure flickers the terminal through alt-screen for nothing.
2. RawModeGuard::Drop only runs on Rust unwinding. SIGTERM/SIGKILL/SIGHUP bypass it. The cleanup escapes (\\x1b[?1049l + \\x1b[?25h) never get written.
3. No signal handler installed to restore terminal state on signal exit.
4. Auto-spawn server always uses DEFAULT_SESSION_NAME ('default') but client asks for whatever was on the CLI. Mismatch causes attach to fail at handshake while client is already in alt-screen.
5. Connection errors surface as 'attach failed: connection refused' — actionable would be 'no phux server at <path>; start one with \`phux server\`' with the exact suggested command.
6. Stale socket files survive a crashed server (separate ticket — file follow-up).

Acceptance for THIS ticket:
- attach::run defers RawModeGuard installation until AFTER handshake + ATTACH succeeds (or skip alt-screen entirely on early failure).
- SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers installed that run terminal cleanup before exit.
- ConnectionRefused/NotFound socket errors produce a one-line clean error WITHOUT entering alt-screen.
- Auto-spawn passes the user's requested session name through to the spawned server.
- Test under the new \`Screen\` harness: a synthetic 'no server' scenario captures stdout and asserts NO alt-screen-enter byte sequence appears.

Out-of-scope: stale-socket cleanup (file follow-up bd if not already covered).

title: feat(server): wire INPUT_KEY/INPUT_MOUSE/INPUT_FOCUS dispatch in handle_client
description: handle_client in runtime.rs falls through input frames to the catch-all _ arm, silently dropping every keystroke from attached clients. Wire FrameKind::InputKey/InputMouse/InputFocus to the existing PaneActor input mpsc via ServerState. Add a wire-level integration test that drives an InputKey frame through a real UDS connection and verifies it reaches the PaneActor PTY (not just direct PaneActor exercise like pty_pump.rs). Validation: drop with warn! on unknown pane_id or unattached client. Closes the gap noted in phux-byc.6.5 description.
