title: byc.8: server-side Terminal placement — spawn_local + LocalSet OR actor pattern
description:
Coming concern for byc.8 (server ATTACH handler). libghostty Terminal is !Send + !Sync (holds NonNull<TerminalImpl>, no unsafe impl Send/Sync in libghostty source).

runtime.rs:258 currently uses tokio::spawn (Send-required) for per-client handler tasks. Today the handler holds no Terminal — only logs unhandled frames. byc.8 will add real ATTACH handling that needs to own a Terminal per pane.

Three viable shapes — byc.8 must pick one:

1. spawn_local + LocalSet — keeps current_thread runtime per ADR-0003; Terminal stays on the runtime thread; preferred.
2. Dedicated pane-supervisor task that owns the Terminal; channels (mpsc) for input/output. The 'actor model' that was flagged earlier in the session as a possible refactor for ServerState shape. Cleaner separation but more plumbing.
3. RefCell<Terminal> behind Rc on a single-threaded executor. Discouraged — fights tokio's spawn conventions.

Do NOT try Arc<Mutex<Terminal>> — won't compile (Mutex requires Send for cross-thread sharing; Terminal isn't Send).

Decision needed at start of byc.8 work. ADR-worthy if the actor pattern is picked.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-0014 (per-terminal TerminalActor on LocalSet) + TerminalActor impl (crates/phux-server/src/terminal_actor.rs, 987 LOC, uses spawn_local + LocalSet per design 3 in original ticket). The ticket was filed when the actor pattern was still being chosen; ADR-0014 picked option 1 (spawn_local + LocalSet, one borrower, no RefCell) and shipped as TerminalActor in phux-byc.5. Unblocks phux-q0e.2.

title: Per-client capability downsampling: define ColorSupport + downsample fn + per-client storage
description:
SPEC §6.2 conformance: `crates/phux-server/src/grid.rs:121-122` unconditionally
emits `Color::Rgb` with a comment that says "the wire carries the final pixel
value" — directly violating SPEC §6.2: "a client advertising Indexed256 MUST
never receive truecolor RGB cells; the server must downsample."

## Design seam: per-pane capture vs per-client fanout

Three options were considered:

1. First-attach floor — capture in the lowest tier any current client
   advertises. Rejected: locks downsampling into the canonical state; a
   later-attaching TrueColor client cannot recover precision.
2. Per-tier cache — capture once in TrueColor, materialize one cached
   diff per active tier. Rejected as premature; complicates invalidation
   and is unnecessary until profiling shows it.
3. On-demand downsample at fanout — capture once in canonical TrueColor;
   each per-client fanout call downsamples to that client's advertised
   tier. Selected. Matches the existing "server owns canonical state,
   clients see derived views" model and keeps the diff-compute path tier-
   agnostic.

## Scope of THIS ticket (substrate only)

- `ColorSupport` enum (TrueColor | Indexed256 | Indexed16) in phux-protocol.
- `downsample(Color, ColorSupport) -> Color` (as helper fn, since `Color` is a
  re-export of libghostty-vt's StyleColor — no inherent impl possible).
- Per-client cap storage on `AttachedClient` in phux-server::state.
  Defaulted to `ColorSupport::TrueColor` (most-permissive; clients without
  advertised caps don't get downgraded).
- New `phux-server::downsample` module with `downsample_op` /
  `downsample_cell` for byc.5's fanout to plug into.
- Comprehensive unit + property tests.
- `diff_spike` MUST remain byte-identical — downsample is per-fanout, not
  per-capture; nothing in the capture path changes.

## Out of scope (follow-up tickets)

- HELLO ColorSupport wiring (SPEC §6.1 conformance — separate task).
- CIELAB perceptual color distance for downsample (better Indexed16 picks).
- Fanout layer itself (byc.5).
close_reason: Substrate landed in cc30ab5. ColorSupport enum + downsample_color + per-client color_support on AttachedClient + phux-server::downsample helper module + comprehensive tests (unit + proptest). diff_spike byte-identical. Follow-ups: phux-7lf (HELLO wiring), phux-i02 (CIELAB), phux-982 (Cow signature).

title: Wire frames: ATTACH/ATTACHED/DETACH/DETACHED + INPUT_KEY/MOUSE/FOCUS/PASTE
description:
phux-byc.4 surfaced that the message-catalog frames from SPEC §7.1-§7.5 + §9 are missing from phux-protocol's FrameKind enum. byc.4 landed the server-side state scaffold but its 5 wire-level integration tests had to be deferred until these variants exist. Until this lands, the byc epic cannot demonstrate end-to-end attach. Likely belongs as a phux-6yl follow-up; filing standalone for visibility.

## Required Skills
rust,tlv,protocol-design
design:
phux-protocol::wire::frame::FrameKind currently has: Hello, Ping, PaneDiff.

Add (per SPEC §7.1-§7.5 + §9):

  C → S
    Attach { session_name: String, role: ?? }   // §7.1
    Detach                                       // §7.3
    InputKey(KeyEvent)                           // §9.1
    InputMouse(MouseEvent)                       // §9.2
    InputFocus(FocusEvent)                       // §9.3
    InputPaste(PasteEvent)                       // §9.4
    InputRaw(Bytes)                              // §9.5 (only if a passthrough is needed; can defer)

  S → C
    Attached { session_id, window_id, pane_id, snapshot: PaneSnapshot }   // §7.2
    Detached                                                              // §7.3
    Bell { pane_id }                                                       // §7.6
    OscEvent { ... }                                                       // §7.7 (defer; not needed for byc.5)
    Alert { ... }                                                          // §7.8 (defer)

Plus the SessionId tagged-union on the wire (per ADR-0007 §3): protocol-level
SessionId is u32 newtype; on-wire it's tagged with the addressed satellite.

For each frame:
  - Add a FrameKind variant
  - Add TLV field IDs in wire/field.rs (per phux-6yl.4)
  - Add encoder + decoder, mirroring how PaneDiff is wired
  - Add an insta hex snapshot covering at least one representative payload
  - Round-trip proptest if the variant has structured payload

phux_protocol::ids::SessionId (wire-side u32) vs phux_core::ids::SessionId
(slotmap key, opaque). They are distinct by design — wire SessionIds are
allocated by the server, slotmap keys are an in-process registry detail.
Add a server-side ::from(phux_core::ids::SessionId) -> wire-side SessionId
mapping + reverse lookup. Don't define a `From` impl in phux-protocol
itself (would force a phux-core dep on phux-protocol).

Verify:
  cargo nextest run -p phux-protocol
  cargo run -p phux-server --example diff_spike   # untouched
acceptance_criteria: FrameKind has all the C→S and S→C variants from SPEC §7. Round-trip + insta snapshots cover each new variant. phux-server's deferred byc.4 integration tests now compile (filing a separate ticket for them).
notes: Discovered by phux-byc.4 agent retro. Blocks byc.5 (e2e test), 9gw.3 (attach loop), and the e2e harness epic phux-a87.
close_reason: Landed in fa335e1. Added FrameKind variants Attach/Detach/InputKey/InputMouse/InputFocus/InputPaste (C->S) and Attached/Detached/Bell (S->C) per SPEC §7.1-§7.5 + §9.1-§9.4. Encoders/decoders mirror PaneDiff pattern, 13 insta snapshots + 7 proptest round-trips. Non-obvious decisions for byc.6: (1) AttachRole {Primary=0, Viewer=1} is phux-defined (not in SPEC §13) -- minimum useful split. (2) PaneSnapshot {cols, rows, ops: Vec<DiffOp>} is minimum per SPEC §8.4 -- cursor/modes/scrollback are TODO. (3) Detached carries no body this wave (SPEC §7.3 {reason, message} deferred). (4) FrameKind dropped Eq (now PartialEq only) because MouseEvent has f64. (5) Added DecodeError::UnknownEnumValue {field, value} for libghostty atom round-trip safety. NOT touched: phux-core, phux-server (per task scope), no From<phux_core::ids::SessionId>. Deferred: OscEvent §7.7, Alert §7.8, InputRaw §9.5. title: Server pane plumbing: PTY + per-pane diff loop
description:
Wire a real pane: spawn child PTY, feed bytes into libghostty_vt::Terminal, run grid::capture each frame, compute DiffOps, gate by FRAME_ACK/snapshot fallback per SPEC §6. Pools RenderState/RowIterator/CellIterator per pane (the spike allocates each call). Single-pane, no IPC yet — that's phux-byc.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `cargo run -p phux-server --example one_pane bash` spawns a real shell, accepts typed input from stdin, prints DiffOp summaries to stderr per frame.
- [ ] Steady-state capture loop allocates zero bytes (validated by criterion bench or dhat-rs heap trace).
- [ ] Clean shutdown on child exit (no zombie process, no panic on EOF).
- [ ] diff_spike example continues to print "replay invariant: snap0 + diff(0→1) == snap1   ✓" after the refactor.
- [ ] `cargo nextest run -p phux-server` green; clippy -D warnings clean.

title: Protocol foundation: input types + wire codec

Blocks all wire-format-dependent work (server runtime, client, transport).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] A KeyEvent constructed in phux-protocol, converted via the server-side From impl, encoded by libghostty_vt's KeyEncoder, produces VT bytes that match committed insta hex snapshots for ≥10 representative cases (incl. ≥3 KIP enhancement levels).
- [ ] Arbitrary `Vec<DiffOp>` round-trips through the wire codec via proptest (≥1024 cases, no shrinks to failure).
- [ ] Insta hex-dump snapshots committed for ≥8 representative diff frames (small change visible in PR diff).
- [ ] `cargo nextest run --workspace` green; `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.
- [ ] No libghostty types leak through phux-protocol's public API (verified by `cargo tree -p phux-protocol` not listing libghostty-vt).

title: Supervise collector lifecycle and deliver compact usage readings

title: Design the isolated usage collector and delivery seam
description: Establish the architecture for an optional Phux usage capability without bloating the terminal hot path. Re-read current plugin runtime, server hooks, process model, Cockpit product direction, and Token Tach reuse candidates. Record: process isolation vs in-process collection; the lifecycle/delivery seam (existing plugin machinery is insufficient as a 30s hook host); first source; measurement scope; supported platforms; fresh-install accounting start; disable/enable behavior; failure/staleness contract; measured resource budgets. Prefer an isolated collector process with Phux owning a narrow lifecycle seam. Do not invent a general plugin framework. Do not import Token Tach history. Allocate any ADR number only at authoring time.

title: Bring Token Tach into Phux as an optional native usage capability
description:

User decisions (2026-09-12): clean cut, no Token Tach history import or compatibility work; collect on the server machine while Phux runs, including when Cockpit is closed; quiet burn and estimated cost in everyday use; richer Instrument view is discoverable optional detail, not a hidden easter egg. Keeping Phux lean is a load-bearing requirement.

Recommended architecture to establish in the design child: an isolated collector process owns transcript/SQLite readers, attribution, pricing and accounting; Phux owns the narrow lifecycle/delivery seam and Cockpit consumes compact projections. Existing plugin execution is child-process based, but current server event hooks time out after 30 seconds and are not a continuous collector host. Do not transplant Token Tach orchestration or invent a general plugin framework for this one feature.

Working assumption, not an additional user requirement: collect the server user’s supported local agents, including those launched outside Phux, and associate them with Phux work only when identity is established. Resolve measurement scope, first source, supported server platforms and fresh-install accounting start semantics in design. Selectively reuse verified code and fixtures from ../token-tach; a whole-app refactor there is not a prerequisite. Standalone retirement follows a usable replacement; filing this epic does not authorize deleting data, archiving a repository or cutting a release.

acceptance_criteria: A one-source end-to-end readout proves the design before fleet expansion. Disabled capability performs no collector scans or polling; enabled collection continues with Cockpit closed and follows server shutdown. Collector failure or slow delivery does not stall terminal input/rendering and yields explicit stale/unavailable readings. CPU, memory, scan work, update volume and terminal latency are measured with reproducible bounds. One accounting implementation supplies all views; exact tokens and estimated cost are distinguished. No legacy Token Tach import is required. Child beads have verified evidence and the optional Instrument view follows the quiet native experience.

title: ATTACH-time reflow tombstones other native pumps without scheduling a resync
description: apply_attach_viewport (runtime/attach.rs ~3824) sends resync_clients: false, but handle_resize calls invalidate_all_native_cursors (resource/terminal/io.rs:265), tombstoning every other client native pump on the pane; apply_resize_request returns None so no resync follows. With the smallest window-size policy a newcomer shrinking the grid can freeze existing native consumers until they lag. Schedule an everyone-resync whenever native cursors are invalidated by a reflow. Found in review of 163cd9bb (phux-auqy).
notes: 2026-09-12: fixed on fix/stale-resync-per-consumer. invalidate_all_native_cursors reports the pumps it tombstoned (owner, stream, bootstrap_id) and an attach-time reflow owes a resync addressed to exactly them; takes_resync admits a named pump that is fenced or retired. Known limit from review: the revival is one-shot - if broadcast_resync fails to synthesize the snapshot, the tombstoned pumps stay frozen until the next everyone-resync (they never retry on their own).
close_reason: Landed on main (d4e85bda..2fcf8e45): gap and stale resyncs are addressed to the pump that fell behind (owner, stream, generation); an attach-time reflow owes a resync to the native pumps it tombstoned; staleness is aged from the later of the read and the replay hand-off. Full bar green before push.

title: Native checkpoint binding keyed by client only: two pumps from one client on a pane tombstone each other

Key the binding by (owner, stream_id). Found in review of 163cd9bb (phux-auqy).

title: Stale-output resync republishes every consumer on the pane

title: Release resolution must filter stable streams and paginate installers and self-update
description: At d5e2977c both curl installers parse only tag_name via sed from first 30 GitHub releases. They ignore prerelease/draft fields, depend on pretty JSON formatting, and stop when stream has no recent release. Core phux update parses JSON and filters draft/prerelease but also only requests 30 entries; curl redirect failure aborts instead of trying list. Need shared behavior contract across self-update and standalone POSIX scripts: exact tags, published stable releases, bounded or Link-driven pagination, actionable failure. Hermetic release-list fixtures must cover interleaved streams, compact JSON, prereleases and stream on later page.
acceptance_criteria: Standalone POSIX installers structurally parse mixed release JSON and required stable metadata, select the correct stream, paginate at most 10 pages with 1 MiB page limits, and report actionable failures. Explicit canonical pins bypass release discovery in installers and updater. Hermetic RED/GREEN coverage and scoped Rust updater gates pass; verified changes committed locally.

Shared POSIX awk parser is embedded verbatim by scripts/sync-install-resolver.sh; runtime requires no jq/Python/new package. Typed serde metadata in updater; both use 10 pages of 30 and 1 MiB response cap. Shell download file limits and Rust bounded stdout reader prevent unbounded index buffering; curl uses connect/total timeouts, wget connect/read timeout and one attempt. Explicit version bypasses discovery in check/dry-run/install modes. Success JSON schema is deliberately bumped to 2 because latest_version becomes nullable for pins/rollback; target_version stays selected tag, common JSON error schema unchanged. description: Remainder of phux-c2td.21 after a7a10475 (coordinator-qualified identity, up to four coordinators, peers attach only when a session is shown). Still open: (1) tab commands on a peer's tab (close, split, reorder, split-drag) are refused because workspace edits go only to the active coordinator; route them to the owning coordinator; New Tab and the available-terminal list should follow the focused coordinator. (2) A showing peer's placements are not saved across relaunch, and only the last remote host is remembered. (3) A failed peer retries only when its row is picked; add backoff retry. (4) Disconnect removes every host; make it per host. (5) A fifth coordinator is refused; decide whether the cap should grow. (6) Placements saved for a remote active host before a7a10475 carry the old provider id; migrate them. (7) A late close event after slot reuse can mark the new peer failed; tag channel events with a slot generation.

Independent review found no violation of the no-attach or owner-only rules; its findings fixed. title: Generate ServerFeature tables and counts from caps.rs instead of hand-maintaining them
description: Every wire-touching branch in epic phux-c2td (.3, .4, .7, .8, .11) conflicted with its siblings on the same hand-maintained copies of the feature set: the caps.rs known-bits mask, the server's advertised-features list (phux-server runtime/client.rs), the proto.md feature table and bit list, the phux status feature-name list (crates/phux/src/commands/status.rs), and the pinned name count in its test. Each landing forced a manual bit-order merge and a count bump from 12 up to 16. Make caps.rs the single source: derive the known-bits mask and a name table from one declarative list, have status.rs and the advertised list read it, replace the pinned count with a test that asserts every ServerFeature variant has exactly one name, and generate the proto.md table (just docs-gen, byte-compared like docs/reference/). The spec CHANGELOG draft-row collisions are a separate process issue; note them here but keep the scope to the feature tables.

description: Follow-up to phux-6xqf. The four pane-kill fixtures in crates/phux-server/src/resource/terminal/tests_lifecycle.rs now use RAII FixtureGroup/FixturePane guards (tests_fixture_groups.rs) that killpg+reap on normal exit and panic unwind. title: Investigate hosted Unix coordinator-start fixture timeout
description: Observed on main bdd8df17 Cockpit CI run34422417547 job102700544639: extension.test.Unix worker ensures selected coordinator before attempting its socket failed src/providers/phux/extension.zig827 asserting fixture ready/disconnect within5s. title: setup-zig cache entries are single-use and accumulate GB per day
description:
The mlugg/setup-zig cache key embeds the run ID (setup-zig-cache-v2-<job>-zig-aarch64-macos-0.16.0--<run_id>-<n>), so every entry is single-use: it can only ever be restored through a restore-key prefix fallback, never by exact match. Eight entries accumulated 2.98 GB in a single day (2026-09-04) and were still occupying the 10 GB repository cache cap five days later.

Context: found while fixing the cache budget in PR #572, which handles the sccache half (PR lanes now write nothing) and adds pr-janitor cache reclamation on PR close. The Zig half is out of that PR's scope because the caches come from mlugg/setup-zig on cockpit-release's install-zig.sh fallback branch and cockpit-sdk-head (manual dispatch) — not from the routed product lanes.

Options to evaluate:
- Set use-cache: false on the manual/fallback lanes; scripts/install-zig.sh is the CI path and does its own toolchain handling.
- Gate the setup-zig cache write to main, matching the sccache/rust-cache policy now documented in docs/RELEASING.md 'Cache budget'.
- Confirm whether the cockpit-release fallback branch (hashFiles('scripts/install-zig.sh') == '') can fire at all; if not, the action invocation is dead code.

Legacy entries were deleted out of band; this is about preventing regrowth.
close_reason: Landed via PR #608 — setup-zig cache no longer single-use/accumulating.

title: Investigate Cockpit experience and propose ambitious native UI overhaul
description: Read current shipping chrome, tabs, focus, motion, menus, settings and product constraints; inspect available visual/runtime evidence; deliver a cohesive ambitious redesign proposal with concrete interaction concepts, implementation seams and acceptance criteria. Proposal only, pending user direction on implementation.
design: Proposed direction: a precision-instrument native workspace. Integrated platform-aware titlebar; restrained lime focus indicators instead of saturated selected-tab slabs; contextual status capsule replaces persistent healthy-state footer. Tactile top/side tabs with stable titles, anchored overflow, close/context actions, drag proxies and Escape rollback. Split composition with drop previews, equalize, reversible focus/peek, and eventual identity-preserving cross-window placement transfer. Window-local palette and genuine modeless native Settings window; one visible input owner and deterministic focus return. One command catalogue projects native menus/context actions/palette/shortcuts with live enabled states. Settings appearance studio: reversible preview, readable rescue theme, ANSI/TUI samples, configuration provenance, comment-preserving edits, explicit apply scope and persistence errors. Motion uses existing 150/200/300ms tokens and platform accessibility preferences, never interpolates terminal grid/viewport geometry. Optional workspace overview and named presentation arrangements, without new execution authority. Exception-driven attention navigates to relevant pane without auto-reordering or focus theft. Delivery: first a coherent native vertical slice covering integrated chrome, tabs, splits, palette and settings; then spatial manipulation and attention. Acceptance spans real host captures, display scale, window/fullscreen sizes, long labels/overflow, keyboard/IME/AX/focus, reduced motion, settings cancel/save failure, zero animation-driven resize storms, execution identity stability and idle/render/input measurements.

title: Audit Cockpit architecture and rank near-term seams
description: Read-only architectural assessment requested by the user, ignoring implementation cost and SDK fork economics. Compare the current shipping Cockpit code with PRODUCT_DIRECTION.md and DURABLE_WORK_ARCHITECTURE.md. Identify responsibility and identity/lifetime coupling, rank useful seams, preserve Phux authority and existing terminal correctness, and specify concrete current-behavior acceptance evidence. This task covers the assessment, not authorization or completion of the proposed refactors.
design:
Architectural assessment, source-only, reconciled against 6bf51affecfc514b47d503b614e6870b8fd22e47 after another session advanced main during inspection. Parent reviewed the intervening diff and reread the load-bearing sites. Independent read-only lanes: ses_f7a4ab789ffe22zcp6zz1IOFVe (topology/content/lifetime/creation/attention) and ses_f7a4ab63cffebztAES5ITqXjxc (interaction/authority/targets/publication). No code changes, live app tests, or performance measurements.

PRIORITY 1: SINGLE-WRITER WORKSPACE TRANSACTIONS AND SYNCHRONOUS INPUT CONTEXT. native_extension.zig:622-628 paintChrome writes engine.model.tab_placement from the optimistic TS projection; core.ts:783-788 optimistically updates placement before the fenced intent. ts_engine.zig:460-479 owns command acceptance/revision. Native paint therefore crosses the writer seam. native_extension.zig:600-611 learns overlay mode during paint/frame and sets input suspension there. Refactor WorkspaceController/InteractionRouter so interaction commits own preferences, selection, focus/modal context and typed effects; renderer consumes state and may report measurements through a distinct geometry interface. Preserve native terminal hot paths. Acceptance: stale placement command plus painting speculative model cannot mutate canonical placement/revision; open/close overlay then immediate key/text/release/pointer/drop before next frame respects committed per-window mode; owner change releases held input/capture. Source hazard, not a reproduced physical input leak.

PRIORITY 2: PUBLICATION AS A TRANSACTION RESULT. native_extension.zig:776-801 announces raw pointer changes only for geometry_changed; ts_engine.zig:1284-1314 can focus a different terminal yet returns consumed. Same-window adoption does not publish. ts_snapshot.zig:113-132 derives title/cwd/attention from the focused split, exposing a missed dependency. topologyWritten at native_extension.zig:313-317 returns only engine_wake although topologyPersisted changes snapshot-visible persistence flags. Return explicit scoped change domains (surface damage, interaction/accessibility, workspace focus/topology, catalog metadata, operation status) from controlled transitions. Keep snapshot-generation coherence and terminal bytes outside chrome. Acceptance: focus quiet splits updates chrome without output; persistence failure/recovery publishes without another command; ordinary output repaints without catalog/snapshot work. These require regression reproduction before bug-fix claims.

PRIORITY 3: IDENTITY-TARGETED COMMANDS WITH CORRELATED OUTCOMES, SEPARATE FROM PLACEMENT. core.ts:745-788 and protocol.ts encode tab/catalog positions plus one global revision despite existing tab IDs/TerminalRefs. ts_engine global revision includes metadata and unrelated config actions. Carry opaque target identities/window incarnation and dependency-specific preconditions; keep replica generation fences and coherent cross-object topology preconditions. Preserve highlighted destination across catalog reorder, not just cursor ordinal. Bridge.send discards applyIntent outcome; Creation.complete/disconnect in durable_creation.zig:100-123 reduce failures/unknown outcomes to terminal_limit_refused; acceptResult:150-157 discards all non-success distinctions. Lower provider operations.Ledger already has request/epoch correlation and unknown_outcome: reuse it. Separate operation receipt/projection from optional PlacementIntent; accepted work and failure to place it are different outcomes. Acceptance: unrelated title change does not refuse identity-targeted close; earlier-row deletion does not change highlighted destination; refused/unknown/accepted-awaiting-publication remain distinguishable; destination close/reuse cannot retarget placement or alter operation result; disconnect never retries spawn. Current receipts remain ephemeral; durable OperationId/result lookup wait for Phux capabilities.

PRIORITY 4: VIEW IDENTITY, CONTENT, AND LIFETIME. layout.zig:44-64 embeds TerminalRef in geometry leaves; model.zig:442-461 Workspace is terminal trees plus web_selected takeover. Retained host browser is out-of-tree/main-window-specific; do not claim it is shipped through the current TS graph. Use process-local ViewId leaves plus a concrete surface/content registry, preserving one resolver; TerminalRef/ReplicaOwner remain inside terminal attachments. model.zig:1413-1454 normalization removes views on terminal membership retirement (pending restored attachments already exempt); explicit attachment/resource retirement must be distinct from user closing a view. Local process-exit auto-close remains explicit terminal policy; missing terminal is not evidence of completed work. Persistence stays presentation-only; do not invent WorkSession IDs. Acceptance: existing terminal geometry/hit-test/resize results hold; inert read-only content and terminal share resolver; nonterminal content emits no terminal input/resize; moving a view preserves binding; provider retirement and user close are separate transitions; no fabricated completion evidence.

PRIORITY 5: RESOURCE/REPLICA STATE VERSUS PER-VIEW INTERACTION. terminal/session.zig:178-235 owns selection, measured_cell/font_size, search along with emulator; local/provider.zig:227-248 bundles PTY and interaction state; phux/host.zig:86-109 has one terminal viewport, :161-168 one host search owner, :739-763 search clears prior results. FFI client.rs:175-192 keys render/selection/gestures/viewport by TerminalId. Extract TerminalView state/lifetime and resource attachment with explicit one resize/control owner policy. Independent simultaneous viewports require a real view-aware kernel/FFI contract or separate appropriately controlled replicas; moving fields alone does not provide it. Initial extraction can preserve one-view invariant; tests must prove independent search/viewport before lifting it. Acceptance: move/rebind/close view cancels exact owned gestures/search borrows and does not reset another view or destroy Phux execution; no competing uncontrolled PTY resize.

PRIORITY 6: ATTENTION AS A SOURCE-QUALIFIED PROJECTION. ts_snapshot.zig:113-128 uses only focused terminal for tab attention; workspace_projection aggregates several local problems into bool; phux/host.zig:804-821 bell is focus-cleared transient state. Introduce summaries with subject/source/severity/acknowledgement behavior and aggregate over all tab leaves. Use existing bells/local failures as first sources; no coordinator Signal store in Cockpit. Acceptance: nonfocused split bell contributes to tab; looking clears only that transient bell; summary is read-only and stable; healthy work adds no standing chrome; future durable Signal acknowledgement remains a typed Phux command.

PRESERVE: authority and work identities in Phux; generation-fenced input; complete publication before placement; frozen proven presentation; remote close as detach; direct local explicitly ephemeral; one geometry; provider inventory independent of placement; existing operation ledger. Host already separates max_catalog_terminals=64 from replica cap=16, so do not claim all discovered terminals allocate emulators. Delay generic plugin/provider interfaces, a local work database, invented durable IDs, and arbitrary capacity increases.

Suggested delivery: workspace/input commit spine plus explicit change domains; typed targets/receipts and placement continuation; view/content/resource lifetimes; attention summaries. A typed query/demand seam can deepen existing catalog-vs-attachment separation when adding first Phux work projection.

Manual complexity baseline for the small load-bearing Zig functions (decision+1, counting if/orelse/catch): paintChrome 3; onFrame 5; Creation.complete 3; acceptResult 6. No functions edited, so after is unchanged; this is architectural coupling despite modest local branching, not a high-CC-only diagnosis.
acceptance_criteria: Source-grounded findings with exact locations; distinguish shipped constraints from future risks; recommend a dependency-ordered first cut with invariant tests; independently inspect surface/topology and interaction/projection lanes.
notes: Parent source baseline 27928a418858dfb9deb0f122919ec3a002fae441. Confirmed resource/view-state coupling: terminal/session.zig Session owns measured_cell/font_size/selection/search/hover alongside libghostty; providers/local/provider.zig Pane owns PTY plus gesture/copy state; providers/phux/host.zig Terminal owns one viewport and projected canvas, Host owns one search_results/search_owner pair, and Host.search clears the previous pair. This extends through crates/phux-client-ffi/src/client.rs:175-192, whose render/selection/gesture/viewport caches are keyed by TerminalId. A view-identity extraction alone cannot provide independent terminal viewports: any multi-view implementation must resolve the underlying replica/view contract and explicitly arbitrate PTY resize/input ownership. Preserve existing generation fences and snapshot publication. Also confirmed good existing catalog-vs-replica separation (host.zig max_terminals=16, max_catalog_terminals=64 and separate detached_catalog); recommend deepening demand/query seam rather than claiming all discovery already allocates emulators. No source edits or runtime/performance claims.
close_reason: Completed source-grounded architecture assessment with two independent read-only audits and parent verification against 6bf51aff. Six ranked seam cuts, dependency-ordered delivery, exact sources, preservation constraints, and current-behavior regression scenarios are recorded in design. No implementation, live repro, or runtime/performance validation is claimed.

title: Cockpit host non-operation partial outgoing staging can replay frames
description: Independent provider-operation review identified pre-existing stageOutgoing behavior: frames are copied to bridge.outgoing one at a time, but the FFI queue is cleared only after all copies succeed. In non-operation callers (sendKey/sendPaste/capturePublishStage), allocation failure midway leaves already-staged frames in the FFI queue; a later call can stage them again. New requestSpawn/requestAttach callers disconnect and clear both queues on any staging failure, so this is outside the new operation path. Add allocator-controlled regression and make partial staging finalization consistent for all callers. Source: clients/cockpit/src/providers/phux/host.zig stageOutgoing and its non-operation callers.
notes:
Second-commit implementation is host.zig-only runtime change: stageOutgoing now has errdefer disconnect() for all failures, using the existing idempotent finalizer to clear both outbound queues, preserve already-observed operation results, and finalize pending requests unknown. New real-host allocator cases cover sendKey, sendPaste, capturePublishStage: metadata pre-reserved, exactly one payload allocation succeeds and matches first FFI frame length, second allocation fails, worker-like prefix/signal consumption followed by allocator recovery cannot replay. title: Evaluate a thinner Cockpit FFI that hands VT bytes to Zig

design: Keep the C ABI as the language boundary during evaluation. Do not reimplement Phux transport/protocol/layout state in Zig. Treat this as post-migration architecture work separate from workspace topology integration.
acceptance_criteria: A measured design compares current and proposed ownership for rendering, damage, scrollback, selection, search, anchors, input modes, reconnect bootstrap, memory, and ABI surface; a prototype or explicit rejection resolves whether removing the Rust terminal mirror simplifies the system without duplicating Phux protocol/state machinery or breaking behavior.

title: Client-core/FFI kernel has no perf metrics: the cockpit path is blind to echo RTT and apply time

Add a perf module to phux-client-core (apply duration, frames, bytes, history page latency) and an FFI export returning the PerfReport JSON so the embedder can render it or forward it. The user's daily driver appears to be the cockpit (no client-*.log since Aug 27 while the server logged 188x48 attaches), so this is where 'the server feels laggy' most likely needs to be measured.
close_reason: Merged as 28e1b6db via PR #511: kernel.* metrics (echo rtt, apply, frames, bytes, input_sent) in phux-client-core, phux_client_perf_json FFI getter declared in include/phux/client.h, phux-perf made wasm-safe.

title: Lane 10: lazy history lease so the scrollback byte ceiling can rise to herdr-class 10MiB
description: Lane 5 (ADR-0094) installed an explicit 2MiB libghostty scrollback byte ceiling (history-limit=50000 lines was inert; only ~300-800 rows were retained). It cannot go higher cheaply because detach_ready eagerly encodes every retained history page in one actor turn on the attach critical path (2MiB=8ms, 10MiB=65ms, 32MiB=222ms per pane, plus 1.7MiB transient per retained MiB) and the multi-pane attach is atomic/sequential. Make the history lease lazy (encode pages on HISTORY_REQUEST, not at capture), then raise MAX_SCROLLBACK_BYTES to 10MiB. Engine-side work on the phall1 libghostty fork may be needed; upstream PR only on explicit request. Consider non-atomic multi-pane attach (focused pane READY first) under phux-slogic.

title: Lane 8: batched cell reads via libghostty-rs get_multi wrapper (fork bump)
description: Lane 1 made the client cell loop allocation-free; it is now FFI-crossing-bound at ~25ns/cell with 4 crossings. libghostty-vt-sys exposes ghostty_render_state_row_cells_get_multi but the safe libghostty-vt crate wraps no get_multi and phux-client forbids unsafe. Add a safe row-batch read API on the phall1/libghostty-rs fork, bump the phux pin, and use it in attach/render.rs. Upstream PR only on explicit request.

title: ws accept errors discard the underlying cause, making TLS failures undiagnosable
description:
transport.rs maps every TLS/upgrade failure with `map_err(|_| ws_accept_error(stage, source_ip))`, so all failure modes collapse into one indistinguishable 'tls_handshake' rejection with no cause -- a genuine handshake failure, a timeout, and a plain EOF are identical in the logs.

The privacy rationale (keeping cert/token material out of default logs) is sound, but DEBUG is already opt-in and transport/quic.rs already logs its errors there (`debug!(%remote, error = %err, ...)`). Retaining the rustls error at debug! would have turned a multi-hour diagnosis into minutes. Refs phux-lbli.
close_reason: Shipped on main via PR #594: WebSocket TLS/upgrade causes are logged at debug; public rejections stay typed stage+IP.

title: Test suites inherit ambient PHUX_* env; audit for real-state leakage
description:
Root cause of the pair_credentials failure in phux-biyx: integration tests spawn the real phux binary WITHOUT clearing inherited env. A maintainer running the suite from inside a phux pane has PHUX_SOCKET, PHUX_WS_TOKENS, PHUX_WS_TLS_CERT/KEY and PHUX_SERVICE_MANAGED exported by the service manager, and those absolute paths override the per-test XDG_* tempdirs.

Concrete damage potential found: pair_credentials' 'default store' cases (tokens: None) operated on the operator's REAL ~/.local/state/phux/remote-tokens. It only failed loudly because that store is legacy-format and mint refused first; on a migrated store it would have minted a live credential and then chmod'd the file to 0o640. Fixed there by env_remove(PHUX_WS_TOKENS).

Remaining audit: 14 test files invoke CARGO_BIN_EXE_phux without pinning --socket/PHUX_SOCKET or calling env_clear (config_check_semantics, config_init_distro, config_plugin_actions, config_show_layers, host_enroll, host_lifecycle, plugin_install, plugin_launch, plugin_lifecycle, workspace_inspect, worktree_json, remote_target_e2e, phux-mcp discovery). They currently pass, but 'passes while reading the operator's real server' is luck, not isolation.

first_five_minutes_e2e.rs is the house-style precedent: it calls env_clear() and documents why. Decide whether to adopt that broadly or scrub the PHUX_* set in a shared test helper.

title: Three test failures reproduce on clean main (local macOS)
description:
Reproduced on clean main at 16f2ffdf, with no working-tree changes, on darwin 25.5.0:

Suspect fallout from the recent auth commits (be85a1ed fail closed on invalid credential reloads, 9b06a601 harden credential store locking): the test's legacy-store fixture now hits the explicit-migration refusal.

2. phux::spatial_e2e spatial_cli_persists_topology_and_preserves_attached_focus — fails all 3 retries, isolated or in-lane: 'type marker through attached client: Os { code: 5, kind: Uncategorized, message: "Input/output error" }' writing to the attached PTY client.

Found while validating phux-3szo (--remote user@host); none are caused by that change. Needs triage for whether these are macOS-local or also red in CI.

title: Reuse control connections for polling agents
description: wait, run, agent wait and prompt reconnect and renegotiate for every 25-150ms GET_SCREEN poll. Add a persistent request-correlated control session and measure connection/CPU reduction.
acceptance_criteria: Polling holds a bounded persistent connection, preserves cancellation/reconnect semantics, and benchmark demonstrates lower connection churn and CPU.
notes:
Focused acceptance evidence committed on test/protocol-polling-evidence as 4c8bd8b6. Added real ServerRuntime/PTTY production-UDS test plus ignored 1/8/32-agent idle/changing matrix comparing get_screen_scrollback one-shot against poll_until persistent reuse. Non-ignored test proves one forced transport loss, exactly one reconnect, repeated reads, and original deadline retention. title: Benchmark state-sync grid and wire-copy stages
description: Instrument or benchmark prepare_tick, per-consumer diff, encoding, and transport payload copies before redesigning the dominant measured server hot path.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks distinguish stage CPU, allocations, and copied bytes across dirty-row and consumer-count cases; resulting optimization has a measured target.
notes: 2026-09-12 audit: add actual end-to-end allocation/copy counters. server_measure.rs:132-149 reports engine READY offset whereas native_state.rs:178-200 sends full blob as prefix; chunks=1, buffer_growths=1 and payload_copies=0 are modeled constants, not observations. Broadcast-only fanout omits pumps/framing/compression/decoding. Opportunities: write_field_with scalar scratch allocations, owned Bytes decode slicing (avoid large slab retention), native scratch copies and input dedupe clone/serialization. Profile before selecting changes; compression already exists for bootstrap/history but not live output. Native correctness tracked phux-erut.

title: 97 wire discriminants are hand-allocated consts, so a duplicate tag is not a compile error
description:
Found 2026-08-17 by the phux-5xtz registry-gate sweep. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-CONSEQUENCE INSTANCE of the identifier-collision class that has now bitten four times (two ADR-0086 files, a reintroduced manifest key, and two branches claiming spec CHANGELOG 0.8.0-draft.4).

THE HAZARD: crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/frame/mod.rs declares ~97 u8 wire discriminants as individual const items, NOT as an enum. So two branches independently allocating the same tag produce NO compile error, NO test failure, and NO gate failure — and unlike an ADR number or a CHANGELOG row, a duplicate here is a PROTOCOL BREAK that ships. Coverage today is partial and accidental: rustc's unreachable_patterns fires only for tags that appear in the decode match, and not at all for spec-reserved consts no arm uses yet (e.g. TYPE_SPAWN_PROCESS). Contrast PhysicalKey and ErrorCode, which are #[repr(u32)] enums where rustc catches duplicates outright — the discriminant consts are the outlier.

COMPOUNDING IT: docs/spec/appendix-reserved.md is literally the 'pick your next number here' file, and the message-ID and feature-bit tables in appendix-reserved.md, L1.md, L3.md and proto.md are ungated on the ID column — the impl-status gate resolves each row's NAME against a const but never reads its ID, so two branches both claiming 0x18 pass every check in the repo.

TWO FIXES, not mutually exclusive: (a) CHEAP AND IMMEDIATE — instantiate the new check_registry_rows helper (landed in phux-5xtz, scripts/check-docs.sh) against the spec ID tables; the agent reports this is a row_re + rank_fn pair away with no new machinery. (b) STRUCTURAL — make the discriminants an enum or add a compile-time uniqueness assertion so rustc owns it, which is what already protects ErrorCode. (b) is the real fix; (a) is worth doing first because it is nearly free.

Deliberately NOT bundled into phux-5xtz: that bead's scope was the doc registries, and touching wire discriminants needs its own review.
notes: Parked on user redirect to phux-mobile; no further normal-phux implementation. Draft worktree /Users/phall/workspace/phux-crank-wire-tags, branch fix/crank-wire-tags, base 27928a41. Uncommitted changes: frame/mod.rs generates collision-reserving trait impls from all existing tag declarations across 13 namespaces; scripts/check-docs.sh + new check-spec-ids.awk add ID-table/bitset duplicate gate; new tests/wire_tag_registry.rs adds compile rejection probes. Verified before latest test/gate additions: doctor core/docs, cargo fmt --all --check, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$WORKTREE/target cargo test --locked -p phux-protocol (52 unit + 1 snapshot + 9 allocation + 128 wire + 1 doctest passed). New docs gate --only=spec-id-unique passed (173 files, 0 violations). Draft compile regression test is NOT validated and currently uses tempfile without a direct dev-dependency; full docs gate/clippy/rustdoc/mutation evidence remain outstanding. No commit/push/integration. User requested stop and unclaim; parent may resume or discard draft deliberately.
close_reason: Shipped on main as c0f2e5bb (PR #592): hand-allocated wire tags are duplicate-proof at compile time.

title: Cross-cutting cleanup pass over the 2026-08-16/17 eight-agent batch
description:
Filed retroactively 2026-08-17 to give a tracked home to a /simplify pass that was run without a bead (a process miss — this repo requires the bead before the code). CONTEXT: eight commits (f3bb7a86..61167c28) were written by eight INDEPENDENT agents who never read each other's work and landed in one batch, which is the condition that breeds duplicated helpers and parallel error-rendering paths. A four-angle review (reuse / simplification / efficiency / altitude) was run over the combined 3671-line diff, then applied in three file-disjoint lanes.

WHAT THE REVIEW FOUND, and what shipped:
- RenderPool had TWO entry points (begin / begin_generation) where choosing wrong is SILENT GRID CORRUPTION, guarded only by a doc comment; collapsed to one, Option state removed, the interleaving-rule test deleted. render_pool.rs 347->289.
- The generation token was threaded as a separate positional parameter through eight render methods, pushing render_at_letterboxed over clippy's arg limit; replaced by a ReplicaWalk struct. too_many_arguments allow DELETED, 38 test call sites simplified, TEST_GENERATION removed from the tree.
- TWO agents wrote the SAME user-facing armed-supervision paragraph (service.rs + doctor.rs) for the same bead, already drifted (semicolon vs period), each pinned by its own test. Now one const, both surfaces assert it verbatim.
- FRAME_TOO_LARGE's peer-visible message was constructed in two modules with only one pinned by a test; now one constructor in phux-protocol.
- metadata_broadcast was extracted from metadata_set but metadata_set still inlined the same two statements; rewired, one fanout implementation for three callers.
- The hub link grew a SECOND three-way transport write dispatch beside send_frame; collapsed to one send-then-condemn path via send_bounded.
- The SPEC section 14 fatal-close assertion existed in three private helpers under three names; promoted to phux-server-testkit.
- phux agent start parsed the ENTIRE plugin tree twice on its default path; one walk now.
- Kind-resolution helpers were pure functions over a phux-plugin type living in a CLI module; moved to phux-plugin so other consumers can reach them.
- The hermetic test env was hand-copied in two builders (which is why the idle backstop had to be added twice); one table now, and the backstop moved onto AutoSpawnedServer, the type that defines the hazard.

TWO INTENTIONAL BEHAVIOUR FIXES shipped with their own tests: doctor's dropped unit_supervises socket guard restored (it would warn about a marker armed for a different profile/socket), and the unclaimed-kind fallback canonicalised.

SHIPPED AS: 3ee24148 (render), 98ff18bb (server), 901ae39b (cli) — one ci-full green over the batch, 3913 tests, zero retries, no .snap.new produced. Follow-ups filed separately rather than fixed here.
close_reason: Delivered as commits 3ee24148 / 98ff18bb / 901ae39b, all pushed to main after one green ci-full (3913 tests, zero retries, no snapshot churn). Deferred items were filed as their own beads rather than folded in.

title: ADR-0071's 1.0 freeze does not name the shipped 'phux agent report-state' verb
description:
Found 2026-08-17 during the ADR-0075/0076/0078 ratification analysis. This is a LIVE breach of the freeze, not a hypothetical.

THE FACT: 'phux agent report-state TARGET STATE' is a shipped, documented CLI verb. Declared at crates/phux/src/commands/agent/mod.rs:115-121 (value_parser working/blocked/done). Documented in docs/reference/cli.md:188 and :399-404, docs/consumers/agents.md:531, and crates/phux/src/help_inventory.rs:103. But grep -n 'report.state' ADR/0071-what-phux-1-0-commits-to.md returns NO MATCH.

CAUSE — a date gap, not an oversight: ADR-0071 was last edited 2026-08-13 (cc9084d7); ADR-0085 shipped report-state on 2026-08-14. ADR-0071 point 7(c) requires anything ratified out of ADR-0075/0076/0078 to be carved into the freeze, but ADR-0085 was not on that list, so nothing forced the amendment. This is precisely the 'no agent verb is discovered post-freeze' failure point 7(c) exists to prevent, arriving through a door 7(c) does not cover.

WORK: (1) add 'agent report-state' to ADR-0071 point 6's verb list — it has no --json and no MCP tool, so it is a one-line addition. (2) WIDEN point 7(c) from 'ADR-0075/0076/0078' to 'any ADR that adds consumer surface', which is the structural fix.

VERIFIED NOT BREACHED (so do not re-file these): AgentExplainJson IS named at ADR-0071:105-106; the agent_state watch event name IS named with its full field list at :121-128; the three error codes capture_unreadable/capture_invalid/unknown_agent_kind are named at :128-132; point 7(b)'s ten-tool MCP freeze is accurate — exactly ten phux_agent_* tools exist. Bead phux-w7z2.2's first section is therefore stale and closeable: all three of its 'shipped but unnamed' items were absorbed into point 6 by commit 8d06829c on 2026-08-09, the day it was filed.
close_reason: Implemented and docs-checked locally in 401a2e2a on fix/crank-batch; parked per user direction, not pushed or integrated.

title: Extend the collision gate to spec CHANGELOG version rows, not just ADR numbers
description: Found 2026-08-17 in the merge queue, one batch after phux-254o landed the ADR-index collision gate. Two parallel branches (w1/frame-too-large and w1/rename-notify) BOTH claimed spec CHANGELOG row 0.8.0-draft.4. This is exactly the failure shape phux-254o was filed for — parallel branches silently claiming the same identifier with no textual conflict against main — but the new adr-index-sync gate only covers ADR/README.md rows, so it did not catch this one. It surfaced as a rebase conflict at integration (better than silence, because both branches insert at the same table anchor) but only because both touched the same file; a per-branch gate would have caught it before the merge queue and saved a gate cycle.\n\nWORK: extend scripts/check-docs.sh with a changelog-version-unique gate asserting that docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md version rows are unique and strictly descending (newest at top), matching the adr-index-sync gate's style. Note the existing spec-version-sync gate only checks that the TOP row matches PROTOCOL_VERSION — it says nothing about duplicates or ordering further down. Also worth considering per phux-254o's own reasoning: any other tracked file where a sequential identifier is hand-allocated (ADR numbers now covered, spec CHANGELOG rows this bead, manifest keys still uncovered) belongs in the same gate family.
notes: DEEPER FIX 2026-08-17 (altitude review), superseding the shallow version of this bead: do NOT hard-code a second instance. scripts/check-docs.sh:588 currently encodes a PATTERN — 'a shared append-only registry needs uniqueness + ordering enforced so parallel branches conflict textually' — as a single hard-coded instance for ADR/README.md. Verified adjacent hole: gate_spec_version_sync (check-docs.sh:663) parses ONLY the head row and compares it to PROTOCOL_VERSION; it has no duplicate-version check and no monotonicity check, so two branches both landing 0.8.0-draft.4 produce two rows and the gate passes clean — which is exactly what happened in this session's batch. FIX: extract check_registry_rows <file> <row-regex> <direction> <label> enforcing (a) no duplicate key, (b) key ordering in the given direction, (c) referent resolution where the row carries a link. Instantiate TWICE: ADR/README.md (ascending, link-resolving) and docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md (descending, no link). CONTRIBUTING.md's new paragraph already generalizes the RULE to 'any other shared registry' — the script should follow it there, so the third collision surface does not have to be learned and hard-coded a third time.
close_reason: Shipped on main as 7b778d74: check_registry_rows enforces uniqueness and descending order on docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md version rows, matching the ADR index gate.

title: Session-seed panes broadcast no PaneSpawned, so server-wide event followers miss headlessly-created sessions
description: Found 2026-08-16 while verifying phux-w7z2.20's wire-change claim. Both AgentEvent::PaneSpawned broadcast sites live inside handle_spawn_terminal (crates/phux-server/src/runtime/attach.rs:1799 and :1898). The FIRST pane of a new session is seeded by seed_session_with_pty_and_colors and broadcasts nothing, on two paths: (a) attach CreateIfMissing (runtime/attach.rs ~680), (b) headless CREATE_SESSION (runtime/commands.rs ~2236-2246) — which is exactly how phux new / phux worktree / an orchestrator creates an agent session (create_session_via_metadata, phux/src/commands/new.rs:325). Consequence: any server-wide event follower (the fleet-inbox sidebar roster, the future phux agent wait --any) misses sessions created after it attached until a Dirty leaks out. Fix: broadcast_event(.., AgentEvent::PaneSpawned) after seeding on both paths — server-side only, no wire change (PaneSpawned already exists; additive emission is compatible per ADR-0061; add a spec CHANGELOG draft entry if the spec enumerates emission sites). Regression test: drive handle_client with a subscribed server-wide watcher, create a session headlessly via CREATE_SESSION, assert PaneSpawned arrives. This also shrinks phux-k0cw.7's poll to a pure safety floor.
notes:
CROSS-REF 2026-08-16: phux-q7ks landed rename broadcasts (branch w1/rename-notify). Its agent independently confirmed the remaining gap is CREATE-side only: create_named_session broadcasts nothing. This bead's seed-pane PaneSpawned broadcast is the event-layer fix for the same gap; landing it removes the last push-coverage hole for session lifecycle (death=PaneClosed, rename=METADATA_CHANGED, create=this).
SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-17 (altitude review): this bead CANNOT be implemented as 'call metadata_broadcast in two more places'. Verified: CREATE is genuinely uncovered — runtime/client.rs:2182 handle_session_create_metadata writes the RESULT to SESSION_CREATE_RESULT_KEY, so a subscriber of phux.session.create/v1 learns nothing about the session existing — and DESTROY has no metadata write at all. The shape chosen for rename does not generalize: create's payload is a REQUEST JSON, not a state transition, and destroy has no write to intercept. So this needs a session-lifecycle EVENT (the AgentEvent::PaneSpawned broadcast this bead already proposes) or a server-written roster key — not the metadata_broadcast tool. Stated here so the next agent does not reach for the wrong one.
close_reason: a new session's seed pane is now announced via AgentEvent::PaneSpawned on both the attach CreateIfMissing and headless session.create paths

title: service status leaks launchctl stderr and contradicts itself on an armed unit
description:
Observed on a real machine 2026-08-16, immediately after 'phux service install --adopt' (phux-m3ot, ADR-0088).

'phux service status' prints the correct armed explanation, then follows it with raw launchctl output that contradicts it:

  unit  /Users/phall/Library/LaunchAgents/com.phux.server.plist
  state armed - installed with --adopt and waiting for the running server to exit

  The server holding this unit's socket is unsupervised and keeps its panes.
  Supervision begins at the next login, or at the first phux command after
  that server exits. phux service uninstall cancels it.

  Bad request.
  Could not find service "com.phux.server" in domain for user gui: 501
  installed, but the init system is not running it.

Two defects in those last three lines:

1. 'Bad request.' and 'Could not find service ... in domain for user gui: 501' are launchctl's own stderr, surfaced verbatim. A user cannot tell whether phux failed, launchctl failed, or nothing failed.

2. The state is not an error at all. An armed unit is BY DESIGN written-but-not-loaded, so launchctl not knowing about it is the expected, correct observation - it is what 'armed' MEANS. Reporting it as though something is wrong directly contradicts the paragraph three lines above, and 'installed, but the init system is not running it' reads as a fault when it is the intended state.

The armed path should either skip the launchctl liveness query entirely (nothing is loaded, by construction) or translate its not-found result into the armed vocabulary rather than passing the error text through.

Adjacent question worth answering while in there: 'phux doctor' reports all checks passing and says nothing about supervision being armed-but-not-active. ADR-0080 made a crash-loop reportable precisely because an invisible supervision state is how a broken server passed for a working one. An armed-and-pending unit is a similar in-between state a user would want surfaced.
close_reason: phux service status renders armed state in phux vocabulary; doctor warns on armed-but-inactive supervision

title: The first-five install lane leaks daemonized servers; phux-whhd only cleared the nextest lane
description:
Found 2026-08-16 while cleaning the dev box. Eight orphaned servers were alive from a single run window (Aug 15 17:13:21-17:18:21), all of the shape:

  <tmpdir>/prefix/bin/phux server --socket <tmpdir>/runtime/first-five.sock --session home --daemonize

They are from the 'first five minutes' install/smoke lane, which installs phux into a temp prefix and starts a daemonized server there. The tempdirs are gone or orphaned; the servers outlive them and hold PTYs indefinitely.

Why this is NOT already covered by phux-whhd: whhd was closed on 2026-08-15 after measuring 'zero stray servers after a full cargo nextest run --workspace', repeated four times including under 16 synthetic CPU burners. That measurement was correct AND the leak is real -- they are different lanes. The nextest lane is clean; this install lane is not. The bead's scope was implicitly narrower than its title.

Also observed, and worth keeping: of ten orphans killed, nine died on SIGTERM and one did not. The survivor (started Aug 11 05:51) predates the server's SIGTERM handler and needed SIGKILL. So 'phux kill --server' / signal-based cleanup only works for servers built after that handler landed -- any pre-handler daemon still alive on a developer box is immortal by design and must be SIGKILLed.

Fix direction: the lane that spawns these needs the same --exit-after-idle backstop phux-nbam added (PHUX_AUTO_SPAWN_EXIT_AFTER_IDLE), or an explicit teardown. Per phux-nbam's finding, the backstop is opt-in and nothing opts in -- this lane is a concrete caller that should.
close_reason: first-five e2e lane now reaps its daemonized server and arms --exit-after-idle 600 backstop

title: [bug] RENAME_SESSION notifies nobody: the handler returns before metadata_set
description:
Found 2026-08-15 during the phux-k0cw recon (PR #478); filed rather than fixed because it is server-side and outside that branch's scope.

THE GAP. crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs (around the rename handler, ~:2337-2361) returns BEFORE calling metadata_set, so renaming a session writes the new name without broadcasting a METADATA_CHANGED. No subscriber learns about it.

Session lifecycle coverage today, for a client subscribed server-wide:
- DEATH  — covered. PaneClosed reaches every EventScope::Server subscriber (crates/phux-server/src/state/client_table.rs:350).
- CREATE — covered only indirectly. create_named_session (crates/phux-server/src/runtime/commands.rs:2203) broadcasts nothing, so a headlessly-created session surfaces when its seed pane first emits Dirty.
- RENAME — covered by NOTHING. This bead.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. Before the cross-session sidebar this was invisible: peer session names were read once at attach and only shown inside a modal the user had just opened. ADR-0089 puts peer session names in always-on chrome (the 'spaces' roster), so a rename now leaves a stale name on screen indefinitely — the roster confidently displays a name that no longer exists.

phux-k0cw.7 works around it client-side with a session-graph poll. Fixing it here would make that poll cheaper or unnecessary, so the two beads should be considered together: if this lands first, .7 may shrink to create-only coverage.

REPRO: attach a client, rename a session from another shell (phux rename <old> <new>), observe no METADATA_CHANGED on the first client and a stale name in its roster.
acceptance_criteria: Renaming a session broadcasts to subscribers of the affected key, so an attached client's session roster and pickers show the new name without a poll or a re-attach. A regression test drives a rename against a subscribed client and asserts the notification.
close_reason: an applied session rename now broadcasts METADATA_CHANGED to L3 subscribers of phux.session.name/v1

title: Tab names and their cmd+N shortcuts drifted apart after one close-then-open
description: The Terminal N fallback name numbered by the registry slot (workspace_projection.terminalTitleInto) while the tab's shortcut numbered by position (view.tabSemantics). The registry never reuses a freed slot, so one cmd+W then one cmd+T made the fourth tab read 'Terminal 5, native terminal, 1 pane(s); ...; shortcut CMD+4'. Fixed on branch fix/tab-name-shortcut-drift by giving both numbers one source, projection.terminalAddress, which numbers by tab position and adds a pane digit so two panes of one split stay distinguishable.

title: The announced tab shortcut CMD+N is a lie for tabs 6..16
description: view.tabSemantics announces 'shortcut CMD+{position}' for every tab up to max_tabs (16), but update.zig only binds cmd+1..cmd+5 (the digit branch tests event.key[0] >= '1' and <= '5'). A screen-reader user on tab 7 is told to press cmd+7, which does nothing at all - the same 'the app announces something untrue about its own chord' class as the Terminal N / CMD+N drift fixed in fix/tab-name-shortcut-drift, found while fixing it. Either bind the remaining digits or stop announcing a chord that does not exist. Evidence: src/cockpit/update.zig:1793 vs src/cockpit/native/view.zig tabSemantics.

title: cmd+T through pressCanvasKey stalls at 2 tabs in the test harness, so the audit's 'full tab strip' is 2 tabs
description:
In chrome_register_tests.zig the 'as full a tab strip as we can open' sweep presses cmd+T max_tabs (16) times via support.pressCanvasKey and only asserts tab_count > 1. Measured on 2026-08-15 with a startCockpit harness, the counts after each of 16 presses are:

  press 0: tabs=2 live=2 latched=false
  press 1..15: tabs=2 live=2 latched=false

so the strip under audit has TWO tabs, not a full one, and terminal_limit_refused never latches. Driving the same message directly reaches the real ceiling:

  state.dispatch(&harness.runtime, 1, .new_terminal)
  press 0: tabs=2  press 1: tabs=3  press 2: tabs=4  press 3: tabs=4 latched=true

So the chord path stops producing terminals after the first one while the message path does not. Either the harness needs a frame pump between presses or the chord is being swallowed; whichever it is, the audit's widest-strip state is currently a fiction and the assertion (tab_count > 1) cannot detect it.

Found while fixing the tab strip trailing reserve (fix/tab-strip-plus-overlap), which had to use the message path to reach the state the live app reaches in five keystrokes.
close_reason: Implemented, guard-red proven where applicable, independently reviewed, integrated on local main, and Phux-inclusive full gate passed

title: Backward tab cycling scrolls the strip a full tab width even when the target tab is already visible
description: Backward tab cycling (cmd+shift+[) scrolled the whole strip a full tab width even when the target tab was already drawn. visibleTabWindowIn recomputed first from the selection alone, pinning any selection past the right edge into the last slot. Reproduced live 2026-08-15 (9 tabs, 1100pt, 7 drawn: Terminal 8 moved 731 -> 859 with six other labels). Fixed on branch fix/tab-window-scroll-into-view (7da9ba9, 20b18f1) by giving Workspace a tab_window_first scroll anchor, clamping it in visibleTabWindowIn so the strip moves only when the selection is out of view, and syncing it from update() for every open window. Guard tab-window-backward-scroll, watched red at 7da9ba9.
