Also re-check the identity re-verification at that point. Today it shares one connection with the ROUTE_INPUT batch, ids 1 then 2, with a staleness bound of one server frame-handling turn on that connection. An APPLY_INPUT batch must preserve that ordering property or the bound stops holding.
acceptance_criteria: agent send-keys delivers over APPLY_INPUT with an operation id, an idempotency test reusing an operation id, and the staleness bound in the module docs re-verified against the new frame ordering.
notes: IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE in feat/agent-epic-fanout and full nix develop -c just ci is green (3525 passed, 72 skipped). Left open because Beads correctly blocks closure on unresolved human ADR ratification phux-w7z2.1 (or, for downstream items, on a bead blocked by it); do not reimplement.

title: Fold the four new agent error codes into json_err::codes so the closed vocabulary claim is true again
description:
Owed follow-up from wave 2, and it is a documentation-truth problem, not tidying.

WHAT HAPPENED. phux agent wait and phux agent send-keys shipped four new JSON error codes - no_agent_record at exit 2, agent_departed at exit 1, agent_mismatch at exit 2 and invalid_key_spec at exit 2. They live in PRIVATE mod codes blocks inside crates/phux/src/commands/agent/wait.rs and crates/phux/src/commands/agent/send_keys.rs, each with a comment saying they belong in json_err. They were put there deliberately because crates/phux/src/commands/json_err.rs was held by a concurrent change in the same wave, which was the right call at the time.

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC. docs/consumers/agents.md 5.3 documented a CLOSED CODE VOCABULARY living in one file. That claim became false the moment these landed. The wave-2 docs pass documented the four codes, because a consumer needs them, and NARROWED the parenthetical rather than asserting a single-file vocabulary that no longer holds. So the docs are honest and the code is fragmented, and the next verb author has two plausible homes to choose from and no reason to prefer either.

TASK: move the four consts into crates/phux/src/commands/json_err.rs codes, delete the private blocks, and revert the narrowed parenthetical in docs/consumers/agents.md 5.3 to the single-file claim. Verify each code exit mapping against crates/phux/src/exit_codes.rs while doing it - the wave-2 docs pass already checked them, so a mismatch found here means something drifted.

Cheap, and it should be done before any further agent verb adds a fifth private block.
acceptance_criteria: grep for mod codes under crates/phux/src/commands/agent returns nothing, all four codes are in json_err::codes, and docs/consumers/agents.md 5.3 states a single-file closed vocabulary again.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

comments.author: phall
comments.text:
PARTIAL. All four codes now exist in crates/phux/src/commands/json_err.rs codes (NO_AGENT_RECORD, AGENT_DEPARTED, AGENT_MISMATCH, INVALID_KEY_SPEC), plus UNSATISFIABLE_WAIT from phux-w7z2.42, each with a doc line and its exit code verified against crates/phux/src/exit_codes.rs (no drift found). The private 'mod codes' block in crates/phux/src/commands/agent/wait.rs is DELETED and both call sites read json_err::codes.

NOT DONE, and it is the acceptance criterion: crates/phux/src/commands/agent/send_keys.rs still has its private 'mod codes'. That file is outside this agent's file ownership in the current fan-out and was being edited concurrently. The remaining edit is mechanical: delete the block and point the two call sites at json_err::codes::AGENT_MISMATCH / INVALID_KEY_SPEC. Until then those two consts in json_err carry a scoped #[allow(dead_code)] naming this bead, because the workspace lints at -D warnings; removing the allow is part of the same edit.

docs/consumers/agents.md 5.3 revert to the single-file claim also not done — docs/consumers/** is owned by a later agent in this run. Prose delta handed back to the orchestrator.

comments.author: phall
comments.text:
SCOPE UPDATE, checked against the tree as it stands after wave-3 fan-out. The fragmentation is now considerably worse than the bead describes, and the acceptance grep ('mod codes under crates/phux/src/commands/agent returns nothing') is no longer a two-file job:

- agent/send_keys.rs mod codes: invalid_key_spec (1 code)
- agent/prompt.rs mod codes: delivery_unknown, input_busy, unknown_occupant, agent_departed (4; agent_departed DUPLICATES the json_err const)
- agent/answer.rs mod codes: no_active_ask, ask_stale, ask_unidentified, no_suggestions, choice_out_of_range, unlisted_answer, invalid_answer, no_answer, answer_delivery_unknown, answer_refused (10)
- agent/start.rs mod codes: invalid_agent_name, unsupported_agent_kind, agent_detection_unavailable, agent_name_taken, agent_pane_busy, agent_pane_not_available, agent_cwd_mismatch, invalid_launch_argv, unknown_integration, agent_start_failed, agent_kind_mismatch (11)

Also: agent_mismatch is no longer emitted from a const at all — the string is built by phux_client::agent_prompt::Refusal::code(), i.e. the vocabulary has now leaked out of the phux binary entirely. The json_err const exists as the documented spelling with a scoped allow.

That is 26 codes in four private blocks plus one in another crate. ADR-0071 point 7(a) makes consolidating them a precondition of the 1.0 freeze, so this bead should be re-scoped from 'fold four codes' to 'fold every agent-verb code, and decide where a code emitted from phux-client is declared'.

title: phux worktree new --json returning terminal_id: the first call in every fan-out script
description:
Completeness-critique F8, ranked fifth of nine and explicitly rated above several tier-1 design items on effort-adjusted value. An afternoon of work.

VERIFIED. Only worktree list carries --json, at crates/phux/src/commands/worktree.rs:83, :119 and :156-179. new, open and remove print PROSE - run_new ends with an outln of worktree PATH BRANCH at worktree.rs:300 and hands off to bind_session, a path whose JSON flag is not plumbed through.

WHY IT IS THE FIRST CALL IN EVERY FAN-OUT SCRIPT. A worktree-per-agent fleet is the use case this entire epic exists for. An orchestrator creating a worktree needs the seed terminal_id to send the first prompt, and today it must either shell-parse prose or issue a second phux ls --json and GUESS which pane it just made. Both are wrong under concurrency, which is exactly when fan-out runs.

PHUX DESIGN HERE IS BETTER THAN HERDR AND THE GAP IS ONLY ERGONOMIC - state that clearly so nobody proposes an architecture change. ADR-0054 derives the session name as a PURE FUNCTION of the path, so no mapping is stored and any client can compute it. herdr worktree.create returns workspace, tab and root_pane because it stores that state. phux does not need to store anything - it needs to RETURN what it just created.

SHAPE: phux worktree new --json emitting schema_version, branch, path, session and terminal_id. Plumb the flag through bind_session and new::run_new. Consider the same for open and remove while the path is open, since a fan-out teardown script has the identical problem.

FROZEN-SURFACE NOTE: this is a new JSON document and ADR-0071 freezes the CLI JSON surface for 1.0, so it must be named in the carve-out phux-w7z2.2 like everything else in this epic.
acceptance_criteria: phux worktree new --json emits a document carrying terminal_id, a test pins the shape, and docs/reference/cli.md is regenerated via just docs-gen since it is byte-compared.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: phux watch --timeout SECS and --until EVENT: a bounded one-shot event wait
description:
Completeness-critique F7. Small, no wire change, and it deletes the worst paragraph in phux own shipped skill.

THE GAP. phux watch is an UNBOUNDED STREAM WITH NO --timeout FLAG. Its own skill documents the workaround, in examples/skills/phux-agent-cli/SKILL.md section 4, and the workaround is to background the watch, sleep, kill it and reap - four places to get it wrong. The MCP adapter had to grow a whole bounded-batch tool, phux_watch in docs/consumers/mcp.md 3.8, to paper over the same gap.

An orchestrating agent that wants block until this pane emits asked, or 120 seconds cannot express that today. herdr has two first-class server-side waits for this - events.wait with match_event and timeout_ms, and pane.wait_for_output with source, lines, match and timeout_ms.

THE FIX: phux watch --timeout SECS and repeatable --until EVENT, exiting 124 on timeout to match phux wait and phux agent wait. The subscription already exists, so this is CLI-side.

TWO THINGS WAVE 2 CHANGED ABOUT THIS:
1. There is now a precedent to copy exactly. phux agent wait shipped with the 124-on-timeout convention and a --json result document that goes to STDOUT with satisfied false rather than to the error contract, matching phux wait. Follow that, do not invent a third shape.
2. THE EVENT VOCABULARY IS PART OF THE FROZEN SURFACE. The watch stream carries no schema_version by design per ADR-0071, so the event-name vocabulary IS the contract. A repeatable --until EVENT names those events on the command line and therefore pins them. Coordinate with the ADR-0071 carve-out phux-w7z2.2.

phux-w7z2.32, the asked-to-answer round trip, NEEDS this: it is what gives ADR-0035 asked a first-class blocking consumer instead of a background-and-kill shell pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: phux watch --timeout exits 124 with no matching event, --until EVENT exits 0 on the first match, an unknown event name is a usage error at argv-parse time, and the SKILL.md background-and-kill paragraph is deleted.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: Two agent-state detectors disagree: agent list runs a client heuristic while agent wait reads the server record
description:
Completeness-critique F4. A divergence between two verbs in the SAME BINARY answering the same question, filed as a bug because that is what it is.

VERIFIED. crates/phux/src/commands/agent/mod.rs:264-280, classify_snapshot, calls pane_evidence for EVERY pane. At mod.rs:284-287 that issues a full get_screen_scrollback with cells enabled, per pane, and then runs the CLIENT-SIDE heuristic classifier at crates/phux/src/commands/agent/detect.rs:8-20. A phux.agent/v1 record short-circuits it at detect.rs:13-17, but nothing else does.

THREE CONSEQUENCES:
1. DIVERGENCE. For a pane the server detector has not yet published, or whose kind has no manifest - which is 16 kinds today, see phux-w7z2.21 - phux agent list reports one state and phux agent wait, which reads the record, sees another. This got worse in wave 2: agent wait now SHIPS, so both answers are reachable from one shell.
2. PROVENANCE IS IN THE WRONG HALF. agent list --json already emits confidence and a ranked sources array at mod.rs:326-345 with schema_version 1 - which is exactly the detection-provenance-on-every-verb this epic wanted. But that provenance describes the CLIENT heuristic, not the ADR-0046 rule that actually drove the published record. Wave 1 built the server-side provenance in crates/phux-server/src/agent_explain.rs and crates/phux/src/commands/agent/offline.rs and it is reachable ONLY offline via --file.
3. COST. N full screen fetches WITH SCROLLBACK on the verb an orchestrator polls most.

THE CHEAP FIX F4 NAMES: make agent list and agent show read the PUBLISHED RECORD as the primary source and demote the client classifier to a compatibility path that runs only for panes with no record. Then carry the SERVER rule id, region and matched evidence into agent list --json sources - the RuleTrace and PredicateTrace types in agent_explain.rs already serialize. That kills the divergence and delivers provenance-everywhere nearly free. schema_version need not move: adding keys to sources entries is additive, the same rule wave 2 applied to the four new ScreenState keys.

NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH THE LEVEL-VERSUS-EDGE RULING now normative in docs/spec/L3.md 3.7. Reading the record makes agent list a LEVEL read, which is correct for a listing - it is not a completion gate. Say so where the divergence is documented, so nobody later mistakes agent list output for evidence a turn finished.
acceptance_criteria: A test that agent list and agent wait report the same state for a pane with a published record, and for one without. agent list --json sources carries the server rule id for detector-derived records. docs/consumers/agents.md 4.7 updated.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

comments.author: phall
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED in crates/phux/src/commands/agent/{detect.rs,model.rs}. ADR-0071 impact, stated exactly.

SHAPE (keys): unchanged except two ADDITIVE optional keys inside sources[] entries — 'rule' (ADR-0046 manifest rule id) and 'region' (manifest region spelling). Both omitted when the source is not a manifest rule. schema_version stays 1, per the additive rule wave 2 used for the new ScreenState keys.

VALUES (this is the part that changed, and it is a behaviour change to a shipped surface):
1. Pane WITH a record: sources[] was one decorative {kind:'agent_record', confidence:0.98} entry. It is now 'agent_record' at confidence 1.0, PLUS 'detector_rule' (rule id + region + the literal patterns that matched) when the record's kind has a compiled manifest and a state-bearing rule matches, or 'detector_fallback' when none does, PLUS zero or more 'detector_flag' entries for visible-blocker / visible-idle / visible-working / skip-state-update. Top-level confidence moved 0.98 -> 1.0 (0.3 for a record whose state is 'unknown'). explanation now names the rule and region.
2. Pane WITHOUT a record: state was derived client-side from screen substrings ('permission' -> blocked, 'complete' -> done, 'thinking' -> working, OSC-133 input cells -> working). ALL of that is GONE. Such panes now report state 'unknown', confidence 0.2, with a new source kind 'no_agent_record'. Source kinds 'screen' no longer exist; 'semantic_cells' survives as evidence-only at confidence 0.1 and never sets a state.
3. RETAINED as state sources without a record, because neither is a re-derivation of the detector's job: the ADR-0035 'phux-ask' title sentinel (kind 'title_ask' -> blocked) and a [[plugins]] config declaration (kind 'plugin_report'). Identity inference is untouched.

New source-kind vocabulary: agent_record, detector_rule, detector_fallback, detector_flag, no_agent_record, title_ask, plugin_report, identity, semantic_cells. ('screen' removed.)

PROVENANCE CAVEAT, stated in the code doc: the server does not put the rule id on the wire, so detector_rule is RECONSTRUCTED by replaying the same compiled manifest (phux_server::agent_explain, the facade 'agent explain --file' already uses) against the viewport this projection already fetched. It never sets the state — the record does — and when the replay disagrees with the record the explanation says the screen moved on after the record was published rather than silently resolving it. Putting the real rule id in the record is a server/wire change and is left as follow-up.

COST (consequence 3 of the bead) NOT fixed: the per-pane get_screen_scrollback in classify_snapshot/pane_evidence lives in crates/phux/src/commands/agent/mod.rs, which is outside this agent's file ownership. Note the screen is still genuinely needed for the detector_rule replay, so the fix is 'stop asking for cells', not 'stop fetching'.

title: Make the compact-chrome breakpoint configurable
description:
The responsive chrome hardcodes its breakpoint: COMPACT_COLS=64 / COMPACT_ROWS=18 in render/overlay/widgets.rs (modal full-bleed) and MIN_PANE_COLS=40 in attach/paint.rs (sidebar yield). Both are defensible defaults derived from content width, but neither is tunable.

Someone running a 100-col terminal who wants full-bleed pickers, or a 55-col one who wants to keep their sidebar, has no knob. Widgets already got per-widget min-cols/max-cols in the same pass, so the config surface for width-conditional chrome exists and this is the chrome-wide peer of it.

Suggested shape: a [chrome] or [layout] section with compact-cols / compact-rows / min-pane-cols, threaded from the driver rather than read as consts at the use sites.

Landed unconfigured in feat/responsive-chrome-and-default-distro; see docs/consumers/tui.md section 4.5 for the current numbers and the arithmetic behind them.

title: visible-blocker and visible-working are parsed, documented, and inert: wire them or delete them
description:
Audit rank 5. A trap for manifest authors: two of three flags are parsed,
documented as meaningful, and inert.

crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/rules.rs parses `visible-blocker`,
`visible-idle`, `visible-working` and `skip-state-update`, and collects them into
`Evaluation` (rules.rs:260). Only `visible_idle` reaches control flow:

  agent_detect/mod.rs:419-421  all three -> trace!() only
  agent_detect/mod.rs:428      visible_idle -> the (derived, visible_idle) tuple
  agent_detect/mod.rs:440      settle_idle(now, visible_idle)
  agent_detect/mod.rs:537      if visible_idle || !releasing_work -> bypass the
                               working->idle hold

`grep visible_blocker crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/mod.rs` returns exactly
one hit, inside the trace!. Same for visible_working. Meanwhile RuleSpec's doc
comment tells an author that visible_blocker means "the screen POSITIVELY shows the
agent is blocked", so a rule author reasonably assumes it does something.

herdr wires both: visible_blocker becomes fallback_visible_blocker
(src/terminal/state.rs:362) driving visible_blocker_overrides_hook (:1737), and
`visible_blocker || visible_working` resets last_visible_signal_refresh
(src/pane.rs:230), a freshness stamp deciding whether screen evidence is newer than
a hook report.

EITHER STATE IS DEFENSIBLE; the current state is not. Two options:
- Wire them. The natural consumer is the declared-state escape hatch (a fresh
  visible blocker overriding a declared non-blocked state) — but that is a policy
  change contradicting ADR-0046 point 8 and needs the ADR amended, not just code.
  Note the narrow liveness bug fix is filed separately and does NOT need this.
- Delete them from the schema. `deny_unknown_fields` is already on RuleSpec
  (rules.rs:77), so removal fails loudly for anyone who used them, which is the
  right failure.

RELATED, mention it in whichever direction is chosen: no shipped manifest sets
`visible-idle` either, so the working->idle hold's fast path at mod.rs:537 is dead
code for every shipped agent — every idle transition pays the full
3-confirmation / 700ms hold.
close_reason: Merged path: DELETE, argued. visible-blocker and visible-working removed from the schema, compiled types, evaluation, explainer, CLI display, and all five shipped manifests. Across every shipped manifest they only ever sat on rules that ALREADY declared the same state, so they were pure restatement; giving them teeth would require letting screen evidence override a declared SET_METADATA, contradicting ADR-0046 point 8. visible-idle is KEPT -- it drives real control flow (bypasses the working->idle hold). Config surface removal done before the ADR-0071 freeze, where it is cheap; after, it would need a deprecation cycle. Bears on phux-w7z2.28 only tangentially: the removed flags never touched idle/done, and visible-idle's fast path remains dead code, noted for whoever takes .28. On branch army/w7z2-18-visible-rules.

title: Parameterized bottom-lines(N) and top-non-empty-lines(N) detection regions
description:
Audit rank 2. The single biggest constraint on manifest authoring today.

`const BOTTOM_LINES: usize = 6` (crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/regions.rs:54).
The bottom N non-empty rows are where a TUI paints its status line and key hints;
small N is a precise anchor ("the last row is the spinner"), large N reaches a
multi-row footer block. They are not the same region and phux can express exactly
one of them.

herdr's shipped manifests need N in {1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 14} — 32 of its 98 rules,
the most-used screen region after whole-screen. A 14-line window (hermes.toml) and
a 1-line window (maki.toml) are both real.

WORK (~50 lines + tests, backwards compatible):
- `Region::BottomLines(u16)`. It stays a valid `HashMap<Region, RegionText>` key in
  CompiledManifest::evaluate (rules.rs:286) — Hash + Eq still derive, and the cache
  gets one entry per distinct N, which is correct.
- Hand-written Deserialize parsing `bottom-lines(8)`; herdr's `region_count`
  (manifest.rs:1294) is the shape to copy. Clamp N.
- Bare `bottom-lines` keeps meaning 6, so no shipped manifest changes.
- Region::ALL / Region::as_str (added this run for the offline explainer) must
  enumerate and render the parameterized form correctly, and the explainer's region
  preview must show which N it resolved.

RIDER, do it here not separately: `top-non-empty-lines(N)` for agents that paint a
persistent header banner (herdr's top_non_empty_lines, manifest.rs:1341). One rule
in one manifest uses it today (grok, N=1), so it is low value alone but ~15 lines
once this bead's parameterized plumbing exists.

DO NOT ALSO ADD herdr's non-filtered `bottom_lines(N)`. phux's bottom_lines
(regions.rs:138) already filters empty rows, so it corresponds to
`bottom_non_empty_lines`; the non-filtered variant is unused by every shipped herdr
manifest.

DO NOT ADD the prompt-marker regions (after_last_prompt_marker et al.). Recorded in
the audit as rank 10 / do-not-build: they bottom out in codex glyph heuristics
(`line == "›"`, bullet glyphs — herdr manifest.rs:1409,1413), four of the five are
used by zero shipped manifests, and phux's OSC-133 machinery cannot implement them
anyway (its scanner has no row index, and the per-cell semantic marks require a
SHELL to emit 133 — an alt-screen TUI agent emits none). If codex needs structure,
it belongs in codex.toml as a line-regex.
notes:
DETECTION-PARITY RANK 10, RECORDED HERE SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT FROM THE REGION COUNT. Do NOT build herdr prompt-marker regions - after_last_prompt_marker, before_current_prompt_marker, whole_recent_without_current_prompt_marker, current_prompt_block_marker, after_current_prompt_block_marker. They are NOT OSC-133-relative, which is the natural wrong assumption. They bottom out in two hard-coded Codex glyph heuristics in herdr manifest.rs - codex_prompt_line at :1409 tests for a single chevron, codex_block_marker_line at :1413 tests for four bullet glyphs. That is one agent bullet glyphs leaking into a generic region vocabulary, a design smell in herdr rather than an asset. Only codex.toml uses one of them, for 2 rules. The other four are used by ZERO shipped manifests. phux OSC-133 machinery could not reproduce them anyway: Osc133Scanner is a byte-stream event scanner yielding no row index, and the per-cell marks only exist when the SHELL emits OSC-133, which a full-screen alternate-screen TUI agent is not. If codex-specific structure is ever needed it belongs in codex.toml as a line-regex, not in the region enum.

ALSO: the 15-versus-5 region count in the audit brief is misleading. Only 8 of herdr roughly 15 regions are used by any shipped manifest. The REAL region gap is exactly three things - parameterized N, which is this bead, a top-anchored region, which is this bead rider, and OSC progress, which is phux-w7z2.16.

TWO PLACES PHUX IS ALREADY AHEAD, do not trade them away chasing region count: phux prompt-box handles box-drawn AND rule-fenced forms, strips borders including a titled border label, and bounds the trailing scan, while herdr prompt_box_body understands only rule fences. And phux after-last-rule returns EMPTY when no rule is found while herdr returns the whole content - herdr widening is exactly what turns a transcript-printed Do you want to proceed into a false blocker.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: Capture whether Claude Code emits OSC 9;4, and whether the title kill-switch suppresses it
description:
Small, cheap, and it gates a ~150-line build. The detection-parity audit lists this
under "Not verified" and says explicitly: capture it before building.

Two questions, answered with a real capture, not from memory or docs:

1. Does the shipped Claude Code emit OSC 9;4 progress at all, in the version the
   crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/fixtures/claude/ captures were taken
   against? What are the exact payloads on the working -> idle transition?
2. Does CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1 also suppress OSC 9;4? If it does,
   the OSC-progress region does NOT fill the hole claude.toml documents (which is
   specifically the title-disabled install) and the value case for that bead
   collapses to "one more corroborating signal" rather than "the missing working
   backstop".

Also worth capturing while the harness is set up: whether codex, opencode and pi
emit 9;4, since the region is generic once it exists.

METHOD: run the agent under a pane and capture the raw PTY byte stream (phux
already has the scanner; a `PHUX_LOG` trace arm in Osc133Scanner::feed, or an
independent `script`/`tee` capture, both work). Land the captures under the
existing fixtures tree so the manifest rules that follow can be written against
real bytes — which is the whole discipline ADR-0046's Tradeoffs section is about:
"the first draft was written against an imagined Claude TUI and every screen rule
in it matched nothing."

Deliverable: captured payloads (or a documented negative result) attached to this
bead, and a go/no-go on the OSC 9;4 region bead.
close_reason: Answered with CAPTURED EVIDENCE, not documentary inference. A real authenticated claude CLI (v2.1.227/228) was run under a pty.fork() harness twice and its raw bytes recorded. Q1: yes, Claude Code emits OSC 9;4 -- exactly three BEL-terminated events per turn (0 at idle, 3/INDETERMINATE at turn start, 0 at turn end), numeric progress value always empty, matching L1.md's existing ProgressState enum. Q2: no, the title kill-switch does NOT suppress it -- with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1 zero title escapes fire but all three OSC 9;4 events still fire byte-identical, so the channels are independent. Deliverable is research/2026-08-12-osc-9-4-claude-code.md with the raw .rawcap fixtures and a reproducible pty_capture.py harness, on branch army/w7z2-15-osc94-capture. Findings and the libghostty blocker recorded on phux-w7z2.16.

title: Detection manifests have no bounds: unbounded rule/regex count on a 100-500ms hot path
description:
Audit rank 6. Resource-exhaustion finding, filed at P2 with an honest threat model
rather than as either P3 polish or an inflated ReDoS claim.

`RuleSet::install` (crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/rules.rs:347) enforces
exactly one thing: `kind` is non-empty. No rule cap, no manifest cap, no nesting
cap, no pattern-length cap. `build()` (rules.rs:417) reads every *.toml in
PHUX_AGENT_RULES_DIR (default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/phux/agent-rules) with no count or
size limit.

WHAT IS NOT TRUE: this is not ReDoS. `regex` 1.12.3 is a finite-automaton engine
with no backtracking — match time is linear in input regardless of pattern — and
`Regex::new` applies a default ~10MB NFA size_limit, so one pathological pattern
fails to compile rather than exhausting memory. Do not write "unbounded regex DoS"
in the commit message.

WHAT IS TRUE:
- Unbounded RULE COUNT on a hot path. Evaluation is O(rules x region bytes) and
  runs per agent pane every 100-500ms (agent_detect/mod.rs:285-304) on a
  current_thread runtime where every terminal actor shares the thread (ADR-0003).
  A large manifest is a sustained single-core burn and nothing caps it.
- Unbounded regex COUNT: 10MB each x N, at load, resident for the process lifetime
  in the thread-local RULES cell (rules.rs:476).
- UNVERIFIED, do not guess: whether a deeply nested `not = { not = { ... } }`
  manifest overflows the stack in `Predicate::compile` (rules.rs:155), which
  recurses with no depth counter, or whether toml 1.1.2's parser rejects it first.
  WRITE THAT TEST FIRST, before adding or dismissing the bound. It is five minutes.

Threat model, stated fairly: the rules dir is a per-user config directory on a
per-user server (ADR-0003), so an attacker who can write there already owns the
account. The realistic exposure is an operator footgun during manifest authoring
and a plugin bundle that installs a manifest. Not RCE; the symptom is a wedged
daemon that is hard to diagnose because it just looks like "phux got slow".

FIX: adopt herdr's constants roughly as-is (manifest.rs:264 —
MAX_RULES_PER_MANIFEST 128, MAX_GATE_DEPTH 8, MAX_TOTAL_GATES 512,
MAX_MATCHERS_PER_GATE 32, MAX_TOTAL_MATCHERS 1024, MAX_MATCHER_CHARS 512) plus a
depth counter in Predicate::compile. They are conservative — phux's largest shipped
manifest is 3 rules. ~40 lines in RuleSet::install, plus the nesting test.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: MCP tools for the new agent verbs, and agent_state on phux_watch
description:
crates/phux-mcp currently exposes none of the agent orchestration surface built
under this epic, and its `phux_watch` tool is events-only: `collect_events` in
crates/phux-client/src/watch.rs filters `WatchItem::AgentState` out, which is why
phux-mcp compiled unchanged when agent-state landed on the watch stream.

Two parts:

1. Surface `agent_state` on the `phux_watch` MCP tool. This was deliberately left
   undone rather than falling out of the streaming change as a side effect: the MCP
   result IS a versioned document (it carries schema_version, unlike the CLI watch
   stream), so adding a new line kind there is a versioned-document decision, not a
   plumbing one.
2. Add MCP tools for whichever agent verbs the ratification bead accepts —
   `agent wait`, `agent prompt` (with its `--wait` ordering guarantee, which an MCP
   caller cannot reproduce by chaining two tool calls: two calls are two
   connections and there is no shared ordering point, per ADR-0076 point 6), and
   the `%name` target form if ADR-0075 lands.

The prompt-then-wait ordering hole is the reason this bead is not trivial: an MCP
`agent_prompt` tool must expose the combined prompt+wait as ONE tool call, or
document that a caller chaining two calls has no ordering guarantee.

Depends on the verbs existing. Also depends on the ADR-0071 carve-out, since MCP
tool results are part of the frozen JSON surface.
notes:
WAVE-2 STATUS. Its agent wait dependency phux-w7z2.4 is CLOSED - phux agent wait and phux agent send-keys both SHIP now, so part of this bead has real verbs to wrap and is no longer purely blocked. Still blocked on agent prompt phux-w7z2.5 and on the ADR-0071 carve-out phux-w7z2.2.

TOOLS THE SHIPPED SURFACE NOW JUSTIFIES:
- phux_agent_wait wrapping the shipped verb. Its description MUST state the two-connection caveat from ADR-0076 point 6 and it must report the pre-wait baseline and whether a transition was observed - the shipped AgentWaitJson already carries baseline, edge with from, to and via, satisfied, observations and a detection object with confidence and sources. Note the shipped verb is EDGE-ONLY, so a pane already resting in a target state TIMES OUT at 124. An MCP description that does not say this will produce orchestrators that read 124 as still working, which it is not - it means no transition was observed.
- phux_agent_send_keys wrapping the shipped verb, with its all-or-nothing validation and identity refusal.
- phux_agent_read for the ADR-0077 read surface. snapshot --tail and --unwrap shipped as client-side projections and are cheap to expose.

THE FUSED TOOL IS THE POINT, completeness-critique F2, and it is why this bead is not plumbing. ADR-0076 point 6 states plainly that the subscribe-then-submit ordering supplies causality because it is one process on one connection, and that the reasoning FAILS for a caller that submits on one connection and waits on another - two MCP calls. That is the MCP case exactly. The only safe agent-prompting MCP tool ADR-0076 admits is a single fused phux_agent_prompt carrying wait inline, submitting and waiting inside one tool call on one connection. A separate wait tool is legitimate for --until blocked on an agent someone else is driving, and unsound for did my prompt finish. Bound timeout_secs the way phux_run does, per docs/consumers/mcp.md 3.4.

WHAT MCP SHOULD DELIBERATELY NOT GAIN, extending the existing take-give and headless-focus reasoning in mcp.md - record the decision rather than re-litigating it: no phux_agent_attach or observe tool, because a raw live ANSI stream has no request-response shape and the one-text-content-block envelope cannot carry it. No auto-answer tool that lets a model click yes on another agent approval prompt without a human. No notification tool - phux answer is hooks.

SEE ALSO the separate R3 bead on splitting phux_agent into distinct tools before ADR-0071 freezes the argument shape. Folding prompt, wait and read into the existing action multiplexer freezes them into a union designed for five read verbs.
IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE in feat/agent-epic-fanout and full nix develop -c just ci is green (3525 passed, 72 skipped). Left open because Beads correctly blocks closure on unresolved human ADR ratification phux-w7z2.1 (or, for downstream items, on a bead blocked by it); do not reimplement.

title: Alternate-screen history harvest, now ADR-0078: the LARGEST item under this epic, multi-week
description:
THE LARGEST SINGLE ITEM UNDER THIS EPIC. Do not schedule it as a rider on anything.

ADR-0077 decision points 2 and 3: recover an alternate-screen agent's transcript by
driving the pane's own scrollback, because an alt-screen TUI keeps no history in
the terminal's scrollback at all — today `snapshot --scrollback` returns nothing
useful for exactly the agents this epic is about.

Mechanism (server-side, in the terminal actor, because only it can guarantee
restore after the caller dies):
- Synthesized SGR wheel reports through the ADR-0044 input lane.
- settle -> probe-bottom -> harvest -> restore. ~15s overall, ~5s restore budget,
  ~120ms per step. Fractional row similarity for overlap detection.
- Concurrent GET_SCREEN is served the frozen pre-traversal viewport; detector
  publication is frozen for the duration of the traversal.

CONJUNCTIVE GATE, every clause required: explicit flag, local PTY-backed terminal,
alternate screen active, wheel routed as mouse reports, published `phux.agent/v1`
state is idle, no foreign input lease, no harvest already in flight, viewport
shorter than the request. A failed clause DEGRADES to the passive read with a typed
`truncated_reason` (agent_not_idle, not_alternate_screen, wheel_not_routed,
input_lease_held, harvest_in_flight), which the CLI turns into exit 2 plus one JSON
error object on stderr.

THE ONE WIRE CHANGE IN THIS EPIC: a trailing additive `request_transcript:
optional<u32>` on GET_SCREEN (0x07), gated behind a NEW MANDATORY ServerFeature
bit. The bit is mandatory because GET_SCREEN's decoder reads a missing trailing
field as a default, so an older server would silently answer a harvest request with
a passive read that looks successful. No PROTOCOL_VERSION bump — ADR-0061 section 2
additive path.

SPEC-FIRST WORK THAT MUST LAND IN THE SAME CHANGE (docs/spec/ is normative):
- docs/spec/L1.md 6.1 currently says GET_SCREEN "reads a Terminal's current
  viewport as structured data with no side effects" and "Walking history is
  side-effect-free". The harvest scrolls the live viewport. That text must be
  narrowed, not quietly contradicted.
- docs/spec/proto.md 6.2 gains the new ServerFeature bit.
- docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md entry + version bump per CONTRIBUTING.md.

FOUR MORE CARRIERS OF THE SAME CLAIM, all must change together:
- docs/consumers/agents.md section 1 (ADR-0077 states the exception paragraph
  verbatim) and section 2's snapshot bullet.
- docs/consumers/pi.md lines ~79 and ~233.
- docs/reference/cli.md ~2024 ("The read is side-effect-free — the server walks its
  own grid...") is GENERATED from the clap `long_about` and byte-compared by
  refdocs::tests::generated_reference_docs_match_the_tree. Change the `snapshot`
  help text in crates/phux/src/commands/ and re-run `just docs-gen` in the same PR,
  or `just test` goes red.

Whoever implements this owns all five doc edits plus the spec change. That
five-place blast radius is a large part of why this is the biggest item here.
notes:
THE ADR MOVED. Wave 2 SPLIT ADR-0077. This work is now ADR/0078-alternate-screen-history.md, a new file, Status Proposed, 201 lines. ADR-0077 was rewritten down to the six additive-JSON decisions that shipped as phux-w7z2.8, which is now CLOSED. The split boundary is DOES THIS DECISION WRITE TO THE PTY - 0077 is pure additive serde on an existing read path and cannot break a running pane, 0078 needs a lease, a role, a capability bit, a restore obligation and an abort matrix. That is also the risk boundary: 0077 was 1 to 2 days, 0078 worst failure is a permanently scrolled pane a user cannot recover.

BLOCKED ON ADR-0078 ACCEPTANCE. The ratification bead phux-w7z2.1 was written for 0075, 0076 and 0077 and must be extended to cover 0078.

SIZE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE THIS BEAD IS THE ONE PEOPLE UNDERESTIMATE: this is MULTI-WEEK, not a sprint item, and it is the only wire change in the epic. Do not schedule it as a rider on anything. The five-place doc blast radius in the description above is real and unchanged. Size honesty is the first Tradeoffs bullet in the ADR itself.

WHAT ADR-0078 SETTLED THAT THIS BEAD LEFT OPEN:
1. THE VIEWPORT-SAFETY CONTRADICTION - the thing this bead must resolve and the reason it cannot ship quietly. docs/spec/L1.md 6.1 and 6.2 say GET_SCREEN reads with NO SIDE EFFECTS and that walking history is side-effect-free. The harvest scrolls the live viewport. ADR-0078 names those sentences and amends them in the same PR with a PRIMARY clause on the gate. It also specifies, but deliberately does NOT perform, the exact rewording of docs/consumers/agents.md section 1. That section was UPDATED in wave 2 for the new snapshot and wait flags and its side-effect-free claim is now load-bearing for four verbs - re-read it before editing.
2. THE LEASE CONTRADICTION resolved toward ACQUIRING under a reserved server holder, with the ADR-0033 amendment it owes stated: no connection to drop, ttl_ms advisory.
3. VIEWPORT SAFETY is opt-in flag plus a bounded documented exception. Unattached-only was considered and is REJECTED in Alternatives.
4. THE IDLE GATE IS A SAFETY GATE AND TAKES THE LEVEL, per docs/spec/L3.md 3.7 which another agent made normative in wave 2. The crashed-pane consequence is ACCEPTED rather than hedged, on the argument that a dead pane does not repaint and so is the traversal safest case. This is the opposite reading from the completion gates in ADR-0076, and that asymmetry is deliberate - read L3.md 3.7 before touching it.
5. truncated IS ALREADY TAKEN. phux-w7z2.8 shipped truncated meaning only the requested window dropped older rows. The harvest MUST mint its own key rather than overloading it. The typed truncated_reason vocabulary in the description above needs re-siting accordingly.
6. A REFUSED HARVEST IS EXIT 0, not 2 and not 3. The read genuinely succeeded, just passively, with a named reason on the payload. Exit 3 carries contested retry semantics across ADR-0075 and 0076.
7. The mouse encoding runs through the actor own encoder. ADR-0044 is NOT inverted by this - its FIFO ordering guarantee is precisely what the traversal relies on.

RISK CARRIED FORWARD, completeness-critique R1: at roughly 15s max and exclusive per Terminal, a supervisor polling five agents serializes into 75 seconds, and this will be remembered as flaky and slow. Consider a transcript-lines cap that short-circuits the traversal and returning partial-with-truncated far more eagerly than the full budget. R1 also corrects the ADR Tradeoffs, which overstate the exposure: agent_state only marks a record declared when a real non-unknown state is written, so a plain agent set --name X does not pin state and only an explicit --state idle opens the gate.

ALSO OWED: ADR-0078 is 201 lines against the roughly-150 convention. Its own remedy is a companion page under docs/architecture holding the traversal body. Points 1, 6 and 7 are where that content sits.
PURE CORE LANDED, BEAD STAYS OPEN. crates/phux-server/src/history_merge.rs (pub(crate), file-level allow(dead_code) with a reason) implements the viewport alignment and upward merge that ADR-0078 section 3 of the design sketch specifies, plus 39 unit tests. Nothing else of the harvest was built: no phase machine, no synthesized wheel events, no terminal-actor arm, no input lane, no GET_SCREEN field, no ServerFeature bit, no spec or consumer doc edits. Nothing calls the module and nothing scrolls a live pane.

WHAT IS IN: viewports_similar (>= SIMILAR_MIN_PERCENT 70 of comparable rows match on trimmed text - this is the spinner and elapsed-counter tolerance, threshold only, no fuzzy row matching); sticky_prefix (leading run of rows identical at the same index, excluded from BOTH scoring and splicing, which is the case naive alignment gets wrong); merge_scrolled_up returning MergeOutcome::Advanced { rows, agreement, seam } / Unchanged / Unaligned, requiring ALIGN_MIN_PERCENT 30 row agreement over the overlap and flagging a splice below SEAM_CONFIDENT_PERCENT 60 as a seam; splice_front. Agreement is an exact matched/compared fraction compared by cross-multiplication, so thresholds and tie-breaks are integer comparisons with no float rounding. Ties break toward the SMALLEST shift (under-splice truncates, over-splice fabricates). An overlap blank on both sides is skipped, never scored 1.0.

Unchanged is defined as viewports_similar at shift 0, checked BEFORE the alignment search - that is the top-reached signal the driver needs, and it also absorbs a spinner-only repaint.

WHAT IS STILL OWED AND WHY THIS BEAD IS NOT CLOSABLE: (a) the empirical prerequisite the ADR Context names - captured viewports from the real agent CLIs, which gate rows-per-notch, settle time, and every constant here. The tests are hand-built sequences that pin the BEHAVIOUR of 70/30/60, not their VALUES; the module doc says so and says any change to a constant must re-run a corpus that does not exist yet. (b) the whole driver, gate, lease, restore obligation, abort matrix. (c) the L1.md 6.1 viewport-safety contradiction, unresolved. (d) the five-place doc blast radius. ADR-0078 is still Proposed and phux-w7z2.1 must be extended to cover it.

KNOWN LIMITS, DOCUMENTED IN THE MODULE RATHER THAN HIDDEN: a header that carries its own spinner is not sticky (exact match only) and can be spliced once per step; a pinned footer does not scroll, so it contributes one guaranteed mismatch per overlap and shows up as a seam (there is a test that asserts exactly this).

title: phux agent send-keys: all-or-nothing key validation and agent-ownership checks
description:
`phux agent send-keys` — an agent-aware sibling of the existing `phux send-keys`,
which is fire-and-forget ROUTE_INPUT with no validation and no idea what is in the
pane.

Two behaviours that distinguish it:

- ALL-OR-NOTHING KEY VALIDATION. Every key name in the argument list is parsed and
  validated BEFORE any byte is delivered. Today a typo in the middle of a key
  sequence delivers the prefix and then errors, leaving the pane in a state nobody
  asked for. Validation vocabulary belongs in crates/phux-config/src/vocab.rs,
  which is already the one CI-pinned source for action/hook names (see the
  ux-epic-validation-vocab memory) — extend it, do not redeclare names.
- AGENT-OWNERSHIP CHECKS. Refuse to write to a pane whose `phux.agent/v1` record
  says a different agent (or none) than the caller addressed, reusing the
  re-verification rule from `agent prompt` rather than restating it.

Rides APPLY_INPUT for the same receipt semantics as `agent prompt`, which is why
it depends on that bead: the typed-error readings, the ACKNOWLEDGED_INPUT gate and
the local-only refusal are all specified there and must not be re-derived.

Open question for the ADR owner: whether this is a distinct verb or a set of flags
on the existing `phux send-keys`. A second send-keys with different safety
semantics is the same one-grammar concern ADR-0065 raises about a second `wait`.
close_reason: Landed in the worktree, wave 2, with ONE SCOPE DEVIATION recorded below and a follow-up filed for it. crates/phux/src/commands/agent/send_keys.rs ships phux agent send-keys TARGET KEYS... --expect-agent NAME --expect-kind KIND --json. BOTH named behaviours are real. All-or-nothing key validation: spec_to_bytes is TOTAL by design, so anything it does not recognise is typed as literal text and a typo like C-cc is silently typed as five characters into someone else's turn. validate_key_specs runs over the whole vector BEFORE a connection is opened and rejects C- with other than one ASCII char, a bare M-, and empty args. Agent-ownership check: GET_METADATA on phux.agent/v1 and the ROUTE_INPUT batch share ONE connection, correlation ids 1 then 2, with a documented staleness bound of one server frame-handling turn on that connection, which closes the resolve-to-type window but explicitly not a concurrent-writer race. Refuses with no_agent_record when the pane has no record, pointing at phux send-keys, whose whole point is that it addresses a pane and deliberately checks no identity. 6 tests. DEVIATION: the bead specified riding APPLY_INPUT for the same receipt semantics as agent prompt. agent prompt does not exist yet, so this shipped on ROUTE_INPUT. The route-failure remedy deliberately does NOT say retry, because all-or-nothing covers validation and not delivery. Moving it to APPLY_INPUT once phux-w7z2.5 lands is filed as a follow-up. Also owed: the four new error codes live in private mod codes blocks in the two verb files rather than in crates/phux/src/commands/json_err.rs, filed separately. EVIDENCE cargo nextest run --workspace 3246 of 3246 passed, fmt and clippy -D warnings clean, docs-check 142 files 0 violations, docs/consumers/agents.md sections 2, 3, 4.7, 5.2 and 5.3 updated and docs/reference/cli.md regenerated.

title: phux agent start: available-shell precondition and readiness phase machine
description:
`phux agent start NAME --kind K --target PANE` launches an agent into an existing
pane and reports when it is actually usable, rather than when the process was
spawned.

Two pieces the herdr comparison says are load-bearing:

- AVAILABLE-SHELL PRECONDITION. Refuse to type a launch command into a pane that
  is not sitting at an idle shell prompt — a pane already running an agent, a
  pager, or a foreground job must be a refusal, not a racy write. phux has the
  inputs for this (the ADR-0046 record's state, and the PTY foreground process
  group that agent_detect::identify already reads).
- READINESS PHASE MACHINE. spawning -> launched -> ready, where ready means the
  detector has published a `phux.agent/v1` record for the pane, with a bounded
  timeout and a distinct exit code per phase it died in. Otherwise every caller
  hand-rolls a sleep.

ADR GAP, FLAGGED: ADR-0076 does NOT cover this verb. It covers `agent prompt` and
`agent wait` only (its Decision has 8 points, none about launching). So this needs
either its own ADR or an extension to 0076 before implementation, at minimum for:
what "available shell" means normatively, who owns the launch command per kind
(the manifests carry `binaries` but not launch argv), and whether the name is
written by the launcher or by the agent's own wrapper (interacts with ADR-0075's
uniqueness-at-set rule).

Depends on `agent wait` for the readiness phase and on `agent prompt` for the
acknowledged write path; both should exist first so this is composition, not a
third copy of the same plumbing.
notes:
WAVE-2 STATUS. Its agent wait dependency phux-w7z2.4 is now CLOSED, so the readiness half has a real primitive to compose against. Still blocked on agent prompt phux-w7z2.5 and on ADR-0076 acceptance phux-w7z2.1.

THE ADR GAP THIS BEAD FLAGGED IS STILL OPEN AND THE WAVE-2 REVISION DID NOT CLOSE IT. ADR-0076 was revised in place and still covers agent prompt and agent wait only. It has no decision point about launching. This verb needs its own ADR or an extension to 0076 before implementation, at minimum for what available shell means normatively, who owns the launch argv per kind - the manifests carry binaries but not launch commands - and whether the launcher or the agent own wrapper writes the name.

THREE THINGS THE WAVE MADE CONCRETE FOR THE READINESS CONTRACT:
1. The ready phase must be an OBSERVED TRANSITION, not a level read, and it must NOT be defined as reaching idle. docs/spec/L3.md 3.7 is now normative on this: idle is the detector fail-safe fallthrough and is equally true of an agent that never started. A start verb that reports ready because the record says idle reports ready for a pane where nothing launched. Compose against agent wait, which already refuses to satisfy on a level, rather than doing an independent GET_METADATA.
2. THE FIRST-PROMPT RACE IS REAL AND NAMED - completeness-critique F5. ADR-0076 point 4 re-verifies ownership from the phux.agent/v1 record. During startup the record is ABSENT, so prompt refuses with no agent here, which is the right refusal with a misleading reason, and it will be filed as a bug by whoever hits it. The readiness contract is what prevents that, so this bead is a prerequisite for anyone scripting spawn-then-prompt, not a nicety.
3. F5 recommends defining agent start as COMPOSITION rather than machinery - spawn plus agent wait with a bounded startup timeout and a distinct exit for spawned but never identified. Keep the herdr available-shell precondition only for the EXISTING-PANE form, since a freshly spawned pane does not need it. The one genuinely new piece is a kind_mismatch outcome, started codex and the detector says claude, which is one comparison against the record and is now cheap.

INTERACTION WITH THE NEW BUGS: on a pane whose kind has no manifest, the detector never publishes at all, so ready is unreachable and the verb must time out with a distinguishable exit rather than hanging. See phux-w7z2.28 and the coverage bead phux-w7z2.21.
IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE in feat/agent-epic-fanout and full nix develop -c just ci is green (3525 passed, 72 skipped). Left open because Beads correctly blocks closure on unresolved human ADR ratification phux-w7z2.1 (or, for downstream items, on a bead blocked by it); do not reimplement.

title: [bug] Frame pump resizes one pane per frame, so multi-pane windows lag a drag
description:
view.onFrame returns at most one Msg and returns on the FIRST pane whose proposed grid differs from its current one. With N panes, convergence takes N frames; during a live window drag the size moves every frame, so only one pane tracks the window at a time and the other N-1 render at a stale grid for the whole gesture.

The related outbound starvation is FIXED (drainEveryPane is now called from the .viewport arm as well as .flush_outbound), and .surface_resized is not actually starved because the .viewport arm commits surface_size itself. What remains is purely the convergence latency.

Fix needs a batched viewport message carrying up to layout.max_panes (ref, cols, rows) triples, computed in onFrame so the single-derivation rule holds. Deliberately not done in the first pass: the Msg union is passed by value through every dispatch and a 16-entry array would inflate it by ~320 bytes, which is a plausible regression against the very latency this is meant to fix. Measure Msg dispatch cost before and after.
close_reason: Convergence moved to the commit path via shared proposedViewportsIn; Msg stays 320 bytes (pinned); guard verified to fail without the fix

title: Sign release artifacts so the checksum is an independent trust root
description:
ADR-0074 records the honest limit of what phux update verifies: the .sha256 sidecar and the .tar.gz come from the same host over the same TLS channel, so the digest catches truncation, corruption, crossed assets, and a mid-flight proxy -- but not a compromised release host, which can simply publish a matching pair.

Closing that gap needs a signature over the checksum with a key that does not live on the release host: minisign/signify or Sigstore cosign keyless are the two obvious shapes. release.yml would sign the sidecar; phux update would verify against a public key compiled into the binary (with a documented rotation story, which is the part that needs thinking -- a key baked into a binary you are about to replace has an obvious bootstrapping problem).

Not a 1.0 blocker: ADR-0074 states the boundary rather than overclaiming it, which is the honest position for a self-updater whose alternative is a user running curl | sh. It becomes more pressing as soon as phux is installed somewhere its operator did not personally choose.
acceptance_criteria: Release artifacts carry a signature over the checksum produced with a key not resident on the release host; phux update verifies it before unpacking and refuses on failure; key rotation is documented and does not require the very update path being secured; ADR-0074 is updated or superseded.

title: Removed CLI spellings get clap's generic did-you-mean, not the actual migration
description:
The 12 deprecated spellings were removed (phux-dpjf). They now fail cleanly with exit 2 and no panic, which is correct, but the guidance is clap's generic nearest-match and it points at the wrong thing:

  $ phux remote add x
  error: unrecognized subcommand 'remote'
    tip: a similar subcommand exists: 'rename'

  $ phux insert-pane @1 @2 --vertical
  error: unexpected argument '--vertical' found
    tip: to pass '--vertical' as a value, use '-- --vertical'

The right answers are 'phux host add' and '--split vertical'. Every user upgrading from 0.12.x who has these in a script hits exactly this, and phux's failure doctrine (crates/phux/tests/failure_ux_e2e.rs) is that a failure names its remedy.

Proposed shape, reusing machinery that already exists: crates/phux/src/deprecations.rs keeps its Deprecation struct, its bidirectional clap pin, and its refdocs generator, but DEPRECATED is now empty. Add a sibling REMOVED table with the same rows plus the release that removed them, consulted when clap reports an unrecognized subcommand or unexpected argument, so the error names the exact replacement. Entries age out after a release or two, at which point the generic clap error is the honest answer. The generated docs/reference/deprecations.md can render it as a 'Removed' section so the migration stays discoverable after the spellings stop being accepted.

Note the flag case is harder than the verb case: clap reports '--vertical' as an unexpected argument on the subcommand, so the hook needs the subcommand context to know that insert-pane/move-pane once took it.
acceptance_criteria: phux remote add, phux satellite ..., phux enroll, and --horizontal/--vertical on insert-pane and move-pane each fail with an error naming the exact replacement; exit codes unchanged; a test per row pins the message; the removed-spelling table is rendered into the generated reference.
close_reason: A REMOVED table beside the empty DEPRECATED one, and report_parse_error appends a hint naming the replacement alongside the scoped-flag hint already there. Verified on the real binary: 'phux remote add x' now adds 'hint: phux remote was removed in v0.12.1; use phux host', and 'insert-pane @1 @2 --vertical' adds the --split vertical migration. A removed flag is hinted ONLY on the verb it hung off, since --vertical never meant anything on phux ls and offering --split there would invent a flag that verb lacks; clap does not report the subcommand being parsed, so the lookup matches the invocation, with the pure form taking argv as a parameter because the crate forbids unsafe and env::set_var is unsafe under edition 2024. Generated reference grew a Removed section so the migration outlives the hint; the two refdocs row-count tests were rescoped to their own table rather than sweeping the page.

title: MCP-native ask and watch result shapes carry no schema_version
description: phux-k8u0 versioned the six CLI --json documents. crates/phux-mcp/src/ask_tool.rs and the MCP-native watch tool are independent reimplementations against the server rather than CLI wrappers, so they were out of that bead's scope and still emit unversioned result objects. ADR-0071 freezes 'the MCP tool names and arguments' at 1.0; decide explicitly whether that freeze covers RESULT shapes too, and if so version these the same way. Cheap now, breaking after 1.0.
acceptance_criteria: An explicit decision recorded on whether MCP result shapes are part of the 1.0 freeze; if yes, ask_tool.rs and the native watch tool carry schema_version with pinning tests and docs/consumers/mcp.md updated.
close_reason: Both result documents now carry schema_version 1, with tests pinning them and docs/consumers/mcp.md updated. The decision the bead asked for: MCP result shapes ARE covered by the ADR-0071 freeze, because unlike the CLI's unbounded NDJSON watch stream these are bounded request/response documents -- the same reason every other MCP result already carried the field. The asymmetry with phux watch --json is recorded at the call site so it does not read as an oversight.

title: ci-metrics DASHBOARD.md success rate counts skipped and cancelled runs as failures
description: DASHBOARD.md reports ci success at 53% over 30 days, which reads as a project with badly broken CI. The raw runs/*.ndjson says otherwise: on main post-arm the ci workflow is 23/23 success, and pre-arm 74/79. The 53% comes from PR runs where 'skipped' (draft PRs, which the workflow deliberately skips) and 'cancelled' (superseded pushes) land in the denominator -- 43 skipped + 12 cancelled out of 87 post-arm PR runs, against only 7 real failures. The rendering should either exclude skipped/cancelled from the success ratio or report them as their own columns. Matters for a 1.0: a public dashboard at phux.phall.io/ci that understates CI health by 40 points is worse than no dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: DASHBOARD.md's success column reflects only concluded runs (success vs failure); skipped and cancelled are reported separately or excluded; the main-branch success rate is visible distinctly from the PR rate.
close_reason: Fixed in the integration branch: render-dashboard.sh now computes success over concluded runs only, with separate concluded, main-branch, and not-run columns. Rendered against the real ci-metrics store, ci goes 53% to 92% concluded and 98% on main across 99 runs; stress 37% to 76%; every other table byte-identical. Also coalesced nullable numerics to a literal null before @tsv in five projections -- @tsv emits an empty field for a jq null and read with a tab IFS collapses runs of tabs, which silently shifted every later column left (the new main-success column hit exactly that on the first render).

title: SDK work lives on an unmerged fork branch
description:
All the toolkit changes phux-cockpit now depends on sit on branch fix/terminal-render-cliff of github.com/phall1/native, at e8bd8488, with NO pull request opened. build.zig.zon pins that commit by tarball, so builds are reproducible today - but the work is one force-push or branch deletion away from unbuildable, and it is not upstream in vercel-labs/native.

Four commits: the packed cell grid, its AppKit decoder plus wire v6, bold/italic font families, and per-window chrome plus the fullscreen verb.

Two things to decide: whether to merge the branch to the fork's own main so the pin sits on a durable ref, and whether any of it should be offered upstream. The cell grid in particular is a general capability - any Native SDK app rendering a terminal or a dense character grid hits the same silent truncation. Note the Windows Direct2D path in that work is unverified (no device), which matters for an upstream offer and not for this app.

One mirrored line fixes it.

One conflict, in runtime/view.zig, where upstream's drag-source latches met the fork's secondary-gesture ones - both additive, both kept. title: Four config keys parse but do nothing
description:
The config file accepts these and they have no effect. Each is honest about WHY in the README, but a knob that parses and does nothing is still a trap.

font-family: the SDK selects faces from a fixed set registered at boot by FontId; mono_font_family is a 4-value enum, not a family name. There is no runtime load-family-by-name. Needs an SDK capability or a documented refusal at parse time.
selection-foreground: canvas.TerminalGrid carries ONE selection_color and the painter draws a wash, not a foreground override. Needs an SDK field.
scrollback-limit: Session.max_scrollback is a comptime const consumed at vt.Terminal.init. Currently harmless because the const equals the config default (50 MB), but it is unconfigurable. Needs to become a per-session parameter.
shell / command: argv construction lives in providers/local/provider.zig and hardcodes the login shell. paneArgvIn is the model to follow for building an argv from a user string - including its POSIX single-quote escaping, since a shell path from a config file is untrusted input.

Minimum acceptable interim: make the parser emit a diagnostic for a key it cannot honour, so the user learns it did nothing instead of assuming it worked.
close_reason: scrollback-limit and shell/command now real; font-family and selection-foreground now report unsupported; all diagnostics now surfaced at startup

title: Local search is always case-insensitive; the phux provider is not
description: vt.search.Screen matches case-insensitively with no option to change it, so cmd+F over a local terminal is always case-insensitive. The remote phux provider's search takes a case_sensitive flag (providers/phux/host.zig:407). One chord therefore drives two different matching rules depending on which kind of terminal is focused, which is the sort of inconsistency nobody notices until it wastes their time. Needs a product decision: force the remote side to case-insensitive for parity, or add a case toggle to the search bar and accept that the local side ignores it, or carry a local case filter on top of the engine's results.
close_reason: One case rule in the provider contract; phux side reads it instead of taking a bool

title: Fullscreen transition is wired but never observed
description: ctrl+cmd+F and View > Enter Full Screen reach fx.toggleFullscreenWindow against the focused window's label, and a diagnostic confirmed the effect fires with the right label and prior state. But no fullscreen transition has ever been WATCHED happen. The automation harness never gives the unbundled binary OS focus - every window reports focused=false and System Events could not front it - and macOS refuses toggleFullScreen for a non-active app. The SDK side is also inspection-only: the agent compiled the toggleFullScreen call and the style-mask read and matched the existing minimize/hidden plumbing, but did not drive a real transition either. Needs one manual run, or a bundled .app that can take focus. Until then treat fullscreen as unverified, not working.

title: The shortcut latch is a full u32
description: consumed_shortcut_keys_held is a u32 and cmd+F / cmd+G took bits 30 and 31. The next chord added needs consumed_shortcut_keys_held, global_shortcut_keys_held and suppressed_canvas_shortcuts widened TOGETHER; a comptime assert at update.zig:1591 guards this so it fails loudly rather than silently dropping a chord.
close_reason: Already done, and this issue went stale. The multi-window work widened appShortcutKeyMask from u32 to u64 across all three of its views (Model.consumed_shortcut_keys_held, CockpitHost.global_shortcut_keys_held, suppressed_canvas_shortcuts) because cmd+N was the chord that exhausted the last bit. The comptime assert guarding the three staying in step is still there, so the next exhaustion fails loudly rather than silently dropping a chord.

title: Scrollback search runs synchronously on the dispatch thread
description: searchAll runs on every keystroke on the dispatch thread. vt.search.Thread is void in a lib-artifact build (GhosttyZig.zig:68), so there is no background searcher to hand it to. Fine for ordinary scrollback; a full 50 MB history will visibly stutter while typing a needle. Fix needs either a search thread in the SDK fork or an incremental tick pump driven from onFrame that does bounded work per frame and reports partial results.
close_reason: Incremental tick pump driven from onFrame; slice sizes measured (1 tick ~285 rows); partial results stream

title: Bold and italic need registered companion font faces
description: The bold and italic flags now reach the packed cell and every renderer, but the painter builds its run with a single mono font id and there is no companion face to switch to, so the glyph is unchanged. Real bold/italic needs bold, italic and bold-italic faces registered at boot from embedded TTF bytes, plus face selection off CellFlags in the reference renderer and the AppKit decoder. This is SDK plus asset work. Note the bundled face is JetBrainsMonoNL, the explicit NO-ligature variant, so ligatures are structurally impossible until the face changes too. Related: while there is no bold face, bold ANSI 0-7 keeps the bright palette entry, and that brightening is the half to reconsider once a real bold face exists.
close_reason: Done. Regular, Bold, Italic and BoldItalic JetBrainsMonoNL Nerd Font Mono faces are bundled under src/fonts and registered in scene.cockpit_fonts at ids 64-67, with workspace_projection naming them in typography.mono_bold_font_id / mono_italic_font_id / mono_bold_italic_font_id. Verified by eye in the running app: bold, italic and plain on one line render as three distinct weights at identical column positions. Ligatures remain out of scope by an explicit decision recorded in phux-cockpit-1ay.

title: Style attributes are dropped: no bold, italic, strikethrough, or underline styles
description: canvas.TerminalCell carries only cp, cluster, fg, bg, a single underline bool, and wide. bold, italic, strikethrough, overline, underline style (single/double/curly/dotted/dashed) and underline color are all present on vt.Style and are discarded in the projection because there is nowhere to put them. TerminalCursor likewise has no blinking field and block_hollow collides with the focus-driven hollow. Bold and italic additionally need registered companion mono faces — the bundled face is the explicit no-ligature variant, so ligatures are structurally impossible today too. Blocked on the same SDK fork work as the packed cell-grid command.
close_reason: Done. bold, italic, strikethrough, overline, all six underline styles (none/single/double/curly/dotted/dashed) and SGR 58 underline colour now project from vt.Style into the packed cell, and the reference renderer already paints everything except bold and italic. The cursor additionally carries blink state, wide-cell coverage, and an explicit block_hollow shape so an emulator-requested hollow no longer collides with the unfocused-pane hollow. Bold ANSI 0-7 deliberately keeps BOTH the bright palette entry and the bold flag: they act on different channels (colour resolution vs weight request) so they cannot double-apply, and dropping the brightening today would make \033[1;31m pixel-identical to \033[31m. Still open elsewhere: bold and italic cannot change a glyph until companion mono faces are registered - that is font/asset work, tracked separately, and the flag is carried rather than synthesised.

title: Single window only: no cmd+N, no fullscreen, no quit binding
description: There is no new-window binding, no fullscreen toggle and no quit chord; the SDK ceiling for extra windows was measured at four. Every other Mac terminal opens windows. Needs the SDK window API wired plus per-window model state, since the Model currently assumes one window.
close_reason: Landed and verified in the running app. cmd+N opens a window with its own tabs, pane trees, selection and focus, up to the toolkit ceiling of five (scene window plus four secondaries), with the sixth refused visibly via a 5 WINDOW LIMIT badge rather than silently. cmd+W closes pane, then tab, then that window, and the app quits only when the LAST window's last tab goes - previously tab_count==0 quit outright, correct for one window and wrong for several. Fullscreen wired to ctrl+cmd+F and the View menu against the focused window. Snapshots reach v4 with windows owning contiguous runs of one flat tab array; a v3 snapshot restores as exactly one window. This needed two SDK changes first: ChromeOptions.build_window plus per-slot on_frame (without which a secondary window painted its tab strip and ZERO terminal cells), and the fullscreen verb the platform layer never had. Verified live: two windows painting live shells simultaneously, independent tabs and splits, closing the second left the first alive and the process RUNNING, closing the first window's last tab QUIT it. Known gap: the fullscreen TRANSITION could not be confirmed because the automation harness never gives the unbundled binary OS focus and macOS refuses toggleFullScreen for a non-active app - the wiring is proven end to end, the transition needs a manual run or a bundled .app.

title: No native menu bar, so every app action is keyboard-or-nothing
description:
`runWithOptions` (src/main.zig:200-214) passes `.shortcuts` but declares no menus, so the SDK builds its fixed default bar (App/File/Edit/View/Window) with standard items only. Registered shortcuts are delivered by a local NSEvent key-down monitor, not by menu items.

This got sharper when the control band became emergent (PR #8). At rest there is no band, so New / Close / Split / surface selection have exactly one affordance each: a key combination the user has to already know. There is nothing to discover and nothing for VoiceOver to enumerate when the band is hidden.

A menu is the native answer — Terminal.app has no on-screen New button either, but it does have File > New Window.
design:
The band being absent at rest is correct and should stay. The menu is what makes that affordable rather than a trade.

Candidate items, all mapping to Msgs that already exist:
- Shell: New Terminal (cmd+T), Close Terminal (cmd+W), Restart
- View: Split/Collapse (cmd+D), Previous/Next Tab, Move Tab Left/Right, surface selection
- The three browser destinations, which are currently ONLY reachable via buttons that render on the Web surface

The SDK exposes an app-declared-menu API (`setMenusWithTitles:` in the macOS host) that this repo never calls. Wiring it also gives 'layout.split', 'pane.previous', and 'pane.next' a legitimate emitter — see phux-cockpit-5k6.
acceptance_criteria: Every action reachable by keyboard is also reachable from the menu bar and enumerable by VoiceOver with the band hidden. The band stays absent at rest.
close_reason: Done. scene.cockpit_menus supplies Shell / Edit / View / Window, verified live against System Events on a running dev build. Shell has New Tab, Split Right, Split Down, Close; Edit has Copy, Paste, Select All, Clear, Find, Find Next, Find Previous; View has the font size trio, tab placement and the Web surface; Window has tab and pane navigation. Every item's command is a name view.onCommand already answered, so the menu adds a surface rather than a second code path - which is what finally made three previously unreachable onCommand entries fire. Note supplying any menu replaces the toolkit's stock bar wholesale, so everything a terminal user reaches for had to be re-stated.

title: Copy success clears the selection highlight on remote terminals but keeps it on local ones
description:
The `.clipboard` success arm treats the two providers differently for the same user gesture.

Local (src/cockpit/update.zig:359-363): only `pane.selecting = false`. The copied range stays highlighted, matching every native macOS terminal — typing, a new selection, or a restart clears it.

Remote (src/cockpit/update.zig:372): calls `clearRemoteSelection(model, state)`, so the highlight disappears the instant the clipboard write confirms.

Same cmd+C, two behaviours depending on which provider owns the terminal.
design:
Left deliberately unfixed during the topology/phux merge (PR #8) rather than changed without understanding provider anchor lifetime.

The two candidate fixes are not equivalent:
1. Stop clearing on remote success — matches local, but leaves the provider's selection anchors held. Need to confirm who releases them and when, or this leaks anchors per copy.
2. Clear on both — consistent and safe, but regresses the deliberate local behaviour documented in the comment at update.zig:360-362.

Whoever picks this up should start by tracing the anchor lifecycle: `beginRemoteSelection` / `applyRemoteSelection` / `clearRemoteSelection` in src/cockpit/update.zig and `createAnchor`/`releaseAnchor` in the provider.
acceptance_criteria: cmd+C on a remote terminal leaves the same visible selection state as cmd+C on a local one, with no unreleased provider anchors. A test pins the equivalence across both providers.
close_reason: Fixed, with the behavior chosen deliberately rather than harmonized arbitrarily. The remote arm cleared the selection on a successful copy while the local arm kept it; local wins. Keeping the highlight is the convention in every Mac terminal these users arrive from, and it is the only confirmation that the copy took the range they meant - clearing it deletes the evidence at exactly the moment you would check it, and makes a re-copy cost a fresh selection. Typing, a new selection, and restart still clear it on both sides. update.zig:494 now calls retainSelectionAfterCopy (update.zig:1449). Fail-before verified: restoring the old anchor-clearing gave 1 fail with 'expected 81, found 0'. Caveat recorded: the remote clipboard arm is only reachable under -Dphux-enabled=true, so the test pins the rule where a default build can reach it; the local half is already pinned end to end.

title: Dedupe test helpers onto phux-server-testkit
description:
phux-server-testkit exports run_local (lib.rs:243), wait_for_socket (:258) and recv_typed (:317), but test files redefine private copies anyway: phux-client/tests/sidebar_branch_e2e.rs:85,98; phux-server/tests/socket_lifecycle.rs:65,107; and private wait_for_socket methods in phux/tests/run_wait_e2e.rs:155, upgrade_e2e.rs:91, plugin_agent_bench_e2e.rs:62, workspace_archive_e2e.rs:61, agent_record_e2e.rs:82.

Surfaced by the knowledge-graph run: these three helpers ranked as the 3rd/4th/5th most-connected nodes in the entire codebase purely because of the duplication. Independent of the ServerState work; touches only tests/.
acceptance_criteria: No test file defines its own run_local/wait_for_socket/recv_typed where the testkit version fits. just test green.
close_reason: Already satisfied, and the bead's premise is stale. Verified 2026-08-07: zero remaining definitions of run_local or recv_typed exist anywhere outside phux-server-testkit/src/lib.rs. The two files named -- phux-client/tests/sidebar_branch_e2e.rs and phux-server/tests/socket_lifecycle.rs -- now import from the testkit; socket_lifecycle.rs even carries a comment recording that these 'used to be hand-copied'. The five wait_for_socket sites in crates/phux/tests are NOT the duplication described and must not be replaced: they are sync ServerGuard methods that poll for the socket file to exist, whereas the testkit's is an async fn(path, deadline) -> UnixStream that connects AND performs the HELLO handshake. Substituting it would open a connection and negotiate a protocol those CLI-driving tests neither need nor want, and crates/phux has no dev-dependency on the testkit. The real residual duplication is the ServerGuard struct itself, verified at 12 copies across crates/phux/tests, which is phux-wcdq item 1's scope, not this bead's.

description: The real work. terminals/terminal_tokens/terminal_tasks/terminal_subscribers/attach_terminal_pumps; attached/next_client_id/client_layers/live_connections/peer_identities; registry/session_last_touched/next_touch_timestamp/session_create_results/session_root. Touches runtime/commands.rs (2920 lines) and terminal_actor/mod.rs.

title: Re-land phux-i0e8.12.5: hide stdio-bridge, attach shadowing help, agent arg docs (closed-but-absent)
description: The G3 gate (phux-i0e8.13.2) found that phux-i0e8.12.5 is CLOSED (reason: 'Wave 5 merged to main (PR 338). stdio-bridge hidden, shadowing documented, agent args doc'd') but none of its deliverables exist in the tree, on main, or anywhere in git history (git log --all -S finds no commit ever adding hide=true to StdioBridge or shadowing text to attach help). Evidence at ux/g3 base decde8631: (1) crates/phux/src/commands/mod.rs:1263 -- #[command(name = "stdio-bridge")] with no hide; root --help lists it twice and completions offer it. (2) phux attach --help says nothing about registry-name shadowing or the --socket escape hatch. (3) AgentAction args in crates/phux/src/commands/agent/mod.rs:32-50 still use about= one-liners; target/json args carry no doc comments. Scope per the original bead: hide the verb (it must keep parsing), document shadowing in attach long help, doc-comment every AgentAction arg, add the three help-output tests. NOTE: hiding stdio-bridge now also drops it from generated completions (completion.rs prunes hidden verbs since the G3 fix) and from docs/reference/cli.md (refdocs omits hidden pages) -- regenerate the reference in the same slice, coordinating with the G4 gate (phux-i0e8.13.3).
