PROOF, and the technique is the best produced today: prepending 'sleep 9' to the fake agent makes the starved child deterministic, converting an unreproducible flake into a mutation test -- 8 of 9 cases fail on pre-fix main, 9 of 9 pass with the barrier. Plus 360/360 repetitions at 6-way parallelism and three full -p phux-server runs green.

Left alone deliberately: a_kind_change_never_leaves_a_stale_kind_beside_a_live_state has the same shape but is far less exposed, since codex is exec'd from an already-scheduled process rather than posix_spawn'ed cold.

title: A failed debounced layout write is dropped with no retry, because pending is cleared when the write starts and the outcome is discarded
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 while auditing for phux-cockpit-64i.

`writeTopologySnapshot` clears `model.state.pending` when the write STARTS:

  model.state.inflight = true;
  model.state.pending = false;
  fx.writeFile(...)

and the result arm discards the outcome entirely:

  .topology_persisted => {
      model.state.inflight = false;
      if (model.state.pending) armTopologyPersist(model, fx);
  },

So a write that FAILS leaves nothing owed. Nothing re-arms, nothing retries,
and the layout change is gone. The `pending` flag means "changed since the
write was POSTED", not "changed since the last write that actually landed".

Verified against the fake effect queue: arm a change, consume the timer, fire
the debounce (one file request out, `pending` false), then feed
`writeCompleted(.io_failed)`. Afterwards `pending` is false, `inflight` is
false, and `fireTimer(topology_persist_timer_key)` returns
`error.EffectNotFound` -- no retry was armed. The probe was thrown away
rather than committed: a passing test asserting this would lock in the
defect.

Not currently a data-loss bug on its own, because `.shutdown` calls
`writeWorkspaceState` UNCONDITIONALLY (no `pending` guard), so a clean quit
still writes the live snapshot. It becomes one in combination with
phux-cockpit-ymo, where every debounced write fails and only the exit saves.

Fix is probably: on a non-`.ok` outcome, restore `pending = true` and re-arm,
with some bound so a permanently unwritable path does not spin. Worth
deciding whether a persistently failing save should surface anywhere, given
the whole path is silent by design.
close_reason: Implemented, independently reviewed, integrated on local main, and full repository gates passed

title: Run the glyph-weight check in sdk-head.yml, where an SDK regression appears first
description:
phux-cockpit-9v1 wired scripts/host-raster-check.sh into ci.yml, which measures the PINNED SDK. That catches a rasterizer regression at the pin-bump PR - one step later than it could be caught.

sdk-head.yml already builds Cockpit against the fork's branch head daily, so it is where 'the fork made every glyph thinner' would show up while it is still the fork's change. The obstacle is that host-raster-check.sh deliberately refuses any checkout that is not the pin, and sdk-head.yml rewrites build.zig.zon to the branch head with scripts/repoint-sdk.sh before building. After that rewrite the branch head IS the pin as build.zig.zon states it, so the existing guard may already agree - that needs checking, not assuming. repoint-sdk.sh materializes no checkout of its own today, so the job would also need build-automation-cli.sh --checkout-only (added by 9v1) to run after the repoint.

A failure there means the fork moved, not that Cockpit is broken, which is already how sdk-head.yml reads its own failures.
close_reason: Implemented, independently reviewed, integrated on local main, and full repository gates passed

title: Tighten the raster ink floor against numbers CI has actually printed
description:
phux-cockpit-9v1 set --min-solid 4000 against a locally measured 4179 that does not jitter at all: 20/20 identical runs, and identical again from an x86_64 build under Rosetta. The entire 4.3% margin exists for the one thing a developer machine cannot measure - the GitHub runner's CoreText on a macOS build this repo has never rasterized against.

Once the CI step has printed cell_grid solid on the runner across a handful of green runs (and across at least one runner image bump), the spread is known and the floor can be tightened with evidence. Read the numbers out of the job logs; do not re-derive them locally, because the point is what the runner measures, not what this laptop measures.

Tighten only. If the runner ever reports LOWER than 4179, that is a finding about the runner's rasterizer and belongs in docs/RENDER_FIDELITY.md, not a reason to lower the floor.
notes: Completed 2026-08-25. Historical hosted evidence recovered after GitHub authentication was restored. GitHub-hosted macOS runs 31971072559 and 32092076828 and Blacksmith macOS 26 runs 32816649797 and 32817202255 all measured cell_grid solid=4179 with AppleFontSmoothing unset. Local negative control --min-solid 4180 failed at measured 4179; --min-solid 4179 passed. PR #55 tightened CI from 4000 to 4179 and hosted run 32818915221 passed with solid=4179 >= 4179.
close_reason: Measured invariant confirmed across GitHub-hosted and Blacksmith runner populations; floor tightened to 4179 in merged PR #55 and verified by hosted CI.

title: Hover preview for a link's real target
description:
Cockpit resolves OSC 8 hyperlinks now (phux-cockpit-89s) and underlines a hovered link, but has nowhere to SHOW where a link actually goes. Because of that, linkAtPoint enforces a display-text-wins rule: when the visible text is itself a URL and disagrees with the OSC 8 href, the visible URL is what opens. That keeps the phishing gap closed without a preview, at the cost of a legitimate shortener/truncator losing its indirection.

A pane-local preview (Ghostty shows the target in a corner of the surface while hovering) would let that rule relax to 'show the href, open the href'. It must NOT be a layout band: the terminal geometry drives the pty resize, so a band that appears on hover would resize the shell.

See the (2) block in Session.linkAtPoint for the full reasoning.
close_reason: Implemented, guard-red proven where applicable, independently reviewed, integrated on local main, and Phux-inclusive full gate passed

title: The settings surface is unreachable in live-app automation: input verbs do not route to Cockpit
description:
Follow-on from phux-cockpit-q4z, and a dependency of any future on-glass proof for a modal surface.

WHAT IS VERIFIED ON GLASS for q4z: the theme reaches the real Metal surface. Launching the packaged automation build with an isolated PHUX_COCKPIT_CONFIG and reading gpu_sample out of the snapshot, with publisher_pid asserted equal to the launched pid each time:

  (no theme)                                  gpu_sample=0xff090b0f
  theme = phux-light                          gpu_sample=0xfffbfcfe
  theme = phux-light + background = #0000ff   gpu_sample=0xff0000ff

Absent, present, and the explicit-key override, all on the real surface.

WHAT IS NOT: cmd+, and the settings panel itself. scripts/automate-smoke.sh's own header records that widget-key, widget-click and widget-action report 'delivered' against this app and DO NOTHING (phux-cockpit-2ml.5) — Cockpit routes keys through its own handleKey on the canvas rather than through the SDK's widget-focus mechanism. So there is no automation path that opens the panel, and its rendering, its modality and its legibility readout are covered by the TestHarness widget-tree tests in src/tests/settings_theme_tests.zig and by nothing on glass.

What would close it: a snapshot-level or automation-level way to deliver a key to a gpu_surface the way the platform does, or an app-side automation command channel that can dispatch a Msg. The second is cheap (onCommand already maps names to Msgs) and would make every modal surface in this app drivable.
close_reason: Premise retracted. It was filed on the stale claim that automation input does not route to Cockpit. It does: cmd+, was driven against the packaged bundle with publisher_pid asserted and a negative control, producing role=text name="Settings" and the legibility readout, and arrowdown moved the theme live. See phux-cockpit-2ml.5.

title: Profile the split/close churn condition, not just steady-state repaint
description: jw4 was recorded under 'ordinary split/close interaction' - layout churn. The harness currently profiles steady-state repaint with three splits at setup, which is where jw4's numbers improved 6x-49x. Churn is exactly where plan and rebuild are expected to spike, so the original worst case may still be unmeasured. Extend scripts/automate-smoke.sh with a churn mode that repeatedly splits and closes panes (cmd+d, cmd+shift+d, cmd+w) under load, and report stage percentiles for that condition separately. Keep the existing refusal discipline: assert the pane count reached, and refuse to print percentiles below the sample floor.
close_reason: Implemented, guard-red proven where applicable, independently reviewed, integrated on local main, and Phux-inclusive full gate passed

title: A milestone-label gate that does not lie about tracker freshness
description:
phux-i7vu labelled every open bead rc-1.0 or post-1.0 and wrote down the criterion. The other half of its acceptance -- a gate that keeps it true -- is not shipped, because the obvious implementation would be wrong.

The tracker is a local Dolt DB; .beads/issues.jsonl is a PASSIVE EXPORT. A CI check that reads the JSONL is checking a snapshot that may predate the DB by any amount, so it would pass while the DB has unlabelled beads and fail while the DB is clean. A gate that can be wrong in both directions is worse than no gate: it trains people to ignore it.

Two shapes that would actually work:

1. A local-only 'just milestone-check' that shells out to bd against the live DB, run by a human or an agent at session close rather than in CI. Honest about being advisory. Cheap.
2. Make the JSONL export freshness itself the gate -- a check that the export is not older than the DB head -- and THEN layer the label check on top of it. Strictly better but depends on the export carrying a comparable stamp; verify before committing to it.

Prefer (1) unless (2) turns out to be easy, and do not put a JSONL-reading label check in CI without solving freshness first.

ACCEPTANCE: either a working gate whose failure mode is understood and documented, or a written decision that the criterion stays convention-enforced with the reason. Cross-reference phux-i7vu.
close_reason:
Shipped shape (1) from the description: 'just milestone-check' (scripts/check-milestone-labels.mjs) queries the live Dolt store through bd, never .beads/issues.jsonl, and prints the store path plus record counts on every run so a verdict cannot be read apart from its provenance. Deliberately not in 'just ci' -- verified against a store-less checkout that 'bd list' exits 1 there, so the only CI-shaped implementation is the JSONL fallback this exists to avoid. No workflow touched (phux-7k11 in flight). Failure modes documented in CONTRIBUTING.md 'Gates that are local-only, and why': missing bd or missing store prints SKIPPED and exits 0 without claiming anything about labels; unlabelled or double-labelled exits 1.

Shape (2) is not merely hard, it is unavailable: the tracked JSONL is a passive export AND deliberately scrubbed (51a33f4c), measured at 785 records against 932 in the store, so no freshness stamp could make it authoritative.

Scope is 'not closed' rather than a status allowlist. i7vu's verification query, 'bd list --status open,in_progress', misses 'deferred' and 'routed' beads -- 'routed' is not even in bd's documented status vocabulary -- and repeating -s silently overwrites rather than unions. Two beads (phux-1hnw, phux-9gw.1.5) were invisible to the original pass for exactly that reason. Labelling left to the owner per instruction; the gate currently reports 5 unlabelled, three of which (phux-994s, phux-u8zm, phux-2o3r) were filed during this session.

title: cargo test --all-features on the phux bin crate is not a valid configuration
description:
Recording this so nobody else chases it. I burned time on it on 2026-08-11.

SYMPTOM: 'cargo nextest run -p phux --all-features --test host_lifecycle' fails deterministically (4/4) on duplicate_configured_satellite_names_are_rejected:

  `--json` failure stderr parses as JSON: Error("trailing characters", line: 2, column: 1)

Without --all-features the same test passes 7/7. It also fails on pristine main, so it is not a regression.

CAUSE (high confidence, worth confirming before acting): crates/phux/Cargo.toml's only feature is dhat-heap, which per its own doc comment 'swaps the global allocator for dhat::Alloc and installs a dhat::Profiler guard for the lifetime of main()'. dhat writes a summary to stderr on shutdown. The test asserts the shared --json error contract: stderr must be EXACTLY one JSON document. dhat's extra line is the 'trailing characters' at line 2.

SO THIS IS NOT A PRODUCT BUG in any shipped configuration, and the test is right to be strict -- phux-i0e8.8.3's contract is that --json failures put one document on stderr and nothing else.

WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY: 'just test' is 'cargo nextest run --workspace' with NO --all-features, so CI never hits this. 'just lint' does use --all-features but only compiles. That split is correct but undocumented, so the natural 'let me run the workspace tests with all features' produces a confusing failure that looks like a real bug.

OPTIONS, pick one:
(a) Document it -- a line in CONTRIBUTING.md or the justfile saying --all-features is a lint/compile configuration only, because dhat-heap swaps the global allocator and writes to stderr. Cheapest, and probably right.
(b) Gate the assertion: have the test tolerate trailing non-JSON lines when built with dhat-heap. Weakens a deliberately strict contract for a profiling build; not obviously worth it.
(c) Move dhat-heap out of the default feature set reachable by --all-features (e.g. require an explicit cfg). Most invasive.

Recommend (a).
close_reason: Merged as #436. crates/phux became a library crate: src/lib.rs holds the logic and exposes pub fn run(), src/main.rs is an 8-line shim, and src/bin/dhat_heap.rs owns the global allocator behind required-features. The plain binary now carries zero dhat-heap code under any feature combination, so the invalid configuration is impossible rather than merely loud. Two other options were rejected on evidence, not preference: a compile_error! guard would NOT have fired in the reported reproduction (--test host_lifecycle builds the binary as a CARGO_BIN_EXE_phux dependency artifact that never gets --cfg test), and dhat 0.3.3's Profiler::drop unconditionally eprintln!s with no suppression option. Verified: cargo nextest run -p phux --all-features on the previously-failing test now passes; the dhat binary still builds and still writes dhat-heap.json. Unit tests moved from the bin target to the lib target with the code, so -p phux --lib is now where the 481 live.

title: Surface OSC 8 hyperlinks, and underline a link on hover
description:
Follow-up to phux-cockpit-bgp, which shipped heuristic URL detection and cmd+click open. Two pieces are deliberately still missing.

OSC 8 hyperlinks are parsed by the engine but never surfaced. They are the EXPLICIT channel - a program saying 'this text is this link' - and where one exists it should win over the heuristic, which is guessing from shape. Needs the hyperlink id carried from the emulator cell through to the pointer hit test.

Hover underline: Ghostty underlines a URL when the pointer is over it with cmd held, so the affordance is discoverable rather than something you have to already know. Cockpit now has the hit test (Session.urlAtPoint) but no hover channel into the grid's cell attributes, so there is nothing to paint the underline with. Needs a per-frame hover span pushed into the render state the way search highlights already are - applySearchHighlights is the model to follow.
close_reason: Integrated onto main in the sweep at caea926; both build graphs, both executables, and a live app run are green

title: No MCP tool for doctor or status: an agent cannot diagnose the server it runs inside
description:
Surface-coverage audit, 2026-08-11. 'doctor' is the fifth most-used verb by real invocation count and 'status' is the machine-readable health surface (schema_version 1, crates/phux/src/commands/status.rs:257-280). Neither has an MCP tool.

An agent driving phux through MCP can ACT on the server -- spawn, kill, send keys, signal -- but has no way to ask whether the server is healthy, crash-looping, running a legacy supervisor unit, version-skewed, or which log files to read. Every health signal phux produces is human-only.

That matters more than it looks, because the health signals are exactly what an agent would need to recover from the failure modes in phux-g60k: a crash-looping supervised server (phux-67wg) is invisible to the thing best placed to notice and report it.

CHEAP VERSION: expose 'phux status --json' as phux_status. It is already a stable, versioned JSON document, it never auto-spawns, and it needs no new logic -- the schema is the contract.

FULLER VERSION: expose doctor's check results too. doctor already supports --json, but note phux-dsg1 -- its server-health conditions are mutually exclusive by early return, so a JSON consumer would see at most one of three concurrent problems. Fix that first or the tool reports a misleadingly clean bill of health.

Note phux status returns pid from SO_PEERCRED, which is None on QUIC/WS transports -- an MCP consumer over a remote transport gets a null pid and should not treat that as 'no server'.
close_reason: Closed

title: phux service install --print fails on unsupported platforms, contradicting ADR-0055
description:
ADR/0055 lines 120-122 commits that a platform with no unit generator gets 'a printed unit and a manual instruction, not an error'. crates/phux/src/commands/service.rs:74-77's own doc comment repeats that claim. The code does the opposite.

Manager::host() (service.rs:78-91) resolves from the COMPILE TARGET, returning None outside macOS/Linux. run_install's None branch (service.rs:476-482) prints 'phux service: no unit generator for this platform; run `phux server` under your own supervisor.' and returns ExitCode::FAILURE.

The --print dry run is gated AFTER that check -- service.rs:476 precedes :487 -- so 'phux service install --print', which needs no platform support at all and is exactly the 'printed unit' the ADR promises, also fails.

run_uninstall (service.rs:682-685) and run_status (service.rs:749-752) have the same None -> error shape.

FIX: move the --print branch above the Manager::host() check so a dry run always renders. Then decide whether install-proper should error or print-and-instruct, and make ADR-0055 and the doc comment agree with whichever is chosen.

RELATED GAP, worth folding in: non-systemd Linux is not detected at all. A Linux build unconditionally writes $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user/phux.service and shells out to systemctl; the failure surfaces only as run_tool's 'could not run systemctl' (service.rs:613-629).
close_reason: Fixed in #427 (3c7a838a). The --print dry run now precedes the Manager::host() check and always renders (systemd unit as the fallback text, per ADR-0055 grouping third platforms with non-systemd Linux). Install proper on an unsupported platform prints the unit plus the instruction and still exits non-zero, because nothing was installed; ADR-0055's tradeoff amended to say so explicitly rather than leave 'not an error' to be read as exit 0. uninstall and status keep their refusal but now say why.

title: Config diagnostics only reach the log, not the app
description: Config parse diagnostics (unknown key, bad value, missing separator, too long, unsupported key) are now emitted at startup via std.log, which from a bundled .app lands in the unified log rather than anywhere the user is looking. That is a real improvement over the previous state - they were collected and NEVER rendered anywhere - but it is not the finished job. Someone who mistypes a key in ~/.config/phux-cockpit/config still gets a terminal that silently behaves differently, unless they think to go read Console. Wants a surface in the app: a one-line banner or a notice the first time a config with diagnostics is loaded, dismissible, naming the line numbers.
notes: VERIFIED ON REAL GLASS 2026-08-12 by the parent session, closing the gap the implementing agent flagged. Against the packaged bundle (zig build package -Dautomation=true), launched with an isolated PHUX_COCKPIT_CONFIG: with a config containing two bad keys (font-familly, not-a-setting), 'automate assert "Config: 2 lines were not applied"' matched, exit 0. Negative control with a valid config: 'automate assert --absent "Config:"' also exit 0. Both halves, so the assertion is known to distinguish the two states rather than being always-true - the discipline 2ml.5 now enforces. Still unverified: the band's COLOURS and icon glyph. Automation screenshots render through the deterministic CPU reference renderer, which per 2ml.3 is structurally blind to GPU-path rendering defects, so a screenshot would not be evidence about on-glass colour anyway. Separately CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY: the use-after-free the agent found is real. In main.zig at 6465c86, readConfig declares 'var bytes: [max_config_bytes]u8' as a STACK LOCAL, calls loadOrDefault(bytes[0..read]) and returns the Config BY VALUE; Diagnostic.text was a slice into that buffer, so every key quoted in the startup log was read from a dead frame, and the model held that Config for the process lifetime. Fixed by an owned bounded copy (max_diagnostic_text_bytes = 64, truncated on a UTF-8 boundary) with a test that memsets the source after parsing, proven red against a reintroduced borrowed field.
close_reason: Implemented and independently verified by the parent session; landed in PR #31

title: zig build test prints 'failed command' on a green run
description: 'zig build test' exits 0 and all 334 tests pass (329 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed), but the build runner still prints a 'failed command: .../test --cache-dir=... --listen=-' line every run. Verified: exit code is 0 across repeated runs whether stdout is a file or a pipe, and the named binary run directly also exits 0 with everything passing. So the line is noise, not a failure - but it is the kind of noise that makes an agent or a human read a green gate as red, which already cost debugging time in this session. Find which step emits it and either fix the underlying non-fatal child failure or stop printing it.
close_reason: Implemented and independently verified by the parent session; landed in PR #31

title: No per-pane surface for degraded scrollback beyond a transient notice
description:
phux-client-core carries a complete per-replica history state machine that the TUI never shows: HistoryLoadState { Idle, Loading, Complete, Gap, Stale, Pruned, Tombstoned } (client-core/src/history.rs ~130-147), HistoryStatus (~149-166), KernelStatus::{History, HistoryUnavailable} (client-core/src/session.rs ~311-344).

phux-ijuj routes HistoryUnavailable into a transient status-bar Notice (7s TTL, newest-wins single slot). That is the right blast-radius fix but it is not a durable surface: a pane whose scrollback is permanently unavailable looks identical to a healthy one 7 seconds later.

Wanted: a persistent per-pane indicator. PaneSlot (client/src/attach/pane_state.rs ~85-155) has no degraded flag today, so this needs a field there plus a chrome affordance.

title: Site-owned CI dashboard, if it comes back
description: phux ADR-0080 retired the ci-metrics branch, its collector workflow, and the observatory lane; phux-site dropped /ci with them. If a CI dashboard returns, it belongs to the site end to end: the site owns collection (Actions API and/or a push from phux) and storage (R2/KV behind the demo Worker), and phux stays a repo that only builds and tests itself. Explicitly NOT a phux branch, and not a phux workflow whose job is feeding a dashboard. Deferred deliberately - the trend line was consulted far less often than it was regenerated.
close_reason: Not planned. ADR-0080 retired the ci-metrics dashboard; reopen only if a site-owned collector is actually wanted.

title: Bound and reap per-connection metadata subscriptions
description: MetadataStore keeps an uncapped flat subscription set, scans it linearly on each changed write, and deliberately retains dead-Terminal entries until disconnect. Long-lived watchers can accumulate stale triples. Add a defensible per-connection bound and reap subscriptions when their Terminal closes; update the unattached watcher test to negotiate L3 with HELLO.
acceptance_criteria: Subscription growth is bounded, closed-terminal entries are reaped, and tests cover the bound and production HELLO handshake.
close_reason: Landed on main. MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_CLIENT = 512, justified the way phux-w7z2.14 justified its manifest caps -- a generous multiple of realistic use (a heavy ~150-pane fleet stays under 500). REFUSE rather than evict: SUBSCRIBE_METADATA has no reply frame, so neither outcome is observable to the client, and evicting would silently break an already-working subscription to admit one that was never established. Deliberately distinct from track_session_create_result's evict-oldest cap, where the resource is one-shot results the connection is expected to drain and staleness is expected. No error code added, since there is no reply path for a consumer to observe a refusal synchronously. THE REAL GAP was not the cap: connection-death reaping already worked, but MetadataStore::forget_terminal cleared the K/V bucket while leaving matching subscription entries in the flat set -- and its own doc comment incorrectly claimed they were 'reaped on detach'. Terminal-death reaping now purges Scope::Terminal subscriptions from the existing reap bookkeeping. No wire change.

title: Fold agent start's local error codes into json_err::codes
description:
crates/phux/src/commands/agent/start.rs declares a private 'mod codes' with 14 stable error codes (invalid_agent_name, unsupported_agent_kind, agent_detection_unavailable, agent_name_taken, agent_pane_busy, agent_pane_not_available, agent_cwd_mismatch, invalid_launch_argv, unknown_integration, agent_start_failed, agent_kind_mismatch, agent_start_unknown, agent_departed, agent_start_timeout).

They belong in crates/phux/src/commands/json_err.rs codes, which owns the closed vocabulary and says so in its doc comment ('Add new codes here rather than inventing strings at call sites'). They are local only because json_err.rs was owned by a concurrent change in the same wave — the same reason wait.rs and send_keys.rs each carry their own 'mod codes'. Fold all three in together, and note that agent_departed is declared in both start.rs and wait.rs with the same spelling.

docs/consumers/agents.md 5.3 documents the vocabulary and is owed the additions.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: Surface an integration template's [agent_identity] kind so agent start can default --integration
description:
phux agent start takes --kind (a detection-manifest slug) and --integration (a launchable template id) and they are different namespaces.

crates/phux-config/src/integration.rs surfaces a template's top-level 'kind', but that is a CATEGORY: examples/plugins/agent-tools/integrations/claude-code.toml declares kind = "terminal-agent". The agent-facing slug lives in [agent_identity] kind = "claude", and the loader IGNORES that block (its module docs say so).

So there is no client-side map from a detection kind to the integration that launches it. start.rs defaults --integration to the --kind slug, which is right for codex (integration id 'codex') and wrong for claude (integration id 'claude-code'), where the caller must pass --integration claude-code.

FIX: parse [agent_identity] into IntegrationTemplate and carry it on ResolvedLaunch / LaunchableIntegration, then let agent start resolve --kind K to the unique enabled integration whose agent_identity.kind == K, refusing on ambiguity and keeping --integration as the override. Cheap, and it makes 'phux agent start build --kind claude --target @7' work with no second flag.
close_reason: phux agent start --kind resolves to the integration whose agent_identity claims that kind

title: Flaky: wrapper_never_relaunches_claude_after_a_mid_session_crash has a hard 10s pty deadline
description:
Pre-existing flake, observed and characterized during the phux-w7z2.26 work.
Not a regression from that change.

crates/phux/src/commands/agent/shim.rs, test
`wrapper_never_relaunches_claude_after_a_mid_session_crash`, carries a hard
10 s pty deadline. Under concurrent compilation it failed twice at about
10.2 s; run in isolation it passes in about 0.7 s, three for three.

Confirmed NOT a regression from the identity-only shim change:
PHUX_TERMINAL_ID is unset in that test, so `set_state` returns immediately at
its guard and the change is inert there.

This is the same class of failure the repo has already diagnosed twice — see
the `agent-detect-flake-root-cause` and `flake-diagnosis-requires-the-message`
memories. A wall-clock deadline in a pty test measures machine load, not the
behavior under test. .config/nextest.toml already documents that a
`pty-serial` group does NOT help, because a group only serializes its members
against each other while non-group tests keep filling the pool;
`threads-required = 'num-cpus'` on the binary is what worked for agent_detect.

FIX OPTIONS, in preference order: (1) replace the deadline with a real
synchronization point — a sentinel file or a marker the test waits on, which
is what fixed the analogous pane_kill test; (2) failing that, apply the
agent_detect remedy and give the binary `threads-required`. Do NOT just widen
the timeout — that is explicitly the wrong move recorded in
`flake-diagnosis-requires-the-message`.

Capture the actual panic message before changing anything.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: phux doctor should flag a stale installed Claude shim schema
description:
Residual gap left by phux-w7z2.26, named by the agent that implemented it.

WHAT LANDED. The generated Claude shim is now version-stamped
(`# phux-shim-schema: N`, currently 2) and `phux agent install-claude` reports
`installed` / `reinstalled` / `upgraded ... (schema 1 -> 2)` by reading the
stamp off disk before overwriting. An installed-but-unstamped wrapper reads as
schema 1, which is exactly what it is.

THE GAP. Upgrading the phux BINARY does not rewrite an already-installed shim.
A user who upgrades and never re-runs `phux agent install-claude` keeps the
schema-1 shim, which declares `--state` on every hook — so on their machine
the ADR-0046 detector stays stood down on every Claude pane and a SIGKILLed
Claude can still leave a stale declaration until the server withdraws it. They
get none of the phux-w7z2.26 fix and no indication anything is wrong.

FIX: a staleness check in `phux doctor` (and/or `phux update`) that compares
`installed_shim_schema()` against the binary's SHIM_SCHEMA and tells the user
to re-run `phux agent install-claude`. The reader function already exists in
crates/phux/src/commands/agent/shim.rs — this is a check and a message, not
new machinery.

Both `doctor` and `update` are outside the ownership of the branch that
created the gap, which is why it was flagged rather than fixed.

ACCEPTANCE: a machine with a schema-1 shim and a current binary gets a clear
doctor warning naming the exact remedy command; a machine with a current shim
gets nothing.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: Detector pid-reuse hardening: pair the foreground pgid with its start time
description:
Deferred sub-part of phux-w7z2.27, filed so the deferral is recorded rather
than forgotten.

WHAT LANDED. phux-w7z2.27's fix made the detector retain the foreground
process group id (crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/identify.rs previously
computed and DISCARDED it), so a same-kind restart in one pane is now an
identity change rather than being invisible by construction. Occupancy is
three-valued: Unresolved | Vacant{pgid} | Agent{kind,pgid}.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN. A pgid alone is reusable. If the OS recycles a pgid to a
new process of the same kind in the same pane, the detector reads it as the
same occupant and misses the swap. The window is narrow and needs pid
wraparound, but it is a real hole and it is the same class of bug as the one
.27 closed.

FIX: pair the pgid with the process start time — `(pgid, starttime)` — so a
recycled id with a different start time reads as a different occupant. Fielded
deliberately behind an `Option<u64>` when .27 landed, so adding it needs no
signature change: the seam is already shaped for it.

WHY IT IS P3 AND NOT DONE ALREADY: it costs a second proc query per identity
recheck on every pane, on a path that runs every 5 s per pane, to close a
window nobody has observed. .27's ruling deferred it explicitly.

UNBLOCKED BY: a demonstrated misidentification. If someone sees a pane
attribute one agent's state to another after a restart, raise this to P1 and
attach the repro — that is the evidence this is waiting for.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: agent wait --until done alone should refuse with exit 2, not time out at 124
description:
CLI honesty follow-up from the phux-w7z2.26 fix. `done` now has ZERO producers
in the shipped binary: no detection manifest emits it (grep 'state *=' over
crates/phux-server/rules/*.toml is five `working` and five `blocked`), and the
Claude hook shim — which was the only `done` writer phux ever shipped — now
declares identity only.

So `phux agent wait --until done @7`, with no other --until, is unsatisfiable
on any pane phux itself instrumented. It currently blocks for the full
--timeout and exits 124, which reads as "the agent did not finish in time"
when the truth is "nothing in this binary can ever say it did".

PROPOSAL: when the resolved --until set is exactly {done} and nothing else,
refuse up front with exit 2 and a diagnostic naming the reason — the same
shape as the existing `unknown --until word` refusal, which also exits 2
before connecting. Leave the DEFAULT set (idle,blocked,done) alone: `done` is
harmless there because idle and blocked can both satisfy it, and dropping it
would break an integration that does write `done`.

CHECK FIRST, this is the reason it is not already done: ADR-0071 is Proposed
and freezes the CLI JSON surface for 1.0. Adding an exit-2 refusal path adds a
typed error to the AgentWaitJson error contract (docs/consumers/agents.md
section 5.3), so it must land before that freeze or be explicitly carved into
it. Confirm against ADR-0071 before implementing.

ALSO CONSIDER, and decide explicitly rather than by omission: whether the
refusal should be conditional on the pane's kind having no `done`-writing
integration, rather than unconditional. Unconditional is simpler and honest
about the shipped binary; conditional is friendlier to a third-party
integration that does write `done`. The unconditional version can be wrong for
someone; say so in the diagnostic either way.

ACCEPTANCE: `agent wait --until done` alone exits 2 with a diagnostic that
names why; the default set still behaves exactly as today; section 5.3's error
table and the `agent wait` entry in docs/consumers/agents.md both updated;
ADR-0071 checked and the answer recorded here.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

comments.author: phall
comments.text:
ADR-0071 CHECKED, answer recorded.

Point 6 enumerates the frozen agent error codes as: capture_unreadable, capture_invalid, unknown_agent_kind, no_agent_record, agent_departed, agent_mismatch, invalid_key_spec. The refusal implemented here adds a fifth agent-verb code, 'unsatisfiable_wait' (exit 2), which is NOT in that list. Point 7(c) is the governing clause: anything ratified out of ADR-0076 is carved into point 6 in the same PR that ships it, and 'agent wait --until' is ADR-0076 point 5 surface. So this lands BEFORE the freeze and REQUIRES a one-line amendment to ADR-0071 point 6's 'Error codes:' enumeration adding unsatisfiable_wait. That ADR edit is NOT in this agent's file ownership and is reported as a required follow-up.

DECISION on conditional-vs-unconditional (the bead asked for it explicitly): UNCONDITIONAL. The refusal fires before the selector resolves and before a socket opens, matching the existing unknown---until-word refusal, so the pane's occupant is not known at refusal time; making it conditional on kind would move it after the connect and turn a usage error into a late failure. The diagnostic states outright that the refusal is wrong for a third-party integration that does publish 'done', and names the fix ('--until done --until idle' still fires on the 'done' edge).

title: phux agent explain --file drops the OSC title, plus two stale ADR-0077 doc lines
description:
Small, self-contained, and it blocks the fixture capture pass (phux-w7z2.40)
because it is the one step where a human silently gets the title wrong.

VERIFIED IN THE TREE. ScreenState gained a `title` field in ADR-0077, but the
offline explainer throws it away:

- crates/phux/src/commands/agent/offline.rs:143 returns only
  `(screen.lines, Some(screen.cols))` from a parsed `phux snapshot --json`
  document — `screen.title` is dropped on the floor.
- offline.rs:64 builds the capture from `--title` alone.

So `phux snapshot --json > cap.json` followed by `phux agent explain --file
cap.json --kind claude` evaluates every title-scoped rule against an EMPTY
region, even though the title is right there in the file. Title is the
detector's highest-ranked evidence (rules.rs ranks by (is_title, priority,
idx), so a title rule beats every screen rule regardless of priority), which
makes this the worst region to silently blank.

FIX: read `screen.title` from the JSON capture when present; keep `--title`
as the override for plain-text captures, which genuinely carry no title.

TWO STALE DOC LINES to fix in the same change — both assert the pre-ADR-0077
reality:

- crates/phux/src/commands/agent/offline.rs:43 (module doc): "a capture
  carries no OSC title"
- docs/consumers/agents.md:345 (in the `agent explain --file` entry): same
  claim. Note this file is generated-adjacent but hand-written; it is safe to
  edit directly. docs/reference/cli.md is NOT — regenerate it if the clap doc
  changes.

ACCEPTANCE: a JSON capture carrying a title evaluates title rules against that
title with no --title flag; a plain-text capture still needs --title and the
report still says the region was empty when it is; both doc lines match.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

comments.author: phall
comments.text:
DONE in crates/phux/src/commands/agent/offline.rs. parse_capture now returns a ParsedCapture carrying ScreenState::title from a JSON document; a new resolve_title(flag, captured) picks the title with --title as the override, the capture's own title next, and empty last, and reports which of the three it used as a TitleOrigin. An empty string from either source is treated as no title. The prose header now prints 'title "..."  (from --title)' or '(from the capture)', and for a text capture with no --title it still says the region is empty and adds that a text capture has nowhere to carry one. The JSON capture object gains an additive 'title_source' key: flag | capture | none.

Stale doc lines: the one inside this agent's ownership (offline.rs run() doc, formerly 'title supplies the OSC title a capture cannot carry') is rewritten. TWO MORE stale lines are outside ownership and are reported to the orchestrator rather than edited: (a) docs/consumers/agents.md:345, owned by the later docs agent; (b) crates/phux/src/commands/agent/mod.rs clap help for Explain — 'A capture carries no OSC title, so pass --title to exercise title-scoped rules' and the --title arg help 'Captures do not carry one, so it defaults to empty'. (b) is now false for JSON captures and its fix regenerates docs/reference/cli.md. A third, informational: phux_server::agent_explain::Capture's doc still says 'a capture does not carry it'.

Tests added: a_json_capture_carries_its_osc_title_without_the_flag, a_text_capture_still_needs_the_title_flag, an_explicit_title_overrides_the_capture, an_empty_title_from_either_source_is_no_title.

title: Re-capture agent detection fixtures to a checklist and record what they show
description:
Re-scoped out of phux-w7z2.28. Read that bead's resolution first — this one is
DELIBERATELY not "author idle rules", and the scoping is the point.

WHY THE SCOPE IS WHAT IT IS. phux-w7z2.28 asked for a positive `idle` rule and
was closed against it on evidence. Part of that evidence: four of the five
committed idle_prompt.txt fixtures are STARTUP SPLASH SCREENS, not post-turn
idle — claude (banner, empty transcript), codex (welcome box plus "Tip: Try
the Desktop app"), opencode (ASCII logo plus placeholder); omp's is a
KeyboardInterrupt. Only pi/idle_prompt.txt depicts a completed turn. The
evidence base does not contain the condition an idle rule would assert, for
four of five kinds. ADR-0046's Tradeoffs already record phux getting burned by
authoring screen rules against an imagined TUI; pre-committing the answer here
is how that happens twice.

SO THE DELIVERABLE IS THE CAPTURE AND THE FINDING, NOT A RULE. Re-capture to a
checklist:

- post-turn idle, captured after a real turn completes, not at startup
- three to four `working` captures spread across one turn, not one
- a fixed viewport size, recorded
- the OSC title recorded alongside each capture (see the blocker below)
- the same set for blocked, so the idle/blocked discrimination is testable

Then WRITE DOWN what the captures show — including, if that is the answer,
that idle and working chrome are byte-identical for a given kind and no
honest rule exists. That finding is a valid and valuable outcome of this bead.
Authoring a rule is permitted only if the captures support one.

BLOCKED IN PRACTICE BY the `agent explain --file` title drop (filed
separately): the capture format is plain .txt viewport and the explainer
throws the title away, so today a human has to supply --title by hand and can
silently get it wrong. Do that one first or this capture pass is unreliable.

ALSO KNOWN, and it constrains any rule this pass might produce:
crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/rules.rs:462-466 ORs `visible_idle` across
every MATCHED rule BEFORE the state-priority race, and mod.rs:537-541 reads a
true `visible_idle` as licence to skip the 3x100 ms working->idle hold. A
matched idle rule that LOSES the state race still arms the bypass and deletes
the hysteresis for that manifest. Any idle rule authored here must be checked
against that, and the write-rate guard tests must stay green.

RELATED: phux-7p8 (gemini, a kind with no manifest at all — different
problem), phux-w7z2.21 (breadth across 16 missing kinds).
notes:
=== 2026-08-15, branch army/w3-detection-manifests (commit 4b0c7086) ===

PARTIALLY DELIVERED: the audit and the checklist land; THE RE-CAPTURE DOES NOT.
New note at research/2026-08-15-agent-detection-fixture-audit.md (frontmatter +
TL;DR, passes docs-check).

CONFIRMED FIRSTHAND, by reading all fifteen fixtures rather than inheriting the
claim: four of five idle_prompt.txt files are startup splash screens (claude =
banner + empty transcript; codex = welcome box + "Find and fix a bug in
@filename" placeholder; opencode = ASCII logo + empty composer) and omp's is an
interrupted run ending in "KeyboardInterrupt: Execution interrupted". Only
pi/idle_prompt.txt depicts post-turn idle. The evidence base still does not
contain the condition a positive idle rule would assert.

Also recorded per kind: the discriminating evidence in each working and blocked
fixture, and the two byte-identical pairs (pi's after-last-rule region; claude's
prompt box and status rows) that make a screen-derived idle rule unauthorable.
Viewports vary 18-25 rows with no recorded reason -- hence the checklist item.

THE FINDING THE AUDIT TURNED UP, and it is a real shipped defect:
claude.toml's title-busy-spinner matched ^[U+2802 U+2810] (braille, verified
against 2.1.207). The committed capture at
research/2026-08-12-osc-9-4-claude-code/claude-title-enabled.rawcap shows
2.1.228 emits U+25D0/U+25D1. Twelve OSC 0 titles in that capture, three distinct
prefixes, NO braille among them -- so claude's highest-priority working rule
matched nothing on 2.1.228. Invisible because (a) the two backstops from
74ee2985 still proved working, and (b) every test built its input from
CLAUDE_TITLE_BUSY_A/B, constants restating the rule's own assumption. Rule and
test agreed with each other while both had drifted off the CLI. Fixed: regex now
matches the union of both known pairs, and a new test
every_busy_title_in_the_committed_capture_reads_as_working replays the real
captured titles (verified to FAIL when the regex is reverted).

This is the general lesson for the re-capture: detection rules key on the most
cosmetic part of an agent CLI's output, they rot on the CLI's release cadence,
and they rot silently. Re-capture is maintenance, not a one-off.

STILL OUTSTANDING: the driven capture session itself (post-turn idle, 3-4
working frames across one turn, fixed recorded viewport, OSC title recorded
alongside each capture). gemini/cursor-agent/aider are not installed here;
claude, codex, opencode and goose are. Checklist and redaction constraint
(byte-length-preserving) are written down in the new note.

title: No shipped manifest asserts idle or done positively, so both states are unfalsifiable claims
description:
BUG, filed P1, and it is the finding the whole wave-2 level-versus-edge ruling was built around. This is completeness-critique F1 plus the ground truth the ruling rests on.

VERIFIED BY GREP over crates/phux-server/rules - the five shipped manifests for claude, codex, opencode, pi and omp contain exactly TEN state-bearing rules: five working and five blocked. ZERO idle rules. ZERO done rules.

idle is therefore not a claim any producer makes. It is the fail-safe fallthrough at crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/mod.rs:424-428, and it is equally true of an agent that finished its turn, an agent that crashed, a half-painted TUI, a pane running less, and a pane whose kind has no manifest at all. crates/phux-server/rules/claude.toml:36-38 records in prose that a positive idle rule was DELIBERATELY declined, and the reasoning there is right - the static U-2733 prefix means not-busy, which covers idle and waiting-on-a-permission-dialog both, and asserting idle from it would mask every permission prompt. Do not undo that.

done is worse than absent. No title-derived or screen-derived rule can honestly produce it, because the agent finished while nobody was looking is not a fact on the screen. The ONLY done writer phux ships is the opt-in Claude hook shim at crates/phux/src/commands/agent/shim.rs, on the Stop hook. So done is inert on any uninstrumented pane.

WHAT THIS ALREADY COST, and what was done about it in wave 2:
- docs/spec/L3.md 3.7 now carries normative consumer rules for reading state as a level versus as an edge, with this manifest count as its durable checkable ground.
- phux agent wait shipped with NO level fast path at all. A pane already resting in a target state times out at 124. That false negative is the price of this bug.
- The default --until set is still idle, blocked, done, which ships a member nothing can match on an uninstrumented pane. F1 option 1 was to drop done from the default. That decision is still open and belongs here.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY FIXABLE, and this is the whole point: authoring a positive idle or done rule requires a CAPTURE SESSION with the real agent CLIs installed and driven into each state. ADR-0046 Tradeoffs documents phux getting burned by exactly the alternative - the first draft was written against an imagined Claude TUI and every screen rule in it matched nothing, silently. Do not author these rules blind. The offline explainer that landed in wave 1, phux agent explain --file PATH --kind KIND, is the tool that makes a capture session cheap rather than speculative, and it is why this is now actionable and was not before.

A NEW OPEN-ENUM VALUE WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED. quiescent, or any similar mint, has no producer, because the only thing that could emit it is a positive idle rule in a manifest, which is this bead. Do not introduce it.

Related to phux-7p8 which is the smallest slice of the capture work, gemini, and to phux-w7z2.21 which is the breadth-and-depth push. This bead is specifically about the two states that no manifest asserts at all, on the kinds phux already ships manifests for - it does not fit inside either.
acceptance_criteria: RE-SCOPED. The 'author a positive idle rule' branch is CLOSED against — do not implement it (see the 2026-08-09 note: a losing idle rule arms the visible-idle bypass and makes agent wait exit 0 mid-turn, and four of five idle fixtures depict startup splash, not post-turn idle). The remaining branch is the written decision, which is half done. What closes this: the --until default's treatment of 'done' is resolved via phux-w7z2.42, and L3.md 3.7's reference-server paragraph matches the final manifest counts. The capture work is phux-w7z2.40; it is not a precondition for closing this.
notes:
Relationship to the two existing manifest beads, so nobody merges them: phux-7p8 is the gemini manifest, a kind with NO manifest at all - a different problem. phux-w7z2.21 is breadth across 16 missing kinds plus depth on shared ones, and it is gated on parameterized regions phux-w7z2.17. THIS bead is narrower and unblocked by either: the five kinds phux already ships manifests for assert nothing about idle or done, and closing that needs only a capture session against CLIs that are already installed. It should be done FIRST because the level-versus-edge ruling and the agent wait false negative both rest on the count staying at zero, and every day it stays at zero is a day phux agent wait times out on healthy panes.
RE-SCOPED AND DOWNGRADED P1 -> P3 on 2026-08-09, branch
fix/agent-detection-p1-bugs. The finding is real and the diagnosis in this
bead is correct. What changed is the conclusion: authoring a positive idle
rule was investigated properly and RULED AGAINST, on evidence. Left OPEN
because one half of the original acceptance is still outstanding.

crates/phux-server/rules/*.toml was FROZEN for the fix branch. No cluster
owned it and nothing in it changed.

THE INVESTIGATION. The shipped `phux agent explain --file` was built against
all 15 committed fixtures to ground every claim; the one experiment used a
throwaway manifest outside the rules dir.

FINDING 1 — THE FIXTURE BASE DOES NOT CONTAIN THE CONDITION. Four of the five
committed idle_prompt.txt fixtures are STARTUP SPLASH SCREENS, not post-turn
idle: claude (banner, empty transcript), codex (welcome box plus "Tip: Try the
Desktop app"), opencode (ASCII logo plus placeholder). The fifth, omp, is a
KeyboardInterrupt. Only pi/idle_prompt.txt depicts a completed turn. Writing
rules against fixtures that do not depict the condition they assert is exactly
the failure ADR-0046's Tradeoffs already records phux making once — the first
draft was written against an imagined Claude TUI and every rule in it matched
nothing, silently.

FINDING 2 — AUTHORABILITY, PER KIND. claude: live chrome is BYTE-IDENTICAL
idle vs working (prompt-box is the same, after-last-rule is the same two
status rows in both); and the U+2733 title prefix means "not busy", which
covers idle AND waiting-on-a-permission-dialog, so a title idle rule would
mask every permission dialog — rules.rs:468-472 ranks by (is_title, priority,
idx), so a title rule beats EVERY screen rule regardless of priority. codex:
the composer placeholder is present behind a running turn (already documented
in codex.toml:128-134). pi: after-last-rule identical in both. omp: prompt-box
resolves EMPTY by construction. opencode is the only draftable one, and the
draft is literally `working-rule AND NOT working-rule`.

FINDING 3 — THE MECHANICAL ONE THAT DECIDES IT, verified empirically.
rules.rs:462-466 ORs `visible_idle` across EVERY MATCHED rule BEFORE the
state-priority race, and mod.rs:537-541 consumes a true `visible_idle` as
licence to skip the 3x100 ms working->idle hold. So a matched idle rule that
LOSES the state race has already armed the bypass. Demonstrated: on a pi
`working` fixture the detector correctly reports state=working while
visible_idle=True. Consequence: the instant a spinner row is absent for one
tick, working->idle publishes immediately. That is a REAL EDGE, so `phux agent
wait` — the completion gate — exits 0 MID-TURN. Total upside of the whole
feature is roughly 250 ms of badge latency. The trade is a silent false
positive on a completion gate in exchange for today's loud false negative. No.
No priority or region assignment avoids it.

FINDING 4 — THE CONSUMER PROBLEM WAS ALREADY SOLVED, without touching a
manifest. The level-vs-edge ruling (spec 0.7.0-draft.2, L3.md 3.7) fixed the
unfalsifiable-claim half, and it works on the 16 kinds phux has NO manifest
for — which a manifest rule never could.

FINDING 5 — `done` IS INHERENTLY HOOK-ONLY and L3.md is already correct about
it. Two refinements: `state = "done"` DOES parse and publish, so the
constraint is epistemic and not mechanical; and phux-w7z2.26 removed done's
only producer, so the shipped binary now has ZERO. That is written down in
L3.md 3.7 and in the `agent wait` entry of docs/consumers/agents.md.

WHY THIS STAYS OPEN. The acceptance offered two branches. The second one — "a
written decision that idle stays fallthrough-only AND the wait default drops
done" — is now half done: the decision is written (here, in L3.md 3.7, and in
docs/consumers/agents.md), but the `--until` default still contains `done`.
That was deliberate: dropping `done` from the default would break an
integration that does write it, and `done` is harmless in the default set
because idle and blocked can both satisfy the wait. The remaining CLI honesty
is phux-w7z2.42 (`--until done` ALONE should refuse with exit 2 rather than
time out at 124, pending an ADR-0071 check).

SPLIT OUT: phux-w7z2.40 (P3) is the capture pass, scoped deliberately to
RE-CAPTURE TO A CHECKLIST AND RECORD WHAT THE CAPTURES SHOW — explicitly NOT
"author idle rules", because pre-committing the answer is the mistake this
bead already made once. phux-w7z2.41 (P3) fixes `agent explain --file`
dropping the OSC title, which blocks a reliable capture pass.

WRITE-RATE WARNING for whoever picks this up: authoring a rule with
`visible-idle = true` deletes the working->idle hysteresis for that whole
manifest (finding 3). A pane whose spinner blanks for one tick then flaps at
roughly 3 Hz; twelve panes is about 36 metadata writes/s, 36 METADATA_CHANGED
per subscriber, and 36 hook events/s against a 64-deep drop-on-full queue —
ADR-0046 decision 7 destroyed, while a_long_working_run_publishes_exactly_once
still passes because it feeds an unchanging screen.


=== 2026-08-15, branch army/w3-detection-manifests (commit 4b0c7086) ===

(The notes above were accidentally overwritten by a `bd update --notes` on
this date and restored verbatim from `bd history --events`. Nothing above
this line was authored on 2026-08-15.)

PREMISE OVERTAKEN. This bead's ground truth -- "ZERO idle rules, ZERO done
rules" -- was already false when it was picked up.

* idle: claude.toml ships `osc-progress-idle`, added by d7e74c45
  ("feat(agent): detect Claude progress from OSC 9;4"). It is a POSITIVE idle
  assertion carrying `visible-idle = true`. The guard test acbd945e cited as
  pinning the count, `no_shipped_manifest_sets_visible_idle`, was renamed to
  `only_claudes_captured_progress_sets_visible_idle` and now asserts the
  exception rather than the absence.
* done: ADR-0085 (Accepted, 2026-08-14) restored an honest producer via
  `REPORT_AGENT_STATE`. FINDING 5's "the shipped binary now has ZERO" is
  stale. `agent wait --until done` is useful again on an instrumented pane.

THE RULING STANDS and was NOT reopened. `osc-progress-idle` is not a
counter-example to it. It reads neither the screen nor the title but OSC 9;4,
where the CLI positively states that progress was removed. Its `visible-idle`
bypass is safe only because `Region::OscProgress` returns a single latest
payload (regions.rs:274), so `4;3;` and `4;0;` are mutually exclusive within
one evaluation -- FINDING 3's hazard ("a matched idle rule that LOSES the
state race has already armed the bypass") cannot fire for this rule pair. A
screen-derived idle rule still has no such guarantee, so FINDING 3 remains
the correct objection to the thing this bead originally asked for.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BROKEN, and it is precisely the remaining acceptance
criterion: docs/spec/L3.md 3.7's reference-server paragraph still claimed
"five `working` rules and five `blocked` rules ... and zero `idle` and zero
`done` rules". The real counts are EIGHT working, FIVE blocked, ONE idle,
zero done. A normative consumer rationale was resting on arithmetic that had
rotted. Fixed, and pinned by a new test,
`the_spec_paragraph_reports_the_real_manifest_rule_counts`, which derives the
counts from the manifests and fails if the sentence stops matching. Spec
CHANGELOG entry 0.8.0-draft.2; PROTOCOL_VERSION untouched at 0.8.0.

Also fixed: claude.toml asserted in prose that no positive `idle` rule was
written while shipping one twelve lines above it.

SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND while auditing the fixtures for phux-w7z2.40, and it is
the more serious one: `title-busy-spinner` -- claude's highest-priority and
primary `working` signal -- matched `^[\u2802\u2810]` (braille, verified
against 2.1.207). The capture committed at
research/2026-08-12-osc-9-4-claude-code/ shows 2.1.228 emits U+25D0/U+25D1
instead. The rule matched NOTHING on 2.1.228. It went unnoticed because the
two backstops from 74ee2985 still proved `working` (no symptom), and because
every test built its input from `CLAUDE_TITLE_BUSY_A/B` -- constants restating
the rule's own assumption, so rule and test agreed with each other while both
had drifted off the CLI. Regex now matches the union of both known pairs.

Per the acceptance text, nothing is outstanding on this bead: phux-w7z2.42
(the `--until done` half) is already closed, and L3.md 3.7 now matches the
manifest counts. Suggest the owner verify and close.

title: Detector-written agent names are kind CONSTANTS, so no name can disambiguate a fleet
description:
BUG in shipped behaviour, surfaced by the wave-2 ADR-0075 revision. Filed P1 because it makes the ADR-0075 percent-name wave address nothing in a real fleet.

VERIFIED IN THE TREE:
- crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/rules.rs:554 - let name = spec.name.unwrap_or_else de-referencing spec.kind, stored on CompiledManifest.
- crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/mod.rs:377 - let name = manifest.name.clone, written into every AgentStateReport.
- crates/phux-server/rules/claude.toml:19-20 - kind = claude and name = claude, a literal constant.

CONSEQUENCE: twelve Claude panes all carry name claude. The name field is documented in docs/spec/L3.md 3.7 as REQUIRED and non-empty, and ADR-0075 builds a whole selector sigil on it, but the detector cannot produce a distinguishing value because a manifest is per-KIND and a name is per-PANE. percent-claude then correctly refuses as ambiguous with twelve candidates enumerated, which is the honest answer and also a useless one. This is completeness-critique risk R4, unnamed consequence: the detector and the shim write most names in practice, so if they write a kind constant the sigil the wave was built around addresses nothing.

WHAT A FIX MUST DECIDE, and it is not obvious:
1. A per-pane default the detector can honestly synthesise. The obvious candidate is kind plus the terminal id, matching what ADR-0075 point 7a already requires of the shim: claude-7. That is unique and stable for the life of the pane. It is also ugly and not what a human would have chosen.
2. Whether the detector should write a name at ALL, versus writing only kind and leaving name to whoever launched the agent. ADR-0046 gives the detector authority over the record it owns, so removing the name is a behaviour change with a docs/spec/L3.md consequence - name is REQUIRED, so an empty one is not spellable.
3. Where the human-readable label goes if the addressable name becomes machine-shaped. herdr has display_agent for exactly this and phux declined it in the detection-parity Tier 3 table. R4 says these two interlock and must be decided together.

BLOCKS the percent-name work in practice even though it does not block it mechanically.
acceptance_criteria: RE-SCOPED. NOT the original criterion — two claude panes getting distinct detector-written names was ruled against and must NOT be implemented (it breaks --expect-agent). What closes this now: (1) the docs and/or the launch path make it discoverable that a per-pane name is set with 'phux agent set TARGET --name X', and (2) ADR-0075's %name is implemented against explicitly-set names, refusing a manifest constant with a message that says why. Both are ergonomics and addressing work, not a change to what the detector writes.
notes:
RE-SCOPED AND DOWNGRADED P1 -> P3 on 2026-08-09, branch
fix/agent-detection-p1-bugs. The premise was RULED not-a-bug. Left OPEN
because a real gap remains, but it is a different and much smaller one than
this bead describes.

THE RULING: the detector never synthesizes a per-pane name. `name` stays the
manifest constant, the shim keeps --name claude, and per-pane naming is an
explicit writer's job. The bead's option 1 (synthesize kind + terminal id,
e.g. `claude-7`) was specifically rejected, as was ADR-0075 point 7a's
requirement that the shim do the same. ADR-0075 has been reworded accordingly
and no longer asks for it.

THREE REASONS, in the order that decided it:

1. IT BREAKS --expect-agent, and this is the one that settles it.
   crates/phux-server/.../send_keys.rs:420-424 matches --expect-agent against
   record.name as an exact, case-insensitive, WHOLE-STRING comparison. Any
   per-pane name — written by the detector OR by the shim — makes every
   shipped `phux agent send-keys --expect-agent claude` script REFUSE. That
   satisfies ADR-0071 on the letter (the JSON shape is untouched) and violates
   it in spirit. Nothing in this epic is worth breaking the safety check on
   the flagship input path.
2. `claude-7` is the pane id laundered into the label field. The record is
   Terminal-scoped — the pane id IS the key, and it is already the selector
   the caller used. Duplicating it into `name` adds zero information and
   lengthens every label.
3. `%claude` SHOULD stay ambiguous. Refusing on twelve Claude panes is the
   honest answer to an ambiguous request. The right fix is for %name to
   resolve against EXPLICITLY SET names and refuse a manifest constant with a
   message that says so — an ADR-0075 rewording, which is done, not a record
   change.

USER-VISIBLE EFFECT OF THE RULING: none. Sidebar entries and tab labels keep
reading `claude`, disambiguated by pane id exactly as today.
AgentStateJson.agent.label is unchanged and agent.id stays the kind slug.
`phux config agents` is unaffected (live_feed.rs:212-217 prefers kind). If
per-pane labels are wanted in the TUI, render `claude @7` from the pane id the
TUI already holds — a presentation change, not a wire-record change.

WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS, and it is why this stays open at P3:

(a) NOTHING PROMPTS A USER TO SET A PER-PANE NAME. The route exists — `phux
    agent set @7 --name reviewer`, which lands in the explicit_identity bucket
    and is now correctly protected from detector overwrite by the ownership
    bits added in phux-w7z2.27 — but nothing in the docs, the launch path, or
    the TUI suggests doing it. This is an ergonomics gap, not a correctness
    one.
(b) ADR-0075's %name is specified against a field that is USUALLY a constant.
    The rewording landed, including the chosen refusal test: refuse a
    candidate whose `name` equals its own `kind`. That is a SHAPE test, not a
    provenance read, because the record carries no provenance field and
    ADR-0075 keeps resolution client-side. It is exact today (all five shipped
    manifests set name = kind) and it has one honest cost, written into the
    ADR: a human who runs `agent set @7 --name claude --kind claude` is
    refused too. If a future implementer wants provenance instead, that is a
    record-shape change and a different spec call.

TESTS PINNING THE DECISION IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, so nobody "fixes" this by
accident: runtime::client::agent_drain_tests::
the_detector_writes_the_manifest_name_and_never_invents_one, and
reasserting_kind_does_not_overwrite_a_humans_name. Also left deliberately
unchanged: agent_detect/mod.rs report_carries_the_manifest_kind_and_name and
the name == "claude" assertions in phux-server/tests/agent_detect.rs.

This bead no longer blocks phux-w7z2.3 (%name addressing) — that work can
proceed against explicitly-set names.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the agent-orchestration branch; full nix develop -c just ci passed (3525 tests, 72 skipped).

title: Cover the narrow-terminal sidebar yield end-to-end through the driver
description:
The sidebar's narrow-terminal yield is tested at the unit level: sidebar_reservation() and content_rect() in attach/paint.rs, plus the prefix-b bell refusal in the toggle-sidebar arm. What is not covered is the composited result — that at 50 columns a full frame paints panes across the whole width with no strip, and that no layout site (dividers, mouse hit-testing, reflow) still believes the strip is there.

The harness now exists: shipped_frame_rows() in attach/driver.rs tests paints a real frame at an arbitrary viewport and replays it through the PTY probe. It currently passes sidebar: None; extend it to take a reservation and add a narrow-viewport case.

Low priority because the sidebar is off by default, so only opted-in users can hit a regression here.

title: Extract the agent rules engine out of phux-server into a shared crate
description:
Recommendation from the offline-explainer implementation, deliberately not done
alongside it because it is a real move rather than a rider.

crates/phux-server/src/agent_explain.rs lives in phux-server only because that is
where agent_detect/rules.rs is. A manifest evaluator is not a daemon concern. The
CLI already depended on phux-server for `default_socket_path`, so nothing new
entered the dependency graph, but the shape is wrong: `phux agent explain --file`
contacts no server and still pulls in the whole daemon crate.

CLEAN SHAPE: a `phux-agent-rules` crate (or a `phux-core::agent_rules` module)
owning regions.rs, rules.rs, the crates/phux-server/rules/*.toml built-ins and the
fixtures. phux-server depends on it for the detector, phux for the explainer, and
phux-mcp / phux-client could use it without pulling in the server.

SCOPE: five files, an include_str! root change, a fixture relocation, and a
Cargo.toml. Mechanical but not small.

The `pub(crate)` boundary agent_explain establishes should SURVIVE the move:
agent_detect's types are the detector's working state, and ADR-0046's premise is
that agent TUIs churn, so freezing Predicate / Screen<'a> / RuleSet as public API
would pin the internals of the module designed to move. The facade
(Capture, kinds(), resolve_kind(), explain()) stays the only public surface,
whichever crate it ends up in.

Do this before, not after, the broader manifest-authoring push — moving files under
a growing rules tree costs more later. Low priority because nothing is blocked on
it today.

title: AskedSource::Scrape: capture-bearing rules, a producer, and a clear path
description:
Audit rank 9: largest work, least certain payoff, and gated on a corpus that does
not yet exist. Filed at P3 honestly rather than pretended to be near-term.

`AskedSource::Scrape` (crates/phux-server/src/agent_asked.rs:12) is declared with
`#[allow(dead_code, reason = "passive scrape source lands after the detector
core")]`. The arbitration it participates in is finished and tested. What is
missing is everything that would produce one:

1. NO PRODUCER, AND NO PLUMBING FOR ONE. The detector's only outbound channel is
   `AgentDetectEvent`, which has exactly two variants (State, Retract), drained at
   runtime/client.rs:112. A scrape source needs a third variant plus a drain arm
   calling `ServerState::report_agent_asked` (state/agent.rs:7).

2. THE RULE ENGINE CANNOT PRODUCE A QUESTION, ONLY A BOOLEAN. `Predicate` evaluates
   to bool (rules.rs:181); `Regex::is_match` is used, never `captures`.
   `Evaluation` (:260) carries a state, four flags and a rule id — no text. An
   `AskedPayload` needs {id, question, suggestions, elapsed_seconds}
   (agent_asked.rs:31). That means CAPTURE-BEARING RULES: named groups for question
   and options, plus a stable synthetic `id` so report's equality-based coalescing
   (:87) does not re-fire every tick on a re-rendered spinner. This is a MANIFEST
   SCHEMA CHANGE, not plumbing, and it is the substantial piece.

3. NO CLEAR PATH. `AskedDetector::clear_terminal` (:103) is called on reap and by
   the hook path. A level-triggered scrape source also needs "the blocker left the
   screen -> clear", which has no representation today.

4. THE CORPUS GATE. ADR-0036's Consequences: "A detector PR must include the
   captured local/CI corpus it claims to support."
   crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/fixtures/ holds 15 captures (idle / working
   / blocked across claude, codex, omp, opencode, pi) — a real start, but every one
   of them was captured to answer "is this blocked", not "what is the question text
   and what are the options". New captures are required.

DEPENDS ON the sentinel-into-AskedSource bead: build the ladder ADR-0036 describes
before adding a third rung to it.

title: Fold the phux-ask title sentinel into AskedSource so ADR-0036's ladder actually exists
description:
ADR-0036 describes a three-tier ask ladder: hook authoritative, `phux-ask` title
sentinel interoperable, screen scrape advisory and never outranking a hook.

TIER 2 IS NOT IN THE LADDER AT ALL. The sentinel bypasses `AskedDetector` entirely:
crates/phux-server/src/terminal_actor/mod.rs:2075 parses
`AskMarker::parse(&self.last_title)` and calls `self.emit_event(AgentEvent::Asked
{...})` directly, with its own private coalescing via `last_ask` (:772). So the
sentinel and a hook report cannot arbitrate against each other — an agent using both
emits two Asked events — and the ADR's "hook outranks sentinel" is implemented
nowhere.

Meanwhile the arbiter itself is done and tested: `AskedSource` (agent_asked.rs:12)
with priority Hook=1 > Scrape=0 (:22), `AskedDetector::report` (:77), unit test
`hook_wins_over_scrape` (:129). It just has one producer — `grep 'AskedSource::'
crates/` outside agent_asked.rs yields two hits, both Hook
(runtime/commands.rs:2947, the REPORT_ASKED 0x12 handler, and a test).

WORK: fold the sentinel into `AskedSource` as a third variant with priority between
Scrape and Hook, and route terminal_actor's sentinel path through
`ServerState::report_agent_asked` instead of emitting AgentEvent::Asked directly.
Watch the coalescing: the sentinel's private `last_ask` dedupe and
AskedDetector::report's equality-based coalescing (:87) must not double up or
cancel out.

Small refactor. It makes the ladder ADR-0036 describes actually exist, and it is a
PREREQUISITE for a scrape source behaving as that ADR specifies — do this before
AskedSource::Scrape, not after.

ALSO: correct ADR-0036's text while here. It states the ladder as implemented when
tier 2 is not, and it closes with "If libghostty-vt later exposes OSC 9 / OSC 777
... that can become another source", which is obsolete — phux has its own raw-byte
OSC scanner and does not need libghostty for that.
close_reason: ask title sentinel now routes through AskedSource so ADR-0036's ladder arbitrates it

title: Agent manifest coverage: 16 missing kinds, and 4x rule depth on the kinds we have
description:
Audit section 3. phux ships 5 manifests and 11 rules; herdr ships 19 screen
manifests and 98 rules across 21 kinds. Both breadth and depth.

BREADTH — 16 kinds with no phux manifest, and `identify` cannot even resolve them,
because `by_binary` (agent_detect/rules.rs:322) is populated only from loaded
manifests' `binaries`, so an unmanifested agent is never identified and `tick`
returns DetectOutcome::Quiet (agent_detect/mod.rs:360):
gemini (see phux-7p8), cursor, devin, agy/antigravity, cline, copilot, kimi, kiro,
droid, amp, grok, hermes, kilo, qodercli, maki, mastracode (hook-only in herdr too).

DEPTH — on shared kinds: claude 3 vs 12, codex 2 vs 7, opencode 2 vs 3.
phux is AHEAD on one: it has an `omp` screen manifest; herdr's omp is hook-only. So
phux is not a strict subset and this is not a copy exercise.

Note claude.toml has NO idle rule and no visible-idle rule at all — idle is reached
only via the fail-safe. That is a deliberate documented choice (three rules were
removed after being checked against the shipped CLI) and the doctrine is right; do
not undo it by adding a static-glyph-means-idle rule. herdr's equivalents are
live_prompt_box, osc_title_idle (`^\x{2733} `) and osc_progress_idle; phux
explicitly rejected the U+2733-means-idle inference because it conflates idle with
waiting-on-a-dialog. OSC progress (separate bead) is the version of that signal
without the conflation.

GATED, and the gate is the point: authoring manifests blind is how ADR-0046 got a
first draft where every screen rule matched nothing. The offline explainer landed
this run (`phux agent explain --file PATH --kind KIND`) and is the tool that makes
this cheap instead of speculative. Parameterized bottom-lines(N) is the other
prerequisite — a large fraction of herdr's rules need an N phux cannot express, so
porting before that lands means rewriting them.

Per-kind pattern to follow (see commits 47c039a, 9b2d8a2): TOML manifest + identify
fixtures + tests, with real captures under
crates/phux-server/src/agent_detect/fixtures/<kind>/. Do not add a manifest without
its captures.

phux-7p8 already tracks the gemini manifest specifically and is the smallest item
on the list; this bead is everything after it.
close_reason: Landed on main. DECLINED all 16 requested kinds rather than invent screens for CLIs it could not authenticate -- a manifest rule matching a screen nobody captured is a guess, which is exactly phux-w7z2.28's complaint. Instead shipped two rules whose strings were ALREADY sitting in committed fixtures and whose manifests carried comments explicitly recording them as 'filed rather than guessed': screen-status-elapsed-backstop (claude, matching by structure -- ellipsis token plus elapsed parenthetical -- rather than the cycling glyph) and screen-working-footer-backstop (codex, exact captured footer as an all-match). Both region-scoped to bottom-lines that other rules already extract, so hot-path cost is unmeasurable; 11 -> 13 rules against a budget of 128. Every new rule has a positive AND negative fixture-backed test. At integration both rules were found to carry visible-working = true, the exact key phux-w7z2.18 deleted -- git reported ZERO conflicts because they were new text blocks -- and the line was removed from both; behaviour unchanged since both already declare state = working.

title: Three sites cite ADR-0067 while describing ADR-0068's agent-session record
description: Found during the ADR-0067 collision cleanup (which renumbered the native-bootstrap decision to ADR-0070). Separate, older citation bug: crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/frame.rs:271, the 0.6.0-draft.4 row in docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md, and docs/spec/L3.md:355 all say 'ADR-0067' while linking or describing the phux.agent-session/v1 record, which is ADR-0068's content. Not caused by the collision; predates it.
acceptance_criteria: All three citations name ADR-0068; a grep for ADR-0067 finds only references to the cache-preserving agent fleet context decision.
close_reason: All three citations now name ADR-0068; the CHANGELOG numbering note rewritten to describe both collisions; ADR-0071's own references repointed to ADR-0070.

title: An emptied main window stands on the web surface instead of closing
description: PRODUCT DECISION, deliberately not taken unilaterally. When the main window's last tab closes while other windows are open, it stays open showing the web surface rather than closing like a secondary window would. macOS apps genuinely vary here - some keep a primary window, most close it. If it should close, retireEmptyWindow (src/cockpit/update.zig:929) is the single place to change, and the quit rule below it already handles the last-window case correctly.
close_reason: Emptied main window now closes like a secondary; last-window path unchanged

title: cmd+A selects the viewport, not the scrollback
description: terminal.select-all composes the existing selection primitives to cover the visible screen. Ghostty's select_all covers the entire scrollback. Matching it needs a session-level select-entire-history primitive rather than a viewport walk. Low priority but a real behavioural divergence from the terminal these users are arriving from, and the kind of thing that silently loses someone half the output they meant to copy.
close_reason: Closed

title: web_panes has no window discriminator
description: ChromeOptions.build_window gained a ChromeContext naming the window; web_panes did not. So every secondary-window rebuild logs 'webview pane phux-cockpit-web: no canvas widget carries semantics label...'. Behaviour is correct - the webview belongs to one window and is found there - but the log is noise on every rebuild of every other window. Giving web_panes the same ChromeContext would let the app return the pane only for the window that owns it. Needs the SDK fork.
close_reason: Closed

title: Automation snapshots keep ghost windows after close
description: After a declared window closes, automation_snapshot.zig still prints its 'window @wN' line - its views are correctly gone, but the window line remains because self.windows[0..count] is not filtered on info.open. This made verifying multi-window close behaviour harder to read than it should have been, and would mislead any smoke test asserting window counts. Needs the SDK fork.
close_reason: Closed

title: Automation harness sends key_down without key_up
description: The automation command channel emits only key_down, never key_up. The app's shortcut latch therefore swallows a repeated chord - driving cmd+G twice in a row does nothing the second time. Not a product bug (real hardware releases keys) but it silently misleads any agent or smoke test driving chords through automation, and cost debugging time already.
