Either the harness should emit a paired release, or widget-key should grow an explicit release action.
close_reason: Closed

title: SDK conflates semantics.hidden with do-not-render
description: In the pinned SDK, widget_render.zig:261 treats semantics.hidden as suppressing RENDERING, not merely the accessibility node. This cost real time: the scrollback search field's magnifier icon and caret painted nothing until hidden was removed from both. The clean fix is an SDK-side split between hidden (invisible to a11y, still painted) and decorative (painted, invisible to a11y) - but note tabAttentionMarker currently RELIES on the conflation to reserve invisible space, so the semantics cannot simply change without updating that call site. Needs the fork.
close_reason: SDK now splits semantics.decorative (a11y-only) from hidden (visibility); hidden still reserves layout so tabAttentionMarker is unaffected

title: Copy and paste are inert while the search field is open
description: cmd+C and cmd+V sit below the modal search gate in handleKey, so they do nothing while the search band has focus. Pasting a needle into the search field is unimplemented, and copying from the terminal while search is open silently fails. Both should work: paste should insert into the needle, and copy should either act on the terminal selection or be explicitly disabled.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ligatures: decided NO, with reasoning
description:
DECISION: do not implement ligatures. Recorded so the question is not reopened without new information.

The packed cell-grid model PERMITS them. An N-cell cluster generalizes the wide/spacer mechanism already in CellWidth: the head cell owns the ligature glyph, continuations ink nothing, positions stay index-derived, and selection and cursor keep addressing individual cells. The primitive is not the obstacle.

The obstacle is WHO DECIDES what ligates. That requires GSUB liga shaping. CoreText has it; the SDK's own font_ttf.Face (glyphIndex/advance/outline) does not. If the AppKit host shapes and the CPU reference renderer does not, the two diverge - and because automation screenshots render through the reference path, the divergence would be INVISIBLE in every screenshot while being wrong on real glass. That is the exact failure mode this whole line of work exists to avoid.

Doing it properly means: a GSUB ligature-substitution reader in font_ttf.zig so the ENGINE decides once; cells carrying glyph IDs rather than only cluster bytes (a ligature is a specific glyph, not a string); then wire format, both renderers, and the glyph-atlas key path following. That is a project, not an increment.

It is also moot today: the app deliberately bundles JetBrains Mono NL, the explicit no-ligature variant. If ligatures are ever wanted, do it engine-side with explicit glyph ids, never by letting each renderer shape for itself.
close_reason: Closed

title: Upstream ghostty bug: vt.highlight.Flattened.init does not compile
description: In the pinned libghostty-vt, highlight.zig around line 141-160, Flattened.init assigns .end_x but the field is named bot_x, which is left uninitialized. Zig's lazy analysis hides it because nothing in this build calls the function. Any code that calls it fails to compile. Use untracked/startPin/endPin/clone instead. Found while scoping scrollback search. Worth reporting to ghostty-org upstream.
notes:
PATCH PREPARED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-10, not submitted.

Confirmed real at the pinned rev 7aa9591 AND on current upstream main (44f06d4e4). Not fixed upstream.

It is TWO compile errors in Flattened.init, both hidden by the same lazy-analysis mechanism (nothing in the tree calls init; every Flattened is either .empty or built field-by-field in search/sliding_window.zig):
  1. '.end_x = end.x' - the field is bot_x.
  2. 'var result: std.MultiArrayList(PageChunk)' - returned as chunks: MultiArrayList(Flattened.Chunk); PageList.PageIterator.Chunk has no 'serial' field, and carrying the flattened serial is the whole difference between the two Chunk types.

bot_x is established as correct from usage, not guessed: it is the field declaration, and it is what the struct doc, empty, clone, endPin and untracked all use, plus render.zig:825,2120 and sliding_window.zig:377,445,535-536. Across all of src/, end_x as a Flattened field appears exactly ONCE - at the bug.

WHERE: branch fix/highlight-flattened-init at ed5f0b7f451dfd57dfa575b491d5b5f723429581, based on upstream main, in a throwaway worktree (the owner's ~/workspace/ghostty checkout was deliberately left untouched on feat/terminal-snapshot-c-api). Standalone patch also written to the session scratchpad as 0001-terminal-fix-Flattened-init.patch. NOTE: both live under /private/tmp and will not survive a reboot - re-generate or move somewhere durable before relying on them.

VERIFIED: 'zig build test-lib-vt' full unfiltered run passes 5480/5516, 36 skipped, 0 failures. Two new tests (single-page and cross-page) cover it, and each was proven to FAIL when its bug is reintroduced - a test that merely constructed a Flattened literal would not have caught either, because the call site is the point. Whole-app 'zig build test' could not run: missing Metal Toolchain, unrelated.

BLOCKED ON A DECISION, not on work: ghostty-org is a third-party repo, so opening the PR needs the owner's explicit per-instance say-so. Nothing was pushed and no fork was created.
close_reason: Fix verified and pushed to phall1/ghostty as fix/highlight-flattened-init (ed5f0b7f). No upstream PR per owner's standing rule.

title: Command budget could return to 2048 now that terminals do not drive it
description: The per-view command ceiling was raised 2048 to 4096 to buy rows for terminal painting. The packed cell_grid command makes a terminal cost a constant 4 commands regardless of size or styling, so that pressure is gone. Dropping back to 2048 would hand back roughly 45 MB of fixed-capacity address space across the 32 view slots (RuntimeView is currently 5.45 MiB, Runtime 174.5 MiB). Needs its own measurement to confirm no non-terminal view depends on the higher ceiling.
close_reason: Taken back. max_canvas_commands_per_view returned 4096 -> 2048 with both host caps following, returning ~45 MiB of fixed-capacity address space across the 32 view slots. Safe because the packed cell grid made terminals - the only reason the ceiling was ever raised - cost about 100 commands. Full SDK suite green at 2048, and the consuming app is green at the resulting chrome_command_envelope of 1792.

title: No URL detection or click-to-open in terminal output
description: OSC 8 hyperlinks are parsed by the engine but not surfaced, and there is no heuristic URL detection for plain output. Ghostty underlines a URL on hover and opens it on click or cmd+click. Needs a hit-test channel from the grid back to the pointer path plus an open-URL effect.
notes: Correction: this was briefly closed with a deferral reason, which was wrong - it is wanted work, not finished work. Reopened. Still needs a hit-test channel from the grid back to the pointer path plus an open-URL effect; OSC 8 hyperlinks are parsed by the engine but never surfaced. Natural time to do it is the next time the pointer path is touched.
close_reason: Heuristic URL detection + cmd+click open, backed by a new SDK fx.openUrl with its own allowlist. OSC 8 surfacing left as a follow-up.

title: pane.previous and pane.next are orphaned command names
description:
`onCommand` maps "pane.previous" and "pane.next" to `.cycle_pane` (src/cockpit/native/view.zig:761-762), but neither id appears in `cockpit_shortcuts` (src/cockpit/native/scene.zig:28-38) and the app declares no native menu. Nothing in the shipped app can ever emit those command names.

Split-pane focus cycling is still reachable via cmd+option+left/right through `handleKey` on the canvas key channel, so this is dead mapping rather than lost capability.

Note: "layout.split" is also unregistered but that one is DELIBERATE — split must not claim a global shortcut while only one terminal may exist. Do not 'fix' it by registering it.
acceptance_criteria: Either the two command names are registered/menu-backed so something can emit them, or the dead mappings are removed. Whichever is chosen, layout.split's deliberate omission is left intact and commented.
close_reason: Reachable now. pane.previous and pane.next are registered as cmd+[ and cmd+] in cockpit_shortcuts (scene.zig:42-43), carry menu rows under Previous/Next Pane (scene.zig:108-109), and resolve to cycle_pane in onCommand (view.zig:877-878). Four pane.focus-* directional commands were added alongside them on cmd+opt+arrows, backed by the layout tree's geometric focusDirection.

title: Chrome band reveal is an instant layout flip with no easing
description:
`chromeRevealed` (src/cockpit/native/workspace_projection.zig:77) flips the band in or out between one frame and the next. The content area jumps by `header_height` in a single step.

The substantive anti-jank work is already done — reveal is driven only by discrete state the operator caused, so the band never moves incidentally, and it is the only thing that resizes the content area. What is missing is easing on the transition that does happen.
design:
The SDK has the machinery; the blocker is a timing anchor, not a capability.

Available (verified in the vendored native-sdk):
- `UiApp.Options.animations` -> `canvas.CanvasRenderAnimation` — per-frame opacity + affine, easing/spring, re-applied after every rebuild with the latest frame timestamp.
- `ElementOptions.transform` — layout-free translate that hit-testing follows, so a sliding band stays interactive without reflowing siblings.

The open question: `CanvasRenderAnimation` needs a stable `start_ns`. The model is a deterministic replay loop and cannot read the clock, so 'when did this reveal begin' has to come from somewhere that does not break replay. Decide that before writing the animation.

Also verify in a RUNNING app, not the null platform — the null-platform tests do not exercise Metal presentation, so they cannot show whether the reveal actually reads as smooth.
acceptance_criteria: Revealing and retracting the band eases rather than jumps, replay determinism is preserved, and the transition is confirmed by eye in the packaged app.
close_reason: Deliberately NOT doing this, with two independent technical reasons rather than a preference. (1) The SDK's layout tween animates the WIDGET TREE only, while the painter, the hit targets and the PTY pump all derive from workspaceChrome - so an eased tree over a stepped content rect leaves all three disagreeing for the length of every animation, which is the exact failure resolvePanes exists to prevent, replayed on every tab open and close. (2) Easing the extent in workspaceChrome instead keeps them in lockstep but moves content.height every frame, and onFrame emits .viewport the moment the proposed row count changes, which calls fx.ptyResize - over a 50pt band and a ~17.5pt cell that is THREE SIGWINCHes per pane per reveal, i.e. three full redraws of whatever TUI is running. The band's CONTENTS may be animated freely (opacity, a slide inside its own rect); only its extent is load-bearing. Reopen only if the extent stops driving pane geometry.

title: Phase 5: extract LeaseTable and Lifecycle
description: Remaining ungrouped fields after Phases 3-4. LeaseTable: input_leases, satellite_leases. Lifecycle: server_incarnation, has_served_client, viewport_clock, upgrade_ctx, live_connections, idle_since. Completes the epic's 8-concern target.
acceptance_criteria: ServerState holds only named sub-structs plus MetadataStore and hook_dispatcher. just ci green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 2 follow-up: window_wire_reverse has zero read sites
description:
IdSpace::window_reverse is inserted (bind_window, intern_window) and removed (retire_window) but never queried - there is no window_from_wire anywhere in the workspace. It exists only for symmetry with terminal_reverse.

Left in place during the Phase 2 extraction because deleting dead state is a behavior question, not code motion. Decide: delete it, or add the missing window_from_wire lookup if a caller was supposed to exist.
close_reason: Single choke point sync_overlays_to_focused_pane in input_dispatch.rs, routed from both the layout_replaced block (covers peer broadcast AND TerminalSpawned/Closed reflow -- verified every reflow_panes:true rides layout_replaced:true) and the refactored SIGWINCH arm. Failing-first test layout_replace_reclaims_the_focused_pane_rect_for_overlays proved the stale clamp before the fix. window_reverse confirmed to have zero read sites workspace-wide and deleted with its three write sites; terminal_reverse untouched.

title: Phase 4: extract HubState and AgentState
description: hub_table, hub_link_statuses, hub_relays; agent_asked, agent_records. Smallest concerns, done last so the pattern is settled.
acceptance_criteria: HubState and AgentState own their fields. just ci green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Completions still offer hidden per-verb flags (--horizontal/--vertical): arg-level pruning or upstream fix
description: Remainder from the G3 gate's completion leak loop. clap_complete 4.6.7's shell generators only consult is_hide_set for possible VALUES; hidden args ride into the emitted option lists. Evidence: generated bash script for insert-pane/move-pane contains opts="-h --split --horizontal --vertical --ratio --json --socket --help" -- the deprecated booleans phux-i0e8.8.4 hid from --help are offered by tab completion. The G3 fix (completion.rs completion_tree) prunes hidden top-level VERBS but cannot prune args: clap::Command has no arg-removal API either, so this needs per-subcommand tree reconstruction, generated-script post-processing, or an upstream clap_complete change (hide-filtering subcommands and args in the AOT generators). Low urgency: completing a hidden flag still parses and warns toward --split; the leak is cosmetic-plus (it advertises deprecated spellings).
acceptance_criteria: Generated bash/zsh completions offer --split but not --horizontal/--vertical on insert-pane and move-pane; a test pins it; approach documented (post-process, reconstruction, or upstream bump with justification).
close_reason: Wave 13 merged. hidden args pruned from completions

comments.author: phall
comments.text: Implemented on branch ux/x2 (85e0862b): completion_tree now routes visible verbs through visible_subtree, which reconstructs any subtree carrying hidden args/subcommands (clap has no removal API) and clones clean subtrees wholesale. BUILD NOTE confirmed: in the nix dev shell on this Mac, the ambient DEVELOPER_DIR/SDKROOT point at the nix apple-sdk-14.4 and the shell's xcbuild xcrun cannot resolve the macosx SDK from them, so libghostty's zig build dies with DarwinSdkNotFound/libsystem-override. Workaround: export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer and unset SDKROOT inside nix develop.

title: task
description: The find-in-scrollback primitive shipped server-side in phux-server/src/search.rs (phux-3sy), but no consumer surface exposes it: copy-mode has no search binding, ACTION_NAMES has no search action, and no CLI verb reaches it. The original UX audit (phux-i0e8.11) found README claiming literal scrollback search as shipped; the claim has been removed from curated docs (phux-i0e8.11.6) and this bead is the tracked home for the promise worth keeping: a copy-mode search affordance (enter a query, jump between matches, extract via the existing libghostty selection wrappers) within the ADR bounds of 'no tmux-style copy-mode reimplementation' (CONTRIBUTING no-list: phux owns only find-in-scrollback; selection/extraction delegates to libghostty).

title: Direct tests for host enroll tails: finish_enroll role routing, ssh-only registration, --json success shape

title: Status-bar widget kinds worth implementing: text and spacer
description: The retired tui.md 8.3 hand table promised seven widget kinds that were never registered (window, pane, host, mode, key-indicator, text, spacer). phux-i0e8.11.3 deleted the phantom rows; the generated docs/reference/widgets.md now covers exactly the registered kinds. Two of the seven are worth actually building: 'text' (a literal styled string, the simplest custom-bar building block; trivially expressible as a WidgetKindSpec with a required 'value' option) and 'spacer' (flexible expanding space so users can push widgets apart within a slot; needs a small composer change since it is width-elastic rather than content-sized). Implement each as a factory + SPEC const in crates/phux-config/src/widget/widgets/, register in WidgetRegistry::with_builtins(), and run 'just docs-gen' - the registry-vs-spec test and the freshness test force the docs to follow. The other five phantoms (window, pane, host, mode, key-indicator) stay unfiled: no demonstrated need, and 'windows'/'cwd' already cover the adjacent use cases.
notes: Progress 2026-08-07: the 'text' kind is DONE (crates/phux-config/src/widget/widgets/text.rs, registered, docs regenerated, value required rather than defaulted so a missing value and a deliberately empty one are distinguishable). 'spacer' is deliberately NOT done, because the bead's 'needs a small composer change' understates it. Reading status_bar.rs: Slot::render concatenates fixed-width cell output and receives only WidgetContext, never the available width; the three slots are then positioned independently (left flush at 0, right flush against width-1, center centered in the remaining gap) with left-biased truncation. So an elastic widget INSIDE a slot has no well-defined width to expand into, and 'push widgets apart' is ambiguous against a slot that is itself already being positioned by that algorithm. Making it real needs a decision first: either slots gain a two-pass layout with an available-width budget, or spacer is redefined as a fixed-width pad (trivial, but not what the bead asks for). Do not guess this one -- ADR-0071 freezes the config surface at 1.0, so a half-designed elastic widget is expensive to take back.

title: Umbrella: `phux host` namespace consolidation + concept-pair help disambiguation
description:
Four near-duplicate concept pairs force users to learn distinctions the product should absorb (decision bead — needs a naming/IA design pass, likely an ADR since it closes a design space):

- phux enroll HOST vs phux satellite enroll HOST (mod.rs:1324-1355 vs 1841-1874): same positional, same five flags, differ only in --session vs --json.
- phux remote vs phux satellite (mod.rs:1431-1472 vs 1826-1922): both add/list/remove registries of other phux servers with --token-file/--cert-fingerprint.
- phux pair vs phux relay pair (mod.rs:1277 vs relay.rs:59): same verb, unrelated objects (device token vs route token).
- phux workspace vs phux worktree (mod.rs:1200 vs 1426): one letter apart, both git-checkout-shaped, workspace inspect vs worktree list overlap.

Also in scope: stdio-bridge is a machine-only verb in the human namespace (consider hiding); agent install-claude/uninstall-claude hard-code a vendor into a generic namespace (agent/mod.rs — also the only subcommand family with zero doc comments on its args; fix those regardless). Attach name-shadowing (remote registry shadows local session, attach.rs:524-529) must at minimum be documented in attach --help.

Constraint: renames are breaking; keep old names as hidden aliases for one release, per the deprecation pattern.
design:
---

DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream E, 2026-08-01) — decided, do not relitigate. (1) remote + satellite + top-level enroll consolidate under `phux host` (`host add|ls|list|rm|remove|enroll`) with a --role remote|satellite axis (default remote); the old three verbs become HIDDEN aliases for one release cycle printing a one-line stderr deprecation note; completions follow the visible tree only. (2) Config stays SPLIT: [[remote]] and [[satellites]] encode deliberately opposite trust directions (phux-config/src/remote.rs:7-12 — collapsing would let phux enroll edit federation topology); no [[hosts]] array, no migration. (3) pair / relay pair / workspace / worktree KEEP their names and get cross-referencing help text only. (4) Enroll asymmetry: --json valid on both roles (remote-role enroll gains JSON output — local, no wire change); --session rejected under --role satellite with a remedy-naming error. (5) Adjacent fixes: agent subcommand arg docs (agent/mod.rs:26-90), attach name-shadowing documented in attach --help (attach.rs:524-529), stdio-bridge hidden (mod.rs:1240-1245); install-claude/uninstall-claude keep their names. Recorded in ADR-0066 (renumbered from the planner's 0065 — stream D's grammar ADR owns 0065). Decomposed into E1-E6; umbrella.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: ADR-0066, host add/ls/rm/enroll, deprecation flip, concept-pair help, enroll tail tests — one namespace for machines.

title: eof_detach test is load-sensitive: 2s deadline fails under parallel load
description:
phux-server::eof_detach pty_eof_drives_terminal_closed_to_attached_client failed at 79.9s during a full-workspace nextest run on a machine also running seven agents and a 12-minute compile. Re-run in isolation on the same tree: PASS in 0.847s.

The test seeds a shell with 'sleep 0.2; exit 0' and asserts TERMINAL_CLOSED arrives within a 'generous two-second deadline'. Two seconds is generous on an idle laptop and not generous on a saturated one, and CI runners are frequently saturated.

Not a correctness bug and not a regression -- the contract it pins is right. But a wall-clock deadline in a test that gates every PR is a future flake. Options: raise the deadline substantially (it costs nothing when the path works), or drive it off an event rather than a timer. Same audit applies to the other two tests nextest reported as 'slow' in that run.
close_reason: Landed in PR #309 (324 sites classified, ~110 fixed). NOTE: one site escaped - see the follow-up bead for concurrent_attach_no_lag.

Fix: derive the list from cargo metadata (jq over .packages[] filtered to workspace members) so a new crate is covered the moment it exists. Then audit the tree for other hand-maintained lists with the same failure mode: the justfile e2e filterset is an explicit binary_id list where a missing entry means tests never run in CI and rot green.

title: rec: playback verb (phux play FILE.cast) - deferred from the recording epic
description:
Deferred out of the built-in recording epic (phux-e7ez) on purpose, not forgotten.

Recording ships write-only: phux rec / phux --rec produce asciicast v2 plus natively-rendered GIF/APNG. Playback is deliberately NOT shipped because 'asciinema play FILE.cast' already reads our output, and the smol manifesto argues against growing a second surface we then have to keep honest.

Revisit if either becomes true:
- users are round-tripping casts and want playback INSIDE a phux pane (a pane whose PTY is fed from a cast is a genuinely different thing from asciinema play in a shell, and is the real argument for building it);
- we ship cast v3 by default and want a reader that does not depend on the user's asciinema version.

Note when picking this up: docs/consumers/tui.md section 10 previously specified 'phux capture --record' and 'phux play' as accepted design. ADR-0060 supersedes that section and retires the 'capture' name; a future playback verb should be called 'play' and read the same cast the recorder writes.
close_reason: Landed in PR #312 as phux play (ADR-0064) - playback as a live pane, not a shell-level viewer.

title: per-consumer link sub-identities on federation link (ADR-0038 deferral)
description: All hub consumers collapse to one identity on the satellite: no per-consumer audit/authz, and link redial frees the satellite-side input lease while hub-side exclusion persists (documented flaw, spec draft.15). Prerequisite for multi-tenant/team (enterprise) deployments. Wire change: sub-identity tagging on relayed frames. Deserves its own ADR extending 0038. Large.

title: federate APPLY_INPUT: route acknowledged idempotent input to satellites
description: ADR-0053 built reconnect-safe input for unreliable remote consumers but scoped it local-only — APPLY_INPUT rejects SATELLITE TerminalIds, so the guarantee is missing exactly where transports fail. Extend over hub relay: operation-id cache on owning satellite, hub passes through verbatim like PUT_FILE (ADR-0059). Care: server_id incarnation semantics across the hop. Medium.

title: agent-detection manifests: gemini-cli (then cursor-agent, aider, goose)
description: Detection framework proven (ADR-0046, crates/phux-server/rules/*.toml, 5 manifests). gemini-cli ships a plugin integration (examples/plugins/agent-tools/integrations/gemini-cli.toml) but no rules manifest — users hit the inconsistency. Each agent = TOML manifest + identify fixtures/tests per verified-manifest pattern (47c039a, 9b2d8a2). Small, high leverage.
notes:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-08 by a detection-parity audit against herdr, and worse than an inconsistency. gemini-cli.toml declares command = "gemini" and launches through phux-agent-wrap.sh, so the pane self-declares a phux.agent/v1 record. But crates/phux-server/rules/ has no gemini.toml, so RuleSet::kind_for_binary("gemini") returns None (by_binary, agent_detect/rules.rs:322, is populated only from loaded manifests binaries), AgentDetector::tick returns DetectOutcome::Quiet before ever reading the screen (agent_detect/mod.rs:360), and the wrapper writes identity only (state left unset), which makes the pane explicit_identity but not declared (agent_state.rs:86). The detector is therefore left running specifically to fill state in (agent_state.rs:59-63) and cannot. User-visible result: a gemini pane shows a name and a kind and a permanently absent state, next to a claude pane with a live badge. A 2-rule gemini.toml (title plus one blocker) closes it; the audit ranks this the smallest of its ten items. The offline explainer that landed 2026-08-08 (phux agent explain --file PATH --kind KIND) makes writing those two rules against a real capture cheap. Linked to the agent-orchestration epic phux-w7z2 (see phux-w7z2.21 for the broader coverage push).

=== 2026-08-15, branch army/w3-detection-manifests (commit 4b0c7086) ===

NOTHING SHIPPED, DELIBERATELY, and the bead stays open.

gemini-cli is neither installed nor configured in this environment (`command -v
gemini` finds nothing; no ~/.gemini). cursor-agent and aider are likewise
absent. goose IS installed and configured, but the bead orders gemini first and
"then cursor-agent, aider, goose ... if the first goes cleanly" -- the first
cannot go at all here.

A gemini.toml could have been written from the plugin integration's declared
command plus a guess at the TUI's chrome. That is exactly the defect
phux-w7z2.28 is about (an unfalsifiable rule) and exactly the failure ADR-0046's
Tradeoffs already record phux making once -- the first detection draft was
written against an imagined Claude TUI and every screen rule in it matched
nothing, silently. Adding more unbacked rules while fixing that bead would be
self-defeating, so none were added. Same reasoning as 74ee2985.

The gap the bead describes is REAL and unchanged: there is still no
crates/phux-server/rules/gemini.toml, so kind_for_binary("gemini") returns None
and a gemini pane shows name + kind with a permanently absent state.

CORROBORATING EVIDENCE FOR WHY A CAPTURE IS NON-NEGOTIABLE, found this session:
claude's title-busy-spinner rule, written against a real 2.1.207 capture, had
already silently stopped matching by 2.1.228 because the CLI changed its spinner
glyphs (U+2802/U+2810 -> U+25D0/U+25D1). If a rule backed by a real capture rots
that fast, a rule backed by a guess never worked in the first place.

UNBLOCKS WHEN: gemini-cli is installed and authenticated on the capture machine.
Then follow the checklist in research/2026-08-15-agent-detection-fixture-audit.md.

description: Two unverified low findings in crates/phux/src/commands/service.rs: (1) systemd unit does not escape % specifiers or $ expansion in ExecStart/Environment (lines ~831-845) — paths containing % or $ generate broken units; (2) with HOME unset, launchd unit files are written into the current directory (lines 66-77, 862-864). title: phux enroll writes bearer token to disk before name/endpoint validation
description: run_enroll (crates/phux/src/commands/enroll.rs:224) calls write_token before NewRemote validation. Scenarios: --name '../../x' writes token outside <state>/remotes via unsanitized join before name rejection; quic endpoint without fingerprint fails AFTER token write, leaving orphaned 0600 bearer-token files. Fix: construct/validate NewRemote first (validate_token_file permits not-yet-existing file), then write_token, then add_or_update. Verified by research team.
notes: Fixed: NewRemote validated before write_token in run_enroll (both ssh-only and paired paths); finish() now takes the pre-built NewRemote so validation happens exactly once, before any disk write.
close_reason: 522: the validate-before-write ordering was already correct in finish_enroll (d2946e3f, carried through the enroll.rs->host.rs refactor) but had NO test pinning it; added enroll_rejects_a_traversal_name_before_writing_any_token and enroll_rejects_unpinned_quic_before_writing_any_token, both asserting zero .token files written. 8wm: both findings reproduced and fixed -- systemd_quote now doubles % and $ (was escaping only backslash and quote), and unit_path/home_dir/config_home became fallible so an unset HOME errors clearly instead of writing launchd units into the cwd across all 5 call sites. title: relay ensure_self_signed silently rotates cert when one of the pair is missing
description: crates/phux-relay/src/tls.rs ensure_self_signed guard is cert.exists() && key.exists(); with exactly one file missing it regenerates BOTH, silently rotating the pinned fingerprint and breaking every connector/consumer pin with opaque TLS failures. Fix: three-way match — both=ok, neither=generate, one=error naming the missing file and warning that deleting both rotates the fingerprint. Verified by research team.
notes: Fixed in BOTH sites (relay tls.rs and phux-server transport/tls.rs — same pattern existed server-side): three-way match, partial pair now errors with PartialTlsPair naming present/missing file instead of silently regenerating. Tests added in both modules.
close_reason: Already fixed by d2946e3f (ancestor of 0.12.1) and never closed; verified against current code this session. 0vp: runtime/client.rs:1090-1105 rejects any non-Hello/non-Ping frame before HELLO with VersionIncompatible and closes, now unconditional across every transport since the client always sends HELLO first including on UDS; hub/link.rs negotiate_link HELLOs first so federation is unaffected; regression test uds_requires_hello_for_stateful_frames_but_ping_remains_stateless passes. tmv: three-way match present in both phux-relay/src/tls.rs and phux-server/src/transport/tls.rs with PartialTlsPair naming the missing file; ensure_self_signed_refuses_a_partial_pair passes in both crates.

title: CI runner disk pressure: test job died with 'No space left on device' before running tests
description: Run 29443995632 (PR #256, 2026-07-15): the test job's runner hit ENOSPC writing its own worker log after the cache-restore steps (nix store via cachix + Swatinem/rust-cache + the new sccache GHA restores), before the tests step started -- every step after rust-cache concluded null and the job failed at runner level. A rerun was issued (may pass on a fresh runner). Standard ubuntu-latest runners have ~14GB free; the restore stack now sits near that edge and will recur as caches grow. Mitigations, cheapest first: (1) add the free-disk preamble (rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /opt/ghc /usr/local/lib/android etc., frees ~25GB, costs ~30s); (2) prune rust-cache's cached target (its cache key already splits check/test profiles -- check sizes via the Actions cache UI); (3) cap what sccache stores. Evidence lives in the run's annotation (System.IO.IOException: No space left on device).
close_reason: Merged as PR #259: disk-headroom preamble (drops dotnet/Android/GHC, ~25GB back) in both compile jobs, with df lines for observability

title: [bug] overlay stub_tailscale_binary_round_trips test is flaky under parallel load
description: commands::overlay::tests::stub_tailscale_binary_round_trips (crates/phux/src/commands/overlay.rs, landed with phux-zndc / PR #237) failed once under full-parallel nextest load in two independent sessions on 2026-07-15, passing in isolation and on clean re-runs both times. It execs a stub tailscale binary, so it is likely sensitive to spawn latency or PATH/tempdir contention under load. Same class as the attach_last flake (phux-mn3b, fixed by polling an observable instead of assuming timing): find the timing assumption and replace it with a bounded poll or generous deadline. It will produce random red CI until fixed.

title: CI never runs the examples/agents smoke test (just placed-fleet-smoke exists but no workflow calls it)
description: justfile:162 has a recipe smoke-testing examples/agents/ scripts against a throwaway server (bash examples/agents/tests/placed-fleet-smoke.sh), but no .github/workflows job invokes it, so the agent-facing example scripts can silently rot (this was flagged as a deferred gap when the agent-surface wave landed 2026-05-29). title: phux fails with a raw 'path must be shorter than SUN_LEN' when PHUX_SOCKET is a long path

The real cause -- the UNIX domain socket path limit, ~104 bytes on macOS -- is never named, and the suggested remedy ('Start a server manually with phux server') does not help since a manual server hits the same limit. Validate the socket path length up front and fail with a message that names the limit and the offending path length. Hit while scripting phux against an isolated socket.

title: Worked example: orchestrate a fleet

This is the executable proof that the epic worked, and it is the thing to run before closing the epic.

Prefer the CLI (per ADR-0022 the CLI is the stable contract) but ALSO include the MCP-flavored equivalent so both surfaces are demonstrated at parity -- the parity bead should have made that possible, and if it is awkward to write, that is a signal parity is not actually done.

title: Config: focus-follows-agent (opt-in directed focus)
description:
The escape hatch for people who DO want the viewport to move on its own -- explicitly opt-in, default off, per ADR-0044.

Gated behind the ADR because an agent silently moving a human's view mid-keystroke is a genuinely bad default: you are typing in pane 3, an agent finishes in pane 7, your cursor is now somewhere else and your next keystroke went to the wrong process. That is a data-loss-shaped bug, not just an annoyance -- which is also why this should probably never apply while the target pane is not idle.
design: Config lives in phux-config (TOML + widgets). Read ADR-0044 for the exact gate semantics before implementing; if the spike found that an agent can ALREADY move a viewport by writing layout metadata, then this bead is not adding a capability -- it is adding the gate that should have been there, and the default-off path needs to actively ignore a remote focused_terminal change.
acceptance_criteria: focus-follows-agent = false by default. When true, an attention event moves the attached client's focus. Documented in docs/consumers/tui.md config section. Off-by-default behavior is tested, not just asserted.
close_reason: Superseded by ADR-0049 and phux-oih5.16: explicit advisory next/return navigation avoids automatic keystroke misdirection.

title: phux move-pane / swap-pane -- CLI verbs for reorganizing
description:
Rearrange an existing workspace: move a pane elsewhere in the tree, or swap two panes. The 'reorganize' half of the ask -- lower priority than focus and split, because those two plus placement-on-launch already cover the main agent-orchestration loop.

Consider whether these are one verb with a flag or two verbs; the TUI has no equivalent action today, so there is no existing naming to match -- pick something and put it in the docs.
design: layout_ops move()/swap() + SET_METADATA. Same registry-file conflict note as the sibling verb beads. If the tree operations get hairy (moving a leaf between subtrees requires collapsing the vacated split), keep the hard logic in layout_ops with unit tests over fixtures rather than in the verb handler.
acceptance_criteria: A pane can be moved and two panes can be swapped, with the attached client re-rendering correctly. Unit tests on the tree ops. e2e test. Docs.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed.

title: Delete the dead phux_client::Agent facade (or fill it) -- it is all stubs and nothing imports it
description:
crates/phux-client/src/agent.rs, 359 lines, exported at lib.rs:46. Status:
  - connect_uds() and get_state() work.
  - run() returns Err('run not yet implemented; use phux_client::run directly')
  - subscribe_events(), send_signal(), attach_or_create() are stubs.
  - wait_for_prompt() is a half-stub (polls once, never checks shell_state).
  - EventType has a single __Placeholder variant.

NEITHER the CLI NOR the MCP adapter imports it. docs/consumers/sdk.md:53-55 already admits it is incomplete. It is a decoy: it is the thing a new contributor (or a swarm agent) will naturally reach for, and it will waste their time or -- worse -- they will 'helpfully' extend it and split the surface in two.

The real shared surface is the free functions in phux-client (selector, snapshot, send_keys, run, wait, watch, ask), which both consumers actually use.
design: Recommend DELETE, and make docs/consumers/sdk.md name the free-function modules as the surface. If you instead choose to fill it, that is a bigger commitment than it looks -- it becomes the thing every new verb in this epic must also land a method on, and nothing in the epic needs it. Deleting is the honest move; sdk.md already says as much.
acceptance_criteria: Either agent.rs is gone and sdk.md documents the free-function surface, or Agent is complete and both CLI and MCP are migrated onto it. Not the current halfway state.
close_reason: Removed dead Agent facade and documented the free-function SDK surface

title: The '=' (last-focused) selector is a lie -- aliased to '.', no MRU tracking exists anywhere
description:
crates/phux-client/src/selector.rs:221: 'Selector::Current | Selector::Last => snapshot.focused_session' -- one arm, both variants. Same aliasing at :175. The module doc admits it at :17 ('same as . here'), but docs/consumers/tui.md:249 advertises '=' as 'last (most recently focused)' to users.

There is NO last-focused / MRU tracking anywhere in the codebase, client or server. No previous-pane pointer, no MRU stack.

Either implement it or remove it from the grammar and the docs. Shipping a documented selector that silently means something else is worse than not having it. This epic makes it matter: 'jump back to where I was' is exactly the move a human wants after being pulled to an agent pane.
design: If implementing: MRU is per-client (focus is client-local, ADR-0019), so it belongs in the client's driver state next to focused_pane (attach/driver.rs:1516), and '=' resolution needs access to it. Note that selector resolution is currently a pure function of the server's GET_STATE snapshot (selector.rs), so a client-local MRU does not fit that signature cleanly -- that is the real design question. For headless CLI/MCP callers there is no meaningful 'last focused' at all, which argues for scoping '=' to the attached TUI and making it an explicit error elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: Either '=' resolves to a genuinely different pane than '.' in the attached TUI (with a test), or it is gone from selector.rs, tui.md:249, and the grammar docs. No third option.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed.

title: Relay roll_back Regated arm clobbers a Retained snapshot (residual L1 9.1 edge on triple-coincidence path)
description: From v45.15 review: roll_back_subscription's Regated arm unconditionally sets the gate to Open, clobbering a SnapshotGate::Retained(snapshot) a return-leg snapshot established between the sync re-gate and the async error reply. Path: B event-subscribed to term 9 upgrades to attach (AwaitingFirst); consumer C attached so a resync snapshot fans to B while B mailbox full -> B.gate=Retained; B's upgrade attach returns transient error -> roll_back forces Open, discarding retained snapshot -> next delta delivered with no snapshot (L1 9.1 violation). Self-heals on next resync; rare triple-coincidence. Fix: roll_back Regated should only reopen when gate is still AwaitingFirst, leave Retained intact. Also the ~1 RTT EVENT-frame suppression during the upgrade AwaitingFirst window (best-effort, bounded).
close_reason: Closed

title: Input lane: ROUTE_INPUT stays inline while INPUT_* routes via lane — mixed frames to one pane lose ordering; interleave test doesn't evidence preemption
description: From 51n6.2 review: (1) handle_route_input (ROUTE_INPUT) still try_sends to the pane mailbox inline on the main thread while INPUT_* frames route via the input lane, so a single client mixing INPUT_* and ROUTE_INPUT to one pane loses wire ordering (not covered by the ADR-0044 INPUT-vs-ACQUIRE/RELEASE timing shift). Route ROUTE_INPUT through the lane too, or document the ordering constraint. (2) lane_routed_input_interleaves_with_a_large_pty_output_burst mirrors the inline test and would pass with inline routing — it exercises the actor's biased-select fairness, not the lane's off-thread preemption; add a test that honestly evidences the root-fix property. Also: a full accept-loop + real-clients shutdown regression test (the class the input_lane drop-hang bug slipped through).
close_reason: Routed local ROUTE_INPUT through dedicated input lane with mixed FIFO, off-thread, lease, satellite, and live-client shutdown regression coverage

title: Wire base_seq on TERMINAL_OUTPUT to close the loss-tolerant residual bound (full Mosh SSP)
description: ADR-0042's loss-tolerant advance-on-ack model heals the dominant loss mode (a frame the relay never delivered) exactly, because the consumer stays at the last-acked state. The residual: a row that flips A->B->A across a DELIVERED-but-unacked frame within one RTT can be missed (the acked->live diff sees A->A). Closing it needs the wire to carry the delta's base seq and the client to apply a delta only when its mirror state matches that base (the Mosh fragment/datagram layer). This is a wire-versioned change (new TERMINAL_OUTPUT field + client base-match apply). See ADR-0042 Tradeoffs and Alternatives (Port Mosh's SSP wire).
notes: Scoping note 2026-07-15: this is a wire change in the same state-sync family as phux-kztd (loss-tolerance activation bit). If both proceed, do them in ONE spec bump/PR wave -- each alone requires docs/spec + CHANGELOG + version bump, and they land on adjacent frames (TERMINAL_OUTPUT here, ATTACH_TERMINAL/caps there). See phux-kztd's design field for the activation-topology decision that this residual-bound work builds on.

title: Relay: SubscribeEvents->Attach upgrade on same terminal leaves snapshot gate Open; Bell dropped for gated subscriber
description: From v45.14 review: (1) register_subscriber's idempotent branch ignores awaits_snapshot, so a same-client upgrade from SubscribeTerminalEvents (gate Open) to AttachTerminal keeps the gate Open and that attach's deltas aren't gated ahead of its snapshot. Pre-existing (event subs already receive fanned TerminalOutput). (2) Bell frames route through fan_out and are suppressed-then-dropped for an AwaitingFirst gated subscriber (only TerminalClosed was routed past the gate via fan_out_close) — acceptable but undocumented intentional drop.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #201 (dedicated input lane ADR-0044 + relay SnapshotGate upgrade edge). Residual follow-ups: phux-51n6.7, phux-v45.16.

title: Relay: second concurrent subscriber can see a delta before its own snapshot
description: From v45.12 review: register_subscriber inits pending_snapshot=None and fan_out delivers deltas unconditionally to a subscriber with no pending snapshot. When hub consumer B attaches to a satellite terminal already streaming to consumer A, B is added to subscribers immediately and the next inbound TERMINAL_OUTPUT (A's stream) reaches B before B's own return-leg snapshot (~1 RTT later) — the L1 9.1 violation v45.12's spec text claims to hold. Pre-existing v45.7, outside v45.12's briefly-full-mailbox scope. Fix: mark a newly-registered subscriber as awaiting-first-snapshot and suppress its deltas until that snapshot lands (reuse pending_snapshot machinery). Also: TerminalClosed/Bell suppressed-then-dropped when a pending-snapshot subscriber is reaped (best-effort close delivery); Seized event hardcodes Running lifecycle.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #198 (SnapshotGate: gate second-subscriber deltas until its own snapshot lands; best-effort TerminalClosed delivery)

title: Copy hygiene: PTY reader BytesMut reuse, vectored write_frame, key-options memoization
description: From the latency map (51n6 CHEAP): (1) PTY reader buf[..n].to_vec() (spawn.rs ~232) -> BytesMut split_to(n).freeze(); (2) collapse per-consumer pump->Outbound mpsc->writer_task hop for single-consumer + write_frame(header, Bytes) with write_all_vectored (attach.rs ~910, client.rs ~1078, encode.rs ~140); (3) memoize set_options_from_terminal (input/key.rs ~76) when grid modes unchanged + send Bytes on input encode. NOTE: TerminalId clone was a misdiagnosis — do not intern. Do NOT chase the FLOOR items (client mirror parse, echo round-trip, TLV scratch).
close_reason: Investigated all three micro-optimizations; landed 0/3 — each fails the clean-win/no-regression bar: (1) PTY-reader uninit BytesMut read is unsound per Read contract and safe alternatives realloc (worse than to_vec for sub-4KB reads); (2) vectored write_frame is a cross-cutting wire-core change (QUIC/WT gain nothing, tokio lacks write_all_vectored) with real correctness risk; (3) encoders already return borrowed slices from reused buffers, Bytes would add allocation. Documented so this isn't re-attempted. FLOOR items correctly left alone.

title: Upstream follow-up: Formatter::new with selection Some(_) still unsound at libghostty-rs 8e1b0f7

But the Formatter::new selection path remains unsound at pin 8e1b0f7: new_inner stores &s.inner where s is the Selection moved out of the by-value Option in the match arm, so the borrow dangles before opts.into() runs (documented in phux-server/src/search.rs module notes). Either fix upstream in libghostty-rs and bump the pin, or keep the standing rule that phux never uses Formatter with selection: Some(_). Parent epic: phux-abi.
notes: Upstream issue filed 2026-07-11: https://github.com/phall1/libghostty-rs/issues/8 (enabled issues on the fork to do so). Documents the Formatter::new_inner dangling-pointer unsoundness with mechanism + suggested fix. Confirmed still present at the current phux pin 81b776c6 (upstream head 0006e130 is only a build tweak, no Formatter fix — so bumping the pin does NOT resolve this). Bead stays deferred until the fork/upstream fixes it and phux repins; phux's format_selection_alloc workaround remains the standing rule.
close_reason: RESOLVED: user fixed the Formatter::new selection unsoundness in their fork (phall1/libghostty-rs@130d9e5) with a borrowed lifetime-tracked with_selection(&Selection) API; phux repinned to the fork via PR #202 (merge e86eeb6, full just ci green, 2239 tests). The dangling-pointer path is gone. Issue filed at phall1/libghostty-rs#8 for the upstream PR. The copy-mode swarm (ADR-0045) can now use with_selection and drop the format_selection_alloc-only workaround.

Repro before fix: 5/20 loaded runs failed, failures at 2.08-2.11s wall. Fix: generous 60s HANG_GUARD const for both continuum completion tests (timeout semantics still covered by action_runtime_times_out_and_reports_cancellation). title: Pane Kill sends group-SIGKILL, gives foreground claude no chance to flush
description: Secondary/lower-priority companion to phux-0db. TerminalSignal::Kill sends a group-SIGKILL via killpg (phux-server/src/terminal_actor/mod.rs:1324-1344, :1340-1343). Killing a pane from the client while claude is the foreground process (instead of exiting claude first) gives claude no chance to flush its transcript. The clean shell-exit path (handle_pty_eof, mod.rs:1749-1756) reaps gracefully and sends no signal, so 'quit claude, then exit the shell' is fine. Consider a graceful SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL with a grace window for pane kills.
notes: Recovered during JSONL/Dolt reconciliation from pre-session .beads/issues.jsonl sha256=49d185e9801b56e9f7e12e6d7548b2143a84803ffb46d01072fa9fa85ec5ccce. Prior differing fields (verbatim JSON): {"close_reason":"Closed","closed_at":"2026-07-04T13:52:13Z","dependencies":[{"created_at":"2026-07-03T15:00:31Z","created_by":"jamesponwith","depends_on_id":"phux-0db","issue_id":"phux-sw1","metadata":"{}","type":"related"}],"dependent_count":0,"notes":"Implemented on branch claude-persistence. Root cause was more precise than the bead's pointer: the killpg-SIGKILL at deliver_signal (mod.rs:1324) is the DELIBERATE ADR-0033 TerminalSignal::Kill control (left as-is on purpose). The actual pane-CLOSE path (kill-pane action -> SPAWN_KILL / phux kill -> handle_kill_terminals -> detach_terminal_actor -> token cancel -> shutdown_pty) hard-killed via std Child::kill (SIGKILL of the shell pid, no grace). Fix: shutdown_pty now async; when the child is still alive it calls new terminate_child_group which SIGHUPs the process group (natural terminal-hangup; interactive shells act on it promptly, so idle-pane close stays snappy), polls try_wait up to PANE_KILL_GRACE (500ms), then SIGKILLs the group as backstop. Master stays open during grace so a foreground claude can still write its transcript flush. Added regression test pane_kill_lets_foreground_process_flush_before_death (traps SIGHUP, writes marker, asserts marker present) - verified it FAILS if the graceful signal is swapped to SIGKILL. fmt+clippy clean; full phux-server suite 596 passed.","started_at":"2026-07-03T20:25:00Z","updated_at":"2026-07-04T13:52:13Z"}

title: WebTransport (HTTP/3 over QUIC) for the browser client
description: The browser-flavored QUIC upgrade (cf phux-84yt). Browsers cannot open raw QUIC/UDP sockets; WebTransport (over HTTP/3 = QUIC) is their only door to QUIC-class transport (multiplexed streams, no HOL blocking, connection migration, datagrams). Scope: when phux wants the QUIC experience in clients/phux-web, add a WebTransport path on the server (quinn + h3 + webtransport) sharing the same QUIC server as native QUIC. NOTE: phux-web only — a native consumer uses raw QUIC via quinn directly and does not need WebTransport. Still inherits QUIC UDP reachability constraints (relay bead). Lower priority; after native QUIC. Relates: phux-84yt, ADR-0025.
close_reason: Merged via PR #190 (WebTransport listener + phux-web fallback)

title: Relay/rendezvous so a phone can reach a NAT'd phux server
description: For reaching a NAT'd phux server when the user is NOT on an overlay/LAN. A server behind NAT/CGNAT cannot accept an inbound connection from a remote client. Solution: a relay with a public IP that both the server and the client dial OUTBOUND, which bridges them (Cloudflare Tunnel / Tailscale DERP / ngrok / VS Code tunnels style). Server side: phux dials OUT to a configured relay and accepts consumers routed back over the wss transport (phux-5vsr). Easiest over TCP+TLS/:443 (commodity L7 proxying) — a reason wss is Phase 1. This is the long-term own-the-whole-stack reachability option, independent of any overlay vendor. ADR alternatives: STUN/ICE hole-punching (fails on symmetric NAT -> TURN), or requiring an overlay.
notes: P3/later: not needed when the user runs an overlay (Tailscale/Headscale/WireGuard) or LAN — the overlay handles NAT traversal + encryption and the server only needs the pairing token. Build only for no-overlay users, after the auth protocol (phux-5vsr), if there is demand. Also the long-term escape from depending on any overlay vendor.
close_reason: ADR-0037 explicitly defers NAT relay/rendezvous to a WireGuard-class overlay network (Tailscale/Headscale) below the wire, and to an enterprise platform — phux stays overlay-agnostic and dials routable IPs with zero new code. Out of scope for phux core by decision.

title: audit: WebSocket write_frame allocates a Vec per frame via to_vec()
description:
CONFIRMED (audit phux-ahk). WsWriter::write_frame (crates/phux-server/src/transport.rs:216) calls frame.to_vec() to own the borrowed frame slice for Message::Binary. Every TERMINAL_OUTPUT frame to a WebSocket client (phux-web) allocates+copies the full frame, per-consumer per-tick on the WS path. The UDS path (UdsWriter::write_frame ~91) writes the borrowed slice directly with no copy.

FIX SKETCH: check whether tokio-tungstenite's Message::Binary can take Bytes/Arc<[u8]> to avoid the copy; if not, pool/reuse a frame buffer at the WsWriter level. Needs a small library-capability investigation (hence a bead). SEVERITY: low (only the WS transport; UDS unaffected).
notes: Still open. Confirmed by audit (WsWriter::write_frame copies the encoded frame per send). Investigated during branch hardening/snapshot-sgr-fidelity work: tokio-tungstenite/tungstenite pinned at 0.24 in Cargo.lock, whose Message::Binary takes Vec<u8>; the Bytes-payload API landed in tungstenite 0.26. The caller also hands write_frame a &[u8] borrowed from a reused encode buffer, so a copy is needed to own it for the async send regardless. UNBLOCK: bump tungstenite to >=0.26 then switch to Message::Binary(Bytes). WS path is the browser consumer, not the UDS/TUI path.
close_reason: Deferred (low value for v0.1, needs a wire-stack change to do right): the WS write_frame copy (frame.to_vec() into Message::Binary) is structural under the pinned tokio-tungstenite 0.24, whose Message::Binary owns a Vec<u8>. Avoiding it requires changing FrameWriter::write_frame from &[u8] to an owned Vec<u8>/Bytes so the WS path MOVES into Message::Binary -- a core Transport-trait signature change that only benefits the secondary browser/WS path (the primary UDS path is already zero-copy: write_all(&frame)). The clean version composes with a future tungstenite 0.26 bump (Bytes-based Message), which also lets the already-Bytes TerminalOutput payload flow through with no copy at all. Not worth the trait churn for the WS path pre-1.0.

title: audit: prime_reference allocates a fresh Vec per row at attach (reuse reset_geometry buffers)
description:
CONFIRMED (audit phux-ahk). SnapshotSynthesizer::prime_reference allocates a fresh Vec<u8> per viewport row at consumer registration (crates/phux-server/src/grid/synthesizer.rs:803) — 24 allocations for an 80x24 grid per attach. reset_geometry (grid/reference.rs:47) already pre-sizes rows_body to empty Vecs; prime could populate those in place by swap (same pattern as synthesize_against_reference ~707) instead of allocating fresh.

Not on the hot tick path (attach-time only), so low priority. FIX SKETCH: iterate the preallocated empty row bodies and fill in place via a single scratch buffer + swap. SEVERITY: low.
notes: SUPERSEDED by commit c345b49 (branch hardening/snapshot-sgr-fidelity). Rather than pool the per-row Vec allocs in prime_reference, register_consumer now SKIPS prime_reference entirely for raw (human) consumers — the reference it builds is never read on that path. So the per-row alloc cost is gone in the dominant mode without the pooling rework. The pooling optimization still applies if/when a tick-managed (StateSync) consumer attaches frequently, but is low priority.
close_reason: Won't-fix (premise doesn't hold): the per-row Vec<u8> bodies prime_reference allocates ARE the consumer's reference grid — N row bodies must be materialized once and retained, so N content allocations are irreducible. reset_geometry's rows_body = vec![Vec::new(); rows] are zero-capacity empties (no heap to reuse), and prime runs ONCE per consumer attach (not per tick). The per-TICK hot path already reuses capacity via mem::swap (synthesize_against_reference). 24 one-time allocs/attach is negligible and irreducible; no real win available.

title: phux-ign Part 1: prove kitty-KIP round-trip for real TUIs, then maybe restore TERM=ghostty
description:
Follow-up to phux-ign (Part 2 landed in commit feat(server): per-Terminal TERM as a phux-config default).

GOAL: prove phux input/output round-trips the kitty keyboard protocol (KIP) for representative TUIs (htop, less, vim, neovim, fzf, btop), then EITHER restore TERM=ghostty as the default (revert 9734d42 swap, with a regression test) OR keep TERM=xterm-256color if a real gap persists.

WHY IT IS NOT DONE:
1. The representative TUIs are NOT nix-pinned. On this host htop/nvim/btop/fzf resolve to /opt/homebrew or /usr/bin (host-provided), and flake.nix declares none of them. The only spawn fixtures the test suite uses are /bin/sh and cat (POSIX-guaranteed). A test depending on host-installed TUIs is non-reproducible and would skip/flake in CI and other contributors sandboxes, so it cannot be the robust proof Part 1 requires.
2. The phux-7vx root cause is that TERM=ghostty terminfo advertises fullkbd, ncurses pushes CSI>Nu, libghostty pivots the per-pane encoder to CSI-u, and htop does NOT parse incoming CSI-u for the keys it owns -> q quit is dropped. That lack of CSI-u parsing is in htop, external to phux. Existing tests (crates/phux-server/tests/htop_keys.rs) already prove: (a) under xterm-256color plain q round-trips as 0x71; (b) the encoder DOES emit CSI-u once an app pushes kitty flags. Restoring TERM=ghostty would re-break htop unless a real KIP round-trip with these apps is demonstrated.

REMAINING MANUAL SMOKE (must be run on a machine that actually has the apps, or after pinning them in flake.nix):
- Build phux, set defaults.term="ghostty" (now a config knob, no code change needed thanks to Part 2).
- phux attach demo; run htop; press q -> must quit. Repeat for F-keys.
- Run nvim/vim: enter/exit insert mode, :q -> must work; arrow keys, function keys.
- Run btop: q to quit, function keys.
- Run less: q to quit, navigation keys.
- Run fzf: type-to-filter, Enter/Esc.
If ALL round-trip cleanly under TERM=ghostty, flip defaults.term default to "ghostty" in phux-config schema + default.toml and add a regression test (ideally after pinning at least one KIP-aware TUI in flake.nix so the test is reproducible). If htop (or any) still drops keys, keep xterm-256color; the per-spawn env override and the new defaults.term knob already let a user opt into ghostty deliberately.

title: audit: search Match.col is a char offset, not a grid column — diverges past wide glyphs
description:
CONFIRMED (latent). search::Match.col/len (crates/phux-server/src/search.rs:86-96) are char offsets into the right-trimmed projected row String, NOT grid columns. For any row containing a wide (CJK/emoji) glyph before the match, char offset != grid column (off by one column per preceding wide glyph). The module doc (search.rs:25-57) already flags that match coordinates are meant to be handed to a libghostty Selection (which is grid-COLUMN based) for extraction. So when the upstream extraction bridge unblocks (the dangling-pointer pin in Formatter::new_inner, search.rs safe_api_selection_formatter_bridge_is_broken_at_pin), naively passing Match.col as a grid column will mis-locate selections.

SEVERITY: low/latent — extraction is currently blocked upstream so nothing consumes these coords as grid columns yet, but the trap will bite whoever wires the bridge. Also affects any UI that highlights a match by grid column.

REPRO/pin: crates/phux-server/src/grid.rs::audit_line_char_offset_diverges_from_grid_column_past_wide_glyph (shows X at char offset 1 but grid column 2 after a wide glyph).

FIX SKETCH: either (a) report a second grid-column coordinate alongside the char offset, computed during find_in_row by walking the row's cells with display widths, or (b) document on Match.col that callers must remap char->grid-col via the row walk before building a Selection, and provide a helper. Parent: phux-ahk.
close_reason: Already resolved on main. Fix-sketch (b) is fully implemented: crates/phux-server/src/extract.rs provides char_col_to_grid_x() — the row cell-walk that inverts char-offset->grid-column, skipping SpacerTail and advancing by display width — and extract_match()/extract_match_in_scope() are the real in-tree consumers that remap before building a libghostty Selection. The search::Match docstring (search.rs) documents the char-offset-vs-grid-column trap at both type and field level and points callers at the helper. Tests prove it: extract::wide_glyph_before_match_shifts_grid_column and scrollback_match_with_wide_glyph_round_trips. Sketch (a) (redundant grid-col field on Match) was deliberately rejected and documented as such (dead weight to keep in sync; add only if a consumer needs the raw column without the walk). No grid-column-highlighting UI consumer exists yet; when one appears it uses the same helper.

title: Wire up libghostty Selection+Formatter extraction bridge once upstream pin fixes Formatter::new_inner
description: phux-3sy shipped find-in-scrollback but could not ship the extraction wrapper (Match coords -> libghostty Selection -> Formatter -> text/VT/HTML). Root cause: at libghostty-rs pin acc4b87, the safe crate's Formatter::new_inner takes &raw const of a match-arm-local copy of the Copy ffi::Selection, so the selection-restricted format path passes a dangling pointer and libghostty returns InvalidValue. The types are all public (screen::Selection, Terminal::grid_ref, fmt::Formatter) — only the upstream pointer bug blocks it. The test safe_api_selection_formatter_bridge_is_broken_at_pin in crates/phux-server/src/search.rs pins the gap and will fail when the pin moves. When it does: bump the libghostty-vt rev, implement extract(terminal, Match, Scope, Format) building a linear Selection from two grid_ref endpoints (note the char-offset vs grid-column mapping caveat for wide glyphs), and flip the pin test into a passing extraction round-trip.
close_reason: Bridge complete: pin 8e1b0f7 fixed the upstream Formatter::new_inner dangling-pointer bug via the sound one-shot format_selection_alloc API (pin test already flipped to safe_api_selection_formatter_bridge_round_trips_at_pin). This wave adds the remaining Format dimension: extract(terminal, Match, Scope, Format) -> Vec<u8> for text/VT/HTML in phux-server/src/extract.rs, String helpers delegate to it, stale blocked-upstream docs removed from search.rs. Note: Formatter::new with selection: Some(_) is STILL unsound at 8e1b0f7 (new_inner stores &s.inner of a moved local); phux uses only the one-shot API. Commit 90f9e10 on wave25/97w-selection-bridge.

title: Scrollback search primitive + safe wrappers for libghostty selection helpers
description: libghostty_vt (pin Uzaaft/libghostty-rs acc4b87) exposes cell/scrollback access (Point::History, total_rows, scrollback_rows), selection helpers (select_word/select_line/select_output OSC-133-aware, in libghostty-vt-sys C API, NOT yet wrapped in the safe Rust API), and a Formatter (fmt.rs) to extract selection text/VT/HTML. It exposes NO search/regex. Verdict from audit: selection+extraction = delegate (write thin safe wrappers over the FFI helpers); search = build a thin find-in-scrollback over the server's existing scrollback mirror (src/grid.rs), handing match coords to libghostty Selection+Formatter for extraction. This is NOT a tmux copy-mode reimplementation. Update the CONTRIBUTING no-list 'no copy-mode reinvention' item to say precisely: selection/copy delegates to host terminal + libghostty; phux owns only find-in-scrollback.
notes:
SEARCH (build) = DONE: find-in-scrollback primitive shipped in crates/phux-server/src/search.rs with full test coverage. CONTRIBUTING no-list updated. SELECTION/EXTRACTION (delegate) = PARTIAL/BLOCKED upstream: verified against pin acc4b87 — the safe Selection+Formatter types are public, but Formatter::new_inner passes a dangling pointer for the selection (Copy ffi::Selection addressed as a match-arm temporary), so selection-restricted formatting returns InvalidValue. Extraction wrapper deferred to phux-97w; gap pinned by a regression test. OSC-133 boundary helpers intentionally not wrapped (that is the engine we refuse to reimplement).
UNBLOCKED (per phux-7143 scoping): the one-shot libghostty select_* API (select_word/select_line/select_all/select_output, safe Terminal wrappers at libghostty selection.rs:201-247; sound per search.rs:39-60) works at the pinned rev 6d49dfd. Only Formatter{selection:Some(_)} (phux-97w) is buggy — search can use the one-shot path. Swarm-able as its own group (server/core search primitive).

title: Gate ROUTE_INPUT on a PRIMARY role policy (reject viewers with PERMISSION_DENIED)
description: phux-3j3 added Command::RouteInput (tag 0x08), a side-effect-free input route. SPEC input.md §7 documents it as primary-only, but the server (handle_route_input in runtime.rs) does not yet enforce a RolePolicy/PRIMARY gate — no role machinery is wired for control commands today. When role enforcement lands for input, ROUTE_INPUT must reject non-primary/viewer connections with PERMISSION_DENIED to match the spec.
design: DESIGN (wave-10 read-only pass, go=WAIT-FOR-TRANSPORT): No materialized role state today — roles are per-TERMINAL (not per-connection), defaulting to PRIMARY on ATTACH (L1.md §7.1). PRIMARY is implicit: a client in terminal_subscribers[tid] has an active subscription. Gate site: runtime.rs:2158 handle_route_input. PermissionDenied error code ALREADY EXISTS. Option 1 (interim, cheap): add client_id to handle_route_input, reject unattached/unsubscribed clients with PermissionDenied — no role map needed. Option 3: full terminal_roles: HashMap<TerminalId,HashMap<ClientId,TerminalRole>>. WHY WAIT: connection identity (ClientId, attached/client_layers/terminal_subscribers) is exactly what the phux-web Transport-trait extraction (phux-486.4) is reshaping; building role enforcement on it now risks a one-way-door rework. Revisit once 486.4 lands; the call-site signature should stay stable (internal lookup changes only).
close_reason: Interim PRIMARY-role gate for ROUTE_INPUT (Option 1): handle_route_input rejects unsubscribed/viewer with existing PermissionDenied; PRIMARY approximated by active subscription. client_id threaded so the full role-map swap is a no-caller-change later. Landed 88477b1.
